<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_mcp_reference.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

An MCP client reaches Doctored through `doctored-mcp`, a stdio MCP server bundled
inside the app at `Doctored.app/Contents/Helpers/doctored-mcp`. **Settings ▸ MCP**
shows its path and copies the command that adds it to Claude Code
(`claude mcp add --scope user doctored -- '<path>'`). The helper answers `initialize`
and `ping` itself, lists tools from the running app (or, when none is running, from
the catalog bundled with it), and opens Doctored in the background on the first
tool call that finds it not running.

The helper reaches the app over a Unix socket the app binds at every launch,
`~/Library/Application Support/Doctored/Agent/agent.sock`, in a folder only its
owner can open; `DR_AGENT_SOCKET` names another path for both. There is no TCP
endpoint.

This build exposes **337 tools**. The reference is generated from the app's
`tools/list` catalog (live, or the snapshot the build writes from the same code),
which is authoritative. Tool results are MCP
content blocks; most calls return a JSON object in a text block, while `render` and
some inspection calls can also return image blocks. Tool failures set `isError: true`
and include a readable message.

Regenerate this page from a running instance's socket, or from a built bundle's
catalog with no app running:

```sh
python3 scripts/generate_mcp_reference.py --socket <the instance's DR_AGENT_SOCKET>
python3 scripts/generate_mcp_reference.py --catalog Doctored.app/Contents/Resources/agent-catalog.json
```

Add `--check` to either to verify that the checked-in page matches the catalog.

## `list_documents`

Lists the images open in Doctored with their ids, sizes, and layer counts.

Takes no arguments.

## `inspect_psd`

Inspects a PSD, a Large Document PSB or a TIFF with Photoshop layers (format says which: PSD, PSB or TIFF) before editing: verified per-file losses, parser observations, general importer limits, embedded RGB profile/PPI, and saved-composite availability. import_precision says which document the file opens as: rgba8, or rgba16 for a 16-bit RGB PSD, which opens as a 16-bit document with either choice, or rgba32 for a 32-bit RGB PSD or PSB, which opens as a 32-bit float document with either choice, or for a 32-bit float RGB TIFF with layers in either byte order, whose layers open as a 32-bit float document. Photoshop Invert, Threshold, Posterize, Levels, Curves, Color Balance, Hue/Saturation, Photo Filter, Exposure, Vibrance, Black & White, Channel Mixer, Selective Color and Brightness/Contrast layers are carried as Doctored adjustment layers (parameters mapped, appearance can differ), and a Pattern Fill layer (PtFl), RGB or CMYK, as a Doctored pattern fill layer with its tile from the file's Patt/Pat2 table, and a Solid Color Fill layer (SoCo), RGB or CMYK, as a Doctored solid color fill layer with its colour (one outside sRGB kept as a wide colour), and a Gradient Fill layer (GdFl), RGB or CMYK, as a Doctored gradient fill layer with its stops, style, angle, scale and reverse (settings it cannot hold named as losses); every other adjustment or fill layer carries no pixels and Import Layers omits it with a per-record loss. Empty layers import as empty canvas-sized layers, and both depths keep clipping. ZIP-compressed channels are read at both depths. A layered TIFF reports stored_composite_available false: its flat image is the ordinary TIFF open (open_document without psd_mode). Creates no document. Pass source_fingerprint to open_document as psd_fingerprint. A CMYK file (colour mode 4) answers import_precision "cmyk" with its layered availability, layered_plan_bytes and the losses its CMYK document cannot hold (the adjustment kinds it does not carry), each named per record; layer effects, knockout and Blend If ranges (Gray, Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black) carry on every record, a Pass Through group included. A Grayscale file (colour mode 1) at 8 or 16 bits — PSD, PSB or a layered gray TIFF — or a 32-bit PSD or PSB answers import_precision "gray": it opens as a Grayscale document with either choice, its effects' Grsc colours carried as gray, Blend If on Gray only, a refused adjustment and every fill layer omitted by name, profile the embedded Gray profile (null when untagged: the working Gray is assigned at open; at 32 bits the linear twin of a built-in names that built-in). A Lab TIFF (CIELab or ICCLab, chunky, 8 or 16 bits, no alpha or an unassociated one), or a Lab PSD, PSB or layered TIFF at 8 or 16 bits (inspect_psd answers import_precision "lab"), opens as a Lab Color document at its own depth with either psd_mode, keeping its L*a*b* values; an embedded profile is not used. An Indexed Color PSD or PSB answers import_precision indexed, layered_available false and its stored composite's availability. A Duotone PSD or PSB (colour mode 8, 8 or 16 bits) answers import_precision "gray", color_mode Duotone and duotone (its options), and opens as a Duotone document. A Bitmap (colour mode 0) PSD or PSB answers import_precision "bitmap": no layers (layered_available false), its stored composite opens as a Bitmap document.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | Absolute or ~ path to a PSD, PSB or layered TIFF file. |

## `open_document`

Opens an image file (PNG, JPEG, PSD, PSB, TIFF, BMP, GIF, WebP, HEIC/HEIF, AVIF, JPEG XL, JPEG 2000, OpenEXR, Radiance HDR, PDF, SVG, camera RAW, Doctored (.doctored, and legacy .rz)) in a new editor window and returns its document id. A camera RAW opens as a 16-bit document, or as a 32-bit float document holding its scene-linear development with raw.output_encoding linear_float (Develop > Document depth). An HDR photo — a gain-map HEIC/AVIF, or a PQ/HLG HEIC, AVIF, PNG (cICP) or JPEG XL — opens as a 32-bit float document in linear light (File > Open HDR Photos as HDR, on by default; hdr_photo overrides it for this open): 1.0 is the gain map's SDR base white, or 203 cd/m2 of a PQ/HLG signal, and the reply's hdr_open says {kind, rendition, reference_white}. hdr_photo "sdr" opens a gain-map photo as its SDR base (disclosed) and refuses a PQ/HLG still by name (it has no SDR rendition); the original file is not kept in the document. A PDF or SVG is RASTERIZED on the way in: pass page (1-based) and ppi to choose which page and at what resolution, and call inspect_vector first for the page count and sizes. PSD requires inspect_psd first and an explicit layers/composite choice; unsupported color/depth never silently falls back to an 8-bit platform decode. A 16-bit RGB PSD (inspect_psd import_precision "rgba16") opens as a 16-bit document, and a 32-bit RGB PSD or PSB, or a 32-bit layered TIFF's layers ("rgba32"), as a 32-bit float document. The PSD layers choice carries Photoshop Invert/Threshold/Posterize/Levels/Curves/Color Balance/Hue-Saturation/Photo Filter/Exposure/Vibrance/Black & White/Channel Mixer/Selective Color/Brightness-Contrast layers as adjustment layers, Pattern Fill layers (PtFl, RGB or CMYK) as pattern fill layers, Solid Color Fill layers (SoCo) as solid color fill layers and Gradient Fill layers (GdFl) as gradient fill layers, omits every other pixel-less adjustment/fill layer, imports empty layers empty, and retains clipping at either depth. A PSB is a PSD here. A TIFF with Photoshop layers opens flat, as one layer, unless psd_mode is layers (with its inspect_psd fingerprint), which imports its layers at the file's depth. A genuine floating-point TIFF, an OpenEXR file (.exr) and a Radiance RGBE file (.hdr) open as a 32-BIT FLOAT document: linear light with an extended range, where values above white and below zero are kept exactly. precision:"rgba8" is refused on one — convert explicitly after opening instead. OpenEXR and Radiance carry no ICC profile: stated Rec.709 primaries (or none) open as sRGB, Display P3 primaries as Display P3, and any other primaries are converted once, in linear light, to sRGB primaries — the import warnings say which. An OpenEXR file opens its first part that is not deep and has R, G and B channels, on a canvas the size of its display window, with its associated alpha unpremultiplied; a file holding a deep part or no RGB part is refused by name. A Radiance file opens opaque; its EXPOSURE and COLORCORR lines are reported and not applied. A CMYK TIFF or JPEG (with its own CMYK profile, or untagged while a working CMYK profile is set) opens as a CMYK DOCUMENT keeping its own ink and profile; a TIFF's transparency is kept, its planar layout read and any extra samples named in the import warnings; precision "rgba8" keeps the conversion to sRGB. A CMYK PSD, PSB or layered TIFF opens as a CMYK document with either psd_mode: "layers" imports its rasters, masks, groups (Normal and Pass Through), clipping, the 27 CMYK modes, opacity, Fill and its Levels, Curves and Hue/Saturation layers; "composite" its saved composite (a TIFF has none: without psd_mode it opens flat). Both follow Color Settings' CMYK policy. A Grayscale PSD, PSB or layered TIFF at 8 or 16 bits, or a PSD or PSB at 32 (inspect_psd import_precision "gray"), opens as a Grayscale document at its depth with either psd_mode, its Gray profile kept (an untagged file takes the working Gray); a one-channel float TIFF with a Gray profile opens as a 32-bit Grayscale document. A Lab TIFF (CIELab or ICCLab, chunky, 8 or 16 bits, no alpha or an unassociated one), or a Lab PSD, PSB or layered TIFF at 8 or 16 bits (inspect_psd answers import_precision "lab"), opens as a Lab Color document at its own depth with either psd_mode, keeping its L*a*b* values; an embedded profile is not used. An Indexed Color PSD or PSB opens from its stored composite (psd_mode composite) as an Indexed Color document, keeping its palette, transparent index and every index. A Duotone PSD or PSB (colour mode 8, 8 or 16 bits) answers import_precision "gray", color_mode Duotone and duotone (its options), and opens as a Duotone document. A 1-bit gray PNG (no tRNS), a 1-bit TIFF or a 1 bpp black-and-white BMP opens as a Bitmap document; precision rgba8 keeps the 8-bit RGB open. A Bitmap PSD or PSB opens with psd_mode composite only (it holds no layers).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `hdr_photo` | `string` | no | one of `hdr`, `sdr` | HDR photos only (gain-map HEIC/AVIF, PQ/HLG stills): hdr opens a 32-bit float document at full headroom, sdr a gain map's SDR base (a PQ/HLG still refuses sdr). Absent = the File > Open HDR Photos as HDR preference (on by default). Revert keeps the rendition a document was opened with. |
| `page` | `integer` | no | — | PDF/SVG only: which page to rasterize, 1-based. Default 1. |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | Absolute or ~ path to the file. |
| `ppi` | `number` | no | — | PDF/SVG only: the resolution to rasterize at, 1…30000. Default 300. |
| `precision` | `string` | no | one of `preserve`, `rgba8` | PNG/TIFF16: preserve samples and profile (default), or deliberately open reduced 8-bit pixels. Native typed files always preserve depth. A floating-point TIFF, OpenEXR or Radiance file opens only as 32-bit float and refuses rgba8. |
| `psd_fingerprint` | `string` | no | — | PSD, PSB and layered TIFF only: source_fingerprint returned by inspect_psd. Changed sources refuse. |
| `psd_mode` | `string` | no | one of `layers`, `composite` | PSD, PSB and layered TIFF only: import supported layers or the file's saved composite as one raster layer (a layered TIFF's composite is its ordinary flat open). |
| `raw` | `object` | no | — | Develop settings for a CAMERA RAW (CR3, CR2, NEF, ARW, DNG, Apple ProRAW, ORF, RW2, RAF, SRW, PEF). Omit it, or any key in it, to keep the value the file itself reports — an empty object is a valid "as shot" develop, and an agent open never shows the Develop dialog either way. Ignored, with a note in the result, for a file that is not developed as a camera RAW — one Core Image will not develop, and one that is already open, use redevelop_raw to change an already-open retained RAW. Keys: exposure (stops, -4..4); temperature (2000..50000 K) and tint (-150..150) — one coupled white balance, so passing either leaves the as-shot balance and the other half comes from the file; tone_curve (0..1, the global curve, 0 = linear); shadows (0..2, no effect while tone_curve is 0); contrast (0..1, LOCAL contrast on edges); sharpness (0..1); detail (0..3); luminance_noise (0..1); baseline_compensation (−4..4 stops relative to each camera's own captured baseline); moire (0..1, only supported camera decoders); vignette {edge_exposure:−4..4, center:[x,y] normalized0..1, falloff:0.25..4} applies calibrated manual source lens compensation after local development. source_geometry is an explicit lens profile {profile_id,center:[x,y],radial:[k1,k2,k3],red_scale,blue_scale,filter}; its native inverse radial/TCA sampling follows local composition. Global transfer preserves each target's native local masks and optical calibration. grain {amount:0..100 (required), size:0.5..4 px (default 1), roughness:0..100 (default 50)} is the Add Grain kernel applied LAST, after local development, vignette and explicit optics; amount 0 removes it, omitted size/roughness take the defaults (not the saved values), and its seed is the first 8 bytes of the embedded camera file's SHA-256, so redevelopment, reopen, presets and sync reproduce identical grain. texture, clarity and dehaze (each −100..100, 0 = off) are Filter ▸ Presence on the finished 16-bit development, after local development, vignette and explicit optics and just before grain (dehaze first, then texture and clarity of the dehazed picture); their radii scale with the image's long side, so the look does not depend on resolution; an omitted one keeps its saved value. color_noise (0..1); lens_correction (bool, Enable Profile Corrections: the lens profile the file carries, or when its decoder has none the bundled Lensfun profile matched at the first development (never both); omitted, it is ON for every file that carries one or matched one, not as shot, and open_document reports lens_profile {lens, supported, enabled, source: decoder\|lensfun\|null, lensfun: {id, model}\|null}); highlight_recovery (bool, needs macOS 26 or newer and refused by name below it). A value outside its range is refused by name rather than clamped. A control this particular file's decoder does not support is refused. output_space selects the retained master encoding, normalized SDR16: srgb (default on initial open), display_p3, adobe_rgb (Adobe RGB (1998)) or prophoto_rgb (ProPhoto RGB at gamma 1.8 with no ROMM linear toe, best in a 16-bit document). A colour outside the chosen space is clamped per channel to 0 or 65535 in it; neutral highlights clip at the same exposure in every space. get_raw_source reports the source; get_color_profile reports the document profile, which redevelopment preserves. Omit output_space during redevelopment to retain the saved choice. output_encoding selects the master: sdr16 (normalized 16-bit SDR, the default on open) or linear_float, the 32-bit float (linear) development: scene-linear f32 in output_space's primaries with the highlights the sensor recorded above the SDR white kept above 1.0. At tone_curve 0, where it starts unless one is named, it is linear in exposure with no highlight shoulder, so it looks brighter in the highlights than the 16-bit development until tone-mapped, and where a channel exceeds white it differs in hue as well (the 16-bit development moves such a colour toward white). With it tone_curve and shadows are the decoder's own under the extended range and keep values above white (shadows is inert at tone_curve 0); grain applies on the display encoding (each channel's encoded value moves by the 16-bit grain's offset for the pixel's encoded luma, unclamped, so a pixel at or above white keeps its value); nonzero texture, clarity or dehaze are refused. It exists only in a 32-bit float document: open_document with it opens one (refused with precision rgba8), place_image into a float document uses it by default, and it refuses on a layer of an 8- or 16-bit document. RAW presets and sync never carry it. as_shot_white_balance:true restores captured as-shot balance and cannot combine with temperature/tint. Omitted redevelopment fields keep saved values. |

## `get_document`

Full state of one document: canvas size and every layer's name, size, offset, opacity, blend mode, visibility, layer mask (has_mask, mask_enabled), and clipped flag (see set_layer_clipped). STRUCTURE is reported on every row: kind ("layer" or "group"), depth, parent, and — on a group — children and open. The array stays flat and bottom-first, with a group's children BEFORE it. content_x/y/width/height is the box of actually opaque pixels (what align_layers and distribute_layers act on); offset/width/height is the pixel BUFFER rect, which is usually a different rectangle, and on a group row is the union of its layers' buffers. locks and linked appear when set; a row inside a locked group also reports inherited_locks (the locks an enclosing group imposes that the row's own locks lack) and lock_owner (each of those names mapped to the index of the nearest group holding it, the layer to clear with set_layer_lock); pixel_layer_count counts leaves, layer_count counts entries. A STYLED layer reports a style object — its whole effect stack and blending options as the canonical JSON set_layer_style takes back — and the document reports global_light (angle, altitude). A re-editable TEXT layer also reports a text object (string, font, size, color, alignment, weight, italic, tracking, leading, baseline_shift, underline, strikethrough, box_width, transform, origin) — those are the layers edit_text_layer can change — a SHAPE layer a shape object (kind, w, h, fill, stroke, stroke_width, radius, transform, origin); a layer without those keys is plain pixels. transform is the layer's 2×2 map [a, b, c, d], row-major — (x, y) maps to (a·x + b·y, c·x + d·y) — and origin the exact canvas position of its source's top-left (the text block's, the shape box's; fractional after a transform). An ADJUSTMENT layer reports is_adjustment true plus an adjustment object (op, params) — those are the layers edit_adjustment_layer can change. A document that carries ALPHA CHANNELS (saved selections, never part of the picture) also reports a channels array of {index, name, overlay_color, overlay_opacity, color_indicates} — list_channels returns the same list. A document that carries GUIDES also reports a guides array of {index, orientation, position} — non-printing lines in canvas pixels that tools snap to, never part of the picture; list_guides returns the same list. ruler is always present: origin_x/origin_y are the ruler's zero point in canvas pixels (document state, set with set_ruler_origin, affecting only what the on-screen rulers LABEL), and unit is the app-wide ruler-unit preference, not part of this document. operation_scope lists supported edit targets; edit_target is the UI target. Layer index 0 is the bottom layer; offsets are measured from the canvas top-left corner, y increasing down. A 16-bit or 32-bit float document reports the same keys in the same shape plus typed extras (subtree_start, bounds, dimensions, link, mask, blend_if, offset, description_bytes, blend_evaluation): the same keys, shape and vocabulary (kind layer/group, opacity to two decimals, adjustment {op, params}), the adjustment object also carrying evaluation; each channel row also carries the typed id, dimensions and provenance. 16-bit documents include precision_support and typed record metadata; display previews never replace source samples. The reply carries an "evaluation" block beside "color_profile": the policy and projection_error, the sentence naming any operator this document cannot evaluate under it. A 32-bit float document also carries a "float" block: its storage, its extended range, its tone map and projection_error, the sentence naming any operator it cannot evaluate. A CMYK document reports color_mode "cmyk", its CMYK profile and declared depth; its pixels are shown through a Display P3 view. Its text, shape and fill objects report their colours as ink in percent (ink, fill_ink, stroke_ink, a stop's ink) beside the sRGB appearance hex. An Indexed Color document reports color_mode indexed and indexed {colors, transparent_index}. A Duotone document reports color_mode duotone and duotone {type, inks}; its gray block and pixels are the Grayscale document's. A Bitmap document reports color_mode bitmap.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `render`

Renders the flattened canvas (or one layer) as a PNG image so you can see it. Use this to inspect the picture before and after edits. scale enlarges the render by an exact integer factor with nearest-neighbour sampling, so every pixel becomes a crisp scale×scale block (for pixel art). Native layer/group and scalar rendering is an explicit byte display derivative. channel=mask shows raw coverage at its canvas placement; effective_mask applies density and feather and ignores the enabled switch for inspection. Neither display becomes editable native source data. region / preview_divisor render the 16-bit or float projection's window at native depth (equal to that crop of the full native render) and then display it like the full canvas; they admit groups (isolated or Pass Through, nested), layer masks, clipping masks, Blend If and layer styles on layers (effects included) and fill-only styles on groups, and layer indices in their refusals are the typed postorder record indices. At 32-bit float a layer, group or colour-plane render (red, green, blue, alpha, luma) goes through the document's tone map like the composite; a plane is read from that display. In a CMYK document channel is "cyan", "magenta", "yellow" or "black": that ink plane of the composite on paper, ink dark; clipping "shadows" or "highlights" is Levels' and Curves' ⌥ display of the composite: black where any ink is at 100 %, or white where every ink is at paper. region with preview_divisor d above 1 is the full view sampled at every d-th pixel of the region (x + i·d, y + j·d), ceil(w/d) × ceil(h/d). A Grayscale document renders its composite with no channel, channel gray (no layer: its one gray plane, the 8-bit display of its codes; at 32 bits of the tone-mapped display), channel mask with a layer, or an alpha channel's name with no layer; any other channel refuses. In a Lab Color document channel lightness, a or b with no layer renders that channel of the composite's codes in grayscale; channel mask takes a layer, an alpha channel is named with no layer, and every other channel refuses. On an Indexed Color document channel composite or index draws the composite (the Index channel through the palette) and an alpha channel's name its plane, with no layer; red, green, blue, alpha, mask or a channel with a layer refuses. A Bitmap document: channel composite or bitmap draws the composite, with no layer; any other channel, or a channel with layer, refuses: A Bitmap document renders its composite or its Bitmap channel (bitmap), with no layer: it has no colour, alpha or mask plane.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `channel` | `string` | no | — | Renders ONE plane as a grayscale PNG instead of the colour image: "red", "green", "blue", "alpha", "luma", or an alpha channel's name (list_channels shows them). With layer it is that layer's plane, canvas-sized with 0 outside the layer's rect; otherwise the flattened composite's. Use mask with a layer to inspect that layer's mask. |
| `clipping` | `string` | no | one of `shadows`, `highlights` | CMYK document only: the ⌥ clipping display. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `exposure` | `number` | no | — | 32-bit float documents only: a view exposure in stops, −20…20 (default 0), applied as gain 2^stops to RGB before the document's tone map; alpha is untouched. A tone-mapped render shows everything above white as white, so render at a negative exposure to SEE the highlights and at a positive one to see the shadows. It changes only this render: the document, its tone map and the window's own exposure (set_view) are not read or changed. For the flattened canvas or a region; refused with layer or channel, outside ±20, and when non-zero on a document that is not 32-bit float. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `max_side` | `integer` | no | — | Longest output side in px (64-4096, default 1024). |
| `preview_divisor` | `integer` | no | — | Integer >= 1 (default 1). Above 1 renders a PREVIEW of the region (the whole canvas when region is absent) that samples the top-left pixel of every divisor×divisor cell. Same refusals as region; not with layer or channel. |
| `region` | `object` | no | — | Renders only this canvas window {x, y, width, height} (integers, canvas pixels, inside the canvas) of the flattened canvas, exactly equal to that crop of the full render. Supported for layers, pointwise adjustments and groups (isolated or Pass Through, with their own opacity and mask, nested), with or without layer masks (density and feather included), and clipping masks over them; layer styles on layers (effects, fill opacity, Blend If, knockout, Blend Interior Effects as Group) and on groups (effects included) at 8 and 16 bits, and a Shadows/Highlights with a guide at the top level, inside isolated groups, directly inside Pass Through groups, as a clipping-mask member (of a styled base too) and inside groups with style effects. Any other stack is refused by name (at 8 bits a Shadows/Highlights with a guide clipped to a base whose style effects sit below opacity 1 (not Dissolve)). Not with layer or channel. |
| `region.height` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `region.width` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `region.x` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `region.y` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `scale` | `integer` | no | — | Integer >= 1: enlarges the render exactly scale× with nearest-neighbour sampling (each pixel becomes a scale×scale block). Replaces max_side and is refused together with it; the longest output side may not exceed 4096 px (use region or a smaller scale). |

## `sample_color`

Reads the color of one pixel of the flattened composite (what you see in a render) — the eyedropper. Returns straight (non-premultiplied) RGBA components (0-255) and the hex string (#RRGGBB, or #RRGGBBAA when not fully opaque). The numbers are the DOCUMENT's, in its own colour space (returned as "space") — not sRGB — so "hex" is what the pixel actually holds. Every color ARGUMENT here is sRGB, so to paint that colour back pass "paint_hex", the CLOSEST sRGB spelling (the same string on an sRGB document). It reproduces the pixel exactly only when the colour is inside the sRGB gamut: when it is not, "paint_hex_exact" is false and a "note" says so — painting that hex back gives a duller colour, and there is no sRGB string that gives the sampled one. Also returns "srgb_rgba" (the pixel as continuous normalized sRGB numbers, for a text or shape layer's rgba/fill_rgba/stroke_rgba) and "srgb_in_gamut". Errors when the point is outside the canvas. 16-bit mode reports schema2 authoritative center_rgba_codes/center_rgba16, exact weighted_sum_rgba_codes/weight_units, mean_rgba_codes/mean_rgba16 and normalized_rgba, with no byte hex approximation, plus srgb_rgba/srgb_in_gamut (continuous sRGB of normalized_rgba; omitted at 32-bit float). Default source is the composite. On a 32-bit float document the reply is linear components rather than codes — center_rgba32, mean_rgba32, weighted_sum_rgba32, weight_units, stops and above_white/below_zero flags; every source and selection apply as at 8 and 16 bits. In a CMYK document the reply adds the composite's ink (ink_percent, ink16, total_ink_percent) beside the view's RGB. An 8- or 16-bit Grayscale document also reports gray_k_percent, 100 × (1 − gray), the Info panel's K. In a Lab Color document the codes are L*, a*, b* and alpha in the ICC v4 16-bit Lab encoding, and the reply adds lab {l, a, b} (L* = 100·v, a* and b* = 255·v − 128, D50) with no srgb_rgba: the document has no RGB reading.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `x` | `integer` | yes | — | Pixel x in canvas coordinates (0 = left edge). |
| `y` | `integer` | yes | — | Pixel y in canvas coordinates (0 = top edge). |

## `histogram`

Info > Histogram: inspect authoritative native-code statistics in either depth. source is composite, raw layer canvas pixels, or backdrop below a bottom-first record boundary; backdrop retains enclosing group gates. Selection is rational coverage weight (default true), not a hard contour. RGB counts alpha>0 without alpha weighting; alpha counts every positively weighted canvas position. Schema2 returns fractional display bins plus exact integer bin_weight_units, coverage_denominator 65535, full weighted native-code sums and separate exact endpoint counts/weights. stride changes display bins only: endpoint and sum statistics always scan the complete scope. Raw layer scope includes transparent canvas padding and excludes offcanvas storage. In 16-bit mode, and for a mask or channel at 32-bit float, source scalar reads the complete raw target plane, including offcanvas storage when unselected; target is required. Canvas selection weights map into that raw extent. Its RGB/luma fields describe the scalar value and analysis alpha is opaque. Read-only; no Undo or dirty change. 16-bit mode reads authoritative native codes in every named scope, including raw groups and selection-weighted backdrops. Exact 0/65535 endpoint counts and coverage weights inspect the complete scope independently of display-bin stride. On a 32-bit float document (storage "rgba32_float") the bins are STOPS — 256 bins over −12…+6 EV — with per-channel below_zero/above_white counts and their coverage weights (below_zero_weight_units_rgba / above_white_weight_units_rgba), the counts of values exactly 0 and exactly 1 (exact_zero_rgba / exact_one_rgba and their _weight_units_rgba), weighted linear sums and exact min/max instead of clipping counts. Every source (composite, layer, backdrop) and selection apply as at 8 and 16 bits. source "scalar" measures a mask or channel:<name>, which are u16 coverage, exactly as at 16 bits (storage "u16_scalar", codes 0…65535, not stops); red, green, blue and alpha refuse, because a float layer's components are not u16 codes. Use source "layer" for their stop-binned histogram. In a CMYK document the reply is the histogram per ink and composite (channels cmyk, c, m, y, k; 256 bins of L = 1 − ink) of the composite, or of layer's own ink; selection true weights by the selection. source "scalar" with target mask, channel:<name> or an ink plate (cyan, magenta, yellow, black: its stored 1 − ink) is that plane's raw scalar histogram, as at 16 bits. A Grayscale document answers channels ["gray"]: bins and bin_weight_units hold the one Gray row (R = G = B), no _luma keys; source scalar takes target mask or channel:<name> (red, green, blue and alpha refuse for good). In a Lab Color document bins and bin_weight_units hold the Lightness, a and b rows (channels lists them; no luma), each bin round(code·255/65535); source scalar reads a mask, an alpha channel (channel:<name>), or target lightness, a or b: the plane of L*, a* or b* codes, its target named so and lab_value_rule reading a code, or target alpha; target red, green or blue refuses.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `below` | `integer` | no | — | Backdrop excludes records at/above this boundary, retaining enclosing groups. 0...layer_count; required only for backdrop. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `selection` | `boolean` | no | — | Weight by current selection coverage when present; default true. |
| `source` | `string` | no | one of `composite`, `layer`, `backdrop`, `scalar` | Named analysis source; default composite. Scalar is a native u16 raw plane (at 32-bit float, a mask or channel only). |
| `stride` | `integer` | no | — | Positive plot sampling stride, default 1. Exact endpoints/sums remain complete. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | Required for scalar: mask, red, green, blue, alpha or channel:<name>. Other source modes do not use target. At 32-bit float: mask or channel:<name> only. |

## `sample_pixel`

Reads one pixel off the flattened composite and reports it every way the Info panel does. r/g/b/a and hex are the DOCUMENT's own numbers, converted nowhere; hsb is derived from them (h in degrees, s and b in percent); lab is CIE L*a*b* against the D50 PCS white computed through the document's OWN profile, so the same bytes read differently in an sRGB and a Display P3 document — it is null when this build cannot model the profile (a LUT profile), and lab_space names the profile it went through. paint_hex is the closest sRGB spelling for a colour argument, with paint_hex_exact false when the pixel is outside the sRGB gamut. sample_size 1, 3 or 5 averages that square about (x, y), the eyedropper's own rule — including its habit of accepting a centre just outside the canvas as long as part of the square is inside. Read-only. The UI path is the Info panel's readout; sample_color is the paint-oriented twin. In 16-bit mode, or when source/selection is supplied, schema2 reports exact center_rgba_codes, integer weighted_sum_rgba_codes/weight_units, mean_rgba_codes and normalized_rgba. All positively weighted in-bounds samples include hidden RGB at alpha 0. Coordinates are always canvas coordinates; layer padding is transparent black. Selection defaults false; explicit true weights fractional coverage. Named backdrop uses the same contribution cut as histogram. 16-bit mode reports schema2 authoritative center_rgba_codes/center_rgba16, exact weighted_sum_rgba_codes/weight_units, mean_rgba_codes/mean_rgba16 and normalized_rgba, with no byte hex approximation. Default source is the composite; sample_pixel additionally exposes raw-layer/backdrop scopes and explicit selection weighting. On a 32-bit float document the reply is linear components rather than codes — center_rgba32, mean_rgba32, weighted_sum_rgba32, weight_units, stops and above_white/below_zero flags; every source and selection apply as at 8 and 16 bits. In a CMYK document the reply adds the composite's ink (ink_percent, ink16, total_ink_percent) beside the view's RGB. In a Lab Color document the codes are L*, a*, b* and alpha in the ICC v4 16-bit Lab encoding, and the reply adds lab {l, a, b} (L* = 100·v, a* and b* = 255·v − 128, D50) with no srgb_rgba: the document has no RGB reading.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `below` | `integer` | no | — | Required backdrop boundary 0...layer_count; enclosing group gates retained. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `sample_size` | `integer` | no | one of `1`, `3`, `5` | Side of the square averaged about (x, y); 1 (the default) is the pixel itself. |
| `selection` | `boolean` | no | — | Weight sample by current selection coverage; default false. |
| `source` | `string` | no | one of `composite`, `layer`, `backdrop` | Default composite; explicit scope returns schema2 exact weighted native-code readout. |
| `x` | `integer` | yes | — | Pixel x in canvas coordinates (0 = left edge). |
| `y` | `integer` | yes | — | Pixel y in canvas coordinates (0 = top edge). |

## `get_color_profile`

The document's colour space: its profile name, whether Doctored can convert with it, the print resolution and the print size that implies. convertible false means Doctored can display the profile and re-embed it on export but cannot transform with it (a LUT-based profile) — assign_profile still works, convert_profile does not. on_open reports what the OPEN did: "unchanged", "converted" into the working space, or "kept" because it could not be converted from. on_open_refusal is null, or the sentence saying what the open did with an embedded profile a document cannot carry: a Gray or CMYK image converted into sRGB through it, or an image read into sRGB without it ("unchanged" then means nothing more was done). get_document's color_profile block carries the same name, convertible, can_decode, on_open and on_open_refusal keys. A file with no profile is assumed sRGB, and is converted when the working space differs. Every #RRGGBB argument in this surface is sRGB and converts into the document's space once, so on a non-sRGB document brush_stroke, fill, gradient and the shape/text tools all lay down the same colour — but the bytes a render or sample_color reports are the document's, not the hex you passed. can_decode is the wider question: on an 8-bit document true when this build can turn the document's numbers into PCS colour, including a LUT profile with a readable A2B table, which convertible is false for. At 16 and 32 bits a conversion's source must be matrix/TRC: can_decode is true for any matrix/TRC model, while convertible also needs curves that pass the high-depth precision checks, so a profile failing them can be converted out of but not into. A CMYK document reports color_mode "cmyk", its CMYK profile and declared depth; its pixels are shown through a Display P3 view. Its text, shape and fill objects report their colours as ink in percent (ink, fill_ink, stroke_ink, a stop's ink) beside the sRGB appearance hex.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `assign_profile`

RELABELS the document with another colour profile. Pixel numbers are NOT touched, so the picture changes appearance — this is the tool for a file that was tagged wrongly. One undo step. Answers changed:false when the document already carries that profile; errors on bytes that are not an RGB ICC profile. In a 32-bit float document the linear values are kept exactly and now mean the new profile's primaries; a profile with no matrix/TRC model, or one whose tone curves fail the precision check, is refused by name. A document holding a RAW layer (a retained image source) REFUSES with a sentence naming the count; rasterize_sources:true is the disclosed way through. On an 8-bit document a profile with no matrix/TRC model REFUSES, naming the layer, while a document_v2 Exposure/White Balance layer exists or the document uses linear_light evaluation. A matrix/TRC profile whose tone curves fail the precision check (describe_profile's export_refusal) is assigned at 8 and 16 bits (a 32-bit float document refuses it, as above), with or without rasterize_sources, unless the document uses linear_light evaluation, holds text/shape artwork or holds a document_v2 Exposure/White Balance layer: each refuses at every depth with one Assign sentence naming the profile (and the layer). On a CMYK document profile is working_cmyk (the default: Edit ▸ Color Settings' working CMYK), installed with name or file with path, a CMYK profile: assign keeps every ink number, convert re-separates each layer's ink through the destination at intent and black_point_compensation (Color Settings' by default), keeping masks, adjustment layers and transparency, and flatten true flattens onto paper first to keep the appearance exactly. convert_profile to an RGB profile (srgb, display_p3, or an installed or file RGB profile) converts the document to RGB, as convert_mode rgb does. On a Grayscale document profile is working_gray (the default: Edit ▸ Color Settings' working Gray), a Gray space (dot_gain_10, dot_gain_15, dot_gain_20, dot_gain_25, dot_gain_30, gray_gamma_18, gray_gamma_22, sgray), installed with name or file with path, a Gray profile; every gray value is kept and only the profile changes. An RGB or CMYK profile (srgb, display_p3, an RGB or CMYK file) refuses by name. Replies color_mode gray, profile, previous_profile and depth. A Lab Color document has no document profile: assign_profile is unavailable in it. On an Indexed Color document, one undo step: every index and the colour table's codes are kept and the table's colours now mean the new RGB profile; a profile that is not RGB refuses. A Duotone document refuses it for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | With profile:"installed", the profile's display name. |
| `path` | `string` | no | — | Path to an .icc/.icm profile; required when profile is "file". |
| `profile` | `string` | yes | one of `srgb`, `display_p3`, `file`, `installed`, `working_gray`, `dot_gain_10`, `dot_gain_15`, `dot_gain_20`, `dot_gain_25`, `dot_gain_30`, `gray_gamma_18`, `gray_gamma_22`, `sgray` | srgb or display_p3 use the built-in profile; file reads the profile at path. On a Grayscale document: working_gray (the default), a Gray space by name, installed or file; srgb and display_p3 refuse there. |
| `rasterize_sources` | `boolean` | no | — | Rasterize every layer still bound to a retained image source, then assign — ONE result and ONE undo step. Without it, a document holding such a source refuses by name rather than reinterpreting a master silently. |

## `convert_profile`

CONVERTS the document to another colour profile: every layer's pixels are transformed so the picture LOOKS the same and its numbers change. Layer masks, alpha channels and layer descriptions are coverage and are untouched, and so are layer-style and text-layer colours: those are authored in sRGB and convert where they are used, so they keep their appearance. One undo step. Answers changed:false when the two profiles describe the same space, or when this build cannot convert from or into one of them (get_color_profile's can_decode). In a 32-bit float document the conversion is the matrix between the two profiles' primaries on the linear values, with no clamp: a colour outside the destination gamut keeps a negative component and values above white stay above white. There it runs at relative, perceptual or saturation intent (all the same result) and refuses intent absolute, black_point_compensation and adjustments preserve_appearance by name, and a profile with no matrix/TRC model answers changed:false. The result reports intent, black_point_compensation and an adjustments array of {index,name,op,action,reason}. profile also accepts "installed" with a name from list_installed_profiles. On an 8-bit document a LUT (A2B/B2A) profile is a valid source AND destination — get_color_profile's can_decode is the bit that says so, while convertible keeps its narrower matrix/TRC meaning. At 16 and 32 bits both profiles must be matrix/TRC; a LUT source or destination answers changed:false with that rule. On a document holding a RAW layer (a retained image source), relative, perceptual and saturation between matrix/TRC profiles, and relative to or from a LUT profile at 8 bits, convert with every source kept bound; black_point_compensation, absolute, and perceptual or saturation with a LUT side refuse with a sentence naming the count and the setting that keeps them bound (intent relative, black_point_compensation false), unless rasterize_sources is true, which rasterizes those layers and converts in one step and reports rasterized_sources. A destination whose bytes are the document's own profile answers changed:false at every intent, black_point_compensation and adjustments setting, before any refusal (at 16 bits, after the conversion's memory admission). Any other matrix/TRC destination whose tone curves fail the precision check (describe_profile: model matrix, high_depth_destination false) is refused by the core's conversion preflight before any work at every depth, with describe_profile's convert_refusal; a document already tagged with such a profile converts OUT of it, its curves read through the parser's repairs (gamma 0 as linear, a falling table as its running maximum). On a CMYK document profile is working_cmyk (the default: Edit ▸ Color Settings' working CMYK), installed with name or file with path, a CMYK profile: assign keeps every ink number, convert re-separates each layer's ink through the destination at intent and black_point_compensation (Color Settings' by default), keeping masks, adjustment layers and transparency, and flatten true flattens onto paper first to keep the appearance exactly. convert_profile to an RGB profile (srgb, display_p3, or an installed or file RGB profile) converts the document to RGB, as convert_mode rgb does. On a Grayscale document profile is working_gray (the default), a Gray space (dot_gain_10, dot_gain_15, dot_gain_20, dot_gain_25, dot_gain_30, gray_gamma_18, gray_gamma_22, sgray), installed with name or file with path, a Gray profile: every layer's gray values are re-encoded so the picture keeps its appearance, R = G = B, on the 8-bit grid in an 8-bit document; intent and black_point_compensation apply at 8 and 16 bits (a 32-bit document's linear gray is the same in every Gray profile, so only the profile changes). An RGB or CMYK profile refuses by name; flatten and adjustments do not apply. Type, shape and fill layers stay editable: each re-renders from its gray colours in the new profile (assign_profile too). A Lab Color document has no document profile: convert_profile converts it, as Image ▸ Mode does, to CMYK Color in a CMYK profile (working_cmyk, the default, or an installed or file CMYK profile) or to RGB Color in an RGB one (srgb, display_p3, or an installed or file RGB profile), at its own depth, with intent, black_point_compensation and flatten as convert_mode takes them. Profile working_gray, a Gray working space (dot_gain_10, dot_gain_15, dot_gain_20, dot_gain_25, dot_gain_30, gray_gamma_18, gray_gamma_22, sgray) or an installed or file Gray profile converts it to Grayscale in that profile, each pixel's L* through its tone curve, as convert_mode gray does (intent and black_point_compensation do not apply); the reply's color_mode is gray. On an Indexed Color document, one undo step: the colour table's entries are converted (each through this conversion, at 8-bit codes) and every index and the transparent index are kept; a profile that is not RGB refuses. A changed reply adds working_memory_plan_bytes, the edit's admitted working memory. A Duotone document refuses it for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `adjustments` | `string` | no | one of `keep`, `preserve_appearance` | What happens to adjustment LAYERS. keep (the default) leaves every parameter as authored. preserve_appearance keeps exposure and white_balance at evaluation document_v2 — both are light-linear through the document's own profile — and BAKES every other adjustment into one disclosed raster layer "<name> (baked)" in its place, leaving the rest of the stack where it is. It refuses, naming the layer, when a to-be-baked adjustment is inside a group, is clipped, or sits over transparent pixels. Into a profile with no matrix/TRC model, document_v2 exposure/white_balance cannot be kept: keep refuses naming the layer, preserve_appearance bakes it (visible, top-level, unclipped, opaque beneath), and a linear_light document refuses the profile. |
| `black_point_compensation` | `boolean` | no | — | ISO 18619 black point compensation; default false. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `intent` | `string` | no | one of `perceptual`, `relative`, `saturation`, `absolute` | Rendering intent; default relative, which is the conversion this tool has always done. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | With profile:"installed", the profile's display name. |
| `path` | `string` | no | — | Path to an .icc/.icm profile; required when profile is "file". |
| `profile` | `string` | yes | one of `srgb`, `display_p3`, `file`, `installed`, `working_gray`, `dot_gain_10`, `dot_gain_15`, `dot_gain_20`, `dot_gain_25`, `dot_gain_30`, `gray_gamma_18`, `gray_gamma_22`, `sgray` | srgb or display_p3 use the built-in profile; file reads the profile at path. On a Grayscale document: working_gray (the default), a Gray space by name, installed or file; srgb and display_p3 refuse there. |
| `rasterize_sources` | `boolean` | no | — | When the settings cannot keep a RAW layer's source bound (black_point_compensation, absolute, or perceptual/saturation with a LUT side), rasterize every such layer first, then convert — ONE result and ONE undo step. Default false, which refuses instead. Settings the sources can follow keep them bound either way. |

## `set_resolution`

Sets the print resolution in pixels per inch. NO pixel is resampled — only the print size changes; use image_size to change the pixel dimensions. Mirrors Image Size…'s Resolution field with Resample off. One undo step; 1-30000 ppi. Answers at EVERY depth: at 16 bits and in 32-bit float every pixel buffer is the very allocation it was, which is what "no pixel is resampled" means there.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `ppi_x` | `number` | yes | 1–30000 | — |
| `ppi_y` | `number` | no | 1–30000 | Vertical resolution; defaults to ppi_x. |

## `get_metadata`

Which metadata packets the document carries and how big they are — presence and byte sizes only, not a parsed EXIF dump — plus its print resolution, its profile name and what the open did (on_open, and on_open_refusal: null or the sentence get_color_profile reports). EXIF, XMP and IPTC are captured where supported in JPEG/PNG/TIFF; RAW/HEIC imports reconstruct standard ImageIO fields and XMP. metadata_import separates supported scope, packet representation and verified omissions. Packets are written on supported exports unless strip_metadata is set. metadata_not_captured: true means this document came from a file whose container was not inspected for capture data (such as a Live Photo frame); packets were never read — absent here does not mean the file had none.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

Selects the layer that untargeted edits apply to.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `index` | `integer` | yes | — | — |

## `new_layer`

Adds an empty transparent layer above the active layer and selects it. Optional `layer` (anchor, default the active layer) and `position` (`above` the anchor, `top` of the root level, or `into_group` for a group anchor, default `above`) choose where it lands; the reply reports the `position` used. Works on a CMYK document: a new layer is bare paper, a mask scales its layer's ink coverage, and applying a mask bakes it into the layer's alpha with the ink kept.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Anchor layer index (default: the active layer). A group is a legal anchor. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | — |
| `position` | `string` | no | one of `above`, `top`, `into_group` | Where the new layer lands relative to `layer`: above it (default), at the top of the root level, or as the top child of a group. |

## `duplicate_layer`

Duplicates a layer, or every layer in layers, in ONE step. A GROUP duplicates with everything inside it. The reply reports the new layer_count — every structural edit renumbers the stack, so re-read get_document before addressing layers again.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `index` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | no | 1–unbounded items | Layers to duplicate, instead of index. |

## `duplicate_to_new_document`

Mirrors Layer > Duplicate to New Document…: copies a layer, or every layer in layers (a GROUP with everything inside it), into a NEW untitled document and opens it; the source is unchanged (no undo step, no dirty change). The new document keeps the source's depth (8, 16 or 32-bit float), canvas size, ICC profile, resolution, evaluation policy and global light. Every copied layer keeps its pixels, offset, name, opacity, blend mode, visibility, mask, style, Blend If, label, locks and text/shape/adjustment description, under a fresh id; a clip survives only over a copied base, a link only when two copies share it. Alpha channels, guides, layer comps, color samplers and EXIF/XMP/IPTC metadata are not carried. name sets the new document's title (default: the untitled name). The reply's document is the NEW one; later calls on the source keep passing its document_id. In an Action, later steps stay on the run's own document; edits made in the duplicate while recording are recorded as a non-replayable placeholder; an MCP-recorded step replays its literal index/layers. Refused inside a Batch. Works on a CMYK document: ink is copied exactly; into an RGB document the layers convert (relative colorimetric with BPC). A Lab Color document's duplicate is a Lab Color document of the same depth holding the same codes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `index` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | no | 1–unbounded items | Layers to copy, instead of index. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | — |

## `delete_layer`

Deletes a layer, or every layer in layers, in ONE step (a group takes its children with it). Refused only when it would leave the document with no layers at all. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good: it needs more than one layer, and an Indexed Color document holds one.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `index` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | no | 1–unbounded items | Layers to delete, instead of index. |

## `merge_down`

Merges a layer into the previous one AMONG ITS SIBLINGS, so a merge inside a group never reaches out of it. With layers (two or more, all sharing one parent) it is Merge Layers: they become one raster layer at the lowest one's position. Masks, styles and adjustment descriptions are baked in and dropped. The merge REPLACES the lower layer's pixels, so its transparency or pixel lock refuses the call; the upper one's locks do not, since it is only removed. At every depth the merged layer keeps the union of the members' extents, so pixels a member holds outside the canvas are kept. In 16-bit and 32-bit float documents a masked adjustment layer also adjusts merged pixels beyond its mask by the mask's outside coverage, where an 8-bit merge leaves them unadjusted. A layer with knockout merges against its REAL backdrop: the hole is filled with the backdrop's own pixels, so the picture is kept wherever that backdrop is opaque. Where no backdrop can be captured — the knockout layer sits inside an isolated group, inside a pass-through group that is itself being merged, is clipped to a base outside the merge, or punches to the root of a document with no qualifying Background layer — the hole bakes as TRANSPARENCY, the merged layer shows whatever lies beneath it, and the reply carries a `note`. Works on a CMYK document: groups, clipping masks and merges composite in ink.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `index` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | no | 2–unbounded items | Layers to merge together, instead of index. |

## `flatten_image`

Flattens all layers into one. The single layer left behind is named "Background": hidden layers are DISCARDED, every layer comp goes with the identities it bound, and the channels, guides and ruler origin are kept. Answers at every depth, and the flat layer is canvas-sized at every depth, like 8-bit. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good: it needs more than one layer, and an Indexed Color document holds one.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `reorder_layer`

Moves a layer (and, for a group, everything inside it) to a new stack position. Omit depth and it lands at the destination's own level, which is what dragging a row onto another means; give a depth to move it INTO or OUT OF a group. `to` numbers the stack with this layer's own subtree ALREADY taken out, so naming that subtree's own start at the same depth puts the layer back where it started and is refused as a no-op. A (to, depth) pair that would not make a well-formed tree is refused too. On an Indexed Color document the one layer is already in its place: no change.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `depth` | `integer` | no | 0–10 | Nesting level at the destination: 0 is the top level, and one more than a group's own depth puts the layer inside that group. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `from` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `to` | `integer` | yes | — | — |

## `set_layer_properties`

Changes any of a layer's name, opacity (0-1), blend mode, visibility, or pixel offset in one undoable step. Pass Through applies to GROUPS only — it is a new group's default, and it is what lets an adjustment layer inside the group reach the layers below it; naming it for a raster layer is refused. A field already holding the value you pass is simply left alone rather than failing the call, so echoing a get_document row back is safe; when NOTHING in the call would change, the reply is changed:false and no undo step is added. offset_x/offset_y that differ from the reported offset are refused on an ADJUSTMENT layer (it has no position of its own; move_layers moves its linked mask) and on a GROUP that contains no pixels (it has no position to move), at every depth. open works at every depth and, like the Layers panel's disclosure triangle, adds no undo step: it is saved with the document (so it marks it edited) and changes no pixel; with other properties in the same call, those are the one undo step, and undoing it also restores the disclosure. In a CMYK document blend_mode is one of Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Color Burn, Linear Burn, Darker Color, Lighten, Screen, Color Dodge, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix, Difference, Exclusion, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity (evaluated on 1 − ink), or Pass Through on a group. In a Grayscale document blend_mode takes Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Color Burn, Linear Burn, Lighten, Screen, Color Dodge, Linear Dodge (Add), Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix, Difference, Exclusion, Subtract, Divide (at 32 bits, those a float document admits), and Pass Through on a group; Darker Color, Lighter Color, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity are unavailable. In a Lab Color document blend_mode takes Normal, Dissolve, Multiply, Linear Burn, Darker Color, Screen, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity (each composited on the L*a*b* values, measured against Photoshop's Lab composite), and Pass Through on a group; Darken, Color Burn, Lighten, Color Dodge, Difference, Exclusion, Subtract and Divide are unavailable. fill_opacity is available. On an Indexed Color document the one layer takes a name, a colour label, locks, visibility (hidden, it renders clear, keeps its indices and saves hidden in .doctored; a kept-palette export refuses until it is shown) and an offset (a whole-pixel move: the layer stays canvas-sized at the origin, so the offset reads 0 after and pixels moved past the canvas are dropped); open applies to groups only; opacity and blend mode are not available in Indexed Color. A Bitmap document: the one layer takes name only; any other change refuses: A Bitmap document's one layer takes a new name only: no opacity, blend mode, visibility, offset or disclosure change.
