| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `index` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | — |
| `offset_x` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `offset_y` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `opacity` | `number` | no | 0–1 | — |
| `open` | `boolean` | no | — | GROUPS only: whether the panel shows it expanded. Saved with the document; it changes no pixel and adds no undo step. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | no | — | — |

## `transform_layer`

Rotates, scales and/or moves a layer's pixels in a single resample — the same pipeline as the app's Free Transform (⌘T). The rotation and the scales act around a pivot (by default the centre of the layer's CURRENT bounds — for a re-editable text or shape layer the exact centre of its description's box, which a turn leaves fixed, so rotate then rotate-back returns it exactly), then the translation is added; the layer is resampled once into the outward-rounded bounding box of its transformed corners, so its offset AND size both change, and it may end up extending past the canvas. The canvas is untouched, and a layer mask rides along, resampled identically. Two entries OTHER than the named layer do follow the same matrix, because a person dragging the box would expect them to: everything inside it when the layer is a GROUP, and every layer LINKED to it (link_layers). Nothing else moves. Pass at least one of rotate, scale, scale_x, scale_y, translate_x, translate_y; the result reports the layer's new bounds so you can verify placement. For whole-document geometry use rotate / flip / image_size instead. On a re-editable TEXT, SHAPE layer nothing rasterizes: the matrix composes into the layer's description and the layer re-renders through it (crisp vector edges; the result says rasterized: false and reports the new transform and origin). Only a layer whose source cannot be rendered right now (a text family not installed here) is resampled as pixels and drops its description, reported as before with the reason (undo restores it). A transform over a SET — a group, or a linked layer — always resamples instead, so every described layer it carries loses its description too; those are listed in rasterized_layers. It ignores any selection; to transform only the selected pixels use transform_selected_pixels. Available in a 32-bit float document: the resample is premultiplied over the extended-range samples, each layer's RGB is clamped to that layer's own visible range so a filter's ringing never leaves it, an output alpha below 2^-24 becomes transparent, and a float result past 67,108,864 pixels refuses before any work. Masks stay 16-bit coverage and resample exactly as at 16 bits. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document the one layer transforms in place: a whole-pixel translation, or a nearest sampler (and, for selected pixels, a selection with no partial coverage), keeps every pixel's index exactly, a floated transparent pixel landing nothing; any other edit resamples the colours and maps each changed pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as uncovered area), unchanged pixels keeping theirs. Uncovered area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour. A warp is applied at once and keeps no editable field (get_warp answers null; clear and bake change nothing). duplicate on transform_layers or transform_again refuses (a copy makes a second layer). Selected pixels of an alpha channel (target {channel: n}) transform as on RGB, the layer untouched; a mask target refuses for good (an Indexed layer holds no mask), and a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses (the one channel is Index). A Bitmap document: not available in Bitmap mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `around` | `string` | no | one of `center`, `top_left` | The pivot the rotation and scale turn/grow around: "center" (default) or "top_left" of the layer's current bounds; center is a described layer's exact centre, shared with the app's ⌘T session. pivot_x / pivot_y override it. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `pivot_x` | `number` | no | — | Explicit pivot x in canvas px; overrides around on this axis. |
| `pivot_y` | `number` | no | — | Explicit pivot y in canvas px; overrides around on this axis. |
| `rotate` | `number` | no | — | Rotation in degrees around the pivot. POSITIVE IS CLOCKWISE on screen (canvas y grows downward), matching the app's Angle field. Default 0. |
| `sampler` | `string` | no | one of `nearest`, `bilinear`, `bicubic`, `lanczos` | Resampling filter, default bicubic (Catmull-Rom). nearest keeps hard pixel edges (pixel art), lanczos is sharpest for big reductions. Whole-pixel moves and mirrors (scale -1) copy pixels losslessly whatever this says; every rotation is resampled, so for a lossless quarter turn of the WHOLE image use the rotate tool instead. |
| `scale` | `number` | no | — | Uniform scale multiplier for both axes: 1 = unchanged (default), 0.5 = half size, 2 = double, negative mirrors. scale_x / scale_y override it per axis. Magnitudes are clamped to 0.001-100 and 0 is refused. |
| `scale_x` | `number` | no | — | Horizontal scale multiplier, overriding scale (1 = unchanged, negative mirrors left-right). |
| `scale_y` | `number` | no | — | Vertical scale multiplier, overriding scale (1 = unchanged, negative mirrors top-bottom). |
| `translate_x` | `number` | no | — | Move right by this many canvas px (negative = left), applied after the rotation and scale. |
| `translate_y` | `number` | no | — | Move down by this many canvas px (negative = up), applied after the rotation and scale. |

## `distort_layer`

Maps the named layer, its group descendants and linked partners through one canvas perspective. corners are TL/TR/BR/BL destinations of the layer rect; for a group they are destinations of its content box. A parallelogram preserves editable text/shape artwork as affine geometry. True perspective rasterizes described artwork only when rasterize_artwork:true is supplied, and reports the affected layers. The canvas and unlinked masks remain in place. Available in a 32-bit float document: the resample is premultiplied over the extended-range samples, each layer's RGB is clamped to that layer's own visible range so a filter's ringing never leaves it, an output alpha below 2^-24 becomes transparent, and a float result past 67,108,864 pixels refuses before any work. Masks stay 16-bit coverage and resample exactly as at 16 bits. In a Lab Color document it runs on the L*a*b* codes, as on an RGB document. On an Indexed Color document the one layer transforms in place: a whole-pixel translation, or a nearest sampler (and, for selected pixels, a selection with no partial coverage), keeps every pixel's index exactly, a floated transparent pixel landing nothing; any other edit resamples the colours and maps each changed pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as uncovered area), unchanged pixels keeping theirs. Uncovered area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour. A warp is applied at once and keeps no editable field (get_warp answers null; clear and bake change nothing). duplicate on transform_layers or transform_again refuses (a copy makes a second layer). Selected pixels of an alpha channel (target {channel: n}) transform as on RGB, the layer untouched; a mask target refuses for good (an Indexed layer holds no mask), and a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses (the one channel is Index). A Bitmap document: not available in Bitmap mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `corners` | `array<array<number>>` | yes | 4–4 items | Four [x, y] canvas points, the destinations of the layer rect's TL, TR, BR and BL corners in that order, e.g. [[0, 0], [80, 10], [75, 60], [5, 50]]. Pixels are y-down: the canvas origin is its top-left. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `rasterize_artwork` | `boolean` | no | — | Authorize true-perspective rasterization of described artwork. |
| `sampler` | `string` | no | one of `nearest`, `bilinear`, `bicubic`, `lanczos` | Resampling filter, default bicubic (Catmull-Rom). Perspective compresses detail toward the quad's narrow side, where bicubic or lanczos hold up best. |

## `add_layer_mask`

Gives a layer a mask: a grayscale coverage channel that gates the layer's alpha without touching its pixels (white shows, black hides, grays are partial), so hiding is non-destructive and reversible. A reveal_all or hide_all mask is the layer's size; a from_selection mask is CANVAS-sized at (0, 0) at every depth, never cropped to the layer. A linked mask moves, transforms and crops with its layer. Replaces any existing mask and enables it. Paint it afterwards with brush_stroke / eraser_stroke and target: "mask". A GROUP takes a mask too: its mask is CANVAS-sized, it gates everything inside the group per pixel — including an adjustment layer's reach over the layers BELOW the group, which is the "group the adjustment layers and mask the group" workflow — and it does not make the group composite as a unit. Works on a CMYK document: a new layer is bare paper, a mask scales its layer's ink coverage, and applying a mask bakes it into the layer's alpha with the ink kept.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `kind` | `string` | no | one of `reveal_all`, `hide_all`, `from_selection` | reveal_all (default) starts fully white — nothing hidden yet; hide_all starts black — the layer disappears until you paint it back; from_selection builds the mask from the CURRENT selection (selected shows, the rest hides), so it requires an active selection from a select_* tool. Re-applying the identical selection mask replies changed: false. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |

## `remove_layer_mask`

Removes a layer's mask. With apply: true the coverage is first BAKED into the layer's alpha — permanent, pixels lost, and it bakes regardless of whether the mask was enabled — so what the mask hid becomes really erased. With apply: false (the default) the mask is simply discarded and the layer is revealed in full again, pixels untouched. Because apply rewrites the alpha channel, a transparency lock refuses it; every other mask operation is gated only by Lock All. Answers at every depth: in a 32-bit float document apply multiplies each alpha by the coverage and keeps every linear RGB value exactly (the reply adds storage: rgba32_float). Works on a CMYK document: a new layer is bare paper, a mask scales its layer's ink coverage, and applying a mask bakes it into the layer's alpha with the ink kept.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `apply` | `boolean` | no | — | Bake the mask into the layer's alpha before dropping it (default false = discard it). |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |

## `set_layer_mask_enabled`

Turns a layer's mask on or off. A disabled mask is kept (and saved) but ignored while compositing, so the layer shows in full — useful to compare with and without. Errors when the layer has no mask. Works on a CMYK document: a new layer is bare paper, a mask scales its layer's ink coverage, and applying a mask bakes it into the layer's alpha with the ink kept.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | yes | — | — |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |

## `set_layer_clipped`

Clips a layer to the one below it (a clipping mask) or releases it. A clipped layer only shows where the first UNCLIPPED layer beneath it AMONG ITS SIBLINGS has content — that base layer's alpha footprint gates the whole group, and the group blends as one unit with the base's blend mode and opacity. Grouping is positional and re-derived WITHIN a level: consecutive clipped layers above a base all clip to it, a clipped layer that is first in its group has no base and composites as if unclipped — a GROUP in that position keeps PASSING THROUGH, since a flag the compositor ignores never forces isolation — and reordering re-derives the groups with no extra bookkeeping. Hiding the base hides its group. CLIPPING A LAYER TO A GROUP makes that group composite as a unit, so an adjustment layer inside it stops reaching the layers below the group — a clip base needs its own alpha footprint, which a pass-through group does not have. Works in 8-bit and 16-bit documents. Pass `layers` instead of `layer` to clip or release several entries as ONE undo step — what the Layer menu does over a multi-selection. The set FOLDS, exactly as set_layer_lock does: an entry the document will not change (at 16 bits, one already in that state) is skipped and listed in `skipped`; the call is refused only when NO entry changed. Non-destructive and reversible: pixels are untouched either way. Works on a CMYK document: groups, clipping masks and merges composite in ink.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `clipped` | `boolean` | yes | — | true clips the layer to the one below it in the same group; false releases it. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | no | — | Several layers, exclusive with `layer`/`index`. In a recorded Action this is {"$layers": "selected"}. |

## `set_layer_style`

Replaces a layer's WHOLE layer style — the effect stack plus blending options — in one undoable step; the same object get_document reports as style. Shape: {"fill_opacity": 0..1 (default 1; scales the pixels, never the effects), "blend_if": null or {channel: gray|red|green|blue (on a CMYK document gray|cyan|magenta|yellow|black), this_layer: [lo0, lo1, hi0, hi1], underlying: [lo0, lo1, hi0, hi1], extra: optional [{channel, this_layer, underlying}, ...] — one more range per other channel, several Blend If channels at once, every range's weight multiplied; a channel named twice is refused}, with 0..255 ramps in order (weight fades in over lo0..lo1 and out over hi0..hi1; [0, 0, 255, 255] is full weight; full ranges are dropped and the rest reported in channel order), "effects": [ ... ]}. Effects: up to 10 each of drop_shadow, inner_shadow, stroke, color_overlay and gradient_overlay (stacked instances; within a type a LATER one draws on top; an 11th is refused by name), at most one of any other type, each with "type", "enabled" (default true), its own "blend" and "opacity" 0..1 — defaults in parentheses: drop_shadow (multiply, color #000000, opacity 0.75, angle 120, use_global_light true, distance 5 px, spread 0..1 (0), size 0..250 px (5), layer_knocks_out true); inner_shadow (multiply, #000000, 0.75, angle 120, use_global_light true, distance 5, choke 0, size 5); outer_glow (screen, #ffffbe, 0.75, spread 0, size 5); inner_glow (screen, #ffffbe, 0.75, choke 0, size 5, source edge|center); stroke (normal, opacity 1, size 3, position outside|inside|center, fill_type color|gradient|pattern, color #000000, gradient, pattern_fill: an object of the pattern_overlay keys pattern/angle/scale/link_with_layer/phase, the same defaults, with its own echoed "anchor", read when fill_type is pattern); color_overlay (normal, #ff0000, 1); gradient_overlay (normal, 1, gradient); pattern_overlay (normal, 1, pattern {"preset": checkerboard|stripes|dots|grid} (checkerboard) or a custom tile {"name", "width", "height" 1..512, "rgba": standard base64 of width x height x 4 straight RGBA8 bytes}, angle: the Angle in degrees, any number normalized into -180..180 (0); rotates the tile about its origin, scale 0.01..10 (1 = 100 %), link_with_layer true, phase [x, y] px ([0, 0]); a linked tile starts at the canvas origin + phase + the layer's moves since it was made (Photoshop's fxrp) and then moves with the layer, and the reply echoes where the layer was made as "anchor": echo anchor to keep the tile, omit it to anchor where the layer was made; at 32 bits tile codes / 255 are linear values; in CMYK each texel converts to ink as a colour overlay's colour does); bevel_emboss (style outer_bevel|inner_bevel|emboss|pillow_emboss, technique smooth|chisel_hard|chisel_soft (smooth), depth 1 = 100 %, direction up|down, size 5, soften 0..16 (0), angle 120, use_global_light true, altitude 0..90 (30), highlight_blend screen, highlight_color #ffffff, highlight_opacity 0.75, shadow_blend multiply, shadow_color #000000, shadow_opacity 0.75); satin (multiply, #000000, 0.5, angle 19, distance 11, size 14, invert true). Wide colours: beside "color" on drop_shadow, inner_shadow, outer_glow, inner_glow, stroke, color_overlay and satin, "linear" [r, g, b] (bevel_emboss: "highlight_linear" / "shadow_linear") gives the colour as linear-light sRGB components, extended range (negative outside sRGB's gamut, each clamped into -4..4): a Display P3 or 16-bit pick a hex cannot hold. One that is an sRGB byte is dropped for its hex; otherwise "color" becomes its nearest sRGB byte. Contours (Layer Style ▸ the Contour picker): drop_shadow, inner_shadow, outer_glow, inner_glow and satin take "contour" (linear) and "anti_aliased" (false); outer_glow and inner_glow take "range" 0.01..1 (0.5 = 50 %); bevel_emboss takes "gloss_contour" and "gloss_anti_aliased", and its Contour sub-panel "contour_enabled" (false), "contour", "contour_anti_aliased" and "contour_range" 0.01..1 (0.5). A contour is {"preset": linear|cone|cone_inverted|gaussian|half_round|ring|ring_double|rolling_slope_descending|rounded_steps|sawtooth_1} or a custom curve {"points": [{"x", "y" 0..255, "corner": true ends a smooth run}, ...]} (2..16 points, sorted by x, a duplicate x keeping the first; the natural spline through them). Each contour key is written back only when it is not at its default; anti_aliased is kept but draws the same pixels. Noise (Layer Style ▸ the Noise slider): drop_shadow, inner_shadow, outer_glow and inner_glow take "noise" 0..1 (0 = 0 %), a fixed grain, added to the effect's coverage, that moves with the layer, written back only when above 0. Texture (Bevel & Emboss ▸ Texture): bevel_emboss takes "texture_enabled" (false) and "texture": an object of the pattern_overlay keys pattern/scale/link_with_layer/phase (the same defaults; no angle) plus "depth" -10..10 (1 = +100 %) and "invert" (false), with its own echoed "anchor"; the tile's Gray is read as height and shades the bevel, painting no colour. The texture is written back when texture_enabled is true or it is not the default. Glow fill (Layer Style ▸ Outer Glow / Inner Glow, the gradient button and Jitter): outer_glow and inner_glow take "fill_type" color|gradient (color), "gradient" (its stops only: every other gradient key is reset) and "jitter" 0..1 (0 = 0 %). A gradient glow places location 0 where the glow is strongest and takes its coverage from the stops' opacity (Foreground to Transparent draws the colour glow); Jitter scatters each pixel's place on the gradient with a fixed field that moves with the layer. fill_type is written back only when gradient, gradient when the fill is gradient or its stops are not the default, jitter when above 0. A gradient is {stops: [{position 0..1, color, opacity, midpoint, opacity_midpoint}, ...] (2..32; midpoint and opacity_midpoint 0.05..0.95, default 0.5: the colour and opacity midpoints toward the next stop, rounded to 0.01, written back only when not 0.5, ignored on a glow; outside the range refused), style linear|radial|angle|reflected|diamond (and shape_burst on a stroke only: the ramp runs across the band, outer edge to inner), angle 90, scale 0.1..1.5, reverse false, align_with_layer true, dither false, smoothness 1 (Smoothness as a fraction: 1 the Classic ramp, 0 linear, between them the two blended; written back only when below 1)}. Blend names are the snake_case forms of the layer blend modes (normal, multiply, screen, linear_dodge, ...); colors are "#rrggbb"; angles are degrees, 0 = light from the right, 90 = from the top (120 casts down-right); sizes are canvas px; spread/choke are fractions of size. Effects with use_global_light read the document's global light (set_global_light). Numbers are stored to 4 decimals; an unknown key is refused by name (an effect's mode key is `blend`), ranges are clamped, and an unknown type or enum value is an error whose message names the key. null (or an omitted style) clears; so does a style with no enabled effect, fill_opacity 1 and no blend_if. Idempotent: an unchanged style reports unchanged: true. The whole style replaces the previous one, so read it back from get_document first to change one knob. Effects render from the layer's shape (alpha × mask) at composite time — render shows them, layer renders and thumbnails do not — and follow moves, mask edits and text re-renders; transform_layer, distort_layer and image_size scale the px sizes (Scale Effects); merge_down and flatten_image bake them in. Interior effects use their own blend mode; the layer's blend mode applies to its pixels. An adjustment layer takes one too: its shape is its mask over the canvas (the whole canvas when unmasked), the adjustment applies after its own Drop Shadow and other below effects and keeps the backdrop's alpha, Blend If's This Layer reads the adjusted colour, and Fill scales the adjustment — on a CMYK document's adjustment layer too, on ink. Two more blending options sit beside fill_opacity and blend_if, and both are written back only when they are NOT at their default, so a style without them reads exactly as it always did: "knockout": "none"|"shallow"|"deep" (default "none") and "blend_interior_as_group": bool (default false). Because this tool takes the WHOLE style, adding one means reading the layer's current style from get_document and sending it back with the key merged in — sending the key alone clears everything else. Knockout makes the layer's shape punch a hole through a backdrop instead of compositing onto it: an isolated group's buffer stops BOTH shallow and deep (the hole then shows what lies beneath the group), a clipped layer punches to its clip base alone, shallow inside a pass-through group punches to what that group's contents started from, and deep punches to the Background layer — the bottom layer when it is a plain, visible, unmasked, unstyled, Normal, opacity-1, canvas-sized layer at (0,0) — or to transparency when there is none. blend_interior_as_group makes the LAYER's blend mode apply to inner_glow, satin and the two overlays — on a clipping base with visible clipped layers too, where those effects recolour the base and its clipped layers together. merge_down (Merge Down and Merge Layers) merges a knockout against its REAL backdrop; where none can be captured the hole bakes as transparency and the reply carries a note. flatten_image, stamp_visible and merge_visible bake it exactly, because all three bake the projection. Both keys are written to a PSD as Photoshop's knko and infx records and are SUPPORTED in 16-bit and 32-bit float documents. On a 16-bit or 32-bit float document the same style is carried on raster layers, adjustment layers and groups (a styled Pass Through group composites isolated) and rendered under the document's global light. In a 32-bit float document an effect's colour composites as its linear light and every effect blend mode must be one the float document admits on a layer (Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Darker Color, Linear Burn, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Pin Light, Difference, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity) — any other, Screen (the 8/16-bit default of outer_glow, inner_glow and the bevel's highlight) included, is refused by name. 16-bit mode carries the whole style (fill opacity, the nine effects, Blend If) on raster layers, adjustment layers and every group (a styled Pass Through group composites isolated). Effects render from the shape quantized to the byte plane through the byte renderers under the document's global light (set_global_light works at 16 bits); ramps evaluate on 16-bit codes with each 0..255 knee at code 257 * knee. A style whose padded plane would pass 100 MP refuses. The two knockout blending options — knockout and blend_interior_as_group — are CARRIED at this depth and render exactly as they do at 8 bits; a 32-bit float document refuses a layer style by name, and both keys are written to a PSD (`knko`/`infx`) at 8 and 16 bits. In a CMYK document every effect composites on ink: each colour slot takes ink [c, m, y, k] as fractions 0–1 (ink; a bevel's highlight_ink and shadow_ink; a gradient stop's ink), which wins over color, whose hex is rewritten to the ink's sRGB; a slot without ink converts its color through the document's profile, except a drop shadow, inner shadow, satin or bevel shadow left black, which is K 100 %. knockout and blend_interior_as_group work; blend_if takes channel gray, cyan, magenta, yellow or black, in the primary range and in each extra one (a plate's ramp reads 255 − its ink code, so 0 is 100 % ink; Gray the luminosity of the ink's naive RGB) and refuses red, green and blue by name in any range, even a full one. An adjustment layer takes a style and Blend If too: its shape is its mask over the canvas, its tone applies after its own below effects and This Layer reads the adjusted ink. Converting to RGB keeps each slot's color and drops its ink. In a Grayscale document every effect is available: each colour (hex, linear, gradient stop, a custom pattern's texels) is stored as its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule and composites R = G = B, effect blend modes take the Grayscale modes, and Blend If takes channel gray only (any other channel refuses). In a Lab Color document a style takes fill_opacity, knockout and every effect; an effect's blend takes Normal, Dissolve, Multiply, Linear Burn, Darker Color, Screen, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity (Darken, Color Burn, Lighten, Color Dodge, Difference, Exclusion, Subtract and Divide refuse); its colours are sRGB, converted at composite by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule and stored as given. A pattern_overlay's or pattern stroke's tile (a preset or rgba) is sRGB too: each texel becomes its 8-bit L*a*b* values by that rule before scale and angle, and the tile is stored as given. blend_if takes channel red, green and blue, which are Lightness, a and b (each range on the stored values, a* = 0 at 128; not measured against Photoshop); gray refuses, an identity range included.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `style` | `['object', 'null']` | no | — | The whole style object described above, or null to clear. |

## `set_global_light`

Sets the document's global light — the direction every effect with use_global_light on (drop shadow, inner shadow, bevel & emboss by default) reads instead of its own angle, so one edit re-lights every styled layer. Either argument may be omitted; the light defaults to angle 120 (down-right shadows), altitude 30. Altitude is clamped to 0..90, the angle normalized to -180..180, both stored to 4 decimals (so the value get_document reports echoes back as unchanged); an unchanged light reports unchanged: true. get_document reports global_light. Works on 8-bit, 16-bit and 32-bit float documents (one undo step at every depth). Works on a CMYK document: the angle and altitude every effect with use_global_light reads. A Grayscale document takes the global light, which its effects read. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `altitude` | `number` | no | 0–90 | Degrees above the canvas plane (bevel shading only). |
| `angle` | `number` | no | — | Degrees: 0 = light from the right, 90 = from the top. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `add_adjustment_layer`

Adds a NON-DESTRUCTIVE adjustment layer above the active layer and selects it: while compositing it recolors everything below it, its own pixels are ignored, and its parameters stay editable with edit_adjustment_layer (get_document reports them) — same math as apply_filter's matching filters, but reversible. The layer always gets a mask gating where the adjustment applies: built from the current selection when one exists (which stays active), else reveal-all; brush/eraser strokes on the layer paint that mask. A colour in an adjustment's params is in the DOCUMENT's numbers, not authored sRGB — an adjustment transforms the pixels it sits over. INSIDE A GROUP: in an isolated group (any blend mode but Pass Through, or a style) it recolors everything below it IN THAT GROUP; in a pass-through group — the default — it reaches the layers below the group too, unless some layer is clipped to that group, which isolates it. A mask or an opacity on a pass-through group does NOT isolate it: it restricts the adjustment to where the mask is white and scales it by the opacity. POSITION: by default the layer lands directly above the anchor layer (the active one unless layer names another); position "top" puts it at the top of the root stack and "into_group" makes it the topmost child of the anchor, which must then be a group. A new layer JOINS a clipping run rather than splitting it: when the entry immediately above the slot is clipped, the new layer is created clipped too, so no neighbour is re-based onto it. Both arguments work at 8 bits, 16 bits and 32-bit float. AUTO (levels only): auto {mode tone|color, clip?} instead of params is the Levels dialog's Auto Tone / Auto Color — per-channel stages measured over the whole visible backdrop where the layer lands (clipped or grouped alike), weighted by the selection, which becomes the new mask; the call runs and records the resolved params. Ops and their params: bcs (brightness, contrast, saturation, each -1..1, default 0; legacy true/false, ABSENT = true, the offset-and-line form that clips; false is the modern form, a brightness power and a contrast S-curve that keep black and white fixed); curves (rgb, r, g, b: each an optional array of 2-16 [in, out] control points, values 0-255, natural-spline-interpolated; a missing channel is identity; per-channel curves apply before rgb; OR the map form a Photoshop pencil curve imports as, rgb_map, r_map, g_map, b_map: each an optional array of 256 integers 0-255, entry i the output for input code i, never both forms); levels (black default 0, white default 1, 0 <= black < white <= 1; gamma 0.1-10, default 1 — here gamma > 1 BRIGHTENS; output_black default 0 and output_white default 1, each 0-1 in either order, map the result into that range, so 1 and 0 invert; r, g, b: each an optional object of the same five keys, a per-channel stage applied BEFORE the master one; absent = identity); hue_rotate (degrees, default 0); threshold (level 0-1, default 0.5); posterize (levels, integer 2-64, REQUIRED); exposure (exposure -20..20 stops default 0, offset -0.5..0.5 default 0, gamma 0.01-9.99 default 1 — computed in linear light, and this is Gamma Correction, the reciprocal power like levels' midtone gamma: above 1 BRIGHTENS); vibrance (vibrance -1..1 default 0: raising it lifts the least saturated pixels most, the lift damped by up to 40% on red and skin hues, and lowering it mutes every hue evenly; saturation -1..1 default 0, a scale about a ProPhoto-luminance anchor, not hue_saturation's, on the document profile's linear values); hue_saturation (hue -180..180 degrees, saturation -1..1, lightness -1..1, all default 0; bands, an object with any of reds/yellows/greens/cyans/blues/magentas, each {hue -180..180 degrees, saturation -1..1, lightness -1..1, all default 0, center 0-360 (360 excluded) degrees defaulting to 60 × the band's index — reds 0, yellows 60, greens 120, cyans 180, blues 240, magentas 300 — inner 0-180 default 15, falloff 0-180 default 30}. A band selects on CHROMA as well as hue: a neutral has no hue to be one of, so it takes no band edit at all, and a near-neutral ramps in, reaching full weight about 13 levels off grey. colorize false, colorize_hue 0-360 (360 excluded) default 0, colorize_saturation 0-1 default 0.25, colorize_lightness -1..1 default 0); color_balance (shadows, midtones, highlights, each {cyan_red, magenta_green, yellow_blue} in -1..1 default 0, acting in whole hundredths; preserve_luminosity default true, a per-tone renormalisation, not a luma rescale); black_and_white (reds 0.4, yellows 0.6, greens 0.4, cyans 0.6, blues 0.2, magentas 0.8, each -2..3; tint false, tint_color "#998a66" — its numbers are set to the grey's luminosity); photo_filter (color "#ec8a00" (Warming 85; Cooling 80 is "#006dff"), density 0-1 default 0.25, preserve_luminosity default true); channel_mixer (monochrome false; red, green, blue, gray, each {r, g, b, constant} in -2..2, defaulting to the identity rows and gray {0.4, 0.4, 0.2, 0}; values are fractions — the dialog's percentages over 100); selective_color (method "relative" or "absolute"; reds, yellows, greens, cyans, blues, magentas, whites, neutrals, blacks, each {c, m, y, k} in -1..1 default 0); shadows_highlights (shadows {amount 0-1 default 0.35, tone 0.01-1 default 0.5}, highlights {amount default 0, tone default 0.5}, radius 0-1000 px default 30, color -1..1 default 0.2, midtone_contrast -1..1 default 0 — the tone estimate is an alpha-weighted large-radius blur of the luma, so local contrast survives and a cut-out gets no halo; it is the one op whose destructive twin sees different pixels, because a layer reads the backdrop below it and a filter reads itself); white_balance (temperature 1667-25000 K default 6504, tint -150..150 default 0; the pair describes the illuminant the pixels were shot under and is Bradford-adapted to D65, so a HIGHER kelvin warms the image and a POSITIVE tint pushes it toward magenta; 6504/0 is the exact identity); Exposure and White Balance accept params.evaluation: document_v2 (default for new RGB edits) uses the document ICC matrix/TRC profile: White Balance stays on a common unclipped linear sRGB reference basis, while Exposure runs per channel in the document's own primaries at the profile's effective gamma (2.2 for sRGB-shaped curves, a pure power's own exponent such as ROMM's 1.8, and 1.883 for an offset curve that fails the precision check such as ITU-709's); legacy_srgb preserves the original sRGB numeric processing. Re-editing a layer preserves its evaluation when omitted. Old Actions without this key remain legacy. Scalar masks, individual planes and saved channels default to legacy grayscale processing and refuse explicit document_v2. LUT-only RGB profiles refuse a new or re-edited document_v2 of either op, and matrix/TRC profiles whose tone curves fail the precision check refuse a new or re-edited document_v2 White Balance (Exposure only when a curve is degenerate) at every depth with the core's sentence; an existing 8-bit document_v2 layer under a matrix/TRC profile whose curves fail the check keeps rendering (one under a LUT-only profile does not render), and legacy_srgb stays admitted under either profile: re-editing a document_v2 layer with params.evaluation legacy_srgb switches it to the original sRGB processing, which changes its look (Adjustment Options… offers the same switch). Alpha is unchanged in both versions. gradient_map (gradient — the same object SHAPE a layer style carries: stops, 2 to 32 of {position 0..1, color, opacity}, plus reverse — but its stop colours are the DOCUMENT's numbers, not the authored sRGB a style's are; method "classic" is the Classic ramp (gradient.smoothness 0..1, default 1; each stop's midpoint / opacity_midpoint 0.05..0.95 toward the next stop), "perceptual" the same over Oklab stops (RGB only); linear and smooth are not offered; no method: linear, keys refuse; the pixel's Rec. 709 luma picks the colour and a stop's opacity blends back toward the original; dither default true adds a deterministic sub-level offset that stops 8-bit banding — it is keyed on the pixel's position, which the layer counts from the canvas and the destructive twin counts from the layer it was handed, so on a layer whose offset is not 0,0 the two land the jitter on different pixels and differ by one code on about half of them; pass dither false to compare them exactly); color_lookup (a .cube LUT, or an .icc/.icm look — an RGB-to-RGB device-link profile applied to the document's numbers, or a Lab-to-Lab abstract profile baked through the document's profile when it loads: pass file, an absolute path this app parses, or the stored form kind "1d"|"3d", size, table (base64 f32), domain_min, domain_max, title, and source_size — the .cube's own size when the table was resampled down to this build's storage cap (3D 33, 1D 1024); strength 0-1 default 1. get_document elides the table but keeps every other key); replace_color (colors, REQUIRED, an array of 1-8 "#rrggbb" sampled colours in the DOCUMENT's numbers; fuzziness 0-200 default 40, a Euclidean RGB distance in 0-255 units: a pixel within fuzziness/2 of its nearest colour takes the whole edit, fading linearly to none at fuzziness; hue -180..180, saturation -1..1, lightness -1..1, all default 0, hue_saturation's master sliders applied to the matched pixels); invert, grayscale, sepia (none). In a 32-bit float document Levels, bcs, Black & White, Channel Mixer, Photo Filter, Exposure, White Balance, Curves, Hue/Saturation (Colorize, master lightness alone, or master hue alone) and Color Balance evaluate the linear values unclipped. Color Lookup runs every table (3D or 1D, any domain, entries inside or outside 0 to 1, a device link or an abstract look) on the linear values: an input outside the table's domain is read at its nearest end, entries above 1 are reached, and the unloaded identity table passes through. Channel Mixer's coefficients are kept in 1/1024 steps, and at 32 bits its constant adds half its 16-bit amount. A point curve continues along its end slope above its last point, and below its first point only when that point sits at input 0; a map (pencil) curve reads each map as straight lines between its entries, its first and last segments continued past 0 and 1, the channel map before the master. Hue/Saturation's lightness leaves a component already past its target unchanged, and its hue turns on a 1/24576-turn grid; saturation, hue with another master slider, or any band edit takes the display-scaled form below. Color Balance continues each channel beyond 0 and 1 along its end slopes. Black & White's Tint brings the tint's numbers to the grey's luminosity with the grey capped at 16. Hue Rotate and Sepia apply their matrix and Grayscale the Rec. 709 luma to the linear values with no clamp. Threshold, Posterize and Gradient Map are display-mapped: the op runs on the display-encoded value clamped to 0 to 1 and its result is decoded, so above white classifies as white. Vibrance, Selective Color, Replace Color and those Hue/Saturation settings are display-scaled: a pixel is divided by m = max(1, its largest component), the op runs on that colour's display encoding and the decoded result is scaled back by m, so a highlight is treated as its colour at m times the intensity. Invert (1 - v has no meaning above 1.0), Shadows/Highlights (its luma curve is defined on 0 to 1 and reverses above white) and a legacy_srgb White Balance (its matrix acts on sRGB-encoded 0 to 1 numbers, and a value above 1.0 has no encoded form) refuse by name. In a CMYK document every op acts on ink: Levels' top-level keys are the CMYK composite stage with optional c, m, y, k stage objects (acting on 1 − ink); Curves takes point lists cmyk, c, m, y, k with points in ink, 0–255 for 0–100 %, or drawn maps cmyk_map, c_map, m_map, y_map, k_map (256 output ink codes each, the composite after the plate's); hue_saturation takes the RGB params (master, bands, colorize) on 1 − C, 1 − M, 1 − Y with K kept (colorize re-separates K from the colorized grey). RGB keys refuse by name; auto (levels and curves) takes Auto Options {algorithm, shadows, highlights}, per_channel keeping black's ink. bcs (no saturation), invert, posterize and shadows_highlights run per plate on 1 − ink; color_balance, color_lookup and photo_filter (params ink [c, m, y, k] as fractions 0–1 in place of color) on the C/M/Y triple, K held; channel_mixer takes rows cyan, magenta, yellow, black and gray of {c, m, y, k, constant} on the ink; selective_color and threshold their RGB params on ink; gradient_map stops {position, ink, opacity, midpoint, opacity_midpoint} (method classic and smoothness as in RGB; perceptual refuses); replace_color inks (1–8 [c, m, y, k] fractions) in place of colors. exposure, vibrance and black_and_white refuse, as do hue_rotate, grayscale, sepia and white_balance (RGB only). In a Grayscale document op is bcs, levels, curves, exposure, invert, posterize, threshold or gradient_map (Levels' and Curves' r, g and b absent or alike); shadows_highlights and replace_color apply to pixels only (apply_filter), and every other op refuses by name. In a Lab Color document op bcs, color_balance, color_lookup, curves, gradient_map, hue_saturation, invert, levels, photo_filter, posterize and threshold run on the L*a*b* values (adjust is bcs), destructively and as a layer, and replace_color and shadows_highlights destructively only (as a layer they refuse): levels and curves adjust Lightness with the composite and their r stage, a* with g and b* with b; bcs adjusts Lightness and its saturation scales a* and b* about 0; invert and posterize act on every channel; threshold gives black and white (a* = b* = 0); hue_saturation of saturation -1 alone (Desaturate) keeps L* and sets a* = b* = 0; the other hue_saturation, color_balance, photo_filter, shadows_highlights and replace_color run on each sample's 16-bit ProPhoto RGB colour, so a colour outside sRGB keeps its chroma, and color_lookup and gradient_map on its sRGB colour (a sample the op leaves alone keeps its values); photo_filter's color is sRGB, and replace_color's colors are the document's own 8-bit #LLaabb Lab values (LL = round(255·L*/100), aa and bb = round(a* + 128), round(b* + 128)). black_and_white, channel_mixer, exposure, selective_color and vibrance refuse; grayscale, hue_rotate, sepia and white_balance as RGB-only. A Levels layer's auto {mode tone} sets Lightness alone (params r; a* and b* are kept); mode color refuses.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `auto` | `object` | no | — | levels only, instead of params: {"mode": "tone" or "color", "clip": fraction 0…0.1 dropped at each end, default 0.001}. Derives per-channel r/g/b stages from the BACKDROP below the layer (see the tool description); refused at 32-bit float. On a CMYK document levels and curves take {"algorithm": "per_channel" or "monochromatic", "shadows", "highlights": clip percent 0–9.99} (Auto Options; every key optional, the saved defaults otherwise, 0.10 %): the ink stages (or the composite's) from the histogram of L = 1 − ink. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | The ANCHOR the position is relative to (default: the active layer). A group is a legal anchor, and into_group requires one; ignored for top. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Layer name (default: the op's display name). |
| `op` | `string` | yes | one of `bcs`, `curves`, `levels`, `hue_rotate`, `posterize`, `threshold`, `invert`, `grayscale`, `sepia`, `exposure`, `vibrance`, `hue_saturation`, `color_balance`, `black_and_white`, `photo_filter`, `channel_mixer`, `selective_color`, `shadows_highlights`, `white_balance`, `gradient_map`, `color_lookup`, `replace_color` | The adjustment operation. |
| `params` | `object` | no | — | Parameters for op (see the tool description); omit for that op's defaults. posterize has no default: its levels is required, and color_lookup needs file or a complete table. |
| `position` | `string` | no | one of `above`, `top`, `into_group` | Where the new layer lands relative to the anchor (default above). |

## `edit_adjustment_layer`

Changes an existing adjustment layer non-destructively by replacing its stored description — one undo step; pixels, mask, opacity, blend mode and stacking are untouched. params REPLACES the whole params object (pass every key you want kept — nothing is merged, with one stated exception); op without params switches the layer to that op's defaults. Ops and params exactly as in add_adjustment_layer. The exception is a color_lookup layer's LUT: because get_document has to elide its table, omitting kind, size, table, source_size, domain_min, domain_max, title and abstract_profile — or passing the elision placeholders back — keeps the LUT the layer already holds (an abstract look is re-baked through the document's profile), so {"strength": 0.5} alone is enough to restrength it. Pass file, an absolute .cube path or an .icc/.icm device-link or abstract profile, to replace the LUT instead. Errors when the target layer is not an adjustment layer. auto (levels only, instead of params) re-derives the stages from the whole visible backdrop below the layer, clipped or inside an isolated group alike, and a live selection does not narrow it; only the layer's own mask weights it, exactly as the dialog's Auto buttons; the resolved params are what is applied and recorded. In a 32-bit float document Levels, bcs, Black & White, Channel Mixer, Photo Filter, Exposure, White Balance, Curves, Hue/Saturation (Colorize, master lightness alone, or master hue alone) and Color Balance evaluate the linear values unclipped. Hue Rotate and Sepia apply their matrix and Grayscale the Rec. 709 luma to the linear values with no clamp. Invert (1 - v has no meaning above 1.0), Shadows/Highlights (its luma curve is defined on 0 to 1 and reverses above white) and a legacy_srgb White Balance (its matrix acts on sRGB-encoded 0 to 1 numbers, and a value above 1.0 has no encoded form) refuse by name. ## `auto_tone`

Stretches EACH channel's own histogram to the full range, clipping clip of the counted pixels at each end (default 0.001 = 0.1 %; fully transparent pixels are never counted), then applies the levels math destructively to the target through selection coverage, using analysis_scope (whole_target by default) independently. Both depths retain native samples; 16-bit supports layer RGB. One undo step. Reports the derived black, white and gamma per channel; changed is false when the image is already at full range (nothing is written). Errors on an adjustment layer's pixel target; its mask is supported. The UI path is Image > Auto Tone (⇧⌘L). A 32-bit float document refuses all three (auto_tone, auto_contrast, auto_color). In a CMYK document the layer's ink takes CMYK Levels from its tone analysis: per channel for auto_tone and auto_color, monochromatic for auto_contrast, clip (default 0.001, 0.1 %) clipped at each end; one ink plate or an alpha channel takes the 16-bit colour plane's or channel's Auto; a mask refuses. In a Grayscale document it runs on the gray values (Auto Tone and Auto Contrast at 8 and 16 bits); auto_color refuses. In a Lab Color document it stretches Lightness alone (a* and b* are kept); target is layer.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `analysis_scope` | `string` | no | one of `whole_target`, `selection` | Measurement scope independently of selected write coverage. whole_target is the historical default; selection weights each sample by its coverage and requires an active selection. Native source codes determine clipping. |
| `clip` | `number` | no | 0–0.1 | Share of the counted pixels dropped at EACH end before the stretch (default 0.001 = 0.1 %). Larger values push more of the image to pure black and pure white. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | layer (default), mask, red, green, blue, alpha or channel:<name>. Analyzes the whole target; writes only through active selection coverage. |

## `auto_contrast`

Auto Tone with ONE black and white point derived from the luma histogram and applied to all three channels, so the colour balance is untouched. The UI path is Image > Auto Contrast (⌥⇧⌘L). In a CMYK document the layer's ink takes CMYK Levels from its tone analysis: per channel for auto_tone and auto_color, monochromatic for auto_contrast, clip (default 0.001, 0.1 %) clipped at each end; one ink plate or an alpha channel takes the 16-bit colour plane's or channel's Auto; a mask refuses. In a Grayscale document it runs on the gray values (Auto Tone and Auto Contrast at 8 and 16 bits); auto_color refuses. In a Lab Color document it stretches Lightness alone (a* and b* are kept); target is layer.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `analysis_scope` | `string` | no | one of `whole_target`, `selection` | Measurement scope independently of selected write coverage. whole_target is the historical default; selection weights each sample by its coverage and requires an active selection. Native source codes determine clipping. |
| `clip` | `number` | no | 0–0.1 | Share of the counted pixels dropped at EACH end before the stretch (default 0.001 = 0.1 %). Larger values push more of the image to pure black and pure white. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | layer (default), mask, red, green, blue, alpha or channel:<name>. Analyzes the whole target; writes only through active selection coverage. |

## `auto_color`

Auto Tone's per-channel stretch plus a per-channel gamma that snaps the midtones neutral. The gamma is derived only from near-neutral midtone pixels and is clamped to 0.5-2.0, so a legitimately coloured scene — a sunset, a forest, a brick wall — is not neutralised; when too few pixels qualify every gamma stays 1. This is a neutral-candidate snap. The UI path is Image > Auto Color (⇧⌘B). In a CMYK document the layer's ink takes CMYK Levels from its tone analysis: per channel for auto_tone and auto_color, monochromatic for auto_contrast, clip (default 0.001, 0.1 %) clipped at each end; one ink plate or an alpha channel takes the 16-bit colour plane's or channel's Auto; a mask refuses.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `analysis_scope` | `string` | no | one of `whole_target`, `selection` | Measurement scope independently of selected write coverage. whole_target is the historical default; selection weights each sample by its coverage and requires an active selection. Native source codes determine clipping. |
| `clip` | `number` | no | 0–0.1 | Share of the counted pixels dropped at EACH end before the stretch (default 0.001 = 0.1 %). Larger values push more of the image to pure black and pure white. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | layer (default), mask, red, green, blue, alpha or channel:<name>. Analyzes the whole target; writes only through active selection coverage. |

## `apply_filter`

Applies a filter or adjustment DESTRUCTIVELY through active selection coverage, preserving every stored code outside coverage in both depths. 16-bit targets layer RGB; byte mode also supports scalar planes. Neighborhood filters sample the whole target. With no selection they edit the whole target. Supports layer pixels, masks, color planes and saved channels (prefer add_adjustment_layer for a reversible color adjustment; this tool refuses adjustment/group pixel targets but supports their masks). Filters and their parameters: grayscale, invert, sepia, edge_detect, emboss (none); blur (sigma above 0, at most 1000 at 8 bits and 64 at 16 bits, default 4); sharpen (amount, default 1); unsharp_mask (radius 0-64 default 1.5, amount 0-5 default 1 where 1 is 100%, threshold 0-1 default 0 in normalized contrast where 0.0039216 is one 8-bit level); high_pass (radius 0-64, default 3); reduce_noise (radius 0-64 default 1, luminance 0-0.25 default 0.01 in normalized units where 0.0039216 is one 8-bit level — the noise LEVEL to remove, so it decides what counts as grain — detail and color each 0-1 default 0.5, where luminance 0 or detail 1 turns the luminance half off and color 0 turns the colour half off, and both off changes nothing); dust_and_scratches (radius 0-64 default 2, the radius of a DISC of whole source pixels where below 1 changes nothing, threshold 0-1 default 0 in normalized contrast, where 0 is a plain median rather than a bypass) — the photographic sharpening and noise-cleanup filters, one kernel at both depths, writing colour only, so alpha stays exact in both depths. adjust (brightness, contrast, saturation, each -1..1, default 0; legacy true/false, absent = true, as add_adjustment_layer's bcs — false is the modern form that keeps black and white fixed); levels (normalized black 0-1, white 0-1, gamma 0.1-10, output_black and output_white 0-1, and optional r/g/b objects of the same five keys for per-channel stages, applied before the master one — all flat beside filter, as add_adjustment_layer's levels; 16-bit code N is N/65535); hue_rotate (degrees); threshold (level 0-1); posterize (levels 2-64); pixelate (block 1-1024); add_noise (amount 0-1, seed); box_blur (radius, an integer 1-1000 default 5: the plain mean of a (2r+1)x(2r+1) clamped-edge window, which filters ALPHA as gaussian_blur does); surface_blur (radius an integer 1-100 default 5, threshold 2-255 default 15 in 8-bit LEVELS at every depth — unlike the normalized 0-1 thresholds above — where a step of 2.5x the threshold or more is left alone; colour only); add_grain (amount 0-100 default 25, where 100 is an RMS of 25.5 levels at mid-grey and black and white are never changed; size 0.5-4 px default 1; roughness 0-100 default 50; seed, an integer, default 1; amount 0 changes nothing; colour only); radial_blur (Filters > Blur > Radial Blur…: amount an integer 1-100 default 10, the arc in degrees for method "spin" (default) or the streak as amount x 0.5% of the distance from the centre for "zoom"; quality "draft" (grainy, deterministic), "good" (default) or "best"; center_x and center_y 0-1 default 0.5; filters alpha); clouds and difference_clouds (Filters > Render > Clouds / Difference Clouds: seed, an integer, default 1; foreground_color and background_color "#rrggbb", default #000000 and #ffffff — not the swatches; high_contrast true/false default false, the menu's Option-click; clouds writes opaque pixels, difference_clouds is |pixel - clouds| on colour and keeps alpha); offset (Filters > Other > Offset…: horizontal and vertical integers in pixels, default 0, positive moving content right and down, any size allowed; undefined_areas "wrap" (default), "repeat" (edge pixels), "transparent" or "background" — on a layer both leave the vacated area transparent (there is no Background layer), on a mask they fill white, on a red/green/blue plane that component of background_color (default #ffffff), on the alpha plane or a channel its Rec. 709 gray; both offsets 0 changes nothing); motion_blur (Filters > Blur > Motion Blur…: angle in degrees -360..360 default 0, positive counterclockwise; distance an integer 1-2000 px default 10 — the mean of distance+1 samples a pixel apart along the line through each pixel; filters alpha); lens_blur (Filters > Blur > Lens Blur…: radius an integer 1-100 default 15, the disc's radius; brightness 0-100 default 0 and threshold 0-255 default 255 in 8-bit LEVELS at every depth — pixels brighter than threshold weigh up to 1 + 8 x brightness/100 times as much, so highlights bloom as discs; filters alpha); tilt_shift (Filters > Blur > Tilt-Shift…: radius an integer 1-100 default 15, the blur far from the focus line; center_x and center_y 0-1 default 0.5, fractions of the whole layer or plane; angle -90..90 default 0, a horizontal line, positive counterclockwise; focus 0-1 default 0.15 and transition 0-1 default 0.25, fractions of the height: within focus of the line nothing blurs, and the radius grows to full over transition; filters alpha). These three take no frame: a selection only confines where the result is written. lens_correction (Filters > Lens Correction…: distortion -100..100 default 0, positive corrects barrel distortion (k1 = -0.0008 x distortion, the radial model RAW development uses); chromatic_red_cyan and chromatic_blue_yellow -100..100 default 0, the red and blue channels' lateral scale 1 + 0.00002 x value about the centre; vignette_amount -100..100 default 0, up to 2 stops at the farthest corner, positive brightens; vignette_midpoint 0-100 default 50, higher keeps more of the middle clear; vertical_perspective and horizontal_perspective -100..100 default 0, negative vertical widens the top and negative horizontal the left; angle -180..180 degrees default 0, positive turns the picture counterclockwise; scale 50-150 percent default 100. The whole layer or plane is resampled about its centre (Catmull-Rom); what falls outside the picture, or past the radial correction's fold, becomes transparent; every default changes nothing; no frame, a selection only confines where the result is written; profile: "auto" applies the bundled Lensfun profile (Lensfun database v0.3.4, CC BY-SA 3.0) matched to the document's EXIF camera and lens at its focal length, f-number and distance, refused in-band when nothing matches or the target is not the camera frame; a lens id from list_lens_profiles applies that lens; "none" or omitted applies none; a profile object (list_lens_profiles' profile) applies as it is. The profile's distortion, chromatic aberration and vignetting are corrected after the sliders' map, in one resample). presence (Filters > Presence…: texture, clarity and dehaze, each -100..100 default 0, 0 being off. texture raises the contrast of medium-fine detail, finer than clarity and coarser than sharpening, without amplifying pixel noise; negative smooths that detail and keeps edges. clarity raises local contrast at a wider radius, weighted toward the midtones so highlights and shadows do not clip, over an edge-aware base so a strong edge gets no halo; negative softens. dehaze removes atmospheric haze, estimating the haze colour from the picture's haziest pixels and how much of it covers each pixel; negative adds haze of that colour. The radii are a share of the longer side of the layer or plane (about 0.05%, 0.3% and 2% of it), so a setting looks the same at any size. Colour only; all three at 0 changes nothing; no frame, a selection only confines where the result is written. In a 32-bit float document all three run on the display-encoded layer, unclamped above white; dehaze measures the haze on that encoding with values above white read as white, and leaves a component above white as it is at a positive amount). develop_filter (Filters > Develop Filter…: the Develop RAW window's global controls on any layer, each 0 by default and 0 being off: temperature and tint -100..100, exposure -4..4 stops, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, texture, clarity, dehaze, vibrance and saturation -100..100. They run in one fixed order, each step skipped when its controls are 0: (1) white balance, temperature being a RELATIVE shift of one mired a unit from a neutral picture (the white_balance illuminant 1e6/(1e6/6504 - temperature) K, so + warms and - cools) and tint passed as white_balance's tint (+ toward magenta); (2) exposure, a linear-light gain of 2^exposure; (3) contrast, the modern adjust S-curve at power 2^(1.5 x contrast/100); (4) highlights and shadows, shadows_highlights at tone 0.5 with color 0 and amounts shadows/100 (shadows/200 below 0) and -highlights/100 (-highlights/200 above 0), so + shadows lifts and + highlights brightens, over the blurred luma of step 3's result at radius 30 x longer side / 2048; (5) whites and blacks, a levels master stage moving the white or black point by up to 0.2 (+ whites lowers white, - raises output_white; - blacks raises black, + raises output_black); (6) texture, clarity and dehaze, exactly presence's; (7) vibrance and saturation, vibrance's at value/100. Not re-editable: a second run starts from the current pixels. Colour only; all thirteen at 0 changes nothing; no frame, a selection only confines where the result is written. In a 32-bit float document temperature, tint and exposure (v x 2^exposure) act on the stored linear values; contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, texture, clarity and dehaze on the display-encoded layer, unclamped (highlights and shadows leave a pixel whose encoded luma is at or above white as it is); vibrance and saturation on the decoded linear value scaled about white, as the vibrance adjustment runs at 32 bits). develop_filter also takes masks (the sheet's Masks section): an array of at most 16 local adjustments applied in order after the global controls, each an object with shape (required): {op: radial, center: [x, y], radius: [rx, ry], hardness 0..1} (smoothstep from hardness to the ellipse's edge), {op: linear, from: [x, y], to: [x, y]} (1 at from, 0 at to), {op: full}, {op: empty}, or {op: subject | people | sky} (made by Vision, or by the sky model, on the layer before the filter runs; a missing sky model and a model that finds nothing refuse by name); coordinates are 0..1 of the layer's width and height, rx in widths and ry in heights, each above 0 and at most 2. brush: [{mode: add | subtract, dabs: [{center: [x, y], radius (a share of the longer side), hardness 0..1, opacity 0..1}]}] painted over the shape, at most 4096 dabs and 256 million evaluated pixels a stroke. invert (false) flips the coverage; density 0..1 (default 1) weights it; feather 0..100 (default 0) blurs it by feather/100 x 4% of the longer side, at most 256 px. range narrows it as Develop's local range does: {luminance: {low, high, low_falloff?, high_falloff?, invert?}, color: {lab: [L, a, b] or sample: [x, y], amount, falloff?, invert?}} (falloffs default 0, invert false; range null is no range), read as CIE L*a*b* of the layer's own pixels through the document's profile, so a local never moves its own range. Each mask takes temperature, tint, exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, texture, clarity, dehaze and saturation in the global ranges (default 0; no vibrance), run as the global controls are over the picture the earlier masks left, so overlapping masks compound, then noise_reduction 0..100 (reduce_noise at radius 0.5, luminance noise_reduction/1000, detail 0, color 0) and sharpness -100..100 (above 0 smart_sharpen at amount 1.5 x sharpness %, radius 1, noise 0, remove gaussian; below 0 gaussian_blur at radius 3 x -sharpness/100), both default 0 and their radii fixed in pixels, and blended by the coverage. masks are refused on a mask, colour plane or channel target ('develop_filter masks edit layer pixels only'), on a 32-bit float layer ('develop_filter masks are not available on a 32-bit float layer') and in CMYK. A recorded step keeps the subject, people and sky shapes as they were asked for, so a replay runs the model again. smart_sharpen (Filter > Sharpen > Smart Sharpen…: amount 1-500 percent default 200; radius 0.1-64 px default 1; noise 0-100 percent default 10, Reduce Noise's luminance smoothing (radius 0.5, luminance noise/1000) before the sharpen; remove "gaussian", "lens" (default) or "motion", the blur the sharpen undoes: each colour becomes D + amount/100 x (D - B), B that blur of the denoised picture D (a Gaussian of sigma radius, a lens disc of the radius, or a line of round(2 x radius) px at angle), so gaussian with noise 0 and no fade is unsharp_mask at the same radius with threshold 0; lens removal also holds each colour within 2 levels of its 3x3 neighbourhood's range, which keeps edges free of halos; angle -180..180 degrees default 0, read only by motion; shadow_fade and highlight_fade 0-100 default 0, shadow_tonal_width and highlight_tonal_width 0-100 default 50, shadow_radius and highlight_radius integers 1-100 px default 1: the amount fades by up to fade% where the neighbourhood luma (a box of that radius) is darker than the shadows' tonal width or lighter than the highlights'. Colour only; never a no-op; no frame, a selection only confines where the result is written. In a 32-bit float document the whole filter runs on the display-encoded layer, unclamped above white, the tonal fades reading luma above white as white). WITH A SELECTION, radial_blur's centre is a fraction of the selection's bounding box on the target and offset shifts and wraps within that box; without one both use the whole layer or plane. Colour-only filters leave alpha exact and fully transparent pixels untouched. Every adjustment-layer op also runs destructively here — curves (rgb/r/g/b arrays of fractional [input,output] points in the historical 0…255 space, or rgb_map/r_map/g_map/b_map arrays of 256 integers 0-255), exposure, vibrance, hue_saturation, color_balance, black_and_white, photo_filter, channel_mixer, selective_color, shadows_highlights, white_balance, gradient_map, color_lookup, replace_color — with its parameters in a params OBJECT (not flat), exactly as add_adjustment_layer takes them. Image > Adjustments > Desaturate (⇧⌘U) is hue_saturation with {"params": {"saturation": -1}}, which is what it records. The older filters listed first read their arguments FLAT. Each style REFUSES the other rather than ignoring it: posterize takes levels beside filter and is refused a params object, and exposure takes {"params": {"gamma": 0.4}} and is refused a bare gamma — which would otherwise have applied the op's defaults and reported success. A flat filter also refuses, by name, any key it does not take (a misspelt "sigmaa" is an error, not the default), and a numeric argument given as null or true/false. In Quick Mask, filter blur softens the Quick Mask coverage instead of a layer (sigma 0.65 to 75.5, default 4): with no target while Quick Mask is on, or with target "quick_mask", which refuses when it is off. Every other filter refuses in Quick Mask. With target mask, filter invert inverts the mask over the whole canvas, including the area outside its stored rectangle. In a 32-bit float document every adjustment its layer admits — levels, black_and_white, channel_mixer, photo_filter, exposure, curves (point or map form), color_balance, color_lookup, adjust (bcs), hue_saturation, a document_v2 white_balance, hue_rotate, grayscale, sepia, threshold, posterize, vibrance, selective_color, gradient_map and replace_color — applies to a layer's pixels exactly as their adjustment layer renders, lerped by the selection with no clamp. Twenty-three filters run on a float layer's pixels, through the same kernels as the other depths, each under one stated rule. In linear light, with no clamp to 0 to 1: blur, box_blur, motion_blur, radial_blur, lens_blur, tilt_shift, offset, lens_correction, unsharp_mask and high_pass (liquify is its own tool), pixelate (the premultiplied mean of the cell's light) and add_noise (v x (1 + delta), so black stays black and a highlight gets proportional grain). A blurred highlight above white spreads its whole energy; unsharp_mask and high_pass may write values below 0, which the document keeps; high_pass adds the stored value 0.5 (linear, lighter than mid-grey on screen); unsharp_mask's threshold compares linear differences; lens_blur's threshold reads linear luma, so a pixel above white always takes the full highlight weight; lens_correction's vignette multiplies the linear values by 2^stops, and its resample is clamped to the range the layer's visible pixels hold. On the layer's DISPLAY ENCODING (the profile's curve to white, a logarithm above it, decoded back; a component the filter leaves alone keeps its bits), so their thresholds and amounts mean what they mean at 16 bits: surface_blur, dust_and_scratches, reduce_noise, add_grain, clouds and difference_clouds (the colours mixed in encoded units), emboss and edge_detect (kept inside the encoded range the layer holds), sharpen (unsharp mask amount 1 on the encoding; unsharp_mask itself stays linear), presence (texture, clarity and dehaze), smart_sharpen (the whole filter; its tonal fades read luma above white as white) and develop_filter (temperature, tint and exposure on the linear values first; contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, texture, clarity and dehaze on the encoding; vibrance and saturation on the decoded linear value, scaled about white). dehaze measures its haze with values above white read as white and, at a positive amount, leaves a component above white as it is; highlights and shadows leave a pixel whose encoded luma is at or above white as it is. A value above white is never clamped to it. Alpha stays in 0 to 1, a result alpha below 2^-24 is transparent, and a result outside +/-65504 refuses. blur is an exact windowed Gaussian there, so its time grows with sigma (about a minute and a half at sigma 64 on 24 MP; it is cancellable). The reply's storage is rgba32_float. Invert, shadows_highlights, a legacy_srgb white_balance and the remaining filters refuse by name. Every filter but develop_filter also runs on target mask, channel:<name> or one of red, green, blue and alpha: the plane is read as opaque gray; a mask, channel or alpha is coverage (never display-encoded) and its result is clamped to 0..1; red, green and blue are linear light, unclamped, each filter in its own domain; a result whose three components differ is their Rec. 709 luma. add_noise on coverage is the 16-bit additive draw. develop_filter on such a target refuses by name, and an Image > Adjustments op there refuses too. The reply's storage is rgba32_float for red, green, blue and alpha and u16 for a mask or channel. In a CMYK document levels (flat, with optional c, m, y, k stages) and curves (params cmyk, c, m, y, k ink points, or the cmyk_map… drawn maps) apply on a layer's ink, and hue_saturation (the RGB params on 1 − C, 1 − M, 1 − Y, K kept but under colorize) and every adjustment below on a layer's ink. On one ink plate (target cyan, magenta, yellow or black: its stored 1 − ink), a layer mask or an alpha channel the adjustments and filters run as on a 16-bit colour plane or channel, with its RGB vocabulary (levels' flat keys, curves rgb / rgb_map; a CMYK key refuses by name). bcs (no saturation), invert, posterize and shadows_highlights run per plate on 1 − ink; color_balance, color_lookup and photo_filter (params ink [c, m, y, k] as fractions 0–1 in place of color) on the C/M/Y triple, K held; channel_mixer takes rows cyan, magenta, yellow, black and gray of {c, m, y, k, constant} on the ink; selective_color and threshold their RGB params on ink; gradient_map stops {position, ink, opacity, midpoint, opacity_midpoint} (method classic and smoothness as in RGB; perceptual refuses); replace_color inks (1–8 [c, m, y, k] fractions) in place of colors. exposure, vibrance and black_and_white refuse, as do hue_rotate, grayscale, sepia and white_balance (RGB only). shadows_highlights and replace_color apply destructively only. The filters available in CMYK run on the layer's ink as two passes of the RGB filter over 1 − ink (C/M/Y, then K) with their RGB arguments; add_noise's K plate takes its own seed; clouds and difference_clouds take foreground_ink / background_ink ([c, m, y, k] percent; default K 100 % over paper). lens_correction, develop_filter, presence and add_grain refuse, as do depth_blur and the red-eye tools (RGB only). In a Grayscale document the adjustments bcs/adjust, levels, curves, exposure, invert, posterize, threshold, gradient_map (stops stored as their gray), shadows_highlights and replace_color run on the gray values; Levels' and Curves' r, g and b must be absent or alike; vibrance, hue_saturation, color_balance, black_and_white, photo_filter, channel_mixer, color_lookup and selective_color refuse, and hue_rotate, grayscale, sepia and white_balance as RGB-only. Every filter runs on the gray values through the RGB kernel, a colour it makes (Lens Correction's fringes, develop_filter's temperature and tint) folded to its Rec. 709 luma and add_noise drawing one full-amplitude delta; clouds' foreground_color and background_color are greyed by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule; target is layer, mask or channel:<name> (red, green, blue and alpha refuse for good). In a Lab Color document filter bcs, color_balance, color_lookup, curves, gradient_map, hue_saturation, invert, levels, photo_filter, posterize and threshold run on the L*a*b* values (adjust is bcs), destructively and as a layer, and replace_color and shadows_highlights destructively only (as a layer they refuse): levels and curves adjust Lightness with the composite and their r stage, a* with g and b* with b; bcs adjusts Lightness and its saturation scales a* and b* about 0; invert and posterize act on every channel; threshold gives black and white (a* = b* = 0); hue_saturation of saturation -1 alone (Desaturate) keeps L* and sets a* = b* = 0; the other hue_saturation, color_balance, photo_filter, shadows_highlights and replace_color run on each sample's 16-bit ProPhoto RGB colour, so a colour outside sRGB keeps its chroma, and color_lookup and gradient_map on its sRGB colour (a sample the op leaves alone keeps its values); photo_filter's color is sRGB, and replace_color's colors are the document's own 8-bit #LLaabb Lab values (LL = round(255·L*/100), aa and bb = round(a* + 128), round(b* + 128)). black_and_white, channel_mixer, exposure, selective_color and vibrance refuse; grayscale, hue_rotate, sepia and white_balance as RGB-only. Every other filter runs on the L*a*b* values, each channel filtered alone at 8 and 16 bits (add_noise draws a* and b* too; clouds' colours become their Lab values); develop_filter, difference_clouds and lens_correction refuse; add_grain and presence as Develop Filter controls disabled in Lab; depth_blur as RGB-only. lens_blur, reduce_noise and smart_sharpen run on the layer per channel, each of L*, a* and b* filtered alone as a gray image; emboss and edge_detect run on Lightness and leave a* = b* = 0 (mixed toward 0 by a partial selection); reduce_noise's color has no effect on Lab (with luminance 0 it changes nothing); offset with undefined_areas background on a lightness, a or b target fills that plane's value of the background colour's L*a*b*. target is layer, mask, lightness, a, b, alpha or channel:<name>: on a mask, an alpha channel or a plane every filter and adjustment runs as on RGB but those that refuse for good and liquify. A Duotone document refuses filter develop_filter, lens_correction and tilt_shift for good. A Bitmap document: not available in Bitmap mode; filter lens_blur refuses: Lens Blur on a Bitmap document is not built in Doctored; convert to Grayscale first.
