## `brush_stroke`

Paints a brush stroke onto a layer's pixels: a smooth polyline through points (canvas coordinates) with round caps and joins. One point paints a dot. Draw shapes with several strokes; use render to check the result. With target: "mask" the same stroke paints the layer's mask instead, revealing what it covers. 16-bit mode supports every existing paint blend and native scalar targets. stroke_version=1 generates native dabs from points/pressure/timing and records canonical replay; unversioned point calls generate the same native dabs with unit pressure and no timing, under the same two core limits (50,000 dabs, 2 billion work units — about 70 soft 5,000 px dabs on a 100-megapixel canvas); over-cap strokes refuse by name; no partial stroke. On an 8-bit document canonical dabs are accepted for the LAYER target with size > 1 (coverage targets and the size-1 pixel brush refuse by name). In a 32-bit float document the stroke composites in linear light with no clamp on colour, in Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Darker Color, Linear Burn, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Pin Light, Difference, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity only; rgba32 replaces color with linear-light numbers, above white included, and the reply's storage is "rgba32_float". A mask or alpha channel target is painted as at 16 bits (storage "u16"); a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses there. background returns a job for a float layer stroke as it does at 16 bits. In a CMYK document this paints in INK on a layer (or its mask): pass ink [c, m, y, k] in percent (exactly the Color Picker's C/M/Y/K), or color, which converts through the document's CMYK profile; every blend mode but Pass Through, evaluated on 1 − ink. Target cyan, magenta, yellow or black paints that ink plate's stored 1 − ink, and channel:<name> an alpha channel, as a 16-bit colour plane or channel is painted: color's grey is painted (white leaves no ink) and ink refuses. On an RGB document ink refuses. In a Grayscale document the colour paints its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule (its luminance in the Gray profile), R = G = B, at 8, 16 and 32 bits; target is layer, mask or channel:<name> (the Gray channel is the layer; red, green, blue and alpha refuse for good), ink refuses, and blend_mode takes the Grayscale modes. In a Lab Color document the colour paints its L*a*b* values by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, at 8 and 16 bits (color_space document takes the L*a*b* values as unit codes, L*/100 and (a* + 128)/255, exactly); target is layer, mask, lightness, a, b, alpha or channel:<name> (red, green and blue refuse: a Lab document's planes are lightness, a and b), ink refuses, and blend_mode takes Normal, Dissolve, Multiply, Linear Burn, Darker Color, Screen, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity; Darken, Color Burn, Lighten, Color Dodge, Difference, Exclusion, Subtract and Divide are unavailable. On an Indexed Color document the stroke paints the RGB storage in Normal mode, then each changed pixel goes back onto the palette: full ink takes the entry nearest the colour, and an edge pixel takes it when its coverage is at least 131/255, else keeps its index (a fixed rule, measured against Photoshop, whose own edge varies from stroke to stroke). Every blend_mode paints: the rule compares each changed pixel with the mode's full-strength colour over its old colour and takes the entry nearest that colour. On a Bitmap document it paints in black and white: the colour becomes black or white by its gray (128 and above is white), the edit runs on the 8-bit gray storage at its opacity, and every pixel goes back to white where its gray over the background at its own alpha reaches 128, else black, so a soft edge lands hard where its coverage reaches about half and a stroke under 50 % opacity changes nothing. blend_mode Normal, Darken or Lighten only (another refuses); sample_all_layers is off (the one layer is the composite). An erased or cleared pixel takes the background, white.

| `angle` | `number` | no | -180–180 | Tip rotation in degrees, counter-clockwise (default 0). Visible only when roundness is below 100. |
| `background` | `boolean` | no | — | 16-bit or 32-bit float layer strokes: return a job_id immediately for job_status/cancel_job (default false waits; Actions always wait). Ignored at 8 bits; refused for mask, channel, Quick Mask and adjustment-layer strokes. |
| `blend_mode` | `string` | no | one of `Normal`, `Dissolve`, `Darken`, `Multiply`, `Color Burn`, `Linear Burn`, `Darker Color`, `Lighten`, `Screen`, `Color Dodge`, `Linear Dodge (Add)`, `Lighter Color`, `Overlay`, `Soft Light`, `Hard Light`, `Vivid Light`, `Linear Light`, `Pin Light`, `Hard Mix`, `Difference`, `Exclusion`, `Subtract`, `Divide`, `Hue`, `Saturation`, `Color`, `Luminosity` | Blend mode the stroke's paint composites with (default Normal) — the layer blend-mode names. Not valid with a coverage target — a mask, a colour plane or a channel. |
| `color` | `string` | no | — | Hex color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA (default #000000). Ignored when target is "mask". |
| `color_space` | `string` | no | one of `srgb`, `document`, `display_p3` | How the colour argument is interpreted, at EITHER depth. Default srgb: an authored sRGB hex (or 16-bit rgba), converted once into the document. document: the hex IS the document's own bytes (sample_color's hex), at 16 bits too, where each hex byte v becomes the exact code v·257 (16-bit numeric rgba is then read as document components). display_p3: the hex (or 16-bit rgba) is Display P3, converted once into the document. Numeric rgba stays 16-bit-only. |

Mutually exclusive with generation options; recorded automatically. Byte commits and replay share one exact dab rasterizer; at 8 bits historical unversioned points keep their prior meaning. |

| `points` | `array<array<number>>` | yes | 1–10000 items | [[x, y], …] along the stroke, in canvas px. |

| `pressure_size` | `boolean` | no | — | Scale dab size by pressure, with a one-pixel floor. |

| `rgba` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items; items: 0–1 | 16-bit documents only: continuous normalized sRGB RGBA, overriding color. Never a byte-preview sample. |
| `rgba32` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | 32-bit float documents only, instead of color: [red, green, blue, alpha] as linear light in the document's primaries (sample_color's center_rgba32 / mean_rgba32), red, green and blue 0–65504 (above 1 is above white) and alpha 0–1, used as they are. Takes no color_space; an 8- or 16-bit document and Quick Mask refuse it. Layer target only: a mask, a channel or an adjustment layer's mask is 0–1 coverage and refuses it. |

| `size` | `number` | no | — | Stroke width in px (1-5000, default 16). |
| `spacing` | `number` | no | 1–200 | Dab spacing as a percent of the brush diameter (default 25). Above 25 the stroke stamps visibly; 150+ reads as a dotted line. |

Byte and 16-bit stroke tools accept this form, including byte mask/plane/channel, pixel and Quick Mask coverage. At 8 bits, omit for the historical point footprint; at 16 bits unversioned points generate the same native dabs (unit pressure, no timing) and refuse by name at the 50,000-dab and 2-billion-work-unit limits; smudge_stroke has its own 256-million-work-unit bound at both depths (it walks the stroke a pixel at a time) and refuses a longer stroke by name. A versioned call refuses a size outside its tool's range by name (1–5000 px; 3–200 for heal_stroke and spot_heal_stroke; 1–200 for blur_stroke, sharpen_stroke, smudge_stroke, sponge_stroke and history_brush_stroke; 1–200 for art_history_brush_stroke); an unversioned call clamps it. Maximum 50,000 dabs; oversized strokes refuse by name; no partial stroke. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | What the stroke paints: "layer" (default) the layer's own pixels, "mask" the layer's mask, "red"/"green"/"blue"/"alpha" ONE colour plane of that layer's pixels, or "channel:<name>" one of the document's alpha channels (list_channels names them). On a mask the stroke REVEALS what it covers. Coverage is not color, so every target but "layer" forces the stroke to WHITE whatever color you pass, opacity becomes partial coverage, and blend_mode is not valid. "mask" needs a layer that already has one (add_layer_mask). On an ADJUSTMENT layer a layer or colour-plane stroke paints the mask instead, whatever this says — a channel target is document state and is never rerouted. A GROUP has no pixels of its own, so "layer" and the colour planes are refused on one, but its canvas-sized MASK is paintable exactly like any other and so is a channel. |
| `times` | `array<number>` | no | items: 0–∞ | Elapsed seconds per point, starting at 0 and nondecreasing; used for 20 Hz airbrush deposits. |

## `eraser_stroke`

Erases along a polyline (same geometry as brush_stroke): pixels under the stroke become transparent. opacity is the eraser strength. With target: "mask" it hides through the layer's mask instead, leaving the pixels intact. On an 8-bit document stroke_version=1 / native_stroke record and replay canonical dabs for the LAYER target with size > 1; a mask, plane or channel target and the size-1 pixel brush refuse by name and keep the historical point footprint. In a 32-bit float document it lowers the layer's alpha and leaves every colour sample as it is, above white included (storage "rgba32_float"); a mask or alpha channel target is erased as at 16 bits, and a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses there. background returns a job for a float layer stroke as it does at 16 bits. Works on a CMYK document: a new layer is bare paper, a mask scales its layer's ink coverage, and applying a mask bakes it into the layer's alpha with the ink kept. In a Grayscale document target is layer, mask or channel:<name>. In a Lab Color document target is layer, mask, lightness, a, b, alpha or channel:<name>. On an Indexed Color document the edit runs on the RGB storage, then each changed pixel goes back onto the palette by the Brush's rule: paint takes the entry nearest the colour (an edge pixel when its coverage is at least 131/255, else it keeps its index), and an erased pixel keeps its index until its alpha falls below 128, when it takes the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the entry nearest the current background colour). Painting takes every blend_mode: a changed pixel is compared with the mode's full-strength colour over its old colour and takes the entry nearest that colour, by the same 131/255 rule; sample_all_layers is off. On a Bitmap document it paints in black and white: the colour becomes black or white by its gray (128 and above is white), the edit runs on the 8-bit gray storage at its opacity, and every pixel goes back to white where its gray over the background at its own alpha reaches 128, else black, so a soft edge lands hard where its coverage reaches about half and a stroke under 50 % opacity changes nothing. blend_mode Normal, Darken or Lighten only (another refuses); sample_all_layers is off (the one layer is the composite). An erased or cleared pixel takes the background, white.

## `clone_stamp`

Clones pixels from one part of the picture onto a layer — the Clone Stamp tool. A snapshot of the sampled picture (sample; the whole composite by default), displaced by (first point − source), is painted through a round-capped stroke along points, so what lands under the stroke comes from a region the same offset away: source_x,source_y is what appears under the FIRST point, and the offset stays fixed along the stroke (aligned cloning). Respects the active selection. Errors on an adjustment layer (no pixels to rewrite). This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). 16-bit mode supports captured native current (default), current_and_below or all sampling, ignore_adjustments, fractional source coordinates/source_transform, new-layer output and explicit destination expansion. blend_mode is honoured at 16 bits as at 8: the cloned pixels composite into the layer through that mode; output new_layer refuses any mode but Normal, because a fresh layer has nothing to blend with. Source RGB never comes from a display preview. In a 32-bit float document it works on a layer's linear-light pixels with the same arguments as at 16 bits: clone_stamp copies linear light with no clamp (a colour above white stays above white) in Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Darker Color, Linear Burn, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Pin Light, Difference, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity only; the healing tools (heal_stroke, spot_heal_stroke, patch_region, remove_stroke, content_aware_fill, content_aware_move) match and blend in a display-like working encoding, write linear light back, take Normal blending only and leave every pixel they do not change bit for bit. A mask, channel, colour-plane or Quick Mask target refuses there. Works on a CMYK document's ink: the sample is the ink (current: the layer's; current_and_below / all: the CMYK composite), the clone composites through its blend_mode on 1 − ink, healing and synthesis run on the four inks, and output new_layer adds a CMYK layer. In a Grayscale document blend_mode takes the Grayscale modes, and the source is the same Grayscale document. In a Lab Color document it clones the L*a*b* values, each channel alone; blend_mode takes Normal, Dissolve, Multiply, Linear Burn, Darker Color, Screen, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity; Darken, Color Burn, Lighten, Color Dodge, Difference, Exclusion, Subtract and Divide are unavailable. On an Indexed Color document the stroke runs on the RGB storage, then each changed pixel takes the palette entry nearest its own new colour: a hard, full-opacity clone copies the source's entries, and a full History Brush stroke restores the earlier state's indices. output new_layer refuses for good (an Indexed Color document holds one layer). A Bitmap document: the clone runs on the 8-bit gray storage and every pixel goes back white where its gray over white at its own alpha reaches 128, else black; blend_mode Normal, Darken or Lighten only (another refuses). output new_layer refuses: add_layer is not available in Bitmap mode.

| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `duration` | `number` | no | 0–2499 | Total stroke seconds, including any hold at the final point; defaults to the last time. |
| `expand_destination` | `boolean` | no | — | Explicitly expand the destination raster to include the canvas (default false). Canvas size is unchanged; transparency-locked targets refuse expansion. |
| `flow` | `number` | no | 1–100 | Per-dab deposit in percent (default 100). Below 100 the stroke builds up where it overlaps itself instead of landing at full strength at once. |

Only an adjustment ENTRY is dropped — a layer style, a Blend If, and a plain raster layer in a tone blend mode are ordinary content and stay in. |

| `opacity` | `number` | no | 0–1 | Strength of the cloned paint (default 1). |
| `output` | `string` | no | one of `layer`, `new_layer` | Where the repair lands (default layer: into the target's own pixels). new_layer puts it on a fresh raster layer directly above the target — same depth, same group, inheriting its clipped flag — so the original pixels stay exactly as they were. Refused with a reason when the target sits inside a group carrying its own blending, opacity, mask or style, where the repair would be gated twice: once in the sampled picture and again by the group. Native-depth output preserves the original raster samples. |

| `pressure_opacity` | `boolean` | no | — | Scale each dab deposit by pressure; stroke opacity still applies once. |

| `roundness` | `number` | no | 1–100 | Tip roundness in percent (default 100). Below 100 the dab squashes into an ellipse — with angle, a calligraphy nib. |
| `sample` | `string` | no | one of `current`, `current_and_below`, `all` | WHICH pixels this gesture reads. current is the target layer's own pixels on a transparent canvas, deliberately raw — its opacity, blend mode and mask say how it composites, not what its pixels are. current_and_below is the picture with everything ABOVE the target contributing nothing, which is what keeps a retouch from being graded twice when an adjustment layer sits over it. all is the whole composite. Above excludes the target's own enclosing groups, whose mask, opacity and blend still say how its level meets the picture. Defaults differ by tool and match what that tool always sampled: all for clone_stamp, heal_stroke, patch_region and content_aware_move, current for spot_heal_stroke, remove_stroke and content_aware_fill. The older sample_all_layers boolean still works and still means the same thing (true = all, false = current); sending both is fine when they agree and refused when they contradict, and current_and_below has no boolean spelling at all. Typed clone/heal retain current as their default; all three modes sample authoritative native-depth sources. |

Maximum 50,000 dabs; oversized strokes refuse by name; no partial stroke. |

## `dodge_burn`

Lightens (dodge) or, with burn: true, darkens a layer's pixels where a round-capped stroke along points covers them — the Dodge / Burn tool. exposure is the strength and range picks the tones that move most: shadows, midtones (default), or highlights. Respects the active selection; repeat the stroke to build the effect up. Errors on an adjustment layer (edit its parameters instead). This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). In a 32-bit float document the stroke classifies on the display-encoded copy and changes linear light: a component v in 0–1 becomes D(shaped(E(v))) (E the profile's curve, D its decode), one above white is scaled by what the tool does to white and one below zero is shifted by what it does to black, held to ±65504, alpha kept (storage "rgba32_float"). With target "mask" or "channel:<name>", at 16 and 32 bits, each u16 sample s becomes 65535·shaped(s/65535) lerped by stroke × selection coverage — a mask is coverage, not light (storage "u16"); an 8-bit document refuses target, and a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses at every depth. Works on a CMYK document's ink: the tool runs on 1 − ink in two passes, C/M/Y together and K alone (Dodge/Burn's Protect Tones holds the C/M/Y ratios; the Sponge moves C/M/Y and keeps K exactly; the History Brush paints from a CMYK state). In a Grayscale document it runs on the gray values (R = G = B) at 8, 16 and 32 bits on the layer, or its mask where an RGB document takes one. In a Lab Color document Dodge and Burn shape Lightness alone (a* and b* are kept); protect_tones is the plain curve on Lightness. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| `protect_tones` | `boolean` | no | — | Protect Tones (default false): each pixel's channels move together — the largest by the tool's curve, the others keeping their ratios to it — so hue and saturation hold. At every depth; on a CMYK document the C/M/Y inks move together and K by the plain curve. A mask or channel target takes the plain curve. |
| `range` | `string` | no | one of `shadows`, `midtones`, `highlights` | Which tones the stroke moves most (default midtones). |
| `roundness` | `number` | no | 1–100 | Tip roundness in percent (default 100). Below 100 the dab squashes into an ellipse — with angle, a calligraphy nib. |
| `size` | `number` | no | — | Stroke width in px (1-5000, default 24). |
| `spacing` | `number` | no | 1–200 | Dab spacing as a percent of the brush diameter (default 25). Above 25 the stroke stamps visibly; 150+ reads as a dotted line. |
| `stroke_version` | `integer` | no | one of `1` | Generate canonical resolved dabs from points and optional pressures/times. Byte and 16-bit stroke tools accept this form, including byte mask/plane/channel, pixel and Quick Mask coverage. At 8 bits, omit for the historical point footprint; at 16 bits unversioned points generate the same native dabs (unit pressure, no timing) and refuse by name at the 50,000-dab and 2-billion-work-unit limits; smudge_stroke has its own 256-million-work-unit bound at both depths (it walks the stroke a pixel at a time) and refuses a longer stroke by name. A versioned call refuses a size outside its tool's range by name (1–5000 px; 3–200 for heal_stroke and spot_heal_stroke; 1–200 for blur_stroke, sharpen_stroke, smudge_stroke, sponge_stroke and history_brush_stroke; 1–200 for art_history_brush_stroke); an unversioned call clamps it. Maximum 50,000 dabs; oversized strokes refuse by name; no partial stroke. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | What the stroke dodges or burns: "layer" (default), "mask" (the layer's mask, which must exist) or "channel:<name>" (an alpha channel). 16-bit and 32-bit float documents only: on a mask or channel each u16 sample s becomes 65535·shaped(s/65535), lerped by stroke × selection coverage. An 8-bit document refuses a target other than "layer", and a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses at every depth. |
| `times` | `array<number>` | no | items: 0–∞ | Elapsed seconds per point, starting at 0 and nondecreasing; used for 20 Hz airbrush deposits. |

## `heal_stroke`

Heals a stroke from a sampled source — the Healing Brush tool. The pixels under the whole footprint are taken from a region (first point − source) away and Poisson-blended into the layer ONCE, at the end of the stroke, so the healed patch keeps the SOURCE's texture and the DESTINATION's illumination and a stroke has no ridges where its dabs overlapped. Use it for a blemish or a wire that sits on a surface you can sample cleanly nearby; use spot_heal_stroke when there is no such source. Coverage below half is not written at all, so hardness SHAPES the footprint rather than fading the heal — the join is already seamless at the edge — and there is no flow: the stroke always deposits full coverage and opacity is the heal's strength. Replace mode is not offered: in this build it would be exactly clone_stamp. Respects the active selection. A dab or a short stroke is a few milliseconds; a stroke enclosing most of a large photograph is seconds (about 16 at the biggest region allowed, and bigger than that is refused with the limit in the message). The solve runs on the shared cancellable worker: the call waits for it by default, and background=true returns a job_id instead. Errors on an adjustment layer (no pixels to rewrite). This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). 16-bit mode supports captured native current (default), current_and_below or all sampling, ignore_adjustments, fractional source coordinates/source_transform, new-layer output and explicit destination expansion. heal_stroke has no blend_mode at either depth: its result is a solved membrane that replaces the covered pixels, so there is no source colour to composite through a mode. Source RGB never comes from a display preview. In a 32-bit float document it works on a layer's linear-light pixels with the same arguments as at 16 bits: clone_stamp copies linear light with no clamp (a colour above white stays above white) in Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Darker Color, Linear Burn, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Pin Light, Difference, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity only; the healing tools (heal_stroke, spot_heal_stroke, patch_region, remove_stroke, content_aware_fill, content_aware_move) match and blend in a display-like working encoding, write linear light back, take Normal blending only and leave every pixel they do not change bit for bit. A mask, channel, colour-plane or Quick Mask target refuses there. Works on a CMYK document's ink: the sample is the ink (current: the layer's; current_and_below / all: the CMYK composite), the clone composites through its blend_mode on 1 − ink, healing and synthesis run on the four inks, and output new_layer adds a CMYK layer. In a Grayscale document it runs on the gray values (R = G = B) at 8, 16 and 32 bits on the layer, or its mask where an RGB document takes one. In a Lab Color document it works on the L*, a* and b* values, each channel alone, at 8 and 16 bits. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| `background` | `boolean` | no | — | Return a job_id immediately for job_status/cancel_job (default false waits; Actions always wait). |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

| `expand_destination` | `boolean` | no | — | Explicitly expand the destination raster to include the canvas (default false). Canvas size is unchanged; transparency-locked targets refuse expansion. |
| `footprint` | `string` | no | one of `automatic`, `dabs` | Brush footprint (default automatic preserves existing Actions). dabs explicitly stamps the tip at its spacing, including a hard default tip; new canvas clone/heal recordings use it for exact replay. |

## `spot_heal_stroke`

Heals a stroke with NO sampled source — the Spot Healing Brush tool. With type content_aware (the default) the footprint is inpainted from a ring of valid pixels around it (PatchMatch); proximity_match copies the whole footprint from the nearby patch whose surroundings best match the stroke's own (it refuses when no clean patch the stroke's size fits beside it); create_texture tiles a texture built from the pixels under the stroke, so a second stroke over the same area adds more texture. Each is then Poisson-blended in exactly as heal_stroke's sampled patch is, so it takes the surrounding illumination. Use it for a blemish with no clean nearby source; heal_stroke is better when you can name one. hardness shapes the footprint rather than fading the heal, there is no flow (the stroke always deposits full coverage), and opacity is the heal's strength. Bounded per CALL, counting every separate part of the footprint together: at most 4,000,000 pixels for the footprint plus its sampling ring while the footprint covers up to 1,000,000 pixels. A footprint over 1,000,000 pixels is not refused for its size: its search runs at half scale (a quarter over 4,000,000) and that bound is four times larger for each halving, so large structure is matched and fine texture is copied from the picture without being matched to the footprint's edge. Beyond a bound it refuses with a message naming the limit, in the words of a stroke (there is no selection and no ring to change — use a smaller brush or a shorter stroke). A brush-sized footprint is well under a second; a long stroke on a large canvas takes several seconds, because cost follows the footprint plus the band it heals from, and the app is busy for that whole time. Respects the active selection. Errors on an adjustment layer. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). In a 32-bit float document it works on a layer's linear-light pixels with the same arguments as at 16 bits: clone_stamp copies linear light with no clamp (a colour above white stays above white) in Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Darker Color, Linear Burn, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Pin Light, Difference, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity only; the healing tools (heal_stroke, spot_heal_stroke, patch_region, remove_stroke, content_aware_fill, content_aware_move) match and blend in a display-like working encoding, write linear light back, take Normal blending only and leave every pixel they do not change bit for bit. A mask, channel, colour-plane or Quick Mask target refuses there. Works on a CMYK document's ink: the sample is the ink (current: the layer's; current_and_below / all: the CMYK composite), the clone composites through its blend_mode on 1 − ink, healing and synthesis run on the four inks, and output new_layer adds a CMYK layer. In a Grayscale document it runs on the gray values (R = G = B) at 8, 16 and 32 bits on the layer, or its mask where an RGB document takes one. In a Lab Color document it works on the L*, a* and b* values, each channel alone, at 8 and 16 bits. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

## `remove_stroke`

Removes whatever a stroke is painted over — the Remove tool. The stroke (round, size px wide, hard-edged) becomes a hole that is filled from the picture around it, in one undo step. mode "model" (the default) fills it with the local inpainting model (MI-GAN, downloaded in Settings ▸ Models): the model runs on a square crop around the stroke at 512 px and its fill is composited back by the stroke's coverage, at 8 and 16 bits; it refuses by name when the model is not installed, and in a 32-bit or CMYK document (use mode "content_aware" there). mode "content_aware" makes the stroke the hole of one Content-Aware Fill (seed applies to it alone), at 8, 16 and 32 bits and in CMYK; a stroke too large to fill refuses with the limit in content_aware_fill's words. Paint over the WHOLE object with a little margin; what the stroke leaves uncovered stays and is sampled from (sample / ignore_adjustments choose the picture both modes sample). A hole with nothing but transparency around it refuses, and so does a hole with no picture around it at all (a model-mode use_selection over Select All). strokes [{points, size?}, …] (1-64) removes several strokes as ONE hole and one undo step, the tool with Remove after each stroke off and its Apply (each size defaults to the call's size). use_selection true takes the hole from the live selection instead (points, strokes and use_selection are exclusive; use_selection refuses without a selection). Use it for an object, a wire or a person; spot_heal_stroke suits a small blemish. A stroke is confined to the active selection. output new_layer puts the result on a new layer ("Remove" in model mode, "Content-Aware Fill" in content_aware mode) and leaves the target's pixels alone. Runs on the shared cancellable worker: the call waits by default, and background=true returns a job_id for job_status/cancel_job. A model reply adds mode, model, crop [x, y, w, h], planned_bytes and covered_pixels; applied adds strokes (their count) when strokes was sent. Layer RGB only: errors on an adjustment layer or a group, and with a mask, colour plane, channel or Quick Mask targeted. In place it rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). In a 32-bit float document it works on a layer's linear-light pixels with the same arguments as at 16 bits: clone_stamp copies linear light with no clamp (a colour above white stays above white) in Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Darker Color, Linear Burn, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Pin Light, Difference, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity only; the healing tools (heal_stroke, spot_heal_stroke, patch_region, remove_stroke, content_aware_fill, content_aware_move) match and blend in a display-like working encoding, write linear light back, take Normal blending only and leave every pixel they do not change bit for bit. A mask, channel, colour-plane or Quick Mask target refuses there. Works on a CMYK document's ink: the sample is the ink (current: the layer's; current_and_below / all: the CMYK composite), the clone composites through its blend_mode on 1 − ink, healing and synthesis run on the four inks, and output new_layer adds a CMYK layer. In a Grayscale document at 8 and 16 bits each removed pixel is folded to one gray value (the model's colour to its Rec. 709 luma), R = G = B. In a Lab Color document the model sees the layer's Display P3 view (the colours the canvas shows) and its fill is converted back to L*a*b* values before it is mixed by coverage on the L*a*b* values; mode content_aware works on the L*, a* and b* values, each channel alone, at 8 and 16 bits. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

Above excludes the target's own enclosing groups, whose mask, opacity and blend still say how its level meets the picture. The older sample_all_layers boolean still works and still means the same thing (true = all, false = current); sending both is fine when they agree and refused when they contradict, and current_and_below has no boolean spelling at all. Typed clone/heal retain current as their default; all three modes sample authoritative native-depth sources. |
| `sample_all_layers` | `boolean` | no | — | The tool's Sample all layers checkbox: true is sample all, false is sample current (default false). Must agree with sample when both are sent. |
| `seed` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | RNG seed (default 0). The fill is reproducible: the same seed over the same pixels gives byte-identical output, and a different one gives a different plausible fill. |
| `size` | `number` | no | — | Stroke width in px (1-1000, default 40). |
| `strokes` | `array<object>` | no | 1–64 items | Several strokes removed together as one hole and one undo step (the Remove tool's Apply with Remove after each stroke off); refuses with points or use_selection. |
| `strokes[].points` | `array<array<number>>` | with parent | 1–10000 items | [[x, y], …] along this stroke, in canvas px. |
| `strokes[].size` | `number` | no | — | This stroke's width in px (default the call's size). |
| `use_selection` | `boolean` | no | — | Take the hole from the live selection instead of a stroke (default false); refuses with points or strokes. |

## `patch_region`

Moves a region's texture from one part of the picture to another and blends it to the destination's light — the Patch tool. direction "source" (the default) HEALS the outlined region using the texture at (offset_x, offset_y) away from it: outline the flaw and point the offset at good pixels. direction "destination" is the opposite gesture — the outlined region is the good texture, and the region it would land on after the offset is what gets healed. The blend is the same native-depth Poisson join heal_stroke uses, in one undo step. Give points for an explicit polygon, or omit them to patch the current selection (which may be any shape, a magic-wand or Select Subject mask included). Both depths run on the shared cancellable worker (16-bit Patch captures native samples); background=true returns a job_id for job_status/cancel_job instead of waiting. Oversized regions refuse with the limit in the message. Errors on an adjustment layer. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). In a 32-bit float document it works on a layer's linear-light pixels with the same arguments as at 16 bits: clone_stamp copies linear light with no clamp (a colour above white stays above white) in Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Darker Color, Linear Burn, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Pin Light, Difference, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity only; the healing tools (heal_stroke, spot_heal_stroke, patch_region, remove_stroke, content_aware_fill, content_aware_move) match and blend in a display-like working encoding, write linear light back, take Normal blending only and leave every pixel they do not change bit for bit. A mask, channel, colour-plane or Quick Mask target refuses there. Works on a CMYK document's ink: the sample is the ink (current: the layer's; current_and_below / all: the CMYK composite), the clone composites through its blend_mode on 1 − ink, healing and synthesis run on the four inks, and output new_layer adds a CMYK layer. In a Grayscale document it runs on the gray values (R = G = B) at 8, 16 and 32 bits on the layer, or its mask where an RGB document takes one. In a Lab Color document it works on the L*, a* and b* values, each channel alone, at 8 and 16 bits. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `background` | `boolean` | no | — | Return a job_id immediately for job_status/cancel_job (default false waits; Actions always wait). |
| `direction` | `string` | no | one of `source`, `destination` | Which end of the drag is healed (default source: the outlined region is). |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `ignore_adjustments` | `boolean` | no | — | Leave adjustment LAYERS above the target out of the sampled picture (default false). A provable no-op with sample current or current_and_below, which already exclude everything above the target, so it is the meaningful control with sample all: take the texture of the layers stacked above me, but not the grade they are read through. Only an adjustment ENTRY is dropped — a layer style, a Blend If, and a plain raster layer in a tone blend mode are ordinary content and stay in. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `offset_x` | `number` | yes | — | How far the region is dragged, in canvas px (x). |
| `offset_y` | `number` | yes | — | How far the region is dragged, in canvas px (y). |
| `points` | `array<array<number>>` | no | 3–10000 items | [[x, y], …] outlining the region, in canvas px (closed automatically, 3 points or more). Omit to use the current selection. |
| `sample` | `string` | no | one of `current`, `current_and_below`, `all` | WHICH pixels this gesture reads. current is the target layer's own pixels on a transparent canvas, deliberately raw — its opacity, blend mode and mask say how it composites, not what its pixels are. current_and_below is the picture with everything ABOVE the target contributing nothing, which is what keeps a retouch from being graded twice when an adjustment layer sits over it. all is the whole composite. Above excludes the target's own enclosing groups, whose mask, opacity and blend still say how its level meets the picture. Defaults differ by tool and match what that tool always sampled: all for clone_stamp, heal_stroke, patch_region and content_aware_move, current for spot_heal_stroke, remove_stroke and content_aware_fill. The older sample_all_layers boolean still works and still means the same thing (true = all, false = current); sending both is fine when they agree and refused when they contradict, and current_and_below has no boolean spelling at all. Typed clone/heal retain current as their default; all three modes sample authoritative native-depth sources. |
| `sample_all_layers` | `boolean` | no | — | Legacy spelling of sample: true is all, false is current (default true). Kept so every recorded call replays unchanged; prefer sample, which also offers current_and_below. |

## `content_aware_move`

Moves an outlined region of the picture somewhere else and fills where it was — the Content-Aware Move tool. mode "move" (the default) first fills the WHOLE outlined region content-aware, as content_aware_fill does at the automatic ring, then heals the region's original pixels in at (offset_x, offset_y) away, joined to their new surroundings with the Poisson blend patch_region uses, all in one undo step. Outline the object with a little margin: the margin is what the join blends across. The two places may overlap. mode "extend" skips the fill, so the object stays where it was and a blended copy lands at the offset (patch_region with direction destination). Give points for an explicit polygon, or omit them to move the current selection's region. Offsets are rounded to whole pixels. Runs on the shared cancellable worker at 8 and 16 bits and in a 32-bit float document: the call waits by default, and background=true returns a job_id for job_status/cancel_job. A region too large to fill refuses with the limit in the message, in content_aware_fill's words. Layer RGB only: errors on an adjustment layer or a group, and with a mask, colour plane, channel or Quick Mask targeted. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). In a 32-bit float document it works on a layer's linear-light pixels with the same arguments as at 16 bits: clone_stamp copies linear light with no clamp (a colour above white stays above white) in Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Darker Color, Linear Burn, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Pin Light, Difference, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity only; the healing tools (heal_stroke, spot_heal_stroke, patch_region, remove_stroke, content_aware_fill, content_aware_move) match and blend in a display-like working encoding, write linear light back, take Normal blending only and leave every pixel they do not change bit for bit. A mask, channel, colour-plane or Quick Mask target refuses there. Works on a CMYK document's ink: the sample is the ink (current: the layer's; current_and_below / all: the CMYK composite), the clone composites through its blend_mode on 1 − ink, healing and synthesis run on the four inks, and output new_layer adds a CMYK layer. In a Grayscale document it fills from the gray values, R = G = B, at 8, 16 and 32 bits. In a Lab Color document it works on the L*, a* and b* values, each channel alone, at 8 and 16 bits. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

## `content_aware_fill`

Edit > Content-Aware Fill: exact native-depth PatchMatch/Poisson synthesis confined to the selection's soft coverage. source_mask edits source eligibility independently; excluded pixels never supply source texture. Current/current-and-below/all sampling and ignore_adjustments match retouch. output=new_layer preserves original layers and descriptions; partial-alpha backdrops can composite differently. In-place edits rasterize artwork. A selection over 1 MP is filled with its search at reduced scale (1/2 to 4 MP selected, 1/4 to 16 MP, 1/8 to 64 MP): structure larger than about 7 px times that reduction is matched, and finer texture is copied from the picture without being matched to the selection's edge. Limits: selection plus ring 4 MP (16 MP for a selection over 1 MP, 64 MP over 4 MP), one part's box 32 MP, 80 MP of component boxes, 1,000,000 separate parts; a refusal names its limit. background=true returns job_id for job_status/cancel_job. Omitted arguments retain legacy defaults. Or pass only preview_id (and optional document_id) to publish the exact reviewed candidate once, with stale source/target/selection refusal. Layer RGB only; scalar targets and Quick Mask refuse. In a 32-bit float document it works on a layer's linear-light pixels with the same arguments as at 16 bits: clone_stamp copies linear light with no clamp (a colour above white stays above white) in Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Darker Color, Linear Burn, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Pin Light, Difference, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity only; the healing tools (heal_stroke, spot_heal_stroke, patch_region, remove_stroke, content_aware_fill, content_aware_move) match and blend in a display-like working encoding, write linear light back, take Normal blending only and leave every pixel they do not change bit for bit. A mask, channel, colour-plane or Quick Mask target refuses there. Works on a CMYK document's ink: the sample is the ink (current: the layer's; current_and_below / all: the CMYK composite), the clone composites through its blend_mode on 1 − ink, healing and synthesis run on the four inks, and output new_layer adds a CMYK layer. In a Grayscale document it fills from the gray values, R = G = B, at 8, 16 and 32 bits. In a Lab Color document it works on the L*, a* and b* values, each channel alone, at 8 and 16 bits. A Duotone document refuses it for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `background` | `boolean` | no | — | Return job_id immediately; default false waits. Actions wait. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `ignore_adjustments` | `boolean` | no | — | Leave adjustment LAYERS above the target out of the sampled picture (default false). A provable no-op with sample current or current_and_below, which already exclude everything above the target, so it is the meaningful control with sample all: take the texture of the layers stacked above me, but not the grade they are read through. Only an adjustment ENTRY is dropped — a layer style, a Blend If, and a plain raster layer in a tone blend mode are ordinary content and stay in. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `output` | `string` | no | one of `layer`, `new_layer` | layer (default) or new_layer. |
| `preview_id` | `string` | no | — | Publish this exact reviewed result. Only document_id may accompany preview_id. |
| `ring` | `integer` | no | 0–512 | Sampling-ring width in px around the region, 0 = automatic (the default). Clamped to 21-512 — the floor is three patch widths, the narrowest band a source patch can move in, so anything from 1 to 20 comes out as 21 — and then widened from below by the region's own size — a ring narrower than the hole offers too few distinct patches and the fill tiles visibly, so on a large region a small number here is raised to half the region's radius. It is a quality control: pass a wide one for a wide neighbourhood, not for speed. It costs little — rule 2 narrows every part's ring together to fit the work caps before anything runs, and the working windows are sized from the ring that survives that, so on a 1131-part selection a ring of 512 measures 3.8 s against 3.6 s at 21. |
| `sample` | `string` | no | one of `current`, `current_and_below`, `all` | WHICH pixels this gesture reads. current is the target layer's own pixels on a transparent canvas, deliberately raw — its opacity, blend mode and mask say how it composites, not what its pixels are. current_and_below is the picture with everything ABOVE the target contributing nothing, which is what keeps a retouch from being graded twice when an adjustment layer sits over it. all is the whole composite. Above excludes the target's own enclosing groups, whose mask, opacity and blend still say how its level meets the picture. Defaults differ by tool and match what that tool always sampled: all for clone_stamp, heal_stroke, patch_region and content_aware_move, current for spot_heal_stroke, remove_stroke and content_aware_fill. The older sample_all_layers boolean still works and still means the same thing (true = all, false = current); sending both is fine when they agree and refused when they contradict, and current_and_below has no boolean spelling at all. Typed clone/heal retain current as their default; all three modes sample authoritative native-depth sources. |
| `sample_all_layers` | `boolean` | no | — | Legacy alias: true=all, false=current. Must agree with sample when both are supplied. |
| `seed` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | RNG seed (default 0). The fill is reproducible: the same seed over the same pixels gives byte-identical output, and a different one gives a different plausible fill. |
| `source_mask` | `object` | no | no extra properties | Optional source eligibility recipe: {version:1, initial:'all'\|'none', operations:[{op:'include_rect'\|'exclude_rect',x,y,width,height}\|{op:'include_brush'\|'exclude_brush',radius,points:[[x,y],...]}]}. Canvas pixel centers, round connected brush segments, ordered last-write wins. 512 operations, 4096 total points, 64 KiB request and 256M evaluated bounding-box work maximum. Geometry is clipped to the canvas. The selection is independent destination coverage. Omission keeps all ordinary source pixels eligible. |
| `source_mask.initial` | `string` | with parent | one of `all`, `none` | — |
| `source_mask.operations` | `array<object>` | with parent | 0–512 items | — |
| `source_mask.version` | `integer` | with parent | one of `1` | — |

## `red_eye`

Removes flash red inside a rectangle — the Red Eye tool's drag. Pixels are scored by red DOMINANCE (the ratio of red to the average of green and blue, gated by saturation and hue), never a naive R > G test, which every skin tone passes: a specular catchlight scores zero and comes out bit-identical. Drag a tight rectangle over ONE eye. Nothing happens if the rectangle holds no red, to a red region bigger than pupil_size allows, or to one that reaches all four sides of the rectangle — put the rectangle AROUND an eye, not inside something red. In a 32-bit float document the red test and the correction run on the layer's display encoding, so a value above white keeps its light ratio. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). A Grayscale document refuses it: Doctored offers Remove Red Eye on RGB documents only. In a Lab Color document the red test and the correction run on each pixel's 16-bit ProPhoto RGB colour, so a colour outside sRGB is kept, and a pixel left alone keeps its values. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `darken` | `number` | no | 0–100 | How far the corrected pupil darkens once the red is neutralised (0-100, default 50; 0 neutralises only). |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `height` | `number` | yes | 1–100000 | Rectangle height in px. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `pupil_size` | `number` | no | 1–100 | Rejects a red region whose larger side exceeds this percent of the rectangle's SHORTER side (default 100). It exists to spare something bigger than an eye — a red shirt caught by a sloppy rectangle — not to require a small pupil, so 100 is the intended default; turn it down when something red was corrected that should not have been. A red region that reaches all four sides of the rectangle is rejected at any pupil_size: the rectangle is then inside the red, with no pupil in it to find. |
| `width` | `number` | yes | 1–100000 | Rectangle width in px. |
| `x` | `number` | yes | -100000–100000 | Rectangle left, canvas px. |
| `y` | `number` | yes | -100000–100000 | Rectangle top, canvas px. |

## `red_eye_auto`

Removes flash red from every eye in the picture — Filters > Remove Red Eye. Vision's face landmarks locate each face's eyes and the same correction red_eye applies runs on each of them, all in ONE undo step. With no face in the picture it reports that and changes nothing — use red_eye with a rectangle, or pass eyes explicitly; eyes also skips the detector entirely, which is how a drawn or synthetic picture can be corrected. In a 32-bit float document each correction runs on the layer's display encoding, as red_eye's does. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). A Grayscale document refuses it: Doctored offers Remove Red Eye on RGB documents only. In a Lab Color document the red test and the correction run on each pixel's 16-bit ProPhoto RGB colour, so a colour outside sRGB is kept, and a pixel left alone keeps its values; detection reads the Lab view. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `darken` | `number` | no | 0–100 | How far the corrected pupil darkens once the red is neutralised (0-100, default 50; 0 neutralises only). |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `eyes` | `array<object>` | no | 1–64 items | Optional explicit eyes; supplying them skips Vision and corrects exactly these discs. radius is the IRIS radius in canvas px and each eye is scanned over a square six times it, so the eyes together are limited to 100 megapixels of picture — a wrong-unit radius is refused with that number rather than freezing the app. |
| `eyes[].radius` | `number` | with parent | −∞–100000; > 0 | — |
| `eyes[].x` | `number` | with parent | -100000–100000 | — |
| `eyes[].y` | `number` | with parent | -100000–100000 | — |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `pupil_size` | `number` | no | 1–100 | Rejects a red region whose larger side exceeds this percent of the rectangle's SHORTER side (default 100). It exists to spare something bigger than an eye — a red shirt caught by a sloppy rectangle — not to require a small pupil, so 100 is the intended default; turn it down when something red was corrected that should not have been. A red region that reaches all four sides of the rectangle is rejected at any pupil_size: the rectangle is then inside the red, with no pupil in it to find. |

## `blur_stroke`

Softens a layer's pixels where a round-capped stroke along points covers them — the Blur tool. Each covered pixel moves toward the Gaussian blur (sigma 2 px) of the layer's own pixels by coverage × strength; repeat the stroke to build the effect up. Alpha is never changed unless sample_all_layers is on. Respects the active selection. 8-, 16- and 32-bit float documents. In a 32-bit float document it works on the layer's pixels only, in linear light with colour never clamped to 0–1 (the reply's storage is "rgba32_float"): a pixel far above white spreads into its neighbours and lifts them above 1. Errors on an adjustment layer. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). Works on a CMYK document's ink: the tool runs on 1 − ink in two passes, C/M/Y together and K alone (Dodge/Burn's Protect Tones holds the C/M/Y ratios; the Sponge moves C/M/Y and keeps K exactly; the History Brush paints from a CMYK state). In a Grayscale document it runs on the gray values (R = G = B) at 8, 16 and 32 bits on the layer, or its mask where an RGB document takes one. In a Lab Color document it works on the L*, a* and b* values, each channel alone, at 8 and 16 bits. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `airbrush` | `boolean` | no | — | Generate 20 Hz held deposits using the declared sample times/duration. |
| `angle` | `number` | no | -180–180 | Tip rotation in degrees, counter-clockwise (default 0). Visible only when roundness is below 100. |
| `background` | `boolean` | no | — | 16-bit or 32-bit float layer strokes: return a job_id immediately for job_status/cancel_job (default false waits; Actions always wait). Ignored at 8 bits; refused for mask, channel, Quick Mask and adjustment-layer strokes. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `duration` | `number` | no | 0–2499 | Total stroke seconds, including any hold at the final point; defaults to the last time. |
| `flow` | `number` | no | 1–100 | Per-dab deposit in percent (default 100). Below 100 the stroke builds up where it overlaps itself instead of landing at full strength at once. |
| `hardness` | `number` | no | 0–100 | Edge hardness in percent (default 100 = crisp). Below 100 the effect feathers out from hardness% of the radius to the rim. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `native_stroke` | `object` | no | — | Canonical RZBR version1 replay: version=1, encoding=le_f64_xy_diameter_opacity, dabs=base64 little-endian binary64 quadruples, hardness, roundness, angle_degrees, pixel. Mutually exclusive with generation options; recorded automatically. Byte commits and replay share one exact dab rasterizer; at 8 bits historical unversioned points keep their prior meaning. |
| `points` | `array<array<number>>` | yes | 1–10000 items | [[x, y], …] along the stroke, in canvas px. |
| `pressure_opacity` | `boolean` | no | — | Scale each dab deposit by pressure; stroke opacity still applies once. |
| `pressure_size` | `boolean` | no | — | Scale dab size by pressure, with a one-pixel floor. |

A versioned call refuses a size outside its tool's range by name (1–5000 px; 3–200 for heal_stroke and spot_heal_stroke; 1–200 for blur_stroke, sharpen_stroke, smudge_stroke, sponge_stroke and history_brush_stroke; 1–200 for art_history_brush_stroke); an unversioned call clamps it. Maximum 50,000 dabs; oversized strokes refuse by name; no partial stroke. |
| `times` | `array<number>` | no | items: 0–∞ | Elapsed seconds per point, starting at 0 and nondecreasing; used for 20 Hz airbrush deposits. |

## `sharpen_stroke`

Sharpens a layer's pixels under a stroke — the Sharpen tool: an unsharp mask (sigma 1 px, amount 100%) applied by coverage × strength. Alpha is never changed unless sample_all_layers is on. Respects the active selection. 8-, 16- and 32-bit float documents. In a 32-bit float document it works on the layer's pixels only, in linear light with colour never clamped to 0–1 (the reply's storage is "rgba32_float"): an overshoot is kept, so an edge may go below zero or further above white, up to the stored bound of ±65504. Errors on an adjustment layer. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). In a Grayscale document it runs on the gray values (R = G = B) at 8, 16 and 32 bits on the layer, or its mask where an RGB document takes one. In a Lab Color document it works on the L*, a* and b* values, each channel alone, at 8 and 16 bits. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

## `smudge_stroke`

Drags a layer's pixels along a stroke — the Smudge tool. The picture under the tip is carried in the stroke's direction, a fraction strength of the way at every pixel of travel, so the smear is continuous and does not depend on spacing; direction and order of points matter, and a single point moves nothing. Transparent areas smear too (alpha moves with colour) unless the layer's transparency is locked. With sample_all_layers the stroke smears the sampled picture into the layer over its part of the canvas, and a pixel the smear does not move keeps the layer's own. Long strokes with a large tip can exceed the brush work limit and are refused by name: use a shorter stroke or a smaller size. Respects the active selection. 8-, 16- and 32-bit float documents. In a 32-bit float document it works on the layer's pixels only, in linear light with colour never clamped to 0–1 (the reply's storage is "rgba32_float"): values above white are carried along the stroke as they are. Errors on an adjustment layer. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). Works on a CMYK document's ink: the tool runs on 1 − ink in two passes, C/M/Y together and K alone (Dodge/Burn's Protect Tones holds the C/M/Y ratios; the Sponge moves C/M/Y and keeps K exactly; the History Brush paints from a CMYK state). In a Grayscale document it runs on the gray values (R = G = B) at 8, 16 and 32 bits on the layer, or its mask where an RGB document takes one. In a Lab Color document it works on the L*, a* and b* values, each channel alone, at 8 and 16 bits. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

## `sponge_stroke`

Changes colour saturation under a stroke — the Sponge tool and its Mode: desaturate moves each covered pixel toward its Rec. 709 luma, saturate doubles its distance from it (clamped), by coverage × strength; vibrance takes the Vibrance target instead. Alpha is never changed. A mask or alpha channel target refuses at every depth: The Sponge changes saturation, and a mask or alpha channel is one gray plane with none; Dodge and Burn work there. Respects the active selection. 8-, 16- and 32-bit float documents. In a 32-bit float document it works on the layer's pixels only, in linear light with colour never clamped to 0–1 (the reply's storage is "rgba32_float"): the luma and the doubled chroma are taken over linear values, unclamped, and held to ±65504. Errors on an adjustment layer. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). Works on a CMYK document's ink: the tool runs on 1 − ink in two passes, C/M/Y together and K alone (Dodge/Burn's Protect Tones holds the C/M/Y ratios; the Sponge moves C/M/Y and keeps K exactly; the History Brush paints from a CMYK state). In a Grayscale document the Sponge moves gray levels away from (saturate) or toward (desaturate) the middle gray; vibrance changes nothing there. In a Lab Color document the Sponge doubles (saturate) or zeroes (desaturate) a* and b* about 0, keeping L*; vibrance changes nothing. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

## `history_brush_stroke`

Paints a layer back toward what it held in an earlier history state — the History Brush. Under the stroke each pixel mixes (premultiplied, alpha included) toward the same layer's pixel at the same canvas position in that state, by coverage × opacity; where the state's layer held nothing the stroke clears, and the layer never grows. Refuses by name when the state does not hold the layer, or has a different canvas size or bit depth. Never recorded into an Action: a state id names this session's history. Respects the active selection. 8-, 16- and 32-bit float documents. In a 32-bit float document it works on the layer's pixels only, in linear light with colour never clamped to 0–1 (the reply's storage is "rgba32_float"): full coverage at opacity 100 restores the state's exact float samples, above white and below zero included. Errors on an adjustment layer. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). Works on a CMYK document's ink: the tool runs on 1 − ink in two passes, C/M/Y together and K alone (Dodge/Burn's Protect Tones holds the C/M/Y ratios; the Sponge moves C/M/Y and keeps K exactly; the History Brush paints from a CMYK state). In a Grayscale document the state must be from after Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale; an earlier RGB state refuses by name. In a Lab Color document the source state must be a Lab Color state (one from before Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color refuses), and a Lab state paints no other document. On an Indexed Color document the stroke runs on the RGB storage, then each changed pixel takes the palette entry nearest its own new colour: a hard, full-opacity clone copies the source's entries, and a full History Brush stroke restores the earlier state's indices. A Bitmap document: it paints the gray storage back toward the state's layer and runs on the 8-bit gray storage and every pixel goes back white where its gray over white at its own alpha reaches 128, else black, so full coverage gives the state's bits back.
