| `spacing` | `number` | no | 1–200 | Dab spacing as a percent of the brush diameter (default 25). Above 25 the stroke stamps visibly; 150+ reads as a dotted line. |
| `state_id` | `string` | no | — | The history state to paint from: an id from list_history. Default: list_history's brush_source_id, the state the History panel marks as the source, which is the oldest retained state until one is set. |
| `stroke_version` | `integer` | no | one of `1` | Generate canonical resolved dabs from points and optional pressures/times. Byte and 16-bit stroke tools accept this form, including byte mask/plane/channel, pixel and Quick Mask coverage. At 8 bits, omit for the historical point footprint; at 16 bits unversioned points generate the same native dabs (unit pressure, no timing) and refuse by name at the 50,000-dab and 2-billion-work-unit limits; smudge_stroke has its own 256-million-work-unit bound at both depths (it walks the stroke a pixel at a time) and refuses a longer stroke by name. A versioned call refuses a size outside its tool's range by name (1–5000 px; 3–200 for heal_stroke and spot_heal_stroke; 1–200 for blur_stroke, sharpen_stroke, smudge_stroke, sponge_stroke and history_brush_stroke; 1–200 for art_history_brush_stroke); an unversioned call clamps it. Maximum 50,000 dabs; oversized strokes refuse by name; no partial stroke. |
| `times` | `array<number>` | no | items: 0–∞ | Elapsed seconds per point, starting at 0 and nondecreasing; used for 20 Hz airbrush deposits. |

## `art_history_brush_stroke`

Paints a layer from an earlier history state in stylized strokes — the Art History Brush and its options (Mode, Opacity, Style, Area, Tolerance). The first point is a click, then every point at least max(area/2, size) px from the last; each click lays the style's strokes, each starting at a random point of the area and coloured from the state's pixel there, composited through blend_mode at opacity. Seeded: the same seed and stroke give the same pixels. Paints from state_id, by default the History panel's source. Recorded into an Action without state_id, so a replay paints from that document's own source. It runs on 8-bit documents only: 8-bit RGB and 8-bit CMYK (in ink) paint, and a 16-bit, 32-bit or 16-bit CMYK document refuses it by name. A mask, channel or Quick Mask target refuses: The Art History Brush paints a layer's pixels. Respects the active selection. Errors on an adjustment layer. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). Works on an 8-bit CMYK document's ink: the strokes take the source state's ink and composite through blend_mode on 1 − ink. A 16-bit CMYK document refuses it by name. A Grayscale document runs it at 8 bits only (16 refuses), from a Grayscale state, with blend_mode Normal, Darken or Lighten; Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity refuse. In a Lab Color document it runs at 8 bits from a Lab Color state (an RGB state refuses), painting the L*, a* and b* values each channel alone; its strokes follow Lightness, and tolerance compares Lightness, a and b. blend_mode Darken and Lighten are unavailable. A 16-bit Lab document refuses.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `airbrush` | `boolean` | no | — | Generate 20 Hz held deposits using the declared sample times/duration. |
| `angle` | `number` | no | -180–180 | Tip rotation in degrees, counter-clockwise (default 0). Visible only when roundness is below 100. |
| `area` | `number` | no | 0–500 | The disc each click's strokes start in, its diameter in px (0-500, default 50); a larger area lays more strokes. |
| `background` | `boolean` | no | — | 16-bit or 32-bit float layer strokes: return a job_id immediately for job_status/cancel_job (default false waits; Actions always wait). Ignored at 8 bits; refused for mask, channel, Quick Mask and adjustment-layer strokes. |
| `blend_mode` | `string` | no | one of `Normal`, `Darken`, `Lighten`, `Hue`, `Saturation`, `Color`, `Luminosity` | The tool's Mode (default Normal); any other name is refused: blend_mode must be Normal, Darken, Lighten, Hue, Saturation, Color or Luminosity. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `duration` | `number` | no | 0–2499 | Total stroke seconds, including any hold at the final point; defaults to the last time. |
| `flow` | `number` | no | 1–100 | Per-dab deposit in percent (default 100). Below 100 the stroke builds up where it overlaps itself instead of landing at full strength at once. |
| `hardness` | `number` | no | 0–100 | Edge hardness in percent (default 100 = crisp). Below 100 the effect feathers out from hardness% of the radius to the rim. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `native_stroke` | `object` | no | — | Canonical RZBR version1 replay: version=1, encoding=le_f64_xy_diameter_opacity, dabs=base64 little-endian binary64 quadruples, hardness, roundness, angle_degrees, pixel. Mutually exclusive with generation options; recorded automatically. Byte commits and replay share one exact dab rasterizer; at 8 bits historical unversioned points keep their prior meaning. |
| `opacity` | `number` | no | 0–100 | Opacity in percent (0-100, default 100). |
| `points` | `array<array<number>>` | yes | 1–10000 items | [[x, y], …] along the stroke, in canvas px. |
| `pressure_opacity` | `boolean` | no | — | Scale each dab deposit by pressure; stroke opacity still applies once. |
| `pressure_size` | `boolean` | no | — | Scale dab size by pressure, with a one-pixel floor. |
| `pressures` | `array<number>` | no | items: 0–1 | With stroke_version=1, one tablet pressure per point; default 1. |
| `roundness` | `number` | no | 1–100 | Tip roundness in percent (default 100). Below 100 the dab squashes into an ellipse — with angle, a calligraphy nib. |
| `seed` | `integer` | no | 0–4294967295 | The random seed the strokes are drawn from (default 0): the same seed and stroke paint the same pixels. |
| `size` | `number` | no | — | Stroke width in px (1-200, default 24). |
| `spacing` | `number` | no | 1–200 | Dab spacing as a percent of the brush diameter (default 25). Above 25 the stroke stamps visibly; 150+ reads as a dotted line. |
| `state_id` | `string` | no | — | The history state to paint from: an id from list_history. Default: list_history's brush_source_id, the state the History panel marks as the source, which is the oldest retained state until one is set. |
| `stroke_version` | `integer` | no | one of `1` | Generate canonical resolved dabs from points and optional pressures/times. Byte and 16-bit stroke tools accept this form, including byte mask/plane/channel, pixel and Quick Mask coverage. At 8 bits, omit for the historical point footprint; at 16 bits unversioned points generate the same native dabs (unit pressure, no timing) and refuse by name at the 50,000-dab and 2-billion-work-unit limits; smudge_stroke has its own 256-million-work-unit bound at both depths (it walks the stroke a pixel at a time) and refuses a longer stroke by name. A versioned call refuses a size outside its tool's range by name (1–5000 px; 3–200 for heal_stroke and spot_heal_stroke; 1–200 for blur_stroke, sharpen_stroke, smudge_stroke, sponge_stroke and history_brush_stroke; 1–200 for art_history_brush_stroke); an unversioned call clamps it. Maximum 50,000 dabs; oversized strokes refuse by name; no partial stroke. |
| `style` | `string` | no | one of `tight_short`, `tight_medium`, `tight_long`, `loose_medium`, `loose_long`, `dab`, `tight_curl`, `tight_curl_long`, `loose_curl`, `loose_curl_long` | The strokes' shape (default tight_short): every style but dab heads along the source's luminance contours, with the brighter side on its right; tight styles hold their heading closely and their length (±20%), loose ones jitter a little more and vary their length more (±50%); short, medium and long set their length (about 0.5, 1.75 and 3 brush diameters of travel; loose_long 2.25); dab lays single dabs; the curl styles turn as they go, always the same way. |
| `times` | `array<number>` | no | items: 0–∞ | Elapsed seconds per point, starting at 0 and nondecreasing; used for 20 Hz airbrush deposits. |
| `tolerance` | `number` | no | 0–100 | In percent (0-100, default 0): a stroke starts only where the source state differs from the layer by at least this much (the largest channel difference, premultiplied), so 100 on an unchanged layer paints nothing. |

## `liquify`

Reshapes a layer's pixels with brush strokes — Filters ▸ Liquify…. The strokes run in order on one displacement field and the layer is resampled once (bicubic), as one undo step. Each stroke is {tool, points, size, strength, density} with points in CANVAS px. Tools: forward_warp pushes the picture along the stroke's direction; pucker pulls it toward the brush centre and bloat pushes it away; twirl_clockwise and twirl_counterclockwise turn it about the centre; reconstruct moves the field back toward the unwarped picture; freeze protects what it paints from every later stroke of this call and thaw removes that protection. Every tool but forward_warp works per dab, so a single point acts once and repeated points build the effect; forward_warp needs at least two different points. Limits: 1-2048 strokes, 1-8192 points a stroke, 131,072 points in all, and 1 billion field updates in all, past which the call is refused by name (use fewer or shorter strokes or a smaller brush). Unknown keys are refused, at the top level and in a stroke. Only the layer's own raster is rewritten: it does not grow, a sample taken past its edge repeats the edge pixel, and points outside it are allowed. Writes only inside the active selection. Strokes that move nothing answer changed: false and add no undo step. The reply carries strokes, the count that ran, and at 16 and 32 bits storage. 8-, 16- and 32-bit float documents: a float layer is resampled in linear light with each colour clamped to the range its visible pixels hold (not to 0 to 1), on the layer's own pixels only. Errors on a group or an adjustment layer. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document it runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. A Bitmap document: the warp runs on the 8-bit gray storage and every pixel goes back white where its gray over white at its own alpha reaches 128, else black.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `strokes` | `array<object>` | yes | 1–2048 items | The strokes, applied in order. |
| `strokes[].density` | `number` | no | 0–100 | How much of the brush radius acts at full strength before the falloff to its rim, in percent (0-100, default 50). |
| `strokes[].points` | `array<array<number>>` | with parent | 1–8192 items | [[x, y], …] along the stroke, in canvas px, each within ±1,000,000. Two equal consecutive points are a dwell: one more dab in place. |
| `strokes[].size` | `number` | with parent | 1–5000 | Brush diameter in px (1-5000). |
| `strokes[].strength` | `number` | no | 0–100 | How far each dab acts, in percent (0-100, default 50): the workspace's Pressure. |
| `strokes[].tool` | `string` | with parent | one of `forward_warp`, `reconstruct`, `twirl_clockwise`, `twirl_counterclockwise`, `pucker`, `bloat`, `freeze`, `thaw` | — |

## `depth_blur`

Blurs a layer by depth — the app's Filter ▸ Neural Filters ▸ Depth Blur…. A local depth model (Depth Anything V2 Small, Core ML) estimates the depth of the layer, or of the active selection's bounding box on it, and pixels away from the focus are blurred with a lens disc whose radius grows with their distance from the focal plane. The focus is the subject (focus_subject, Vision's subject mask, the default), a focal point (focal_x, focal_y in canvas px, which turns focus_subject off unless it is given), or focal_distance. focal_range keeps a band of depth sharp; haze lightens far pixels; warmth, brightness and saturation grade the result; grain adds film grain; depth_map_only writes the depth map as grey (near is white) instead. output new_layer writes a copy of the layer above it, named "<name> Depth Blur". One undo step; writes only inside the active selection. The reply carries changed, output_layer, focal_distance_used (the focus in percent) and the model's id and version. 8-, 16- and 32-bit documents: a float layer is blurred in linear light. Refused by name when the model is not installed (the user downloads it in Settings ▸ Models; downloads stay a user action, because they fetch tens of MB from a third-party host under a licence the user must accept), on an empty layer, and when Vision finds no subject for focus_subject. A re-editable text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good. A Duotone document refuses it for good. A Bitmap document: not available in Bitmap mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `blur_strength` | `number` | no | 0–100 | How strong the blur is (0 to 100, default 50). |
| `brightness` | `number` | no | -50–50 | Brightens or darkens the result (-50 to 50, default 0). |
| `depth_map_only` | `boolean` | no | — | Write the depth map instead (default false). |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `focal_distance` | `number` | no | 0–100 | The focal depth when there is no subject or point, 0 nearest (0 to 100, default 0). |
| `focal_range` | `number` | no | 0–100 | The band of depth around the focus kept sharp (0 to 100, default 20). |
| `focal_x` | `number` | no | — | Focal point x in canvas px (with focal_y). |
| `focal_y` | `number` | no | — | Focal point y in canvas px (with focal_x). |
| `focus_subject` | `boolean` | no | — | Keep Vision's subject in focus (default true without a focal point). |
| `grain` | `number` | no | 0–100 | Film grain amount (0 to 100, default 0). |
| `haze` | `number` | no | 0–100 | Lightens pixels by their depth (0 to 100, default 0). |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `output` | `string` | no | one of `layer`, `new_layer` | The layer itself (default) or a new layer above it. |
| `saturation` | `number` | no | -50–50 | Saturates or desaturates the result (-50 to 50, default 0). |
| `warmth` | `number` | no | -50–50 | Warms (positive) or cools the result (-50 to 50, default 0). |

## `list_models`

Lists the local models of Settings ▸ Models with their state (not_downloaded, downloading with progress 0 to 1, ready, failed with failure), bytes on disk, whether the user accepted the licence of this version, the licence (name, url, tier) and the training-data note. Read only: downloading is a user action in Settings ▸ Models, because it fetches tens of MB from a third-party host under a licence the user must accept.

Takes no arguments.

## `super_zoom`

Enlarges a layer into a NEW document — the app's Filter ▸ Neural Filters ▸ Super Zoom…. The layer's pixels on its canvas are zoomed 2x or 4x (zoom) by a local super-resolution model (Real-ESRGAN x4plus, Core ML) run tile by tile and stitched seamlessly; enhance_details false uses a classical Catmull-Rom resample instead. remove_jpeg_artifacts runs the JPEG artifacts model (FBCNN, Medium) on the source first. noise_reduction (Reduce Noise on the source) and sharpen (Unsharp Mask on the result) are classical. The new document has one layer, "Background", the source's profile and resolution, and the title "<name> Super Zoom ×N"; the source is not changed and the selection is ignored. The reply carries the new document_id, its width and height, the zoom, tiles, planned_bytes and the models used. 8- and 16-bit RGB documents; 32-bit and CMYK documents are refused by name. A result past 100 megapixels is refused by its size (choose a smaller zoom). Refused by name when a needed model is not installed (the user downloads it in Settings ▸ Models: Real-ESRGAN always, FBCNN for remove_jpeg_artifacts). In an 8- or 16-bit Grayscale document the model reads the gray values and its result is folded to its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule (Super Zoom's new document is Grayscale in the same Gray profile); a 32-bit Grayscale document refuses, as a float document. In a Lab Color document the model reads the layer's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows) and its result returns to L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, on the 8-bit grid at 8 bits; a new document is Lab Color at the source's depth. A Duotone document refuses it for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `enhance_details` | `boolean` | no | — | Run the super-resolution model (default true); false resamples. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `noise_reduction` | `number` | no | 0–100 | Noise reduction on the source (0 to 100, default 0). |
| `remove_jpeg_artifacts` | `boolean` | no | — | Remove JPEG artifacts from the source first (default false). |
| `sharpen` | `number` | no | 0–100 | Sharpening of the result (0 to 100, default 0). |
| `zoom` | `integer` | no | one of `2`, `4` | The enlargement: 2 (default) or 4. |

## `jpeg_artifacts_removal`

Removes JPEG compression artifacts (blocking, ringing) from a layer — the app's Filter ▸ Neural Filters ▸ JPEG Artifacts Removal…. A local model (FBCNN colour, Core ML) runs tile by tile over the layer's own pixels; strength low, medium (default) or high is the model's quality factor 70, 40 or 10. output layer (default) rewrites the layer; new_layer writes the result to a new layer "<name> JPEG Artifacts Removal" directly above it. Alpha is kept exactly; the selection is ignored. One undo step. The reply carries changed, output_layer, strength, quality_factor, tiles, planned_bytes and the model. 8- and 16-bit RGB documents; 32-bit and CMYK documents are refused by name. Refused by name when the model is not installed (the user downloads FBCNN in Settings ▸ Models). A re-editable text or shape layer drops its description with output layer (undo restores it). In an 8- or 16-bit Grayscale document the model reads the gray values and its result is folded to its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule (Super Zoom's new document is Grayscale in the same Gray profile); a 32-bit Grayscale document refuses, as a float document. In a Lab Color document the model reads the layer's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows) and its result returns to L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, on the 8-bit grid at 8 bits. A Duotone document refuses it for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `output` | `string` | no | one of `layer`, `new_layer` | The layer itself (default) or a new layer above it. |
| `strength` | `string` | no | one of `low`, `medium`, `high` | low, medium (default) or high. |

## `neural_colorize`

Colors a layer from its luminance — the app's Filter ▸ Neural Filters ▸ Colorize…. A local model (DDColor, Core ML) predicts the colour (Lab a*, b*) from the layer's lightness once at 512²; the colour is upscaled onto the layer's own full-resolution lightness in the document's profile, so luminance and detail are kept exactly and only chroma is added (colours past the profile's gamut lose chroma, never hue or lightness). The classical sliders: saturation scales the colour (-50 gray, +50 double); cyan_red, magenta_green and yellow_blue push it towards red, green or blue (positive) or cyan, magenta or yellow (negative); color_artifact_reduction blurs the predicted colour to remove blotches. output layer (default) rewrites the layer, new_layer writes a new layer "<name> Colorize" directly above it (one undo step either way), new_document opens the layer's canvas colorized as a NEW document "<name> Colorize" (the reply carries its document_id, width and height). Alpha is kept exactly; the selection is ignored. The reply carries changed, output, planned_bytes and the model, plus layer and output_layer for the layer outputs. 8- and 16-bit RGB documents; 32-bit and CMYK documents are refused by name. Refused by name when the model is not installed (the user downloads DDColor in Settings ▸ Models). A re-editable text or shape layer drops its description with output layer (undo restores it). A Grayscale document refuses it for good: a Grayscale layer holds no colour. Convert to RGB Color first. In a Lab Color document the model reads the layer's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows) and its result returns to L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, on the 8-bit grid at 8 bits; a new document is Lab Color at the source's depth. A Duotone document refuses it for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `color_artifact_reduction` | `number` | no | 0–100 | Smoothing of the predicted colour (0 to 100, default 0). |
| `cyan_red` | `number` | no | -50–50 | Cyan (negative) to red (positive) (-50 to 50, default 0). |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `magenta_green` | `number` | no | -50–50 | Magenta (negative) to green (positive) (-50 to 50, default 0). |
| `output` | `string` | no | one of `layer`, `new_layer`, `new_document` | The layer itself (default), a new layer above it, or a new document. |
| `saturation` | `number` | no | -50–50 | Colour saturation (-50 to 50, default 0). |
| `yellow_blue` | `number` | no | -50–50 | Yellow (negative) to blue (positive) (-50 to 50, default 0). |

## `sky_replacement`

Replaces the sky of a raster layer — the app's Edit ▸ Sky Replacement…. The local sky model (Select ▸ Sky's) finds the sky of the document; shift_edge grows (positive) or shrinks the mask and fade_edge softens it. The new sky is a library sky or one of the user's own skies (sky: an id or name from list_skies), or an image file (sky_path); brightness and temperature adjust it, scale, offset_x and offset_y (canvas fractions, -1 to 1) and flip place it. The foreground is harmonized toward the sky: lighting_mode (multiply or screen) with lighting, color_adjustment and edge_lighting (the sky's light spilling over the horizon). output new_layers (the default) adds an editable Pass Through group "Sky Replacement Group" above the layer holding, bottom first, "Foreground Edge" (only with decontaminate: the edge's decontaminated colour, masked to the edge), "Foreground Color" and "Foreground Lighting" Curves adjustment layers (the lighting one in lighting_mode's blend mode) and the masked "Sky" layer; decontaminate removes the old sky's colour from the horizon's edge in either output; output duplicate_layer adds ONE flattened layer named "Sky Replacement" directly above the layer. The output entry becomes active; the layer itself is not changed. One undo step. The reply carries changed, output, decontaminate, output_layer (the group or the new layer), the sky used (kind library, user or file), the model's id and version, sky_share (the share of the canvas the model found sky) and planned_bytes. 8- and 16-bit RGB documents only. Refused by name when the sky model or the sky library is not installed (the user downloads them in Settings ▸ Models), for a group or adjustment layer, an unknown sky, and when the model finds no sky. A Grayscale document refuses it for good: Doctored offers Sky Replacement on RGB documents only. A Lab Color document refuses it for good: Doctored offers Sky Replacement on RGB documents only.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `brightness` | `number` | no | -100–100 | Brightens or darkens the sky (-100 to 100, default 0). |
| `color_adjustment` | `number` | no | 0–100 | How strongly the sky's colour is carried into the foreground (0 to 100, default 50). |
| `decontaminate` | `boolean` | no | — | Removes the old sky's colour from the horizon's edge pixels (default false; the dialog's checkbox is on by default). With output new_layers it adds a "Foreground Edge" raster layer, masked to the edge, at the bottom of the group. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `edge_lighting` | `number` | no | 0–100 | The sky's light spilling over the foreground along the horizon (0 to 100, default 0). |
| `fade_edge` | `number` | no | 0–100 | Softens the mask's edge (0 to 100, default 3). |
| `flip` | `boolean` | no | — | Mirror the sky horizontally (default false). |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `lighting` | `number` | no | 0–100 | How strongly the sky's light tints the foreground (0 to 100, default 50). |
| `lighting_mode` | `string` | no | one of `multiply`, `screen` | How the sky's light blends into the foreground (default multiply). |
| `offset_x` | `number` | no | -1–1 | Moves the sky right by this fraction of the canvas width (default 0). |
| `offset_y` | `number` | no | -1–1 | Moves the sky down by this fraction of the canvas height (default 0). |
| `output` | `string` | no | one of `new_layers`, `duplicate_layer` | Where the result goes: new_layers, the editable Sky Replacement Group (default), or duplicate_layer, one new flattened layer. |
| `scale` | `number` | no | 25–400 | The sky's size in percent of the size that covers the canvas (25 to 400, default 100). |
| `shift_edge` | `number` | no | -100–100 | Grows (positive) or shrinks the sky mask (-100 to 100, default 0). |
| `sky` | `string` | no | — | A library sky id or the name of one of the user's skies (list_skies). |
| `sky_path` | `string` | no | — | An image file to use as the sky, instead of sky. |
| `temperature` | `number` | no | -100–100 | Warms (positive) or cools the sky (-100 to 100, default 0). |

## `list_skies`

Lists the skies Edit ▸ Sky Replacement… offers: the sky library's state (not_downloaded, downloading, ready or failed) and version, its skies (id, name, category blue, sunset, dramatic or night, source_url and license; empty until the library is downloaded in Settings ▸ Models) and the user's own skies (name, width, height), added from files in the dialog. Read only.

Takes no arguments.

## `generative_fill`

Fills the current selection from a cloud image model — the app's Edit ▸ Generative Fill…. The area around the selection (a crop twice its size on each axis where the canvas allows, at the aspect of the provider's native size nearest the selection's, never past the canvas) and the selection itself are sent with prompt (empty or absent: fill from the surrounding picture) to provider (openai, the default: OpenAI's image edit API; gemini: Google's Gemini image model, one request a variation; fal: fal's FLUX.1 Fill [pro], one request a variation) with the USER'S OWN API key, and each call is billed to that key. variations (1–3, default 3) pictures are asked for. The first lands on a NEW layer directly above layer (any layer kind; default the active layer), named after the prompt (else "Generative Layer N"), masked by the selection and tagged as generated; every picture is kept on the layer as its variations (saved in .doctored) to switch with select_generative_variation. Pixels outside the selection do not change. The new layer becomes active. One undo step; one job with progress that can be cancelled. Refused before anything is sent unless the user turned on “Allow MCP agents to use cloud tools” in Settings ▸ Cloud (off by default), accepted the provider's terms and saved a key there; refused with no selection, under Quick Mask and with a mask, colour plane or channel targeted. A provider's refusal (a bad key, a content policy) is answered with its own message and adds no layer. Reply: {ok, changed, output_layer, provider, model, native_size: [w, h], crop: [x, y, w, h] (the canvas area sent), planned_bytes, prompt (the prompt sent), variations (how many the layer keeps), selected_variation, variations_requested (the count asked for), variations_received (the pictures that came this run), short_reason (only when fewer came than asked: the provider's own sentence)}. 8- and 16-bit RGB and 8-bit CMYK documents (32 bits and 16-bit CMYK are refused). Not recorded into Actions: replaying it would bill the key again. In an 8- or 16-bit Grayscale document the provider sees the gray composite and every picture lands folded to its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule, R = G = B; a 32-bit Grayscale document refuses, as a float document. In a Lab Color document the provider sees the composite's Display P3 view and every picture lands as L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, on the 8-bit grid at 8 bits.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `prompt` | `string` | no | — | What to generate in the selection; empty fills from the surroundings. |
| `provider` | `string` | no | one of `openai`, `gemini`, `fal` | The cloud provider (default openai). |
| `variations` | `integer` | no | 1–3 | How many pictures to ask for (default 3). |

## `generative_expand`

Fills the area the picture leaves transparent from a cloud image model — the app's Edit ▸ Generative Expand…. Every pixel the composite leaves not fully opaque is filled, with coverage 1 − its alpha; add that area first with canvas_size (grow the canvas, the picture placed where it should stay) or with crop past the canvas (a rectangle beyond its edges, delete_cropped false so the new area stays transparent). crop with fill: "generative_expand" does both as one undo step, the Crop tool's Fill popup. The shared selection is ignored and not changed. The crop around that area is sent exactly as generative_fill sends one, with prompt (empty or absent: continue the picture) to provider (openai, gemini or fal) with the USER'S OWN API key, billed to it; variations (1–3, default 3). The first answer lands on a NEW layer directly above layer (default the active layer) masked to that area, so the pixels the picture already covers do not change; every answer is kept as its variations. One undo step; one job. Gated exactly as generative_fill. Refused when nothing is transparent ("the picture has no transparent area to expand into: enlarge the canvas first"), under Quick Mask and with a mask, colour plane or channel targeted. Reply: generative_fill's. 8- and 16-bit RGB and 8-bit CMYK documents (32-bit and 16-bit CMYK are refused). Not recorded into Actions. In an 8- or 16-bit Grayscale document the provider sees the gray composite and every picture lands folded to its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule, R = G = B; a 32-bit Grayscale document refuses, as a float document. In a Lab Color document the provider sees the composite's Display P3 view and every picture lands as L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, on the 8-bit grid at 8 bits. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `prompt` | `string` | no | — | What to add in the transparent area; empty continues the picture. |
| `provider` | `string` | no | one of `openai`, `gemini`, `fal` | The cloud provider (default openai). |
| `variations` | `integer` | no | 1–3 | How many pictures to ask for (default 3). |

## `generative_variations`

Reports a Generative Layer's kept variations, as the app's Layer ▸ Generative Variations… shows "Variation k of N". layer defaults to the active layer. Reply: {ok, layer, count, selected (0-based), native_size: [w, h], crop: [x, y, w, h], prompt (the selected variation's)}. A layer whose pixels or position were edited since (a paint, a filter, a move, a transform, Convert or Assign Profile), or whose mask was deleted or moved, has dropped its variations (a mask edit keeps them) and is refused ("generative layer N holds no variations"). Sends nothing. In an 8- or 16-bit Grayscale document the provider sees the gray composite and every picture lands folded to its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule, R = G = B; a 32-bit Grayscale document refuses, as a float document. In a Lab Color document the provider sees the composite's Display P3 view and every picture lands as L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, on the 8-bit grid at 8 bits. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |

## `select_generative_variation`

Switches a Generative Layer to its kept variation index (0-based), as the app's Layer ▸ Generative Variations… Previous / Next: the layer is re-rendered from that picture inside the area the fill covered, its mask is kept and its tag becomes that picture's. One undo step; selecting the current one changes nothing (changed false). Refused for a layer holding no variations, an index out of range and a pixel lock. Sends nothing. Reply: {ok, changed, layer, selected, count}. In an 8- or 16-bit Grayscale document the provider sees the gray composite and every picture lands folded to its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule, R = G = B; a 32-bit Grayscale document refuses, as a float document. In a Lab Color document the provider sees the composite's Display P3 view and every picture lands as L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, on the 8-bit grid at 8 bits. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |

## `generate_variations`

Asks the provider for a NEW set of variations of a Generative Layer, as the app's Layer ▸ Generative Variations… ▸ Generate: the same area the fill sent (the picture with that layer hidden, its own mask as the selection) with prompt (default the selected variation's) to provider (default the one that made it), variations (1–3, default 3) pictures, with the USER'S OWN API key, billed to it. They are appended to the layer's variations (24 at most) and the first new one is selected. Gated exactly as generative_fill. One undo step. Reply: generative_fill's. In an 8- or 16-bit Grayscale document the provider sees the gray composite and every picture lands folded to its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule, R = G = B; a 32-bit Grayscale document refuses, as a float document. In a Lab Color document the provider sees the composite's Display P3 view and every picture lands as L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, on the 8-bit grid at 8 bits. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |

## `select_sky`

Select the sky — the app's Select ▸ Sky. A sky segmentation model (U²-Net small, Core ML) gives a soft matte over the whole image. Refuses "No sky was found in this image." when less than 0.2% of it is sky. The reply adds sky_share, the share of the canvas the model covered at half or more. The model reads the document's composite (at 16 and 32 bits its display-encoded copy, as Vision does) and its low-resolution mask becomes 16-bit coverage, refined against the picture by Select and Mask's edge stage with Smart Radius. One selection Undo; pixels unchanged; refine: false skips the edge stage and keeps the model's own matte. The reply carries ok, bounds, selection_empty and the model's id and version. Refused by name when the model is not installed (the user downloads it in Settings ▸ Models; downloads stay a user action). A Grayscale document is read through its view, R = G = B, as the model sees an RGB document. In a Lab Color document the model reads the document's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows); the selection is colour-free coverage. A Duotone document refuses it for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `feather` | `number` | no | 0–250 | Feather radius in pixels (0 to 250, default 0). |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | How the new shape combines with the current selection (default replace). add unions, subtract removes the new shape from the current selection, intersect keeps the overlap; an empty result clears the selection. |
| `refine` | `boolean` | no | — | Refine the model's matte against the picture's edges (default true). |

## `select_person_parts`

Select parts of people — hair, face_skin (facial skin), body_skin and clothes — from MediaPipe's multiclass selfie segmenter, as the app's Select ▸ Person Parts…. people chooses 1-based person numbers from inspect_subjects model "people" (left to right); omit it for everyone. Each person is read on their own box and clipped to their own coverage. When Vision cannot separate a crowd, omitting people reads everyone at once (person_count 0); naming people then refuses. Refuses "No people were found in this image." and "None of the chosen parts was found on the chosen people." The reply adds parts and person_count. The model reads the document's composite (at 16 and 32 bits its display-encoded copy, as Vision does) and its low-resolution mask becomes 16-bit coverage, refined against the picture by Select and Mask's edge stage with Smart Radius. One selection Undo; pixels unchanged; refine: false skips the edge stage and keeps the model's own matte. The reply carries ok, bounds, selection_empty and the model's id and version. Refused by name when the model is not installed (the user downloads it in Settings ▸ Models; downloads stay a user action). A Grayscale document is read through its view, R = G = B, as the model sees an RGB document. In a Lab Color document the model reads the document's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows); the selection is colour-free coverage. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

## `object_finder_select`

Select an object from a prompt with Segment Anything 2.1 (Core ML; Large when downloaded, else Tiny), as the Object Selection tool's Object Finder: points are clicks in canvas pixels, include true (the default) for the object and false to exclude a part of it; box is a dragged rectangle around it. Give points, a box or both, at most 14 prompt tokens (a box counts two). A new prompt combines with the selection by mode after feather. continue: true refines the selection the previous object_finder_select made (still the current selection): points and box are then the WHOLE prompt (the earlier points plus the new ones), the result replaces that step's, and mode and feather come from the prompt being continued, so passing them refuses. continue without such a selection refuses "continue needs the selection the previous object_finder_select made." Refuses "No object was found at the prompt." The reply adds score (the decoder's own quality estimate) and continued. The model reads the document's composite (at 16 and 32 bits its display-encoded copy, as Vision does) and its low-resolution mask becomes 16-bit coverage, refined against the picture by Select and Mask's edge stage with Smart Radius. One selection Undo; pixels unchanged; refine: false skips the edge stage and keeps the model's own matte. The reply carries ok, bounds, selection_empty and the model's id and version. Refused by name when the model is not installed (the user downloads it in Settings ▸ Models; downloads stay a user action). A Grayscale document is read through its view, R = G = B, as the model sees an RGB document. In a Lab Color document the model reads the document's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows); the selection is colour-free coverage. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `box` | `object` | no | — | — |
| `box.height` | `number` | with parent | — | — |
| `box.width` | `number` | with parent | — | — |
| `box.x` | `number` | with parent | — | — |
| `box.y` | `number` | with parent | — | — |
| `continue` | `boolean` | no | — | Refine the previous object_finder_select's prompt (default false). |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `feather` | `number` | no | 0–250 | Feather radius in pixels (0 to 250, default 0). |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | How the new shape combines with the current selection (default replace). add unions, subtract removes the new shape from the current selection, intersect keeps the overlap; an empty result clears the selection. |
| `points` | `array<object>` | no | 0–14 items | — |
| `points[].include` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `points[].x` | `number` | with parent | — | — |
| `points[].y` | `number` | with parent | — | — |
| `refine` | `boolean` | no | — | Refine the model's matte against the picture's edges (default true). |

## `add_text`

Rasterizes text onto a layer's pixels — the characters become pixels and cannot be changed afterwards, so prefer add_text_layer when the text may need editing. x,y is the TOP-LEFT corner of the text block; long lines wrap at the canvas edge and \n starts a new line. Returns the rendered text size so you can position follow-ups.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `color` | `string` | no | — | Hex color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA (default #000000). |
| `color_space` | `string` | no | one of `srgb`, `document`, `display_p3` | 8-bit documents: how the color hex is read. Default srgb (authored sRGB); document: the hex IS the document's own bytes (sample_color's hex); display_p3: a Display P3 hex. add_text is unavailable at 16 bits and float. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `font` | `string` | no | — | Font family or PostScript name (default: system font). |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `size` | `number` | no | — | Font size in px (4-1000, default 48). |
| `text` | `string` | yes | — | — |
| `x` | `number` | yes | — | — |
| `y` | `number` | yes | — | — |

## `add_text_layer`

Adds a RE-EDITABLE text layer above the active layer and selects it. The layer remembers the string, font, size, color, alignment, typography (weight, italic, tracking, leading, baseline shift, underline, strikethrough), wrap width and transform it was rendered from (get_document reports them, edit_text_layer changes them, transform_layer composes onto them, and they survive saving to .doctored), unlike add_text which just bakes characters into pixels. x,y is the TOP-LEFT corner of the text block in canvas px (its origin in get_document; rounded to whole px for an untransformed block, kept exact under a transform), positioned exactly like add_text; \n starts a new line and long lines wrap at wrap_width. Returns the new layer's index and bounds. NOTE: painting on the layer afterwards (brush, eraser, fill, gradient, add_text, apply_filter) drops the text and leaves plain pixels. In a 32-bit float document colours are the document's own linear-light numbers (#2E80C8 is 46/255 linear); red, green and blue may be above white, 0–65504, and alpha stays 0–1 (8/16-bit documents keep 0–1). A layer pasted into or converted out of 32 bits has its numbers rewritten so it looks the same; converting to 16 or 8 bits clips each channel at 1. get_document reports `ink`. Optional `layer` (anchor, default the active layer) and `position` (`above` the anchor, `top` of the root level, or `into_group` for a group anchor, default `above`) choose where it lands; the reply reports the `position` used. In 16-bit mode this creates editable retained artwork at the slot position names, exactly as at 8 bits. Authored colors and generated vector area coverage remain native; intrinsic bitmap glyph assets retain their disclosed byte precision. Works on a CMYK document: the layer's colours are stored as ink in the document's profile — pass ink (fill_ink, stroke_ink, a run's or a stop's ink) as C, M, Y, K percent for exact ink, or a colour, which separates through the profile (relative colorimetric with BPC); an edit that passes no colour keeps each ink exactly, and the reply reports the ink in percent beside the appearance hex. In a Grayscale document every colour — a run's, a stop's, a custom pattern's texels — is stored as its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule and renders R = G = B; get_document reports the gray; ink refuses. In a Lab Color document the colours stay authored sRGB (pass color; ink refuses) and render as L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule (a pattern's tile too, texel by texel; a gradient between its converted stops), an 8-bit layer on the ×257 grid; Image ▸ Mode conversions re-render the layer in the new mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `alignment` | `string` | no | one of `left`, `center`, `right` | How lines align within the text block (default left). The block stays anchored at x,y — only the lines inside it shift, so single-line text looks the same for all three values. |
| `baseline_shift` | `number` | no | -100–100 | Baseline shift in px, -100 to 100, positive raises the text, default 0 — the options bar's Baseline field. |
| `color` | `string` | no | — | Hex color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA (default #000000). |
| `color_runs` | `array<object>` | no | 0–64 items | Sorted nonoverlapping {location,length,rgba} UTF-16 complete-character ranges; [] clears runs. In a CMYK document a run may pass ink (C, M, Y, K percent) for rgba. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `font` | `string` | no | — | Installed font FAMILY name, e.g. "Helvetica Neue" or "Times New Roman" (not a PostScript face name). Default: the text tool's own default family. |
| `ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items; items: 0–100 | CMYK document only: the text colour as ink, C, M, Y, K in percent 0–100, stored exactly (a colour argument instead separates through the document's profile; its alpha still applies). Replies report ink beside the appearance hex. An RGB document refuses it. |
| `italic` | `boolean` | no | — | Italic face (default false). |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Anchor layer index (default: the active layer). A group is a legal anchor. |
| `leading` | `number` | no | 0–1000 | Line height in px, 0 to 1000; 0 (default) = the font's natural height — the options bar's Leading field. |
| `position` | `string` | no | one of `above`, `top`, `into_group` | Where the new layer lands relative to `layer`: above it (default), at the top of the root level, or as the top child of a group. |
| `rgba` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | Continuous normalized sRGB, alternative to color, preserved at both depths. sample_color's srgb_rgba is this spelling of a sampled pixel. |
| `size` | `number` | no | — | Font size in px (4-1000, default 48). |
| `strikethrough` | `boolean` | no | — | Single strikethrough (default false). |
| `text` | `string` | yes | — | — |
| `tracking` | `number` | no | -100–100 | Extra spacing between glyphs in px (kern), -100 to 100, default 0 — the options bar's Tracking field. |
| `transform` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | The layer's 2×2 linear map [a, b, c, d], row-major — (x, y) maps to (a·x + b·y, c·x + d·y) — applied to the text before it is placed at x,y; default [1, 0, 0, 1]. Rotation by θ clockwise is [cos θ, -sin θ, sin θ, cos θ]. transform_layer composes onto it; get_document reports it. |
| `underline` | `boolean` | no | — | Single underline (default false). |
| `weight` | `integer` | no | 0–15 | NSFontManager weight 0-15: 3 light, 5 regular (default), 6 medium, 8 semibold, 9 bold — the options bar's Weight popup. |
| `wrap_width` | `number` | no | — | px; the block wraps at this SOURCE-space width and remembers it (box_width); 0 = point text that never wraps (at most 100000 px, the app's own editor cap). Default: from x to the canvas's right edge. |
| `x` | `number` | yes | — | — |
| `y` | `number` | yes | — | — |

## `edit_text_layer`

Re-renders a text layer made by add_text_layer (or by the app's text tool) from changed parameters: pass any subset of text, font, size, color, alignment, weight, italic, underline, strikethrough, tracking, leading, baseline_shift, wrap_width and transform, and everything you omit keeps the layer's current value. The layer keeps its position (the block is re-laid-out from its origin, keeping its transform unless you pass one, so the bounds follow the new text), its opacity, blend mode, mask, style and stacking. Errors when the target layer is not a text layer — add_text_layer makes one. Returns the resulting bounds and the layer's full text object. In a 32-bit float document colours are the document's own linear-light numbers (#2E80C8 is 46/255 linear); red, green and blue may be above white, 0–65504, and alpha stays 0–1 (8/16-bit documents keep 0–1). A layer pasted into or converted out of 32 bits has its numbers rewritten so it looks the same; converting to 16 or 8 bits clips each channel at 1. get_document reports `ink`. Works on a CMYK document: the layer's colours are stored as ink in the document's profile — pass ink (fill_ink, stroke_ink, a run's or a stop's ink) as C, M, Y, K percent for exact ink, or a colour, which separates through the profile (relative colorimetric with BPC); an edit that passes no colour keeps each ink exactly, and the reply reports the ink in percent beside the appearance hex. In a Grayscale document every colour — a run's, a stop's, a custom pattern's texels — is stored as its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule and renders R = G = B; get_document reports the gray; ink refuses. In a Lab Color document the colours stay authored sRGB (pass color; ink refuses) and render as L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule (a pattern's tile too, texel by texel; a gradient between its converted stops), an 8-bit layer on the ×257 grid; Image ▸ Mode conversions re-render the layer in the new mode. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `alignment` | `string` | no | one of `left`, `center`, `right` | How lines align within the text block; omit to keep the layer's current alignment. |
| `baseline_shift` | `number` | no | -100–100 | Baseline shift in px, -100 to 100, positive raises the text, default 0 — the options bar's Baseline field. |
| `color` | `string` | no | — | Hex color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA. |
| `color_runs` | `array<object>` | no | 0–64 items | Sorted nonoverlapping {location,length,rgba} UTF-16 complete-character ranges; [] clears runs. In a CMYK document a run may pass ink (C, M, Y, K percent) for rgba. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `font` | `string` | no | — | Installed font FAMILY name (not a PostScript face name). |
| `ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items; items: 0–100 | CMYK document only: the text colour as ink, C, M, Y, K in percent 0–100, stored exactly (a colour argument instead separates through the document's profile; its alpha still applies). Replies report ink beside the appearance hex. An RGB document refuses it. |
| `italic` | `boolean` | no | — | Italic face (default false). |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `leading` | `number` | no | 0–1000 | Line height in px, 0 to 1000; 0 (default) = the font's natural height — the options bar's Leading field. |
| `rgba` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | Continuous normalized sRGB, alternative to color, preserved at both depths. sample_color's srgb_rgba is this spelling of a sampled pixel. |
| `size` | `number` | no | — | Font size in px (4-1000). |
| `strikethrough` | `boolean` | no | — | Single strikethrough (default false). |
| `text` | `string` | no | — | — |
| `tracking` | `number` | no | -100–100 | Extra spacing between glyphs in px (kern), -100 to 100, default 0 — the options bar's Tracking field. |
| `transform` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | The layer's 2×2 linear map [a, b, c, d], row-major — (x, y) maps to (a·x + b·y, c·x + d·y) — replacing the layer's current one (default: keep it); default [1, 0, 0, 1]. Rotation by θ clockwise is [cos θ, -sin θ, sin θ, cos θ]. transform_layer composes onto it; get_document reports it. |
| `underline` | `boolean` | no | — | Single underline (default false). |
| `weight` | `integer` | no | 0–15 | NSFontManager weight 0-15: 3 light, 5 regular (default), 6 medium, 8 semibold, 9 bold — the options bar's Weight popup. |
| `wrap_width` | `number` | no | — | px; the block wraps at this SOURCE-space width and remembers it (box_width); 0 = point text that never wraps (at most 100000 px, the app's own editor cap). Default: keep the layer's stored width — a layer saved before widths were stored (box_width null in get_document) re-wraps from its origin to the canvas's right edge, as this tool always did (the app's own editor caps that legacy default at 600 px; the two differ only for lines wider than that), and stores that width from then on. |

## `add_shape_layer`

Adds a RE-EDITABLE shape layer above the active layer and selects it — the same parametric layers the app's shape tools drag out: the kind, box size, fill, stroke and corner radius become the layer's description and the pixels are only their rendering. x,y is the TOP-LEFT corner of the shape box in canvas px (its origin in get_document) and w,h its size; the shape lands exactly there (the layer's raster is a few px larger on every side for stroke overhang and antialiasing), through transform when one is given. rect and ellipse take fill and/or stroke — pass at least one; a line is stroke-only and runs across the box's diagonal, top-left to bottom-right, or bottom-left to top-right with flipped: true. Returns the new layer's index and name. NOTE: painting on the layer afterwards drops the shape description and leaves plain pixels. In a 32-bit float document colours are the document's own linear-light numbers (#2E80C8 is 46/255 linear); red, green and blue may be above white, 0–65504, and alpha stays 0–1 (8/16-bit documents keep 0–1). A layer pasted into or converted out of 32 bits has its numbers rewritten so it looks the same; converting to 16 or 8 bits clips each channel at 1. get_document reports `ink`. Optional `layer` (anchor, default the active layer) and `position` (`above` the anchor, `top` of the root level, or `into_group` for a group anchor, default `above`) choose where it lands; the reply reports the `position` used. In 16-bit mode this creates editable retained artwork at the slot position names, exactly as at 8 bits. Authored colors and generated vector area coverage remain native; intrinsic bitmap glyph assets retain their disclosed byte precision. Works on a CMYK document: the layer's colours are stored as ink in the document's profile — pass ink (fill_ink, stroke_ink, a run's or a stop's ink) as C, M, Y, K percent for exact ink, or a colour, which separates through the profile (relative colorimetric with BPC); an edit that passes no colour keeps each ink exactly, and the reply reports the ink in percent beside the appearance hex. In a Grayscale document every colour — a run's, a stop's, a custom pattern's texels — is stored as its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule and renders R = G = B; get_document reports the gray; ink refuses. In a Lab Color document the colours stay authored sRGB (pass color; ink refuses) and render as L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule (a pattern's tile too, texel by texel; a gradient between its converted stops), an 8-bit layer on the ×257 grid; Image ▸ Mode conversions re-render the layer in the new mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `fill` | `string` | no | — | Hex fill color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA; omit for no fill. Ignored for lines. |
| `fill_ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items; items: 0–100 | CMYK document only: the fill as ink, C, M, Y, K in percent 0–100, stored exactly (a colour argument instead separates through the document's profile; its alpha still applies). Replies report ink beside the appearance hex. An RGB document refuses it. |
| `fill_rgba` | `['array', 'null']` | no | 4–4 items | Continuous normalized sRGB fill, alternative to fill; null removes it. sample_color's srgb_rgba is this spelling of a sampled pixel. |
| `flipped` | `boolean` | no | — | Line only (default false): false runs top-left to bottom-right across the box, true bottom-left to top-right. |
| `h` | `number` | yes | — | Shape box height in px (>= 1; a line may have 0 on one axis). |
| `kind` | `string` | yes | one of `rect`, `ellipse`, `line` | What to draw: rect, ellipse, or line. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Anchor layer index (default: the active layer). A group is a legal anchor. |
| `position` | `string` | no | one of `above`, `top`, `into_group` | Where the new layer lands relative to `layer`: above it (default), at the top of the root level, or as the top child of a group. |
| `radius` | `number` | no | — | Rect corner radius in px (default 0 = square corners; ignored by ellipse and line). |
| `stroke` | `string` | no | — | Hex stroke color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA; omit for no stroke (a line requires one). |
| `stroke_align` | `string` | no | one of `inside`, `center`, `outside` | Which side of the path the stroke's width lies on (default center). A line takes only center. |
| `stroke_dash` | `string` | no | one of `none`, `dashed`, `dotted` | The stroke's dash pattern (default none): dashed is 4 stroke widths on, 2 off; dotted is round dots one stroke width across, every 2 widths. |
| `stroke_ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items; items: 0–100 | CMYK document only: the stroke as ink, C, M, Y, K in percent 0–100, stored exactly (a colour argument instead separates through the document's profile; its alpha still applies). Replies report ink beside the appearance hex. An RGB document refuses it. |
| `stroke_join` | `string` | no | one of `miter`, `round`, `bevel` | How the stroke's corners meet (default miter). |
| `stroke_rgba` | `['array', 'null']` | no | 4–4 items | Continuous normalized sRGB stroke, alternative to stroke; null removes it. sample_color's srgb_rgba is this spelling of a sampled pixel. |
| `stroke_width` | `number` | no | — | Stroke width in px, centered on the path (0-200, default 2; a line needs at least 1). |
| `transform` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | The layer's 2×2 linear map [a, b, c, d], row-major — (x, y) maps to (a·x + b·y, c·x + d·y) — applied to the box before it is placed — the box's top-left stays at x,y; default [1, 0, 0, 1]. Rotation by θ clockwise is [cos θ, -sin θ, sin θ, cos θ]. transform_layer composes onto it; get_document reports it. |
| `w` | `number` | yes | — | Shape box width in px (>= 1; a line may have 0 on one axis). |
| `x` | `number` | yes | — | Shape box top-left x, canvas px. |
| `y` | `number` | yes | — | Shape box top-left y, canvas px. |

## `edit_shape_layer`

Changes an existing SHAPE layer's description and re-renders its pixels — the box, fill, stroke, stroke width, corner radius, line direction or transform — as one undo step, the way double-clicking the layer in the app reopens it. Works only on layers get_document reports a "shape" object for; the kind (rect / ellipse / line) is fixed at creation. Omitted arguments keep the layer's current values (x,y default to its origin, transform to its current map); the mask and style ride along. Pass fill or stroke as "" to remove that paint (at least one visible paint must remain). In a 32-bit float document colours are the document's own linear-light numbers (#2E80C8 is 46/255 linear); red, green and blue may be above white, 0–65504, and alpha stays 0–1 (8/16-bit documents keep 0–1). A layer pasted into or converted out of 32 bits has its numbers rewritten so it looks the same; converting to 16 or 8 bits clips each channel at 1. get_document reports `ink`. Works on a CMYK document: the layer's colours are stored as ink in the document's profile — pass ink (fill_ink, stroke_ink, a run's or a stop's ink) as C, M, Y, K percent for exact ink, or a colour, which separates through the profile (relative colorimetric with BPC); an edit that passes no colour keeps each ink exactly, and the reply reports the ink in percent beside the appearance hex. In a Grayscale document every colour — a run's, a stop's, a custom pattern's texels — is stored as its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule and renders R = G = B; get_document reports the gray; ink refuses. In a Lab Color document the colours stay authored sRGB (pass color; ink refuses) and render as L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule (a pattern's tile too, texel by texel; a gradient between its converted stops), an 8-bit layer on the ×257 grid; Image ▸ Mode conversions re-render the layer in the new mode. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `fill` | `string` | no | — | Hex fill color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA; "" removes the fill (default: keep). Ignored for lines. |
| `fill_ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items; items: 0–100 | CMYK document only: the fill as ink, C, M, Y, K in percent 0–100, stored exactly (a colour argument instead separates through the document's profile; its alpha still applies). Replies report ink beside the appearance hex. An RGB document refuses it. |
| `fill_rgba` | `['array', 'null']` | no | 4–4 items | Continuous normalized sRGB fill, alternative to fill; null removes it. sample_color's srgb_rgba is this spelling of a sampled pixel. |
| `flipped` | `boolean` | no | — | Line only: false runs top-left to bottom-right across the box, true bottom-left to top-right (default: keep). |
| `h` | `number` | no | — | New box height in px (default: keep). |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `radius` | `number` | no | — | Rect corner radius in px (default: keep; ignored by ellipse and line). |
| `stroke` | `string` | no | — | Hex stroke color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA; "" removes the stroke (default: keep; a line requires one). |
| `stroke_align` | `string` | no | one of `inside`, `center`, `outside` | Which side of the path the stroke's width lies on (default: keep; new shapes use center). A line takes only center. |
| `stroke_dash` | `string` | no | one of `none`, `dashed`, `dotted` | The stroke's dash pattern (default: keep; new shapes use none): dashed is 4 stroke widths on, 2 off; dotted is round dots one stroke width across, every 2 widths. |
| `stroke_ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items; items: 0–100 | CMYK document only: the stroke as ink, C, M, Y, K in percent 0–100, stored exactly (a colour argument instead separates through the document's profile; its alpha still applies). Replies report ink beside the appearance hex. An RGB document refuses it. |
| `stroke_join` | `string` | no | one of `miter`, `round`, `bevel` | How the stroke's corners meet (default: keep; new shapes use miter). |
| `stroke_rgba` | `['array', 'null']` | no | 4–4 items | Continuous normalized sRGB stroke, alternative to stroke; null removes it. sample_color's srgb_rgba is this spelling of a sampled pixel. |
| `stroke_width` | `number` | no | — | Stroke width in px, centered on the path (0-200; default: keep). |
| `transform` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | The layer's 2×2 linear map [a, b, c, d], row-major — (x, y) maps to (a·x + b·y, c·x + d·y) — replacing the layer's current one (default: keep it); default [1, 0, 0, 1]. Rotation by θ clockwise is [cos θ, -sin θ, sin θ, cos θ]. transform_layer composes onto it; get_document reports it. |
| `w` | `number` | no | — | New box width in px (default: keep). |
| `x` | `number` | no | — | New shape box top-left x, canvas px (default: keep). |

## `add_fill_layer`

Adds a FILL layer and selects it: one color (kind solid), one gradient (kind gradient) or one tiled pattern (kind pattern) over the whole canvas, re-editable with edit_fill_layer. A fill layer always covers the canvas: it is re-rendered when the canvas is cropped, resized or rotated; a quarter turn or a flip of the canvas also turns a linked pattern fill's tile into a turned custom tile under the same name. A solid or gradient fill cannot be moved or transformed; a pattern fill can (move_layers, an offset, transform_layer): it is re-rendered over the canvas, its mask moves, a linked tile follows the layer and an unlinked one stays on the canvas origin, and a transform keeps its Scale and Angle. Align and distribute refuse every fill. To show it in part of the image, give it a mask (add_layer_mask, then paint or fill with target "mask"). Colors are authored sRGB at 8, 16 and 32 bits; in a CMYK document they are stored as ink (pass ink for exact C, M, Y, K, else the colour separates through the document's profile); a pattern fill's tile separates to ink at render, as a Pattern Overlay's does. Returns the new layer's index and name. NOTE: painting on the layer's own pixels drops the fill description and leaves plain pixels. Optional `layer` (anchor, default the active layer) and `position` (`above` the anchor, `top` of the root level, or `into_group` for a group anchor, default `above`) choose where it lands; the reply reports the `position` used. At 16 and 32 bits the fill layer is retained artwork rendered at the document's depth from the same description, at the slot position names; at 32 bits its colors are carried into linear light and a gradient interpolates there. A pattern fill's tile codes are document values: at 32 bits code / 255 is linear light. Works on a CMYK document: the layer's colours are stored as ink in the document's profile — pass ink (fill_ink, stroke_ink, a run's or a stop's ink) as C, M, Y, K percent for exact ink, or a colour, which separates through the profile (relative colorimetric with BPC); an edit that passes no colour keeps each ink exactly, and the reply reports the ink in percent beside the appearance hex. In a Grayscale document every colour — a run's, a stop's, a custom pattern's texels — is stored as its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule and renders R = G = B; get_document reports the gray; ink refuses. In a Lab Color document the colours stay authored sRGB (pass color; ink refuses) and render as L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule (a pattern's tile too, texel by texel; a gradient between its converted stops), an 8-bit layer on the ×257 grid; Image ▸ Mode conversions re-render the layer in the new mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `color` | `string` | no | — | Solid only: hex color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `gradient` | `object` | no | — | Gradient only. stops is required: 2 to 32 colors, each at a position 0 to 1 with its own opacity and optional midpoints. style defaults to linear, angle to 90, scale to 1, reverse to false, smoothness to 1 and align_with_layer to false. The gradient spans the whole canvas; with align_with_layer true it spans the bounds of the layer's mask (none yet on a new layer: add_layer_mask, then edit_fill_layer re-renders it over the mask). |
| `gradient.align_with_layer` | `boolean` | no | — | Align with Layer: true spans the gradient over the bounds of the layer mask's coverage (the canvas without a mask); false over the canvas. A later mask edit takes effect at the next re-render. |
| `gradient.angle` | `number` | no | — | Degrees; 0 runs left to right, 90 bottom to top. |
| `gradient.reverse` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `gradient.scale` | `number` | no | 0.1–1.5 | — |
| `gradient.smoothness` | `number` | no | 0–1 | Smoothness as a fraction: 1 (100 %) is the Classic ramp, 0 the linear one, between them the two blended. |
| `gradient.stops` | `array<object>` | no | 2–32 items | — |
| `gradient.stops[].color` | `string` | no | — | Hex color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA (or ink in a CMYK document). |
| `gradient.stops[].ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items; items: 0–100 | CMYK document only: the stop's colour as ink, C, M, Y, K in percent 0–100, stored exactly (a colour argument instead separates through the document's profile; its alpha still applies). Replies report ink beside the appearance hex. An RGB document refuses it. |
| `gradient.stops[].midpoint` | `number` | no | 0.05–0.95 | The colour midpoint toward the next stop as a fraction: where the colour is half way between this stop and the next (default 0.5, 50 %; rounded to 0.01; the last stop's is ignored). Outside 0.05…0.95 is refused. |
| `gradient.stops[].opacity` | `number` | no | 0–1 | Default 1. |
| `gradient.stops[].opacity_midpoint` | `number` | no | 0.05–0.95 | The opacity midpoint toward the next stop as a fraction: where the opacity is half way between this stop and the next (default 0.5, 50 %; rounded to 0.01; the last stop's is ignored). Outside 0.05…0.95 is refused. |
| `gradient.stops[].position` | `number` | with parent | 0–1 | — |
| `gradient.style` | `string` | no | one of `linear`, `radial`, `angle`, `reflected`, `diamond` | — |
| `ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items; items: 0–100 | CMYK document only: a solid fill's colour as ink, C, M, Y, K in percent 0–100, stored exactly (a colour argument instead separates through the document's profile; its alpha still applies). Replies report ink beside the appearance hex. An RGB document refuses it. |
| `kind` | `string` | yes | one of `solid`, `gradient`, `pattern` | solid takes color; gradient takes gradient; pattern takes pattern. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Anchor layer index (default: the active layer). A group is a legal anchor. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | The layer's name (default Color Fill, Gradient Fill or Pattern Fill). |
| `pattern` | `object` | no | — | Pattern only (default: checkerboard, angle 0, scale 1, linked, phase [0, 0]). The tile repeats over the whole canvas. Linked (link_with_layer true), its origin is the canvas origin + phase + the layer's reference point (where it was made, moved by canvas edits); unlinked, the canvas origin + phase. Unknown keys, anchor included, are refused. Replies echo the tile as {preset} or {name, width, height} without rgba. At 32 bits tile codes / 255 are linear values. |
| `pattern.angle` | `number` | no | — | The Angle in degrees; turns the tile about its origin. |
| `pattern.link_with_layer` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `pattern.pattern` | `object` | no | — | {"preset": checkerboard\|stripes\|dots\|grid} or a custom tile {"name"?, "width", "height" 1..512, "rgba": standard base64 of width x height x 4 straight RGBA8 bytes}. |
| `pattern.phase` | `array<number>` | no | 2–2 items | The tile's offset [x, y] in canvas px. |
| `pattern.scale` | `number` | no | 0.01–10 | 1 = 100 %. |
| `position` | `string` | no | one of `above`, `top`, `into_group` | Where the new layer lands relative to `layer`: above it (default), at the top of the root level, or as the top child of a group. |

An omitted argument, and an omitted key inside gradient or pattern, keeps the layer's current value; the mask and style ride along. Works on a CMYK document: the layer's colours are stored as ink in the document's profile — pass ink (fill_ink, stroke_ink, a run's or a stop's ink) as C, M, Y, K percent for exact ink, or a colour, which separates through the profile (relative colorimetric with BPC); an edit that passes no colour keeps each ink exactly, and the reply reports the ink in percent beside the appearance hex. ## `select_rect`

Selects a rectangle (canvas coordinates). Selections confine brush/eraser strokes, fill, and gradient, and define Crop.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `feather` | `number` | no | 0–250 | Feather the new shape before combining (pixels, default 0). |
| `height` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | How the new shape combines with the current selection (default replace). add unions, subtract removes the new shape from the current selection, intersect keeps the overlap; an empty result clears the selection. |
| `width` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `x` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `y` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
