| `feather` | `number` | no | 0–250 | Feather the new shape before combining (pixels, default 0). |
| `height` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | How the new shape combines with the current selection (default replace). add unions, subtract removes the new shape from the current selection, intersect keeps the overlap; an empty result clears the selection. |
| `width` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `x` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `y` | `integer` | yes | — | — |

## `select_polygon`

Selects a polygon through the given vertices (at least 3, closed automatically).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `anti_alias` | `boolean` | no | — | Soften the edge (default true); false selects each pixel whose coverage is at least half, fully, for a hard 0/255 edge. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `feather` | `number` | no | 0–250 | Feather the new shape before combining (pixels, default 0). |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | How the new shape combines with the current selection (default replace). add unions, subtract removes the new shape from the current selection, intersect keeps the overlap; an empty result clears the selection. |
| `points` | `array<array<number>>` | yes | 3–10000 items | [[x, y], …] polygon vertices in canvas px. |

## `select_magic_wand`

Selects the region of similar color around a seed point, sampled from the flattened composite (what you see in a render). tolerance (historical 0–255 units, default 32) bounds how far each of R, G, B, A, R−G, G−B and R−B may lie from the seed's; native mode accepts fractional thresholds and reads original u16 samples; contiguous (default true) limits to the connected region. sample_all_layers: false reads one layer alone instead (the wand's Sample: Current layer): its own pixels on a transparent canvas, ignoring its opacity, mask and blend mode. sample_size (the wand's Sample Size, default 1 = Point Sample) compares against the per-channel mean of that square about the seed instead, clipped to the canvas (3, 5, 11, 31, 51 or 101 by 101 Average). In a 32-bit float document the tolerance or colour distance compares the display-encoded copy (the document profile's curve over each value clamped to 0–1, never the tone map), so a value above white compares as white; the output is native 65,536-level coverage. In a CMYK document the wand compares the INK, not the view: each ink as its naive RGB (1 − C)(1 − K), (1 − M)(1 − K), (1 − Y)(1 − K) at the document's depth, a pixel taken when its R, G, B, alpha, R−G, G−B and R−B each lie within tolerance (8-bit codes) of the seed's, four-connected when contiguous, admitting K and GCR twins alike; sample_all_layers false reads the active layer's own ink. sample_size averages that naive RGB over its box. In a Lab Color document it compares 8-bit Lab codes at both depths (measured against Photoshop): L, a and b within ± tolerance of the seed's, and the halved differences (a − L), (b − a) and (L − b) within ± half the tolerance; a 16-bit document's codes are read through Photoshop's 15-bit Lab grid. The Paint Bucket fills the same region. On an Indexed Color document a colour selection samples the palette colours, each pixel its index's colour (so a duplicate entry's pixels select with its twin's); the selection, Quick Mask and alpha channels work as on RGB and change no index. A red, green, blue or alpha channel, or the luminosity, refuses (the one channel is Index). A Bitmap document: not available in Bitmap mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `contiguous` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `feather` | `number` | no | 0–250 | Feather the new shape before combining (pixels, default 0). |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | With sample_all_layers: false, the layer to sample (default: the active layer). |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | How the new shape combines with the current selection (default replace). add unions, subtract removes the new shape from the current selection, intersect keeps the overlap; an empty result clears the selection. |
| `sample_all_layers` | `boolean` | no | — | true (default) samples the composite; false samples `layer` alone. |
| `sample_size` | `integer` | no | one of `1`, `3`, `5`, `11`, `31`, `51`, `101` | — |
| `tolerance` | `number` | no | 0–255 | — |
| `x` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `y` | `integer` | yes | — | — |

## `select_subject`

Selects the prominent foreground subjects — people, animals, objects — that macOS's Vision segmentation finds in the flattened composite. This is the same model behind Preview's Copy Subject, so it needs no seed point and no tolerance, unlike select_magic_wand. Mirrors Select > Select Subject. Omit instance to select every subject at once; pass instance (1-based) for a single one. Every result reports "instances", the number of subjects found, so you can select each in turn and compare their bounds to tell them apart. In a 32-bit float document Vision reads the tone-mapped 8-bit display at view exposure 0, so a subject entirely above white under the Clip tone map is found poorly: set the tone map to Reinhard first. In a CMYK document this reads the document's Display P3 view of its ink (sample_color's center_rgba16 are that view's codes), and the selection is coverage at document size. In a Lab Color document the model reads the document's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows); the selection is colour-free coverage. A Duotone document refuses it for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `feather` | `number` | no | 0–250 | Feather the new shape before combining (pixels, default 0). |
| `instance` | `integer` | no | 1–∞ | Which single subject to select (1-based). Omit to select all of them. |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | How the new shape combines with the current selection (default replace). add unions, subtract removes the new shape from the current selection, intersect keeps the overlap; an empty result clears the selection. |

## `select_all`

Selects the whole canvas. Mirrors Select > All. Prefer this over a full-canvas select_rect: it is canvas-RELATIVE, so a recorded action replays correctly on a differently sized document, where literal coordinates would not.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | How the new shape combines with the current selection (default replace). add unions, subtract removes the new shape from the current selection, intersect keeps the overlap; an empty result clears the selection. |

## `deselect`

Clears the selection.

| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

Reads selection bounds and Quick Mask state. Samples retain legacy 0–255 coverage plus exact coverage16 (0–65535) and report authoritative storage.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |

| `points` | `array<object>` | no | 0–4096 items | — |

| `points[].y` | `integer` | with parent | — | — |

## `set_quick_mask`

Enters/exits Quick Mask. Mode changes and each coverage stroke are undoable without dirtying the saved document. Works on a CMYK document: Grow and Similar compare the ink as the Magic Wand does, the Magnetic Lasso reads the view, and the rest edit coverage. In a Lab Color document Quick Mask is colour-free coverage, as on an RGB document (fill_selection takes target quick_mask). On an Indexed Color document a colour selection samples the palette colours, each pixel its index's colour (so a duplicate entry's pixels select with its twin's); the selection, Quick Mask and alpha channels work as on RGB and change no index. A red, green, blue or alpha channel, or the luminosity, refuses (the one channel is Index). A Bitmap document: it edits the selection only; the plane is unchanged.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `active` | `boolean` | yes | — | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `quick_mask_stroke`

Applies one canonical Quick Mask coverage stroke to the transient selection. Supply exactly one encoding: coverage_rle is base64 of 6-byte runs (little-endian UInt32 count, premultiplied gray byte, alpha byte); coverage_rle16 uses 8-byte runs with little-endian u16 gray and alpha. Native selection values remain exact. Runs cover the entire canvas in top-first row order; gray ≤ alpha. Output is gray + round(old × (255-alpha)/255). Recorded UI strokes include actual pressure, opacity and airbrush output. Works with either marquee or Quick Mask display; dimensions must match exactly. 16-bit generation also accepts stroke_version=1 with points/pressure/timing, or canonical native_stroke instead of RLE. Canonical dabs keep the native coverage job bounded and cancellable; opacity and erase describe the final selection deposit. Works on a CMYK document: Grow and Similar compare the ink as the Magic Wand does, the Magnetic Lasso reads the view, and the rest edit coverage. In a Lab Color document Quick Mask is colour-free coverage, as on an RGB document (fill_selection takes target quick_mask). On an Indexed Color document a colour selection samples the palette colours, each pixel its index's colour (so a duplicate entry's pixels select with its twin's); the selection, Quick Mask and alpha channels work as on RGB and change no index. A red, green, blue or alpha channel, or the luminosity, refuses (the one channel is Index). A Bitmap document: it edits the selection only; the plane is unchanged.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `airbrush` | `boolean` | no | — | Generate 20 Hz held deposits using the declared sample times/duration. |
| `coverage_rle` | `string` | no | — | — |
| `coverage_rle16` | `string` | no | — | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `duration` | `number` | no | 0–2499 | Total stroke seconds, including any hold at the final point; defaults to the last time. |
| `erase` | `boolean` | no | — | Remove Quick Mask coverage instead of adding white. Byte canonical calls require size and use byte RLE; 16-bit calls use native coverage. |
| `flow` | `number` | no | 1–100 | — |
| `hardness` | `number` | no | 0–100 | — |
| `height` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `native_stroke` | `object` | no | — | Canonical RZBR version1 replay: version=1, encoding=le_f64_xy_diameter_opacity, dabs=base64 little-endian binary64 quadruples, hardness, roundness, angle_degrees, pixel. Mutually exclusive with generation options; recorded automatically. Byte commits and replay share one exact dab rasterizer; at 8 bits historical unversioned points keep their prior meaning. |
| `opacity` | `number` | no | 0–1 | — |
| `points` | `array<array<number>>` | no | 0–10000 items | — |
| `pressure_opacity` | `boolean` | no | — | Scale each dab deposit by pressure; stroke opacity still applies once. |
| `pressure_size` | `boolean` | no | — | Scale dab size by pressure, with a one-pixel floor. |
| `pressures` | `array<number>` | no | items: 0–1 | With stroke_version=1, one tablet pressure per point; default 1. |
| `size` | `number` | no | 1–5000 | — |
| `stroke_version` | `integer` | no | one of `1` | Generate canonical resolved dabs from points and optional pressures/times. Byte and 16-bit stroke tools accept this form, including byte mask/plane/channel, pixel and Quick Mask coverage. At 8 bits, omit for the historical point footprint; at 16 bits unversioned points generate the same native dabs (unit pressure, no timing) and refuse by name at the 50,000-dab and 2-billion-work-unit limits; smudge_stroke has its own 256-million-work-unit bound at both depths (it walks the stroke a pixel at a time) and refuses a longer stroke by name. A versioned call refuses a size outside its tool's range by name (1–5000 px; 3–200 for heal_stroke and spot_heal_stroke; 1–200 for blur_stroke, sharpen_stroke, smudge_stroke, sponge_stroke and history_brush_stroke; 1–200 for art_history_brush_stroke); an unversioned call clamps it. Maximum 50,000 dabs; oversized strokes refuse by name; no partial stroke. |
| `times` | `array<number>` | no | items: 0–∞ | Elapsed seconds per point, starting at 0 and nondecreasing; used for 20 Hz airbrush deposits. |
| `width` | `integer` | yes | — | — |

## `modify_selection`

Transforms the current selection (errors when nothing is selected, except invert, which is then a no-op success): invert selects the complement over the canvas; feather Gaussian-softens the selection edge by radius px, so later fills, gradients, and strokes fade out across it; grow/shrink (Select ▸ Modify ▸ Expand/Contract) move the selection edge outward/inward by radius px (corners round into arcs); border replaces the selection with a band width px wide straddling its edge; smooth rounds corners and evens out jagged edges without moving long straight ones. An empty result clears the selection. For the colour-based Select ▸ Grow/Similar use select_similar. Works on a CMYK document: Grow and Similar compare the ink as the Magic Wand does, the Magnetic Lasso reads the view, and the rest edit coverage. In a Lab Color document it is colour-free and runs as on RGB. On an Indexed Color document a colour selection samples the palette colours, each pixel its index's colour (so a duplicate entry's pixels select with its twin's); the selection, Quick Mask and alpha channels work as on RGB and change no index. A red, green, blue or alpha channel, or the luminosity, refuses (the one channel is Index).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `operation` | `string` | yes | one of `invert`, `feather`, `grow`, `shrink`, `border`, `smooth` | — |
| `radius` | `number` | no | — | Radius in px (0-250; required for feather, grow, shrink, and smooth). |
| `width` | `number` | no | — | Band width in px (0-250; required for border). |

## `fill`

Bucket fill: flood-fills the similar-color region around the seed point on a layer's own pixels with a color. Respects the active selection. tolerance as in select_magic_wand. blend_mode lays the color down through a blend mode, and sample_all_layers grows the region over the composite instead of the layer alone (the Fill tool's Mode and Sample all layers); both apply to a layer target only, at 8 and 16 bits. 16-bit targets support selected color-match bucket fill. Set fill_mode=color_match explicitly for noncontiguous RGB matching; historical typed contiguous=false without fill_mode retains selection-wide fill. In a 32-bit float document the bucket's tolerance compares the display-encoded copy (the document profile's curve over each value clamped to 0–1, never the tone map), so a value above white compares as white, and the region is filled in linear light in Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Darker Color, Linear Burn, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Pin Light, Difference, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity only; rgba32 replaces color with linear-light numbers, above white included, on every layer fill (color_match, contiguous false, fill_mode selection and sample_all_layers), and the reply's storage is "rgba32_float". A mask or alpha channel target fills as at 16 bits (storage "u16") and refuses rgba32; a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses there. In a CMYK document this paints in INK on a layer (or its mask): pass ink [c, m, y, k] in percent (exactly the Color Picker's C/M/Y/K), or color, which converts through the document's CMYK profile; every blend mode but Pass Through, evaluated on 1 − ink; sample_all_layers grows the region over the composite's ink, as the Magic Wand does. Target cyan, magenta, yellow or black paints that ink plate's stored 1 − ink, and channel:<name> an alpha channel, as a 16-bit colour plane or channel is painted: color's grey is painted (white leaves no ink) and ink refuses. On an RGB document ink refuses. In a Grayscale document the colour paints its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule (its luminance in the Gray profile), R = G = B, at 8, 16 and 32 bits; target is layer, mask or channel:<name> (the Gray channel is the layer; red, green, blue and alpha refuse for good), ink refuses, and blend_mode takes the Grayscale modes. In a Lab Color document the colour paints its L*a*b* values by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, at 8 and 16 bits (color_space document takes the L*a*b* values as unit codes, L*/100 and (a* + 128)/255, exactly); target is layer, mask, lightness, a, b, alpha or channel:<name> (red, green and blue refuse: a Lab document's planes are lightness, a and b), ink refuses, and blend_mode takes Normal, Dissolve, Multiply, Linear Burn, Darker Color, Screen, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity; Darken, Color Burn, Lighten, Color Dodge, Difference, Exclusion, Subtract and Divide are unavailable. On an Indexed Color document the edit runs on the RGB storage, then each changed pixel goes back onto the palette by the Brush's rule: paint takes the entry nearest the colour (an edge pixel when its coverage is at least 131/255, else it keeps its index), and an erased pixel keeps its index until its alpha falls below 128, when it takes the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the entry nearest the current background colour). Painting takes every blend_mode: a changed pixel is compared with the mode's full-strength colour over its old colour and takes the entry nearest that colour, by the same 131/255 rule; sample_all_layers is off. On a Bitmap document it paints in black and white: the colour becomes black or white by its gray (128 and above is white), the edit runs on the 8-bit gray storage at its opacity, and every pixel goes back to white where its gray over the background at its own alpha reaches 128, else black, so a soft edge lands hard where its coverage reaches about half and a stroke under 50 % opacity changes nothing. blend_mode Normal, Darken or Lighten only (another refuses); sample_all_layers is off (the one layer is the composite). An erased or cleared pixel takes the background, white.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `blend_mode` | `string` | no | one of `Normal`, `Dissolve`, `Darken`, `Multiply`, `Color Burn`, `Linear Burn`, `Darker Color`, `Lighten`, `Screen`, `Color Dodge`, `Linear Dodge (Add)`, `Lighter Color`, `Overlay`, `Soft Light`, `Hard Light`, `Vivid Light`, `Linear Light`, `Pin Light`, `Hard Mix`, `Difference`, `Exclusion`, `Subtract`, `Divide`, `Hue`, `Saturation`, `Color`, `Luminosity` | How the color blends with the layer (default Normal). |
| `color` | `string` | no | — | Hex color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA (default #000000). |
| `color_space` | `string` | no | one of `srgb`, `document`, `display_p3` | How the colour argument is interpreted, at EITHER depth. Default srgb: an authored sRGB hex (or 16-bit rgba), converted once into the document. document: the hex IS the document's own bytes (sample_color's hex), at 16 bits too, where each hex byte v becomes the exact code v·257 (16-bit numeric rgba is then read as document components). display_p3: the hex (or 16-bit rgba) is Display P3, converted once into the document. Numeric rgba stays 16-bit-only. |
| `contiguous` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `fill_mode` | `string` | no | one of `color_match`, `selection` | 16-bit targets: color_match uses contiguous/noncontiguous target similarity and requires a selected seed. RGB ink can expand raw storage. selection fills the selected area, or the RGB canvas/complete raw scalar target when no selection exists. Historical RGB contiguous=false without this field preserves its selection-wide behavior. |
| `ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | CMYK document only: C, M, Y, K ink in percent 0–100. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `opacity` | `number` | no | 0–1 | Explicit native fill_mode only: global opacity, separate from color alpha; default 1. |
| `rgba` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items; items: 0–1 | 16-bit documents only: continuous normalized sRGB RGBA, overriding color. Never a byte-preview sample. |
| `rgba32` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | 32-bit float documents only, instead of color: [red, green, blue, alpha] as linear light in the document's primaries (sample_color's center_rgba32 / mean_rgba32), red, green and blue 0–65504 (above 1 is above white) and alpha 0–1, used as they are. Takes no color_space; an 8- or 16-bit document and Quick Mask refuse it. Layer target only, on every layer fill (color_match, contiguous false, fill_mode selection, sample_all_layers): a mask or channel is 0–1 coverage and refuses it. |
| `sample_all_layers` | `boolean` | no | — | Grow the region over the flattened composite (default false: over the layer's own pixels). The color still lands on `layer`. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | What the fill lands on: "layer" (default) the layer's own pixels, "mask" the layer's mask, "red"/"green"/"blue"/"alpha" ONE colour plane of that layer's pixels, or "channel:<name>" one of the document's alpha channels (list_channels names them). A mask, plane or channel target holds COVERAGE, not color, so the color enters as its gray (its luma) and its alpha is the strength. Writing "alpha" is the one exception to that: every pixel whose new alpha is 0 loses its colour bytes as well, so re-running the edit does not bring them back. |
| `tolerance` | `integer` | no | 0–255 | — |
| `x` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `y` | `integer` | yes | — | — |

## `gradient`

Paints a gradient over a layer (the whole layer, or the active selection if one exists): two colors (start_color, end_color), or stops, 2 to 32 colors each at a position with its own opacity. Linear runs along (x0,y0)->(x1,y1); radial spreads from (x0,y0) with radius to (x1,y1); angle sweeps clockwise around (x0,y0) starting along the line; reflected is linear mirrored about (x0,y0); diamond spreads from (x0,y0) as a diamond reaching (x1,y1). end_color defaults to transparent (a fade-out). Give start_color or stops. blend_mode lays the ramp down through a blend mode (the Gradient tool's Mode), on a layer target only. 8 and 16 bits. color_space qualifies the hex endpoints and every stop's color at either depth (srgb, document, display_p3); numeric start_rgba/end_rgba stay 16-bit-only. In a 32-bit float document the ramp interpolates in linear light, in the same blend modes as brush_stroke there; start_rgba32 with end_rgba32 give both ends as linear-light numbers, above white included, and the reply's storage is "rgba32_float". A mask or alpha channel target takes the ramp as at 16 bits (storage "u16"); a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses there. In a CMYK document the ramp is INK: start_ink / end_ink [c, m, y, k] in percent, or start_color / end_color (or stops' colours) converted through the document's CMYK profile; every blend mode but Pass Through, evaluated on 1 − ink. Target cyan, magenta, yellow or black paints that ink plate's stored 1 − ink, and channel:<name> an alpha channel, as a 16-bit colour plane or channel is painted: color's grey is painted (white leaves no ink) and start_ink / end_ink refuse. In a Grayscale document the colour paints its gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule (its luminance in the Gray profile), R = G = B, at 8, 16 and 32 bits; target is layer, mask or channel:<name> (the Gray channel is the layer; red, green, blue and alpha refuse for good), ink refuses, and blend_mode takes the Grayscale modes. In a Lab Color document the colour paints its L*a*b* values by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, at 8 and 16 bits (color_space document takes the L*a*b* values as unit codes, L*/100 and (a* + 128)/255, exactly); target is layer, mask, lightness, a, b, alpha or channel:<name> (red, green and blue refuse: a Lab document's planes are lightness, a and b), ink refuses, and blend_mode takes Normal, Dissolve, Multiply, Linear Burn, Darker Color, Screen, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity; Darken, Color Burn, Lighten, Color Dodge, Difference, Exclusion, Subtract and Divide are unavailable. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good. A Bitmap document: it runs on the 8-bit gray storage and every pixel goes back white where its gray over white at its own alpha reaches 128, else black, so the ramp lands hard where it crosses 128; its colours are used as given, not snapped to black or white; blend_mode Normal, Darken or Lighten only (another refuses).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `blend_mode` | `string` | no | one of `Normal`, `Dissolve`, `Darken`, `Multiply`, `Color Burn`, `Linear Burn`, `Darker Color`, `Lighten`, `Screen`, `Color Dodge`, `Linear Dodge (Add)`, `Lighter Color`, `Overlay`, `Soft Light`, `Hard Light`, `Vivid Light`, `Linear Light`, `Pin Light`, `Hard Mix`, `Difference`, `Exclusion`, `Subtract`, `Divide`, `Hue`, `Saturation`, `Color`, `Luminosity` | How the ramp's colors blend with the layer (default Normal). A mask, plane, channel or Quick Mask target holds coverage and refuses any other mode. |
| `color_space` | `string` | no | one of `srgb`, `document`, `display_p3` | Endpoint colour interpretation. Default srgb: authored sRGB, converted once into the document. display_p3 reads start_color/end_color (or the 16-bit numeric endpoints) as Display P3 at EITHER depth, converted once into the document. document: start_color/end_color ARE the document's own hex bytes (sample_color's hex) at either depth (exact v·257 at 16 bits); numeric 16-bit endpoints are document components. Every value is converted once and quantized to the document's numbers. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `end_color` | `string` | no | — | Hex color; omit to fade to transparent. |
| `end_ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | CMYK document only: C, M, Y, K ink in percent 0–100. |
| `end_rgba` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items; items: 0–1 | 16-bit continuous normalized RGBA endpoint, including alpha. |
| `end_rgba32` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | 32-bit float documents only, instead of end_color and always with start_rgba32: [red, green, blue, alpha] as linear light in the document's primaries (sample_color's center_rgba32 / mean_rgba32), red, green and blue 0–65504 (above 1 is above white) and alpha 0–1, used as they are. Takes no color_space, stops or other endpoint; layer target only; an 8- or 16-bit document and Quick Mask refuse it. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `opacity` | `number` | no | 0–1 | 16-bit gradient opacity; scales interpolated endpoint alpha once. |
| `shape` | `string` | no | one of `linear`, `radial`, `angle`, `reflected`, `diamond` | — |
| `smoothness` | `number` | no | 0–1 | Smoothness as a fraction: 1 (100 %, the default) is the Classic ramp, 0 the linear one, between them the two blended. Diamond ignores it. |
| `start_color` | `string` | no | — | Hex color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA. |
| `start_ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | CMYK document only: C, M, Y, K ink in percent 0–100. |
| `start_rgba` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items; items: 0–1 | 16-bit continuous normalized RGBA endpoint, including alpha. |
| `start_rgba32` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | 32-bit float documents only, instead of start_color and always with end_rgba32: [red, green, blue, alpha] as linear light in the document's primaries (sample_color's center_rgba32 / mean_rgba32), red, green and blue 0–65504 (above 1 is above white) and alpha 0–1, used as they are. Takes no color_space, stops or other endpoint; layer target only; an 8- or 16-bit document and Quick Mask refuse it. |
| `stops` | `array<object>` | no | 2–32 items | The ramp's stops, replacing start_color and end_color, in order of position. Colors interpolate between neighbouring stops, half way at the left stop's midpoint. |
| `stops[].color` | `string` | with parent | — | Hex color, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA. |
| `stops[].midpoint` | `number` | no | 0.05–0.95 | The colour midpoint toward the next stop as a fraction: where the colour is half way between this stop and the next (default 0.5, 50 %; rounded to 0.01; the last stop's is ignored). Outside 0.05…0.95 is refused. |
| `stops[].opacity` | `number` | no | 0–1 | Scales the color's alpha (default 1). |
| `stops[].opacity_midpoint` | `number` | no | 0.05–0.95 | The opacity midpoint toward the next stop as a fraction: where the opacity is half way between this stop and the next (default 0.5, 50 %; rounded to 0.01; the last stop's is ignored). Outside 0.05…0.95 is refused. |
| `stops[].position` | `number` | with parent | 0–1 | 0 at (x0,y0), 1 at (x1,y1); never below the stop before it. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | What the ramp lands on: "layer" (default) the layer's own pixels, "mask" the layer's mask, "red"/"green"/"blue"/"alpha" ONE colour plane of that layer's pixels, or "channel:<name>" one of the document's alpha channels (list_channels names them). On a mask, plane or channel the colors enter as their grays — coverage, not color — with their alpha as the strength. Writing "alpha" is the one exception to that: every pixel whose new alpha is 0 loses its colour bytes as well, so re-running the edit does not bring them back. "quick_mask" paints the Quick Mask coverage instead (refused when Quick Mask is off); while Quick Mask is on, a call with no target paints it too. |
| `x0` | `number` | yes | — | — |
| `x1` | `number` | yes | — | — |
| `y0` | `number` | yes | — | — |
| `y1` | `number` | yes | — | — |

## `clear_selection`

Erases the active selection out of a layer: the selected pixels lose their color and become transparent, in proportion to the selection's coverage, so a feathered selection cuts a soft-edged hole. Only the one layer changes — whatever sits below it shows through. Errors when nothing is selected; make a selection with the select_* tools first. In a Grayscale document it erases the selected pixels of a Grayscale layer, mask or alpha channel. In a Lab Color document it erases the selected pixels of a layer, as on an RGB document. On an Indexed Color document the edit runs on the RGB storage, then each changed pixel goes back onto the palette by the Brush's rule: paint takes the entry nearest the colour (an edge pixel when its coverage is at least 131/255, else it keeps its index), and an erased pixel keeps its index until its alpha falls below 128, when it takes the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the entry nearest the current background colour). Painting takes every blend_mode: a changed pixel is compared with the mode's full-strength colour over its old colour and takes the entry nearest that colour, by the same 131/255 rule; sample_all_layers is off. On a Bitmap document it paints in black and white: the colour becomes black or white by its gray (128 and above is white), the edit runs on the 8-bit gray storage at its opacity, and every pixel goes back to white where its gray over the background at its own alpha reaches 128, else black, so a soft edge lands hard where its coverage reaches about half and a stroke under 50 % opacity changes nothing. blend_mode Normal, Darken or Lighten only (another refuses); sample_all_layers is off (the one layer is the composite). An erased or cleared pixel takes the background, white.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |

## `copy`

Copies a layer's raw pixels (default the active layer) inside the selection's bounds — the whole canvas without one — to the clipboard, with alpha multiplied by the selection's coverage (Edit ▸ Copy). At 16 bits and 32-bit float the clipboard also carries a private typed payload that round-trips samples, alpha, profile, offset, coverage and PPI bit for bit; the public TIFF/PNG beside it is a rendering. At 8 bits the clipboard carries a byte-origin typed payload too (its codes exactly ×257, the document's profile, offset and PPI), so paste in_place and a 16-bit paste work from an 8-bit copy. With no selection, a text, shape or adjustment layer's copy also carries its editable record at every depth (an adjustment layer copies as transparent pixels plus its settings), which paste restores; a selection copy, a raster layer or a RAW layer copies pixels only. A group copies its own composite at every depth: its children blended together, without the group's own opacity, blend mode or mask. Reply: typed, depth, width, height, offset, public_types, typed_bytes, editable ("text", "shape", "adjust" or null). While recording, the call is recorded as a step that copies from the replaying document; no pixels are stored. mode "auto" decides as Edit ▸ Copy does, from this document's own state: with a pixel selection it is pixels of the given layer (default the active layer); with none it is layers, of the given layers (default the SELECTED layers). A recorded Edit ▸ Copy is this step, so a replay re-decides on the replaying document. mode "layers" ignores any pixel selection and copies the given layers (layers, or layer/index; default the active layer), each with its whole subtree and every property, to an in-process layer clipboard that paste restores; the pasteboard still receives a flat image — one root's whole-layer copy, or the copied layers' merged composite when several roots are copied (flat "copy" or "copy_merged"). Layers reply: ok, mode, source_layers, records, depth, width, height, typed, typed_bytes, public_types, editable, flat. A typed payload larger than the system pasteboard accepts (over 255 MiB) stays in this Doctored instance, named on the pasteboard by a token; other apps and other Doctored instances get only the flat TIFF/PNG. typed_store reports where the typed payload is: "pasteboard", "process" (held in this instance) or null. Works on a CMYK document: the copy is the layer's (or the composite's) INK, a CMYK typed payload (RZCB v4) in the document's CMYK profile and declared depth; a CMYK adjustment layer has no ink to copy (use copy_merged). Copying from a Grayscale document makes a Grayscale payload (its Gray profile and depth); the pasteboard's TIFF is a one-channel gray image with that profile embedded (two channels with transparency), the PNG an RGB rendering. In a Lab Color document the payload keeps the L*a*b* codes (a Lab Color payload); the pasteboard's image for other apps is the RGB rendering (Display P3). On an Indexed Color document the edit runs on the RGB storage, then each changed pixel goes back onto the palette by the Brush's rule: paint takes the entry nearest the colour (an edge pixel when its coverage is at least 131/255, else it keeps its index), and an erased pixel keeps its index until its alpha falls below 128, when it takes the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the entry nearest the current background colour). Painting takes every blend_mode: a changed pixel is compared with the mode's full-strength colour over its old colour and takes the entry nearest that colour, by the same 131/255 rule; sample_all_layers is off. A Bitmap document: the copy holds each bit as black or white gray.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | no | 1–unbounded items | Layers to copy in mode layers, instead of layer. |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `pixels`, `layers`, `auto` | pixels (default) copies pixels as described; layers copies whole layers (Edit ▸ Copy with no selection); auto is pixels with a pixel selection and layers (the selected layers) without one, as Edit ▸ Copy decides. |
| `public_copy_path` | `string` | no | — | Absolute path ending in .tiff; receives the same TIFF bytes placed on the clipboard. |

## `copy_merged`

Copies the flattened composite inside the selection's bounds (the whole canvas without one) to the clipboard (Edit ▸ Copy Merged). Typed at 16 bits and float, as copy. While recording, the call is recorded as a step that copies from the replaying document; no pixels are stored. Works on a CMYK document: the copy is the layer's (or the composite's) INK, a CMYK typed payload (RZCB v4) in the document's CMYK profile and declared depth; a CMYK adjustment layer has no ink to copy (use copy_merged). Copying from a Grayscale document makes a Grayscale payload (its Gray profile and depth); the pasteboard's TIFF is a one-channel gray image with that profile embedded (two channels with transparency), the PNG an RGB rendering. In a Lab Color document the payload keeps the L*a*b* codes (a Lab Color payload); the pasteboard's image for other apps is the RGB rendering (Display P3). On an Indexed Color document the edit runs on the RGB storage, then each changed pixel goes back onto the palette by the Brush's rule: paint takes the entry nearest the colour (an edge pixel when its coverage is at least 131/255, else it keeps its index), and an erased pixel keeps its index until its alpha falls below 128, when it takes the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the entry nearest the current background colour). Painting takes every blend_mode: a changed pixel is compared with the mode's full-strength colour over its old colour and takes the entry nearest that colour, by the same 131/255 rule; sample_all_layers is off. A Bitmap document: not available in Bitmap mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `public_copy_path` | `string` | no | — | Absolute path ending in .tiff; receives the same TIFF bytes placed on the clipboard. |

## `cut`

Copies a layer's selected pixels to the clipboard exactly as copy does, then clears them out of the layer as ONE undo step (Edit ▸ Cut). Requires a selection. A transparency-locked layer keeps its pixels (the clipboard still receives the copy) and the call reports it. In a 32-bit float document the erase scales alpha by (1 − coverage) and keeps RGB. Works on a CMYK document: the copy is the layer's (or the composite's) INK, a CMYK typed payload (RZCB v4) in the document's CMYK profile and declared depth; a CMYK adjustment layer has no ink to copy (use copy_merged). Copying from a Grayscale document makes a Grayscale payload (its Gray profile and depth); the pasteboard's TIFF is a one-channel gray image with that profile embedded (two channels with transparency), the PNG an RGB rendering. In a Lab Color document the payload keeps the L*a*b* codes (a Lab Color payload); the pasteboard's image for other apps is the RGB rendering (Display P3). On an Indexed Color document the edit runs on the RGB storage, then each changed pixel goes back onto the palette by the Brush's rule: paint takes the entry nearest the colour (an edge pixel when its coverage is at least 131/255, else it keeps its index), and an erased pixel keeps its index until its alpha falls below 128, when it takes the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the entry nearest the current background colour). Painting takes every blend_mode: a changed pixel is compared with the mode's full-strength colour over its old colour and takes the entry nearest that colour, by the same 131/255 rule; sample_all_layers is off. A Bitmap document: Cut pixels take the background, white.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `public_copy_path` | `string` | no | — | Absolute path ending in .tiff; receives the same TIFF bytes placed on the clipboard. |

## `paste`

Pastes the clipboard as a new layer and selects it (Edit ▸ Paste, or Edit ▸ Paste Special ▸ Paste in Place with placement in_place, which needs a Doctored typed payload's offset). placement auto (the default) is Edit ▸ Paste's rule (measured against Photoshop), read from the view named by view (the document's first view without it): with an active selection (not in Quick Mask) the layer is centred on the selection's bounds, with no mask (placement selection); otherwise it is centred on the visible part of the canvas (view) and never keeps its source position, however visible the copied area is. With no window the visible part is the whole canvas, so the last case is the canvas centre (centered). placement in_place keeps the copy's source coordinates when this canvas is the size of the one it was copied from, and otherwise keeps the copy's centre at the same fraction of the canvas, the corner floored (placement relative_in_place), whatever the view and any selection; a payload_path paste keeps its own coordinates. A pixel paste made with an active selection deselects it in the same undo step (reselect restores it). placement centered is always the canvas centre, and at puts the layer's top-left exactly at x, y. Paste Special ▸ Paste Into (placement into) and Paste Outside (outside) need an active selection and are refused in Quick Mask: the layer is centred on the selection's bounds and gets a CANVAS-sized, unlinked mask at (0, 0) — the selection's coverage (into), or its inverse with outside coverage 255 (outside) — so the pasted pixels can be moved or the mask painted anywhere on the canvas. The selection is consumed in the same undo step (reselect restores it) and the layer, not its mask, stays the edit target. The pasted pixels are converted into this document's depth and profile at every depth, with no refusal for either: a float copy is tone-mapped under its own map into 8 or 16 bits, a 16-bit or 8-bit copy and an image from another app are promoted into a 32-bit float document (decoded to linear light, then converted into its profile), an image from another app enters 16 bits exactly (×257) and an 8-bit document converts any typed payload or payload_path file through the core. An untagged image from another app keeps its numbers in this document's profile. profile "preserve" is the Paste Profile Mismatch alert's Don't Convert (the menu asks only with Image ▸ Mode ▸ Working Space ▸ Ask When Pasting on): the pixels keep their numbers and take this document's profile. Paste in Place of an image from another app, which has no source position, lands like placement auto. A payload carrying an editable record (a whole-layer copy of a text, shape or adjustment layer) restores it — the artwork re-rendered at this document's depth, the adjustment re-created from its settings — before any depth or profile rule; a 32-bit float document restores editable artwork too, its colours rewritten into linear light so it looks the same, and a record that cannot be restored pastes as pixels with its reason. Reply: layer, name, placement (where it landed: in_place, relative_in_place, selection, view, centered, into, outside or at), offset, depth, typed, origin_depth, converted, external, narrowed, profile (same, converted or preserved; null for a restored record), editable (null or {type, restored, reason?}), mask (null, or for into/outside {x, y, width, height, linked, outside_coverage, frame [x, y, w, h]}), ppi {payload, document, match}, color_conversion (null, or {from, to, from_profile, to_profile, engine, intent, black_point_compensation} when the pixels changed colour model — RGB ↔ CMYK — or CMYK profile: engine "doctored" is the core's relative colorimetric conversion with black-point compensation, "platform" a Gray, Lab or CMYK image CoreGraphics converted while decoding it); a PPI mismatch is named in the history row ("Paste Layer (300 → 72 ppi)"), and so is a change of colour model ("Paste Layer (CMYK → RGB)"). While recording, a paste is one of two kinds of step. By default it is live: it stores no pixels and no position (the requested placement, x and y only for at, name and mode only when passed), a replay pastes whatever the clipboard holds then — pixels or copied layers — and the step fails when the clipboard holds no image, so record the copy that feeds it too. With payload_path or record_payload it is a saved-payload step: the landed payload is written as a .drcb file, the step names it as payload_path (package_action carries it as an asset) and replays without the clipboard, and an auto paste or an in_place paste that landed relative_in_place is recorded as at with the landed offset. view is not recorded. mode "auto" (default) pastes the layer clipboard when the clipboard still holds a layers copy and pixels otherwise; "layers" requires one, "pixels" ignores it. A layers paste lands every copied layer with its structure, masks, blend modes, styles, clipping and adjustment layers as ONE undo step: auto (default) centres the pasted roots' combined content box on a selection or the view (placement selection or view; centered with no window) and never keeps its source position; centered centres that box on the canvas; in_place keeps their source canvas coordinates on a canvas of the source's size and otherwise moves the box to the same relative location (placement relative_in_place); a layers paste keeps the selection; into, outside, at, x, y, payload_path, record_payload and name are pixel-paste arguments and are refused. While a layers copy is held, placement into or outside with mode auto is refused; mode "pixels" pastes their flat image there. Into 8 and 16 bits any copy pastes (but one holding a 32-bit float Camera RAW development, refused by name until it is redeveloped with raw.output_encoding sdr16 or rasterized), its depth converted (narrowed, or promoted exactly ×257) and its profile converted (profile "convert", the default; RAW layers re-render from their sources and keep them) or kept ("preserve", Don't Convert: every layer keeps its numbers and RAW layers keep their sources; refused by name only when the document's profile fails the Assign check for the copied text/shape or calibrated layers). Into a 32-bit float document any copy pastes too, promoted into linear light under the same profile choice: a RAW layer keeps its source (re-rendered from its development into linear light under "convert", its numbers kept under "preserve"), text and shape layers stay editable (their colours rewritten into linear light so they look the same; under "preserve" only when the copied layer is in the document's own profile, else they land as their pixels), while warps land as their pixels (rasterized), a Pass Through group lands Pass Through, and the blend modes reset at 32 bits land Normal (blend_reset), layer styles and Blend If ride with an outer_glow, inner_glow or bevel highlight in Screen landing linear_dodge (effect_blend_reset); a copied layer the float mode cannot hold (an effect blend mode outside the float set, another unavailable blend mode, an adjustment the float mode cannot evaluate (Hue/Saturation, a Color Lookup other than a 3D table within 0 to 1, and the others refused at 32 bits)) refuses the whole paste, naming the layer and the feature. The copied layers bring no layer comp, alpha channel, guide or color sampler, the document keeps its own and its global light (a pasted style that uses the global light casts by this document's), and at 8 and 16 bits a linked RAW layer stays linked, its file missing or not. Layers reply: ok, mode, placement, offset {x, y}, layers (the pasted roots), layer, records, depth, origin_depth, converted, narrowed, profile_converted, profile (same, converted or preserved), rasterized [{layer, reason}], blend_reset [{layer, from}], effect_blend_reset [{layer, effect, from, to}] (all three empty unless a float document promoted the copy), ppi {clipboard, document, match}, history. Optional `layer` (anchor, default the active layer) and `position` (`above` the anchor, `top` of the root level, or `into_group` for a group anchor, default `above`) choose where it lands; the reply reports the `position` used. CMYK: between CMYK documents of the same profile the ink is kept bit for bit; another CMYK profile converts (relative colorimetric with black-point compensation) or, with profile "preserve", keeps the ink. Across modes — an RGB copy or another app's RGB image into a CMYK document, a CMYK copy or a CMYK TIFF from another app into an RGB document — the pixels always convert through the profiles' own tables, and profile "preserve" refuses. A copied layers clip of the other mode is converted first (an adjustment layer CMYK cannot hold refuses by name). color_conversion reports what was crossed. Into or out of a Grayscale document the pixels always convert (into Gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's luminance, a CMYK payload through ProPhoto RGB; out of Gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ RGB Color's conversion) and profile preserve refuses; color_conversion names the crossing (from or to "Gray", intent relative, black_point_compensation false). Between Grayscale documents the same Gray profile keeps the codes, and another one converts under convert and keeps the numbers under preserve. Another app's gray TIFF pastes the same way. Into or out of a Lab Color document the pixels always convert across modes: into Lab by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule (relative colorimetric, no black point compensation), out of Lab relative colorimetric with black point compensation, Grayscale and CMYK through 16-bit ProPhoto RGB; profile preserve refuses across modes. Between Lab documents both profiles keep the codes, and a 16-bit payload lands on an 8-bit document's grid. On an Indexed Color document the paste lands IN the one layer (layer 0; Paste Into and Outside mask it by the selection): the payload of any mode is converted to the document's RGB, merged and each changed pixel mapped to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 to the transparent index, or with none the entry nearest white), so a paste from an Indexed document of the same palette keeps every index. The reply adds working_memory_plan_bytes, the paste's admitted working memory. mode layers refuses for good: an Indexed Color document holds one layer, so a paste cannot add one. A Bitmap document: not available in Bitmap mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `convert` | `boolean` | no | — | Accepted and ignored (older recordings carry it): every paste converts. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `external` | `string` | no | one of `promote`, `refuse` | promote (default) or refuse: refuse rejects an image from another app at 16 bits and 32-bit float instead of promoting it. |
| `index` | `integer` | no | — | Anchor layer, as layer. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Anchor layer index (default: the active layer). A group is a legal anchor. |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `auto`, `layers`, `pixels` | auto (default): the copied layers when the clipboard holds a layers copy and the placement is auto, centered or in_place with no payload_path, else pixels — but into and outside are refused while a layers copy is held; layers requires a layers copy; pixels ignores it. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Default: an editable record's own layer name, otherwise "Pasted Layer". |
| `payload_path` | `string` | no | — | Absolute path to a .drcb payload file, pasted instead of the clipboard: the saved-payload form of a paste (what a saved-payload step replays, and what records one). |
| `placement` | `string` | no | one of `auto`, `centered`, `in_place`, `into`, `outside`, `at` | auto (default) — Edit ▸ Paste's rule: the selection's bounds, else the centre of the visible canvas; centered — the canvas centre; in_place — the offset the payload was copied from, or the same relative location on a canvas of another size; into / outside — centred on the selection's bounds and masked by the selection or its inverse; at — exactly at x, y. Pasted layers take auto, centered or in_place only. |
| `position` | `string` | no | one of `above`, `top`, `into_group` | Where the new layer lands relative to `layer`: above it (default), at the top of the root level, or as the top child of a group. |
| `profile` | `string` | no | one of `convert`, `preserve` | convert (default): pixels or layers in another profile are converted into this document's, keeping their appearance; preserve: Don't Convert — they keep their numbers and take this document's profile. |
| `record_payload` | `boolean` | no | — | While recording, save the landed payload as a .drcb file and record the step with payload_path, so the step replays without the clipboard. Pixel pastes only. A Doctored agent feature. Default false. |
| `view` | `integer` | no | — | Which view (window) placement auto reads its visible canvas from, as list_views reports it; omit it for view 1. Pixels and layers alike; not recorded. |
| `x` | `integer` | no | — | Placement at only (required with it): the pasted layer's left edge in canvas pixels. |
| `y` | `integer` | no | — | Placement at only (required with it): the pasted layer's top edge in canvas pixels. |

## `get_clipboard`

Reports what the clipboard holds: typed (a Doctored typed payload is present), mode ("rgb" or "cmyk", the typed payload's colour mode; null without one), info (its version, mode, storage, depth, origin_depth — 8 for an 8-bit copy, a CMYK copy's declared depth beside cmyk_depth — width, height, offset, ppi, profile_description, has_coverage, editable — null, or {type, name, anchor (artwork), record_bytes} for a copy carrying an editable record — and, for a float payload, tone_map), public_types, source (null, or the {width, height} of the canvas a Doctored copy was made on, which paste in_place reads) and layers: null, or the held layer clipboard's {records, depth, profile_description, width, height} while the clipboard still names it. A typed payload larger than the system pasteboard accepts (over 255 MiB) stays in this Doctored instance, named on the pasteboard by a token; other apps and other Doctored instances get only the flat TIFF/PNG. typed_store reports where the typed payload is: "pasteboard", "process" (held in this instance) or null. mode is "gray" for a payload copied from a Grayscale document. mode is "lab" for a Lab Color payload; its info carries lab_depth.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `new_from_clipboard`

Creates a new document from the clipboard and opens it (File ▸ New from Clipboard): a Doctored typed payload makes a document at the payload's own depth (8 for an 8-bit copy, 16, or 32-bit float with its tone map), profile and PPI, sized to its content — the box of every pixel with alpha > 0 (a fully transparent payload keeps its whole window); an image from another app makes an 8-bit document at its own size. A copied text or shape layer opens as that editable layer (still editable when its font is installed); a copied adjustment layer opens as an 8-bit document with the adjustment above a transparent "Background", whatever the source depth (origin_depth 8); a record that cannot be restored opens as pixels, with editable.reason saying why. A held layers copy (copy mode layers) makes a document the size of the copied layers' content box at their depth (a float copy at 16 bits), profile and PPI, with a white Background under the copied layers, each kept by name. Not recorded in actions. Reply: typed, origin_depth, depth, width, height, ppi, profile_description, tone_map (float), document, editable (null, or {type, restored, reason?}), trimmed (the payload was cut to its content box), source_offset ([x, y]: where the new canvas's origin sat on the source canvas; null for an image from another app), layers (the copied layers' record count for a layers copy, else null). A pixel copy of a Duotone document makes a Grayscale document of the copied gray at the source's Gray profile and depth, without the inks.

Takes no arguments.

## `list_guides`

Lists the document's GUIDES: non-printing lines the tools snap to, drawn across the whole canvas and never part of the picture. Each is {index, orientation, position}, sorted by orientation then position — so an index is stable only until the next guide edit. position is an absolute canvas pixel coordinate (x for a vertical guide, y for a horizontal one), measured from the canvas top-left, NOT from the ruler origin. The reply also carries the same ruler block get_document reports — origin_x/origin_y plus the app-wide ruler unit — so placing a guide relative to what a ruler LABELS needs no second call.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `add_guide`

Adds a guide — View ▸ New Guide…, and dragging one out of a ruler strip. position is an absolute canvas coordinate: x for a vertical guide (0 to the canvas width), y for a horizontal one (0 to the canvas height), both ends legal because a guide may sit exactly on an edge. It is NOT measured from the ruler origin, which get_document reports separately. A position another guide of the same orientation already occupies changes nothing and says so. Guides ride along with crop, canvas size, image size, rotate and flip exactly as the pixels do, and persist in .doctored. One undo step.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

Deletes one guide by its index in list_guides — the same edit as dragging it back into its ruler, or pressing Delete while it is grabbed. Indices shift after any guide edit, so read list_guides immediately before. One undo step.

## `set_ruler_origin`

Moves the rulers' zero point — dragging from the box where the two ruler strips meet (double-clicking it resets to 0, 0). x and y are canvas pixels inside the canvas. This affects ONLY what the on-screen rulers label and what View ▸ New Guide… seeds its field with: the grid, every snap target and every coordinate any tool reports or accepts stay measured from the canvas top-left. Document state, so it persists in .doctored and rides along with the geometry ops. One undo step.

## `list_channels`

Lists the document's ALPHA CHANNELS: named canvas-sized coverage planes (0 = out, 255 = in, in between = a soft edge) that are saved selections. A channel is never part of the picture — its overlay colour, opacity and color_indicates only say how the app draws it as a rubylith. Use the index or the name wherever a tool takes `channel`. The rows are get_document's channels array at every depth. spot is a SPOT channel's ink, {lab: D50 [L, a, b], solidity: 0–100}, its plane the ink's coverage (add_spot_channel), and null for an alpha channel. A Grayscale document holds alpha channels, as an RGB document does. On an Indexed Color document alpha channels work as on RGB and change no index; a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses (the one colour channel is Index).

| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `add_channel`

Adds an alpha channel — the Channels panel's New Channel, and Save Selection as Channel. from: "empty" (default) an all-zero channel; "selection" the current selection's coverage (errors when nothing is selected); "layer_alpha" a layer's transparency; "layer_mask" a layer's mask; "plane" one colour plane of the flattened composite. One undo step. In a Grayscale document from plane takes plane gray (the Gray row: the composite's own gray codes) or alpha; red, green and blue refuse for good. In a Lab Color document plane is lightness, a or b (the stored L*, a* and b* codes), luma (= Lightness) or alpha; red, green and blue refuse. On an Indexed Color document alpha channels work as on RGB and change no index; a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses (the one colour channel is Index).

## `load_selection`

Loads a plane as the selection — Select > Load Selection…, and ⌘-clicking a channel row or a layer thumbnail in the app. Sources: an alpha channel (default), a layer's transparency, a layer's mask, or one colour plane of the flattened composite. A selection is not an edit: one transient undo step and no file-dirty change. An all-zero source clears the selection and reports selection_empty. Select > Portrait Matte is from: "channel" with the matte's channel name ("Portrait Matte", "Skin", "Hair", "Teeth", "Glasses" or "Sky" on an iPhone photo). In a CMYK document from "plane" takes cyan, magenta, yellow or black (the plate's 1 − ink), luma (the composite's luminosity) or alpha; red, green and blue refuse by name. In a Grayscale document from plane takes plane gray (the Gray row: the composite's own gray codes, whatever the working Gray) or alpha; red, green and blue refuse for good. In a Lab Color document plane is lightness, a or b (the stored L*, a* and b* codes), luma (= Lightness) or alpha; red, green and blue refuse. On an Indexed Color document a colour selection samples the palette colours, each pixel its index's colour (so a duplicate entry's pixels select with its twin's); the selection, Quick Mask and alpha channels work as on RGB and change no index. A red, green, blue or alpha channel, or the luminosity, refuses (the one channel is Index).

## `save_selection`

Writes the current selection into an alpha channel — Select > Save Selection…. With `name` (or neither) it creates a new channel; with `channel` it combines into that existing one, where `mode` says how. Errors when nothing is selected. One undo step. On an Indexed Color document a colour selection samples the palette colours, each pixel its index's colour (so a duplicate entry's pixels select with its twin's); the selection, Quick Mask and alpha channels work as on RGB and change no index. A red, green, blue or alpha channel, or the luminosity, refuses (the one channel is Index). A Bitmap document: Save Selection on a Bitmap document is not built in Doctored: a Bitmap document holds no alpha channel; convert to Grayscale first.

Ignored without `channel`. The current selection is never changed. |

## `apply_image`

Image > Apply Image…: blends ONE source plane onto the target — a layer's pixels (as one colour, plane for plane), one colour plane of them, or an alpha channel — at an opacity. The source is a layer or the flattened composite ("merged"), read as its whole colour image, one plane, or a channel; source_plane "rgb" against a single-plane target uses the source's luma. Writes layer pixels destructively for a layer or plane target, so a re-editable text or shape layer drops its description. One undo step. Answers at 8 and 16 bits; a 32-bit float document refuses it by name (its blend runs on planes clamped to 0…1, which float pixels are not) — use calculations there, which writes a channel or a selection. On a CMYK document the target is the layer (its four ink plates, plate for plate, each a one-plane blend, so the HSL modes refuse), one ink plate (its stored 1 − ink) or an alpha channel, and source_plane "cmyk" is the CMYK composite: its matching plate onto the layer, its luminosity onto one plate or channel. In a Grayscale document target is layer (its Gray, blended as one plane and written R = G = B, one undo step) or channel:<name>; source_plane is gray, alpha or an alpha channel's name; blend_mode takes the Grayscale modes; a 32-bit Grayscale document refuses, as a float document. In a Lab Color document each channel's codes blend alone: target is layer (Lightness, a and b each from the source's own), lightness, a, b, alpha or channel:<name>; source_plane is lab (the composite or layer, channel for channel; Lightness onto one plane), lightness, a, b, alpha or an alpha channel's name; blend_mode takes Normal, Dissolve, Multiply, Linear Burn, Screen, Linear Dodge (Add), Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light and Hard Mix (a layer set to the same mode composites by its Lab arm instead).

| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `blend_mode` | `string` | no | one of `Normal`, `Dissolve`, `Darken`, `Multiply`, `Color Burn`, `Linear Burn`, `Darker Color`, `Lighten`, `Screen`, `Color Dodge`, `Linear Dodge (Add)`, `Lighter Color`, `Overlay`, `Soft Light`, `Hard Light`, `Vivid Light`, `Linear Light`, `Pin Light`, `Hard Mix`, `Difference`, `Exclusion`, `Subtract`, `Divide`, `Hue`, `Saturation`, `Color`, `Luminosity` | Any mode onto "layer", which blends the three planes as ONE colour. Onto a single plane or a channel the four HSL modes (Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity) are refused: they are defined over an RGB triple and say nothing about one 8-bit plane. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `invert` | `boolean` | no | — | Invert the source plane first (default false). |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `opacity` | `number` | no | 0–1 | — |
| `source` | `string` | no | — | "merged" (default) or a layer index. |
| `source_plane` | `string` | no | — | "rgb" (default), "red", "green", "blue", "luma", "alpha", or an alpha channel's name. On a CMYK document: "cmyk" (default), "cyan"/"magenta"/"yellow"/"black", "luma", "alpha" or an alpha channel's name. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | "layer" (default), "red"/"green"/"blue"/"alpha", or "channel:<name>"; on a CMYK document "layer", "cyan"/"magenta"/"yellow"/"black" or "channel:<name>". |

## `calculations`

Image > Calculations…: blends TWO source planes into a new plane, which becomes a new alpha channel (default) or the selection. Source 1 is the blend layer and source 2 the base it is applied to. Each source is a layer or "merged", one of its planes or a channel, optionally inverted. A new channel is one undo step; a selection is not an edit at all. Answers at every depth; in a 32-bit float document each colour or luma plane is read clamped to 0…1, and the result is 16-bit coverage as at 16 bits. On a CMYK document each source is the CMYK composite's luminosity ("cmyk"), one ink plate (its stored 1 − ink), luma, alpha or a channel. In a Grayscale document source1_plane and source2_plane are gray, alpha or an alpha channel's name, and blend_mode takes the Grayscale modes. In a Lab Color document source1_plane and source2_plane are lab (Lightness), lightness, a, b, alpha or an alpha channel's name, and blend_mode takes Normal, Dissolve, Multiply, Linear Burn, Screen, Linear Dodge (Add), Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light and Hard Mix, each on the codes.

Every other mode applies. (Onto a whole LAYER, apply_image does take them.) |
