## `add_luminosity_masks`

Select > Add Luminosity Masks: appends nine channels built from the composite's Rec. 709 luma L — "Lights 1".."Lights 3" (L, L², L³), "Darks 1".."Darks 3" ((1−L), (1−L)², (1−L)³) and "Midtones 1".."Midtones 3" (the complement of each squared pair, peaking at mid grey) — the photographer's tone-selection set. Load one with load_selection. Refused when nine more channels would not fit. One undo step. Answers at every depth; in a 32-bit float document L is the composite's linear luminance clamped to 0…1. Works on a CMYK document: Grow and Similar compare the ink as the Magic Wand does, the Magnetic Lasso reads the view, and the rest edit coverage. In a Lab Color document the nine masks read Lightness (the L* codes).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `rotate`

Rotates the whole document clockwise by ANY finite angle, normalized into (-180, 180]. What happens depends on the angle, and the core decides which it is. A whole number of full turns (0, 360, -720) moves nothing and answers {"ok": true, "changed": false} with a note — no undo step, no dirtying and no recorded Action step — at 8 bits, 16 bits and 32-bit float. A content-identical exact quarter turn has the same successful no-op and recording behavior. An EXACT quarter turn (90, 180, 270, -90, and 450 or -270, which normalize onto them) is a lossless permutation: re-editable text and shape layers stay re-editable because the op composes into their descriptions, the ppi axes swap, guides swap orientation with the picture, and it is available at all three depths. ANY OTHER angle is a destructive arbitrary rotation at EVERY depth: the canvas GROWS to the rotated bounding box (the reply reports the new canvas and the origin the old canvas's top-left landed at), every layer, every mask and every saved channel is resampled with `sampler`, and re-editable text and shape layers are re-rendered from their descriptions and stay re-editable. Guides are shifted by that origin and DROPPED if they leave the new canvas, the ruler origin is clamped, and the ppi is NOT transposed: 90 degrees and 89.999 degrees are deliberately different operations. The canvas may also SHRINK on an axis (100x10 at 80 degrees is 28x101). In a 32-bit float document the rotation resamples premultiplied extended-range samples: each layer's RGB is clamped to that layer's own visible range so ringing never leaves it, an output alpha below 2^-24 becomes transparent, and a float result past 67,108,864 pixels refuses before any work. A RAW layer turns with the rest at 8 and 16 bits: it is re-rendered from its retained source at the new angle. AFTER a recorded arbitrary rotation, later Action steps in `relative` or `anchor` geometry mode are remapped per axis against the expanded canvas, exactly as after any canvas-changing step — but the recorded space is no longer an axis-aligned copy of the original picture, so on a DIFFERENT-SIZE target those rectangles do not follow the rotated content. THREE BEHAVIOUR CHANGES from before this release: an unreadable `degrees` ("abc") used to be read as 90 and rotate silently and now refuses by name; 90.7 used to truncate to 90 and now rotates by 90.7; and 0, 45, 360, -270 and 450 used to be errors. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document a move or a nearest sampler (crop, canvas size, the quarter turns and flips, nearest resize, rotation and perspective crop) keeps every pixel's index exactly; any other sampler resamples the colours and maps each pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as new area). New canvas area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the current background colour); a crop past the canvas takes the entry nearest its background_color. On an Indexed Color document the reply adds working_memory_plan_bytes, the edit's admitted working memory. On a Bitmap document the quarter turns are bit-exact: every pixel keeps its bit. Any other angle refuses: Arbitrary rotation is not available in Bitmap mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `degrees` | `number` | yes | — | Any finite angle in degrees; POSITIVE IS CLOCKWISE. Normalized into (-180, 180]. It must be a number; an unreadable value refuses at every depth rather than rotating by 90 silently. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `sampler` | `string` | no | one of `nearest`, `bilinear`, `bicubic`, `catmull-rom`, `lanczos` | How a non-quarter rotation resamples (default bicubic, the same vocabulary as crop and transform_layer). Ignored on an identity or an exact quarter turn, which resample nothing. |

## `flip`

Flips the whole document. Re-editable text and shape layers stay re-editable: the op composes into their descriptions. Available at 8 bits, at 16 bits and in a 32-bit float document: a flip is an exact permutation, so no sample is ever combined. If the complete stored result is identical, the reply has changed:false and no undo, dirty or recorded Action step is added. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document a move or a nearest sampler (crop, canvas size, the quarter turns and flips, nearest resize, rotation and perspective crop) keeps every pixel's index exactly; any other sampler resamples the colours and maps each pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as new area). New canvas area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the current background colour); a crop past the canvas takes the entry nearest its background_color. On an Indexed Color document the reply adds working_memory_plan_bytes, the edit's admitted working memory. On a Bitmap document it is bit-exact: every pixel keeps its bit. New canvas area is the background, white.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `axis` | `string` | yes | one of `horizontal`, `vertical` | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `crop`

Crops the document to a rectangle (canvas coordinates, origin top-left). A nonzero angle straightens first — the Crop tool's straighten slider: every layer — and every alpha channel, so saved selections keep lining up — is rotated by −angle about the rect's center, then the canvas is cropped, as one undo step. Straightening resamples every layer's pixels; re-editable text and shape layers are re-rendered from their descriptions and stay re-editable. At angle 0 the crop only moves the canvas window and every description stays valid. A 16-bit document takes both: the straighten is ONE native op equal to rotating every layer, every mask and every channel and then cropping, in one undo step. A 32-bit float document takes both too: the zero-angle crop keeps every allocation and moves the window only, and the straighten resamples premultiplied extended-range samples, clamping each layer's RGB to that layer's own visible range so ringing never leaves it (an output alpha below 2^-24 becomes transparent). A zero-angle crop to the WHOLE canvas changes nothing and answers {"ok": true, "changed": false} with a note rather than an error, at every depth: no undo step and no dirtying. So does a non-zero angle too small to move any pixel of the whole canvas; over a smaller rectangle such an angle still crops. When straightening, take the box from fit_crop or detect_horizon's suggested_crop, or the corners show transparent wedges. Pixels outside the new canvas are kept (moving a layer reveals them) unless delete_cropped is true. A rectangle past any canvas edge (negative x or y, or beyond the far edge; at most 100 megapixels) EXTENDS the canvas, turned or not, as the Crop tool dragged past the canvas does: with delete_cropped true an opaque Background (the bottom layer: visible, Normal, 100%, unmasked, unstyled, canvas-sized and fully opaque) is filled with background_color in the new area, and every other layer's new area is transparent (with delete_cropped false nothing is filled). Such a reply adds "extended": true and "planned_bytes". fill (the Crop tool's Fill popup) chooses what that new area holds, only for a rectangle past the canvas: background (default, the Background fill above); content_aware runs Content-Aware Fill (default settings) on the bottom layer over the new area, grown by the sampler's reach on a turned crop so no pad-coloured seam is left, and needs that layer to be the opaque Background (delete_cropped is forced on; false is refused); generative_expand sends the picture to a cloud image model as generative_expand does (prompt, provider, variations, gated the same way) and lands the answer on a new Generative Layer above the active layer, masked to the new area. Either is one undo step with the crop and one waited job; its reply is the job's report with "extended": true, "fill" and "planned_bytes". A generative_expand crop is not recorded into Actions. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. A crop past the canvas pads the Background with background_color converted by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule; Generative Expand fills the new area (fill generative_expand), its pictures landing as L*a*b* codes by the same rule. On an Indexed Color document a move or a nearest sampler (crop, canvas size, the quarter turns and flips, nearest resize, rotation and perspective crop) keeps every pixel's index exactly; any other sampler resamples the colours and maps each pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as new area). New canvas area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the current background colour); a crop past the canvas takes the entry nearest its background_color. On a Bitmap document a crop at angle 0 is bit-exact: every pixel keeps its bit. A rectangle past the canvas fills with background_color thresholded to black or white (white by default); fill other than background refuses (Generative Expand and Content-Aware Fill are not available in Bitmap mode). A nonzero angle runs on the 8-bit gray storage with its sampler and every pixel goes back white where its gray over the background at its alpha reaches 128, else black; a whole-pixel move or nearest sampler keeps each bit.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `angle` | `number` | no | -45–45 | Straighten angle in degrees (-45 to 45, default 0): the content rotates by −angle, so a positive angle turns the picture counter-clockwise on screen — the same sign as the app's Straighten field. It must be a number; an unreadable value refuses at every depth rather than cropping silently. |
| `background_color` | `string` | no | — | The Background fill of a rectangle past the canvas, #RRGGBB (default #FFFFFF, the Crop tool's background swatch). Read only for such a rectangle. |
| `delete_cropped` | `boolean` | no | — | The Crop tool's Delete Cropped Pixels (default false): each plain raster layer is trimmed to the new canvas, and one wholly outside becomes empty. Masks, groups, adjustment layers and re-editable text, shape and placed layers keep their pixels. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `fill` | `string` | no | one of `background`, `generative_expand`, `content_aware` | What a rectangle past the canvas fills its new area with (default background). Refused for a rectangle inside the canvas. |
| `height` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `prompt` | `string` | no | — | fill generative_expand only: what to add in the new area; empty continues the picture. |
| `provider` | `string` | no | one of `openai`, `gemini`, `fal` | fill generative_expand only: the cloud provider (default openai). |
| `sampler` | `string` | no | one of `nearest`, `bilinear`, `bicubic`, `catmull-rom`, `lanczos` | How the straighten resamples (default bicubic, the same vocabulary as transform_layer). Ignored at angle 0, which resamples nothing. The Crop tool straightens with whatever the Free Transform options bar is set to, so a recorded straighten carries that choice here. |
| `variations` | `integer` | no | 1–3 | fill generative_expand only: how many pictures to ask for (default 3). |
| `width` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `x` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `y` | `integer` | yes | — | — |

## `image_size`

Scales the whole document to a new size (max 100 megapixels). Re-editable text and shape layers stay re-editable: the scale composes into their descriptions, and text and shapes re-render crisply. Alpha channels are canvas-sized and are resampled too, so a document carrying many of them is refused past the format's total channel-pixel budget (900 million): the error names how many the new canvas would hold, and delete_channel is the way out. The Image Size sheet can present dimensions as percentages of the pixel size captured when the sheet opened; each scaled axis rounds to the nearest integer pixel, halfway away from zero. This tool and recorded Image Size steps deliberately take those resolved integer pixels, not a relative percentage, so replay always reproduces the accepted result. Refused on a document whose evaluation policy is linear_light: Image Size resamples in the stored encoding, which linear-light evaluation does not support yet (get_evaluation reports the sentence). A 32-bit float document is linear light by construction and is NOT refused: its samples are already linear, so it resamples them directly. Available in a 32-bit float document: the resample is premultiplied over the extended-range samples, each layer's RGB is clamped to that layer's own visible range so a filter's ringing never leaves it, an output alpha below 2^-24 becomes transparent, and a float result past 67,108,864 pixels refuses before any work. Masks stay 16-bit coverage and resample exactly as at 16 bits. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document a move or a nearest sampler (crop, canvas size, the quarter turns and flips, nearest resize, rotation and perspective crop) keeps every pixel's index exactly; any other sampler resamples the colours and maps each pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as new area). New canvas area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the current background colour); a crop past the canvas takes the entry nearest its background_color. On a Bitmap document it runs on the 8-bit gray storage with its sampler and every pixel goes back white where its gray over the background at its alpha reaches 128, else black; area it uncovers takes the background, white; a whole-pixel move or nearest sampler keeps each bit.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `filter` | `string` | no | one of `nearest`, `bilinear`, `catmull-rom`, `lanczos3` | Resampling filter, default lanczos3. |
| `height` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `width` | `integer` | yes | — | — |

## `canvas_size`

Resizes the canvas WITHOUT scaling the pixels; the anchor pins the existing content. Layers keep their pixels and can extend outside the canvas; alpha channels are padded with 0. GROWING the canvas grows every channel with it, so the same total channel-pixel budget image_size names can refuse it — delete channels and retry. Available at 8 bits, at 16 bits and in a 32-bit float document: the operation reads no sample, so every layer, mask and guide simply moves by the anchor's offset. A RAW layer rides the canvas and keeps its source — no rasterize needed. A call that would change NOTHING — the same width and height, whatever the anchor — SUCCEEDS with changed: false and a note: it adds no undo step and does not dirty the document, at 8 bits, at 16 bits and at 32-bit float alike, so a recorded canvas_size step replays cleanly on a document that is already the target size and a batch normalizing canvas size across mixed inputs does not halt on the files that already match. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document a move or a nearest sampler (crop, canvas size, the quarter turns and flips, nearest resize, rotation and perspective crop) keeps every pixel's index exactly; any other sampler resamples the colours and maps each pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as new area). New canvas area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the current background colour); a crop past the canvas takes the entry nearest its background_color. On a Bitmap document it is bit-exact: every pixel keeps its bit. New canvas area is the background, white.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `anchor` | `string` | no | one of `top-left`, `top`, `top-right`, `left`, `center`, `right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom`, `bottom-right` | Where the existing content is pinned; default center. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `height` | `integer` | yes | — | — |
| `width` | `integer` | yes | — | — |

## `group_layers`

Wraps the given layers in a new GROUP and selects it. They must all sit in the same group already (get_document reports each layer's parent), and a group cannot be grouped with one of its own children. The new group is Pass Through at 100 %, so its children keep compositing against the layers below it exactly as before — grouping alone never changes the picture. The reply carries the group's index, its children's NEW indices, and two things the operation had to change: cleared_clip (the bottom layer's clipping mask was released, because the layer it clipped to stayed outside) and reordered (a non-contiguous set is gathered together, so layers left between them change their relative order). Works on a CMYK document: groups, clipping masks and merges composite in ink.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | yes | 1–unbounded items | The layers to group. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Group name; default "Group N". |

## `ungroup_layers`

Dissolves a group: its children take its place at its level, in order, and the group entry disappears. A group's own mask, style, opacity, blend mode and clipped flag cannot be expressed on its children, so they are DISCARDED — the reply's discarded array names whichever of them was set, and undo restores the group. The reply also carries cleared_clip: the bottom layer of the group was clipped to nothing inside it, so its clipping mask is RELEASED rather than silently re-pointed at the layer below the group (the mirror of group_layers' own cleared_clip). Works on a CMYK document: groups, clipping masks and merges composite in ink.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `index` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |

## `set_layer_lock`

Sets a layer's locks, replacing whatever it had. transparency freezes the ALPHA channel — every pixel keeps its alpha exactly: a transparent pixel stays empty, and on a semi-transparent one paint mixes in at its own opacity × coverage, not boosted by the kept alpha, so the layer's shape cannot change and an eraser cannot punch a hole; pixels refuses every pixel edit (the layer's MASK can still be painted); position refuses moves, offsets and transforms; all is the three together and additionally freezes the mask. A transform is a POSITION edit, never a pixel one: a transparency-locked layer still transforms. A GROUP's locks cover its contents: every layer inside a locked group answers to the group's locks as well as its own, and a refusal names the group to unlock. Locks never block delete, duplicate, reorder, group, rename, opacity, blend mode, visibility or styles. Pass `layers` instead of `layer` to write the same set to several entries as ONE undo step — what the Layer > Lock menu does over a multi-selection; an entry that already carries exactly those locks is skipped. Answers at every depth: 16-bit and 32-bit float layers carry the same locks with the same meanings. On an Indexed Color document the one layer takes a name, a colour label, locks, visibility (hidden, it renders clear, keeps its indices and saves hidden in .doctored; a kept-palette export refuses until it is shown) and an offset (a whole-pixel move: the layer stays canvas-sized at the origin, so the offset reads 0 after and pixels moved past the canvas are dropped); open applies to groups only; opacity and blend mode are not available in Indexed Color.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | no | — | Several layers, exclusive with `layer`/`index`. In a recorded Action this is {"$layers": "selected"}. |
| `locks` | `array<string>` | yes | items: one of `transparency`, `pixels`, `position`, `all`, `none` | The locks to set; [] or ["none"] unlocks. |

## `align_layers`

Aligns the given layers' CONTENT bounds — content_x/y/width/height in get_document, the box of actually opaque pixels, NOT the pixel buffer rect — to one edge of the selection's union (to: layers, the default) or of the canvas (to: canvas). A layer with nothing opaque in it is skipped. Linked layers and a group's children follow the move; a position lock anywhere in that expanded set refuses the whole call BY NAME, even on a layer this alignment would not have moved. A pixel selection is never the reference here. Answers at 8 bits, 16 bits and 32-bit float. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document it runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good: it needs more than one layer, and an Indexed Color document holds one.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `edge` | `string` | yes | one of `left`, `horizontal_center`, `right`, `top`, `vertical_center`, `bottom` | — |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | yes | 1–unbounded items | The layers to align. |
| `to` | `string` | no | one of `layers`, `canvas` | What to align to; default layers (their union). |

## `distribute_layers`

Spaces the given layers evenly along one axis: the two outermost keep their positions and the GAPS between adjacent CONTENT bounds are made equal (distribute spacing, not distribute centers). Needs at least three layers with opaque pixels. A gap can come out negative when the content is wider than the span; that is arithmetic, not an error. Like align_layers it moves through the expanded set — linked layers and a group's children — and a position lock anywhere in it refuses the whole call by name. Answers at 8 bits, 16 bits and 32-bit float. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document it runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good: it needs more than one layer, and an Indexed Color document holds one.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `axis` | `string` | yes | one of `horizontal`, `vertical` | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | yes | 3–unbounded items | The layers to distribute. |

## `link_layers`

Links the given layers: from now on each of them moves and transforms with the others whatever the call targets. Linking is not a group — the stack is unchanged and nothing composites differently. get_document reports the link id as linked. Answers at every depth. A Grayscale document takes it as on an RGB document. A Lab Color document takes it as on an RGB document. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good: it needs more than one layer, and an Indexed Color document holds one.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | yes | 2–unbounded items | The layers to link. |

## `unlink_layers`

Clears the given layers' link. A link group left with a single member is cleared too, since a link of one is not a link. Answers at every depth. A Grayscale document takes it as on an RGB document. A Lab Color document takes it as on an RGB document. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good: it needs more than one layer, and an Indexed Color document holds one.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | yes | 1–unbounded items | The layers to unlink. |

## `layer_via_copy`

Copies the current selection out of a layer into a NEW layer directly above it, at the same canvas position (Layer ▸ Layer Via Copy, ⌘J). With no selection the whole layer is copied. This op RASTERIZES: the new layer keeps neither a text/shape description nor a layer style, and a group or an adjustment layer is refused — use duplicate_layer, which keeps all of them. (The app's ⌘J routes those cases, and a multi-selection, to Duplicate Layer for exactly this reason: this tool takes ONE layer, so a set would silently lose all but the first.) Answers at every depth (a 16-bit reply adds storage: rgba16_unorm and a 32-bit float one storage: rgba32_float; a whole-layer copy keeps the pixels the layer holds outside the canvas at every depth). In a 32-bit float document the copy keeps each linear RGB value exactly, above white and below zero included, and weights alpha by the selection. Works on a CMYK document: ink is copied exactly; into an RGB document the layers convert (relative colorimetric with BPC). In a Lab Color document it runs on the L*a*b* codes, as on RGB.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | — |

## `layer_via_cut`

Layer Via Copy that also CLEARS the selection from the source layer (⇧⌘J). Same rasterizing rules, and the source layer's own locks apply to the clear half — a pixel-locked source refuses the whole call. On a text or shape layer the description is dropped and the reply says so. Answers at every depth; in a 32-bit float document the cut lowers the source's alpha by the selection and leaves its RGB values as they are. Works on a CMYK document: ink is copied exactly; into an RGB document the layers convert (relative colorimetric with BPC). In a Lab Color document it runs on the L*a*b* codes, as on RGB.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | — |

## `merge_visible`

Replaces every layer that CONTRIBUTES to the picture — visible, with every enclosing group visible — with one flat layer holding the current composite. Everything that does not contribute SURVIVES untouched, including a visible layer inside a hidden group. Needs at least two contributing raster layers. Answers at every depth; the flat layer is canvas-sized at every depth, like 8-bit, so anything a contributing layer held outside the canvas is discarded. It bakes the current composite, so a layer with knockout bakes EXACTLY — like flatten_image and stamp_visible. Works on a CMYK document: groups, clipping masks and merges composite in ink.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `stamp_visible`

Adds the current composite as a NEW layer and leaves every existing layer alone (⇧⌥⌘E). The new layer lands UNCLIPPED directly above the given layer's whole subtree, at that layer's own level. Answers at every depth, and it is canvas-sized at every depth, like 8-bit. In 16-bit and 32-bit float documents it needs one contributing RASTER layer; an adjustment layer does not count. Works on a CMYK document: groups, clipping masks and merges composite in ink.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `above` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Layer name; default "Stamp". |

## `arrange_layer`

Moves a layer within its own group: to the front, one step forward, one step backward, or to the back AMONG ITS SIBLINGS. It never moves a layer into or out of a group — reorder_layer with a depth does that. The reply gives the layer's new index. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good: it needs more than one layer, and an Indexed Color document holds one.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `to` | `string` | yes | one of `front`, `forward`, `backward`, `back` | — |

## `auto_select_layer`

Which layer a Move-tool click at (x, y) would activate: the topmost one whose own coverage there is at least half, skipping hidden layers and adjustment layers. With group: true the answer is that layer's top-level GROUP instead. Answers layer: null when nothing opaque is under the point — a miss, not an error. Activates the layer it found unless activate is false, replacing the selection or — with mode: "add" — adding to it and becoming the primary, which is what a ⇧-click on the canvas does.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `activate` | `boolean` | no | — | Make the found layer active (default true). |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `group` | `boolean` | no | — | Answer the top-level group instead of the layer. |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add` | replace (default) makes the hit layer the whole selection; add appends it and makes it primary. |
| `x` | `number` | yes | — | — |
| `y` | `number` | yes | — | — |

## `set_selected_layers`

Selects several layers at once — what the app's ⇧/⌘-click multi-selection does. It only retargets the app's own set-aware commands and adds no undo step; the tools here always take their own explicit layers array, so a script never needs this except to leave the app in a particular state.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | yes | 1–unbounded items | The layers to select. |
| `primary` | `integer` | no | — | Which of them becomes the active layer; default the topmost. |

## `transform_layers`

Apply one affine matrix or one perspective quad to a layer set, group descendants, linked entries and linked masks atomically. Editable artwork stays editable under affine geometry; true perspective requires rasterize_artwork:true and reports the exact rasterized layer indices. The canvas is unchanged. duplicate:true mirrors Layer ▸ Free Transform a Copy (⌥⌘T) with no selection: it duplicates layers (unlinked copies, directly above their sources), transforms the COPIES with the same matrix or quad and records ONE "Transform Copy" step; the copies become the selection. The reply adds duplicate and copies, and layers lists the copies' subtrees. An identity matrix answers changed:false with copies [] and duplicates nothing. It refuses a Position lock on an original's subtree. The copies take the UI's described rules: at 8 bits ONE copied text or shape layer under a matrix or a parallelogram composes into its own description and stays editable; otherwise the rules above apply to the copies — a true perspective over described copies needs rasterize_artwork:true, and rasterized_layers lists the copies whose description was dropped (indices in the resulting document). An optional pivot [x, y] (only with matrix) records the point the matrix was built around; it does not change the result here, and a relative Action replay keeps the angle, scale and skew about it. Available in a 32-bit float document: the resample is premultiplied over the extended-range samples, each layer's RGB is clamped to that layer's own visible range so a filter's ringing never leaves it, an output alpha below 2^-24 becomes transparent, and a float result past 67,108,864 pixels refuses before any work. Masks stay 16-bit coverage and resample exactly as at 16 bits. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document the one layer transforms in place: a whole-pixel translation, or a nearest sampler (and, for selected pixels, a selection with no partial coverage), keeps every pixel's index exactly, a floated transparent pixel landing nothing; any other edit resamples the colours and maps each changed pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as uncovered area), unchanged pixels keeping theirs. Uncovered area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour. A warp is applied at once and keeps no editable field (get_warp answers null; clear and bake change nothing). duplicate on transform_layers or transform_again refuses (a copy makes a second layer). Selected pixels of an alpha channel (target {channel: n}) transform as on RGB, the layer untouched; a mask target refuses for good (an Indexed layer holds no mask), and a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses (the one channel is Index). On an Indexed Color document a changed reply adds working_memory_plan_bytes, the edit's admitted working memory. A Bitmap document: not available in Bitmap mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `corners` | `array<array<number>>` | no | 4–4 items | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `duplicate` | `boolean` | no | default `False` | — |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | yes | 1–unbounded items | — |
| `matrix` | `array<number>` | no | 6–6 items | — |
| `pivot` | `array<number>` | no | 2–2 items | — |
| `rasterize_artwork` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `sampler` | `string` | no | one of `nearest`, `bilinear`, `bicubic`, `lanczos` | — |
| `source_rect` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | — |

## `get_warp`

Read one layer's re-editable displacement lattice. The layer index is bottom-first; an absent layer means the active layer. A CMYK document keeps no warp field: field is null. In a Lab Color document it runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. The warp is applied at once and keeps no field (get_warp answers null), as in a Grayscale, CMYK or 32-bit document.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | — |

## `warp_layer`

Set, clear or bake one persisted warp at native depth. A set has a 2…16 by 2…16 row-major lattice in the original plane's pixel-edge rectangle. Each finite dx/dy is within 30000 pixels and every cell obeys the non-folding contraction bound. Pixels move a linked mask; mask-only accepts raster, group and adjustment masks. An unlinked mask stays exact. The whole plane is warped, regardless of selection. In a 32-bit float document a set resamples premultiplied extended-range samples and is applied at once: it keeps no re-editable field, so get_warp reports null and clear and bake change nothing. Each set warps the current pixels again, its lattice over the current layer bounds; undo to adjust or remove a warp. Bake before other geometry or paint. Encoded-space bilinear or bicubic sampling preserves the original for re-edit and native save. Available in a 32-bit float document: the resample is premultiplied over the extended-range samples, each layer's RGB is clamped to that layer's own visible range so a filter's ringing never leaves it, an output alpha below 2^-24 becomes transparent, and a float result past 67,108,864 pixels refuses before any work. Masks stay 16-bit coverage and resample exactly as at 16 bits. In a CMYK document a warp is applied at once to the ink (and a linked mask) and keeps no re-editable field: get_warp answers null, clear and bake change nothing, and each warp reshapes the current pixels. In a Grayscale document a warp is applied at once and keeps no field (get_warp answers null; clear and bake change nothing), as at 32 bits and in CMYK. In a Lab Color document it runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. The warp is applied at once and keeps no field (get_warp answers null), as in a Grayscale, CMYK or 32-bit document. On an Indexed Color document the one layer transforms in place: a whole-pixel translation, or a nearest sampler (and, for selected pixels, a selection with no partial coverage), keeps every pixel's index exactly, a floated transparent pixel landing nothing; any other edit resamples the colours and maps each changed pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as uncovered area), unchanged pixels keeping theirs. Uncovered area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour. A warp is applied at once and keeps no editable field (get_warp answers null; clear and bake change nothing). duplicate on transform_layers or transform_again refuses (a copy makes a second layer). Selected pixels of an alpha channel (target {channel: n}) transform as on RGB, the layer untouched; a mask target refuses for good (an Indexed layer holds no mask), and a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses (the one channel is Index).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `columns` | `integer` | no | 2–16 | — |
| `displacements` | `array<array<number>>` | no | — | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `filter` | `string` | no | one of `bilinear`, `bicubic` | — |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | — |
| `operation` | `string` | yes | one of `set`, `clear`, `bake` | — |
| `rows` | `integer` | no | 2–16 | — |
| `target` | `string` | no | one of `pixels`, `mask` | — |

## `puppet_warp`

Bends a layer by pins on a triangle mesh — Edit ▸ Puppet Warp. The mesh covers the layer's opaque pixels grown by expansion px; each pin holds the mesh vertex nearest its from and moves it to its to, and the rest of the mesh follows as rigidly as it can (as-rigid-as-possible). mode rigid resists every stretch, distort allows uniform scaling, normal is between. density fewer, normal or more sets how fine the mesh is. A pin's depth decides what draws on top where the mesh overlaps itself; rotate fixes the mesh's angle at the pin. With a selection active, only the selected pixels float and warp; they land source-over and leave a hole where they were, and the selection stays. The layer is resampled once (bicubic) as one undo step; the layer form grows to the deformed mesh. Unmoved, unrotated pins answer changed: false and add no undo step. The reply carries the pins snapped to their vertices ({from, to}), the mesh's vertices and triangles, storage and write_scope. Refused by name: no pins, more than 256, a pin outside the mesh, two pins on one vertex, a layer with no pixels at the expansion, a result past the pixel limit, a group or adjustment layer, and a locked layer. 8-, 16- and 32-bit float documents; a float layer keeps each colour within the range its visible pixels hold. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document it runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good. A Duotone document refuses it for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `density` | `string` | no | one of `fewer`, `normal`, `more` | Default normal. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `expansion` | `integer` | no | -100–100 | How far the mesh reaches past the opaque pixels, in px (default 2; negative pulls it in). |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `rigid`, `normal`, `distort` | Default normal. |
| `pins` | `array<object>` | yes | 1–256 items | The pins, 1-256. |
| `pins[].depth` | `integer` | no | -1000–1000 | Pin Depth (default 0): where the mesh overlaps itself, the part nearest the higher-depth pin draws on top. |
| `pins[].from` | `array<number>` | with parent | 2–2 items | [x, y] in canvas px, inside the mesh: the pin snaps to the nearest vertex of the mesh triangle there. |
| `pins[].rotate` | `['number', 'null']` | no | — | Fixed rotation in degrees, clockwise on the canvas, of the mesh at the pin; null or absent is Auto. |
| `pins[].to` | `array<number>` | with parent | 2–2 items | [x, y] in canvas px where that vertex lands, moved by to - from when from is not exactly the vertex. |

## `perspective_warp`

Warps a layer by planes — Edit ▸ Perspective Warp. Each quad names a plane of the picture (from: its four corners, such as a building face or a table top) and where those corners go (to); the plane is resampled through its own homography. Quads whose from corners coincide share that corner (its to must match) and, along a common side, an edge: joined planes stay continuous there. The rest of the layer follows as rigidly as it can, continuing each plane across its border. straighten levels or plumbs edges exactly (the warped corners move; the first entry per edge that applies is kept). With a selection active, only the selected pixels float and warp; they land source-over and leave a hole where they were, and the selection stays. The layer is resampled once (bicubic) as one undo step and grows to the warped extent. Unmoved corners answer changed: false and add no undo step. The reply carries the resolved quads ({from, to}, straightening applied), the shared edges as pairs of from points, storage and write_scope. Refused by name: no quads or more than 64, a malformed quad, a degenerate quad (three corners in a line or self-crossing), a warped quad that folds or turns the other way, joined corners warped apart, a bad straighten entry, a result past the pixel limit, a group or adjustment layer, and a locked layer. 8-, 16- and 32-bit float documents; a float layer keeps each colour within the range its visible pixels hold. This rewrites the layer's pixels, so a text or shape layer drops its description (undo restores it). Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document it runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. A Duotone document refuses it for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP — get_document says which, and a group has no pixels of its own. |
| `quads` | `array<object>` | yes | 1–64 items | The planes, 1-64. |
| `quads[].from` | `array<number>` | with parent | 8–8 items | [x0, y0, x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3] in canvas px: the plane's four corners in the picture, any consistent winding, convex with no three in a line. |
| `quads[].to` | `array<number>` | with parent | 8–8 items | The same four corners where they go (the pins), in the same order; convex, turning the same way. |
| `straighten` | `array<object>` | no | 0–256 items | Edges to level or plumb (Shift-click in Warp). |
| `straighten[].direction` | `['string', 'number']` | no | — | auto (default: horizontal within 30° of level, vertical within 30° of plumb, else as drawn), near_horizontal or near_vertical (only when within 30° of that axis), horizontal, vertical, or an angle in degrees, clockwise on the canvas. |
| `straighten[].edge` | `integer` | with parent | 0–3 | Edge k runs from corner k to corner k + 1 (mod 4). |
| `straighten[].quad` | `integer` | with parent | 0–∞ | The quad's index. |

## `undo`

Undoes the most recent edit. An undo whose state's display goes over the working limit still proceeds and returns memory_warning naming the overage. While a job is still running on the document it refuses, naming the job_id: cancel_job it or wait for job_status, then undo.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `redo`

Redoes the most recently undone edit. A redo whose state's display goes over the working limit still proceeds and returns memory_warning naming the overage. While a job is still running on the document it refuses, naming the job_id: cancel_job it or wait for job_status, then redo.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `save_copy`

Exports the document to a file without changing the open document. Format comes from the extension (.tif/.tiff and .jpg/.jpeg both work) unless given explicitly. doctored (.doctored) writes the full layered document (layers, masks, metadata); rz is its legacy name and writes the same file; raster formats flatten. The result's "wrote" and "dropped" arrays name what the chosen format actually carried. flat_save_losses lists editing state or sidecar data the flat copy cannot preserve on reopen; get_document.save_preservation: save_types/save_as_types are File > Save's policy; losses_by_format is what a flat copy in each format loses (on a 16-bit document, save_copy's flat_save_losses at the highest depth it writes in that format — 16 for png/tiff, else 8 — and heic and avif at export_image's 16; a 32-bit float document reports it the same way, its 16-bit copy tone-mapped). A kind is dropped when the format cannot hold it, when it was too large for the format's segment, or when you asked for it to be left out. metadata_not_captured: true means the source file's EXIF/XMP/IPTC was never read in (a platform-decoded HEIC or Live Photo), so none of it could travel out either. 16-bit master exports keep the master unchanged and report depth/alpha/structure losses. A 32-bit float master's flat copy at 8 or 16 bits is tone-mapped through the document's tone map (the export workspace's float stage) and reports master_bit_depth 32. At bit_depth 32 a float master writes its samples untone-mapped as tiff, OpenEXR (.exr: associated alpha, ZIP, the document profile's primaries as chromaticities) or Radiance (.hdr: RGBE, opaque, values below zero written as zero) — the same bytes export_image writes for those settings — and flat_save_losses names what each container has no place for. save_copy writes no HEIC or AVIF; an HDR photo (hdr_encoding gain_map or pq at bit_depth 32) is export_image's. A CMYK document saves as doctored (or rz), tiff or jpeg (CMYK, its composite on paper, at its declared depth; JPEG 8-bit); export_psd writes its layers as a PSD, PSB or layered TIFF. flat_save_losses is File > Save's own list: the layers, masks, styles, layer properties, bounds, saved channels, guides, paths and transparency the flat file has no place for, empty when it reopens as the document. A Grayscale document saves as doctored (or rz), png, tiff or jpeg: the image formats as ONE channel (two with transparency) with its Gray profile embedded, bit_depth 16 by default (8 for jpeg and an 8-bit document, 32 for a 32-bit document's tiff: a one-channel float TIFF); a PSD is export_psd's, and every other format refuses (convert to RGB Color first). At 8 and 16 bits flat_save_losses is File > Save's own list for the copy's depth: the layers, masks, styles, layer properties, bounds, saved channels, guides, color samplers, paths, layer comps and global light the file has no place for (and transparency in jpeg), empty when the copy reopens as the document. A Lab Color document saves as doctored (or rz) or tiff: a TIFF 6.0 CIELab file of the flattened composite at the document's own depth (another bit_depth refuses), no ICC profile; export_psd writes its PSD, and every other format refuses (export_image writes an RGB copy). An Indexed Color document saves doctored (or rz), png, gif or tiff (tif), keeping its palette, transparent index and every index (bit_depth 8 and dither none by default; flat_save_losses names what the copy drops); every other format refuses: use export_image for an RGB copy or convert_mode rgb. A Duotone document saves doctored (or rz) only, keeping its inks; PSD and PSB are export_psd's and every other format is an export through its inks, so other formats refuse by that sentence. A Bitmap document saves doctored (or rz), a 1-bit png, tif or bmp keeping its plane (the reply's bit_depth is 1), or jpg through its 8-bit Grayscale render (bit_depth 8, the loss named in flat_save_losses); bit_depth defaults to 8 and no other value is taken for the 1-bit files. Every other format refuses; convert_mode gray first.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `bit_depth` | `integer` | no | one of `8`, `16`, `32` | 16-bit master flat export: 16 (default) for PNG/TIFF, or explicit 8 for deliberate reduction. 32 is a 32-bit float document's exact copy as tiff, exr or hdr, and the default for exr and hdr, which exist at no other depth. Native retains its mode and refuses this option. |
| `dither` | `string` | no | one of `none`, `ordered` | 8-bit output RGB dithering; alpha is rounded without dithering. Refused for native output. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `embed_profile` | `boolean` | no | — | Embed the document's ICC profile (default true). PNG, JPEG, TIFF and WebP can carry one; BMP and GIF cannot. |
| `float_samples` | `string` | no | one of `f32`, `f16` | bit_depth 32 only: f32 (default) or f16, the nearest 16-bit half, for tiff and exr. hdr has one sample form (RGBE) and refuses f16. |
| `format` | `string` | no | one of `doctored`, `rz`, `png`, `jpeg`, `tiff`, `bmp`, `gif`, `webp`, `exr`, `hdr` | exr (OpenEXR) and hdr (Radiance) are 32-bit float deliverables: written only from a 32-bit float document, at bit_depth 32. |
| `jpeg_quality` | `integer` | no | 1–100 | — |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | — |
| `strip_metadata` | `boolean` | no | — | Drop EXIF/XMP/IPTC (default false). Kept packets are re-spliced with the EXIF orientation reset to 1, since the rotation is already baked into the pixels. |

## `list_actions`

Lists the saved Actions — named, replayable sequences of these tools. Mirrors the Actions window's list. Files that could not be read come back in "broken" with the exact reason, never silently dropped. With `name` the reply also carries `parameters` (what run_action and run_batch must be given) and `missing_assets` (the full paths of {"$asset": …} files that are not there, so a broken bundle is visible BEFORE a run changes anything).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Omit to list every action; give one to return that action's full steps. |

## `run_action`

Plays a saved Action on a document, as ONE undo step for the whole run. Mirrors the Actions window's Play button. Steps that reference "the active layer" or "the current selection" resolve against THIS document. A step's coordinates are absolute canvas pixels unless it carries a "geometry" mode, so a size difference on an absolute step is reported in canvas_mismatch rather than guessed at. Values for the action's declared parameters go in `parameters`; a missing required one, an unknown name or a wrong-typed value refuses the whole call with NOTHING applied — list_actions {name} reports what it declares. It never asks: a failed step follows its own on_error, or stop_on_error when given; the Continue / Stop prompt belongs to the Actions window's Play.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | — |
| `parameters` | `object` | no | — | Values for the action's declared parameters, as {name: value}. Every declared name without a default has to be here. |
| `stop_on_error` | `boolean` | no | — | Overrides every step's own on_error for this run. |

## `save_action`

Creates or replaces an Action. Mirrors Stop Recording > name it, and the Actions window's JSON editor. Each step is {"tool", "arguments", optional "enabled", "on_error", "note"} with document_id omitted — the player rebinds it. Write {"$layer": "active"} for the active layer, {"$layer": "Sky"} for one by name, {"$layers": "selected"} for the current layer selection. Schema 2 adds four more: {"$layer": {"name", "id", "session"}} resolves by its STABLE id when `session` matches get_document's identity_session; in another session by its id only when that layer also carries the recorded name (layer ids are persisted in the file), otherwise by name. Its {"$channel": …} twin resolves by its id only when `session` matches (channel ids are per-launch), otherwise by name; {"$param": "<name>"} is a declared parameter's value; {"$asset": "<file>"} is a file in the action's bundle, which only package_action writes. A step may also carry "geometry": {"mode": "absolute" (the default) | "relative" | "anchor", "anchor": "bottom-right"}, which remaps its canvas coordinates onto a differently sized document and needs recorded_canvas. A file is written at schema 1 when it uses none of those. Every step is validated before a byte is written, and an unknown tool is refused by step index. A step may not name, for example, a tool that runs or edits actions or batches (run_action, run_batch, save_action, delete_action, list_actions, start_recording, stop_recording, package_action, import_action), writes a file to a literal path (save_copy, export_image, export_pdf, export_psd), closes the document, or writes a preset, policy or workspace library; the refusal gives the reason and, where there is one, what to record instead. save_copy's recorded path is absolute, so a batch would write every file over that one path: record quick_export (a destination plus a pattern containing {name}, never overwriting) or let Batch choose the folder, the format and the name. undo and redo are refused as steps as well: an action IS one undo entry, so an undo inside it throws the document's redo history away and reports success.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | — |
| `overwrite` | `boolean` | no | — | Replace an action of this name (default false). |
| `parameters` | `array<object>` | no | — | Declared parameters: [{"name", "type" (number\|integer\|string\|boolean), optional "default", optional "description"}]. A step references one with {"$param": "<name>"}, and run_action/run_batch bind the values. A name with no default is REQUIRED. |
| `raw` | `object` | no | — | Camera RAW develop settings Batch opens RAW files with. Same shape as open_document's raw. |
| `recorded_canvas` | `object` | no | — | {"width", "height"} — the canvas the steps' coordinates are expressed in. REQUIRED when any step carries a non-absolute "geometry", which remaps against it. |
| `steps` | `array<object>` | yes | — | — |

## `delete_action`

Deletes a saved Action. Mirrors the Actions window's Delete button.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | — |

## `start_recording`

Starts recording every edit — yours and the user's alike — into a new Action. Mirrors File > Automate > Start Recording. Read-only tools, undo, redo, save_copy and open_document are not recorded (an action is replayed on a document that already exists, and in Batch on a different file every time); a user command with no tool of its own (Quick Mask) lands as a visible "__unrecorded" placeholder that names it rather than a silent gap. Copy, Copy Merged and Cut are recorded as steps that copy from the replaying document, and Paste as a step that pastes the clipboard at replay. Refused while a stopped-but-unsaved recording is still pending, since starting one throws those steps away.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `discard` | `boolean` | no | — | Throw away a pending unsaved recording and start a new one anyway. Default false. |

## `stop_recording`

Stops recording and returns the steps. Mirrors File > Automate > Stop Recording. Pass name to save them as an Action; omit it to read the steps back without saving.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Save the recording under this name; omit to return the steps without saving. |

## `inspect_psd_export`

Preflight for writing this document in Adobe Photoshop format (PSD, PSB or a TIFF with layers): a PSD, a Large Document PSB or a TIFF with layers (format) at the document's depth (8-, 16- or 32-bit RGB), the report File > Export as PSD… shows: available, refusal, per-document losses and observations, general export limitations, layer/group counts and the worst-case file size. Writes nothing and reads no pixels. A 32-bit float document reports depth 32: a PSD, PSB or TIFF with layers is available, and its layers mode refuses a gradient or pattern fill layer, a style that would be rasterized or an adjustment layer with no Photoshop record (flattened always writes); a Solid Color fill layer is written as Photoshop's SoCo. The reply's format and container name the file (PSD, PSB or TIFF), and bake_scratch_bytes is the working memory any baked adjustment layers need. A CMYK document writes a colour-mode-4 file in every format and both modes at its declared depth (the report's depth "cmyk" and bit_depth) with its CMYK profile: layers keeps its rasters, masks, groups, clipping, modes, Fill and its Levels, Curves and Hue/Saturation layers as Photoshop's own records; flattened writes its composite on paper. A Grayscale document writes a Grayscale (colour mode 1) PSD, PSB or layered TIFF at its declared bit_depth (8 or 16) in Photoshop's gray layout: ONE gray composite channel (no merged-alpha plane; a layered TIFF of one sample), its Gray profile embedded, effect colours as Grsc, Blend If on Gray; color_mode gray in the report. A 32-bit Grayscale document writes a 32-bit Grayscale PSD or PSB (Raw f32 channels, the linear gamma-1.0 twin of its Gray profile embedded, as Photoshop does); its layered TIFF refuses: the 32-bit layered TIFF is RGB only. A Lab Color document writes a Lab Color (colour mode 9) PSD, PSB or layered TIFF at its own depth (8 or 16 bits), as Photoshop writes Lab: its L*a*b* values as Photoshop stores them (16-bit a* and b* on Photoshop's 15-bit grid), no ICC profile, the composite over Lab white, layer effect colours as Lab; every adjustment layer is written as a pixel layer of the picture up to it, reported in losses. An Indexed Color document writes an 8-bit colour-mode-2 PSD or PSB in either mode, in Photoshop's own form: the palette, the transparent index and every index, no layer record (a renamed layer's name is a loss), at bit_depth 8; format tiff refuses (save_copy writes its palette TIFF). A Duotone document writes a Duotone PSD or PSB (colour mode 8, its gray channel and its inks as Photoshop's duotone specification; inks unchanged since the open keep the file's duotone data byte for byte) at 8 bits, Photoshop's Duotone depth: a 16-bit document is written from an 8-bit copy (bit_depth 8, one loss line; the document keeps 16 bits); a layered TIFF refuses. A Bitmap document writes a 1-bit colour-mode-0 PSD or PSB (1 is black, no profile, the same file in both modes; bit_depth 1, the report's depth 1 and color_mode bitmap); its TIFF with layers, and a side past the container's limit, refuse.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Document id from list_documents; omit for the active document. |
| `format` | `string` | no | one of `psd`, `psb`, `tiff` | psd (default) writes a classic PSD (30000 px per side, 2 GiB); psb a Large Document PSB (300000 px per side); tiff a flat TIFF with Photoshop's layer block. |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `layers`, `flattened` | layers (default) writes the editable stack; flattened writes one composited raster layer. |

## `export_psd`

Writes this document in Adobe Photoshop format (PSD, PSB or a TIFF with layers): a classic RGB PSD, a Large Document PSB or a TIFF with layers (format; the result echoes it) at the document's depth (8-, 16- or 32-bit RGB; the result reports bit_depth) (File > Export as PSD…): raster layers, ordinary masks, groups, clipping, opacity, blend keys, ICC and PPI, with a white-matted composite preview. Fails with inspect_psd_export's refusal when the mode is unavailable; returns the losses and observations it could not avoid. A 32-bit float document writes a 32-bit PSD, PSB or TIFF with layers (linear-light float samples, Raw channels, records in Lr32; the TIFF's flat image is float, Macintosh byte order; a Solid Color fill layer is Photoshop's SoCo, and style and fill colours are linear light x 255); in layers mode a gradient or pattern fill layer, a style that would be rasterized or an adjustment layer with no Photoshop record is refused with the core's sentence. Layer styles are written as Photoshop layer effects and blending options (lfx2, iOpa, blending ranges) and reported, and are baked into their layer only when Photoshop cannot hold them; knockout and Blend Interior Effects as Group ride that style as Photoshop's own knko and infx records at both depths, and a baked style writes neither; invert, threshold, posterize, levels, curves, color_balance, hue_saturation, photo_filter, exposure, vibrance, black_and_white, channel_mixer, selective_color and bcs (without saturation) adjustment layers are written as Photoshop adjustment records (parameters mapped, appearance in Photoshop not qualified) and every other adjustment layer is written as a pixel layer holding the picture up to that layer, reported as a loss; editable text, RAW layers' camera originals, alpha channels, guides, layer comps and metadata packets are not written; spot channels are written to PSD and PSB at 8 and 16 bits (not Lab), and to a layered TIFF from RGB and CMYK at 8 and 16 bits as its trailing extra samples (a Grayscale, Duotone, Lab or 32-bit TIFF refuses); layer locks are written as Photoshop's lspf. A CMYK document writes a colour-mode-4 file in every format and both modes at its declared depth (the report's depth "cmyk" and bit_depth) with its CMYK profile: layers keeps its rasters, masks, groups, clipping, modes, Fill and its Levels, Curves and Hue/Saturation layers as Photoshop's own records; flattened writes its composite on paper. A Grayscale document writes a Grayscale (colour mode 1) PSD, PSB or layered TIFF at its declared bit_depth (8 or 16) in Photoshop's gray layout: ONE gray composite channel (no merged-alpha plane; a layered TIFF of one sample), its Gray profile embedded, effect colours as Grsc, Blend If on Gray; color_mode gray in the report. A 32-bit Grayscale document writes a 32-bit Grayscale PSD or PSB (Raw f32 channels, the linear gamma-1.0 twin of its Gray profile embedded, as Photoshop does); its layered TIFF refuses: the 32-bit layered TIFF is RGB only. A Lab Color document writes a Lab Color (colour mode 9) PSD, PSB or layered TIFF at its own depth (8 or 16 bits), as Photoshop writes Lab: its L*a*b* values as Photoshop stores them (16-bit a* and b* on Photoshop's 15-bit grid), no ICC profile, the composite over Lab white, layer effect colours as Lab; every adjustment layer is written as a pixel layer of the picture up to it, reported in losses. An Indexed Color document writes an 8-bit colour-mode-2 PSD or PSB in either mode, in Photoshop's own form: the palette, the transparent index and every index, no layer record (a renamed layer's name is a loss), at bit_depth 8; format tiff refuses (save_copy writes its palette TIFF). A Duotone document writes a Duotone PSD or PSB (colour mode 8, its gray channel and its inks as Photoshop's duotone specification; inks unchanged since the open keep the file's duotone data byte for byte) at 8 bits, Photoshop's Duotone depth: a 16-bit document is written from an 8-bit copy (bit_depth 8, one loss line; the document keeps 16 bits); a layered TIFF refuses. A Bitmap document writes a 1-bit colour-mode-0 PSD or PSB (1 is black, no profile, the same file in both modes; bit_depth 1, the report's depth 1 and color_mode bitmap); its TIFF with layers, and a side past the container's limit, refuse.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Document id from list_documents; omit for the active document. |
| `format` | `string` | no | one of `psd`, `psb`, `tiff` | psd (default) writes a classic PSD (30000 px per side, 2 GiB); psb a Large Document PSB (300000 px per side); tiff a flat TIFF with Photoshop's layer block. |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `layers`, `flattened` | layers (default) writes the editable stack; flattened writes one composited raster layer. |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | Absolute or ~ path to write. Overwrites atomically. |

## `export_preview`

File > Export…: encode the document with these settings and return the picture DECODED FROM THE ENCODED BYTES plus the exact byte size and encoded_sha256. Writes nothing and changes no document state. settings also accepts profile:"file" with profile_path, profile:"installed" with profile_name, intent (perceptual, relative, saturation, absolute; default relative) and black_point_compensation (default false). At their defaults the bytes are unchanged. A matrix/TRC destination whose tone curves fail the precision check (list_installed_profiles: model matrix, high_depth_destination false) is refused by the core before encoding at every depth, with describe_profile's export_refusal, unless the destination's bytes are the document's own profile under a non-absolute intent without black_point_compensation, which exports it unchanged. profile "document" never converts, so it is never refused this way and ignores intent and black_point_compensation; a LUT destination converts at every depth. bit_depth 32 is the 32-bit float document's extended-range deliverable, in one of three containers: format "tiff" (four samples, unassociated alpha, Deflate, the document profile embedded), "exr" (OpenEXR: RGBA, ZIP scanlines, associated alpha, the document profile's primaries as chromaticities) or "hdr" (Radiance RGBE: opaque, each colour multiplied by its alpha, values below zero written as zero, a PRIMARIES line). float_samples "f16" writes a tiff or exr at half width, each sample the nearest 16-bit half; the reply's float_samples says f32, f16 or rgbe. "exr" and "hdr" exist only at bit_depth 32 and convert no pixel. A 32-bit export requires no sharpen, profile "document" and dither "none". The preview is decoded from the written bytes and shown under the document's tone map. A size mode resamples the composite through Image Size's extended-range resample (premultiplied, RGB clamped to the composite's own visible range, an alpha below 2^-24 transparent); size mode none writes the samples exactly. At 8 or 16 bits the document's tone map runs first. hdr_encoding (v1.x) makes a 32-bit heic an HDR photo: "gain_map" (an SDR base with an ISO 21496-1 gain map, the document profile's primaries, 1.0 written as the base's white) or "pq" (BT.2100 PQ in BT.2020, 1.0 written as 203 cd/m2); it requires bit_depth 32 and heic or avif, and the reply adds hdr_encoding and content_headroom (the largest linear value written, at least 1). This system's AVIF encoder writes no HDR AVIF, so an avif request refuses by name after the encode. Without hdr_encoding a 32-bit heic or avif is refused. On a CMYK document profile "document" keeps CMYK for jpeg and tiff: the composite on paper, resized on ink by size and filter, output-sharpened per plate, tiff at bit_depth 8 or 16 (16 → 8 rounds), with the metadata policy and its stamp (left at the defaults, the CMYK save's bytes); a tiff bit_depth other than 8 or 16, and dither on an 8-bit tiff of a 16-bit document, refuse by name, and jpeg ignores dither. Every other format, and srgb, display-p3 or file, flattens on paper and converts to sRGB ("document"), Display P3 or the file profile at intent and black_point_compensation. A Grayscale document with profile document keeps gray, as export_image: png, tiff or jpeg as ONE channel at bit_depth 8 or 16 with its Gray profile embedded, and a 32-bit document's tiff at bit_depth 32 too; another format has no one-channel export. A Lab Color document exports through RGB: the composite is converted by Image ▸ Mode ▸ RGB Color's rule (the request's intent and black_point_compensation; out-of-gamut colours clip) after resampling and before sharpening, and profile document writes sRGB. An Indexed Color document with profile document and format png, gif or tiff keeps Indexed: the palette, the transparent index and every index are written as they are (png colour type 3 with PLTE and tRNS; gif89a with the colour table padded black to a power of two, no profile or metadata; tiff Photometric 3 with the colour map padded black to 256 and a transparent index kept only where a pixel uses it), at bit_depth 8 with no size or sharpen (each refuses by name). Every other format or profile exports the palette's colours as RGB. A Duotone document exports through its inks: the file is RGB in the document's profile, rendered as the canvas shows it, and the reply's duotone says so. A Bitmap document with profile document exports png, tiff or bmp at 1 bit a pixel (bit_depth 8 in the request, 1 in the reply; no size or sharpen) and jpeg through its 8-bit Grayscale render; any other format refuses with profile document, and profile srgb, display-p3 or file exports RGB.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `metadata_policy` | `string` | no | — | Name of a saved metadata policy (list_metadata_policies). Resolved before the encode, so a recorded step carries the policy itself. It overrides settings.metadata. |
| `settings` | `object` | yes | — | The export request: format (png\|jpeg\|tiff\|bmp\|gif\|webp\|heic\|avif\|jxl\|exr\|hdr), jpeg_quality 1–100 (it is also HEIC's and AVIF's quality dial), bit_depth 8\|16\|32 (16 is png/tiff/heic/avif on a 16-bit document; HEIC and AVIF are encoded by the host, so the RESULT's bit_depth is the depth that was actually written, 8 or 10; jxl is lossless JPEG XL, 8-bit only, written as sRGB (set profile srgb when the document is not sRGB), each side at least 2 px, carrying no profile or metadata; 32 is the float deliverable a 32-bit float document writes and requires format tiff, exr or hdr (or heic/avif with hdr_encoding gain_map\|pq, the HDR photo deliverable), no sharpen, profile document and dither none — exact at size mode none, resampled through Image Size's extended-range resample otherwise; exr (OpenEXR: RGBA, ZIP, associated alpha) and hdr (Radiance RGBE: opaque, each colour multiplied by its alpha, values below zero written as zero) exist ONLY at bit_depth 32, convert no pixel, declare the document profile's primaries in their header and carry no ICC profile or metadata), float_samples f32\|f16 (default f32; f16 writes the nearest 16-bit half and requires bit_depth 32 and tiff or exr; the result's float_samples reports f32, f16 or rgbe), dither none\|ordered, size {mode:none\|width\|height\|long_edge\|scale, value}, filter nearest\|bilinear\|catmull-rom\|lanczos3, profile document\|srgb\|display-p3\|file\|installed (file takes profile_path, installed takes profile_name — see list_installed_profiles), intent perceptual\|relative\|saturation\|absolute (default relative), black_point_compensation (default false), sharpen {radius 0–64, amount 0–5, threshold 0–1} (Unsharp Mask; method "unsharp_mask" may be given) or {method:"smart_sharpen", and any of apply_filter's smart_sharpen keys at their defaults: amount 1–500 % (200), radius 0.1–64 px (1), noise 0–100 (10), remove gaussian\|lens\|motion (lens), angle (0), shadow_/highlight_fade 0–100 (0), _tonal_width 0–100 (50), _radius 1–100 px (1)} or null, embed_profile, strip_metadata, and metadata {exif\|xmp\|iptc\|density: default\|keep\|drop, stamp:{author,copyright}\|null}. Omitted fields keep today's export behaviour. |
