## `quick_export`

File > Quick Export: write the document into a preset's destination folder under its naming pattern, with no dialog. Give preset (the library name), or settings + destination + pattern, or none of the four: then it uses the Quick Export default (list_export_presets.default_preset), and with no default set a built-in preset — a PNG named {name} beside the document's own file, or in ~/Downloads for a document with no file. It NEVER overwrites: by preset name or with no arguments a taken name gets -2, -3, … and the result adds requested_path (the name that was taken) beside path; settings + destination + pattern refuses an existing path, which is the form a recorded step and a batch use. This is recordable as an Action step, because its name comes from a pattern that must contain {name}; the step carries the resolved settings, destination and pattern. index and count feed {index} (1-based, zero-padded to count's digit width), which is how a batch names its outputs. On a CMYK document profile "document" keeps CMYK for jpeg and tiff: the composite on paper, resized on ink by size and filter, output-sharpened per plate, tiff at bit_depth 8 or 16 (16 → 8 rounds), with the metadata policy and its stamp (left at the defaults, the CMYK save's bytes); a tiff bit_depth other than 8 or 16, and dither on an 8-bit tiff of a 16-bit document, refuse by name, and jpeg ignores dither. Every other format, and srgb, display-p3 or file, flattens on paper and converts to sRGB ("document"), Display P3 or the file profile at intent and black_point_compensation. A Grayscale document with profile document keeps gray, as export_image: png, tiff or jpeg as ONE channel at bit_depth 8 or 16 with its Gray profile embedded, and a 32-bit document's tiff at bit_depth 32 too; another format has no one-channel export. A Lab Color document exports through RGB: the composite is converted by Image ▸ Mode ▸ RGB Color's rule (the request's intent and black_point_compensation; out-of-gamut colours clip) after resampling and before sharpening, and profile document writes sRGB. An Indexed Color document with profile document and format png, gif or tiff keeps Indexed: the palette, the transparent index and every index are written as they are (png colour type 3 with PLTE and tRNS; gif89a with the colour table padded black to a power of two, no profile or metadata; tiff Photometric 3 with the colour map padded black to 256 and a transparent index kept only where a pixel uses it), at bit_depth 8 with no size or sharpen (each refuses by name). Every other format or profile exports the palette's colours as RGB. A Duotone document exports through its inks: the file is RGB in the document's profile, rendered as the canvas shows it, and the reply's duotone says so. A Bitmap document with profile document exports png, tiff or bmp at 1 bit a pixel (bit_depth 8 in the request, 1 in the reply; no size or sharpen) and jpeg through its 8-bit Grayscale render; any other format refuses with profile document, and profile srgb, display-p3 or file exports RGB.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `count` | `integer` | no | default `1` | — |
| `destination` | `string` | no | — | An existing destination folder. It is never created. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `index` | `integer` | no | default `1` | — |
| `metadata_policy` | `string` | no | — | Name of a saved metadata policy (list_metadata_policies). Resolved before the encode, so a recorded step carries the policy itself. It overrides settings.metadata. |
| `pattern` | `string` | no | — | Naming pattern; {name} is required. Tokens: {name} (required), {width}, {height}, {format}, {date}, {preset}, {layer} and {index} (layer exports and batches only). {index} is the item's position within that one run, so re-running a batch over a folder that has gained or lost files renumbers its outputs rather than colliding with the earlier run's. |
| `preset` | `string` | no | — | Export preset name, 1–120 characters. |
| `settings` | `object` | no | — | The export request: format (png\|jpeg\|tiff\|bmp\|gif\|webp\|heic\|avif\|jxl\|exr\|hdr), jpeg_quality 1–100 (it is also HEIC's and AVIF's quality dial), bit_depth 8\|16\|32 (16 is png/tiff/heic/avif on a 16-bit document; HEIC and AVIF are encoded by the host, so the RESULT's bit_depth is the depth that was actually written, 8 or 10; jxl is lossless JPEG XL, 8-bit only, written as sRGB (set profile srgb when the document is not sRGB), each side at least 2 px, carrying no profile or metadata; 32 is the float deliverable a 32-bit float document writes and requires format tiff, exr or hdr (or heic/avif with hdr_encoding gain_map\|pq, the HDR photo deliverable), no sharpen, profile document and dither none — exact at size mode none, resampled through Image Size's extended-range resample otherwise; exr (OpenEXR: RGBA, ZIP, associated alpha) and hdr (Radiance RGBE: opaque, each colour multiplied by its alpha, values below zero written as zero) exist ONLY at bit_depth 32, convert no pixel, declare the document profile's primaries in their header and carry no ICC profile or metadata), float_samples f32\|f16 (default f32; f16 writes the nearest 16-bit half and requires bit_depth 32 and tiff or exr; the result's float_samples reports f32, f16 or rgbe), dither none\|ordered, size {mode:none\|width\|height\|long_edge\|scale, value}, filter nearest\|bilinear\|catmull-rom\|lanczos3, profile document\|srgb\|display-p3\|file\|installed (file takes profile_path, installed takes profile_name — see list_installed_profiles), intent perceptual\|relative\|saturation\|absolute (default relative), black_point_compensation (default false), sharpen {radius 0–64, amount 0–5, threshold 0–1} (Unsharp Mask; method "unsharp_mask" may be given) or {method:"smart_sharpen", and any of apply_filter's smart_sharpen keys at their defaults: amount 1–500 % (200), radius 0.1–64 px (1), noise 0–100 (10), remove gaussian\|lens\|motion (lens), angle (0), shadow_/highlight_fade 0–100 (0), _tonal_width 0–100 (50), _radius 1–100 px (1)} or null, embed_profile, strip_metadata, and metadata {exif\|xmp\|iptc\|density: default\|keep\|drop, stamp:{author,copyright}\|null}. Omitted fields keep today's export behaviour. |

## `list_export_presets`

File > Export… > Manage…: list the bounded versioned export-preset library and the Quick Export default. Presets live outside every document. A file that is not a readable preset is reported as a `broken` row — {file, code, reason, repairable} with code one of unreadable, oversize, not_json, unknown_version, invalid_schema, duplicate_name — instead of refusing the whole library; repair is RAW-only, so repairable is always false here.

Takes no arguments.

## `delete_export_preset`

File > Export… > Manage… > Delete: remove ONE library file. Pass exactly one of name (a listed preset) or file (any library file, including a broken one that has no name); passing both or neither is refused. Recorded Quick Export steps keep their resolved settings.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `file` | `string` | no | — | A library file basename from list_export_presets (a row's `file`). Pass exactly one of name or file; a broken entry has no name. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Export preset name, 1–120 characters. |

## `set_default_export_preset`

File > Export… > Manage… > Set as Quick Export: choose the preset File > Quick Export uses, or null to clear it (after which Quick Export uses its built-in PNG preset).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `name` | `['string', 'null']` | no | — | Preset name, or null to clear the default. |

## `export_layers`

File > Export Layers…: deliver every selected (or visible, or every) top-level layer or group as its own file, each rendered in isolation against transparency. Give preset, or settings + destination + pattern; the pattern must contain {layer} or {index}. Nothing is overwritten and no folder is created. A partial run is NOT an error: ok is false and every item reports its path or its refusal. The document is unchanged. A Grayscale document with profile document writes each layer as a one-channel PNG, TIFF or JPEG with its Gray profile embedded, as export_image. A Lab Color document exports through its Lab → RGB conversion, as Export As does (a contact sheet cell is its Display P3 view). On an Indexed Color document the one layer exports untrimmed with profile document as png, gif or tiff keeping the palette and every index; trimmed or any other format exports its RGB colours. A Duotone document exports through its inks: the file is RGB in the document's profile, rendered as the canvas shows it, and the reply's duotone says so.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `destination` | `string` | no | — | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `items` | `string` | no | one of `selected`, `visible`, `all` | Which TOP-LEVEL layers or groups to use. selected takes the top-level ancestor of every selected entry. |
| `metadata_policy` | `string` | no | — | — |
| `pattern` | `string` | no | — | Must contain {layer} or {index}. Tokens: {layer} (the item's name), {index} (its position in this run, zero-padded), {name} (the document's name), {width}, {height}, {format}, {date}, {preset}. |
| `preset` | `string` | no | — | — |
| `settings` | `object` | no | — | — |
| `trimmed` | `boolean` | no | default `False` | Deliver the alpha bounding box instead of the canvas. A fully transparent item is then refused. |

## `contact_sheet`

File > Contact Sheet…: compose this document's items into a grid, as a new document or straight to a file. Cells are 8-bit sRGB, never upscaled and centred; a transparent item shows the background. A 16-bit item is reduced to 8 bits and a 32-bit float item is tone-mapped by the document's tone map first. The document is unchanged. A Lab Color document exports through its Lab → RGB conversion, as Export As does (a contact sheet cell is its Display P3 view). A Duotone document exports through its inks: the file is RGB in the document's profile, rendered as the canvas shows it, and the reply's duotone says so.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `items` | `string` | no | one of `selected`, `visible`, `all` | Which TOP-LEVEL layers or groups to use. selected takes the top-level ancestor of every selected entry. |
| `layout` | `object` | no | — | Grid layout: columns 1–32, cell_width/cell_height 16–2048, gutter 0–256, caption_height 0–128, captions (bool), background "#rrggbb"\|"#rrggbbaa", filter nearest\|bilinear\|catmull-rom\|lanczos3. width = gutter + columns*(cell_width+gutter); height = gutter + rows*(cell_height+caption_height+gutter). |
| `output` | `object` | no | — | {"kind":"document"} opens the sheet as a new document, or {"kind":"export", preset \| settings + destination + pattern, metadata_policy?} writes it. A sheet is composed at 8 bits, so an export output with bit_depth 16 is refused before any cell is built. |

## `contact_sheet_from_sources`

The same sheet built from FILES or other open documents. It has no single document to replay against, so it is not recordable as an Action step. The sources are opened read-only and never modified. An open 16-bit or 32-bit float document's cell is its 8-bit display rendering (a float one through its tone map). profile_refusals lists each file whose embedded colour profile the open converted from or ignored, and each untagged CMYK file, converted from the working CMYK profile.

| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |

| `files` | `array<string>` | no | — | — |
| `layout` | `object` | no | — | Grid layout: columns 1–32, cell_width/cell_height 16–2048, gutter 0–256, caption_height 0–128, captions (bool), background "#rrggbb"\|"#rrggbbaa", filter nearest\|bilinear\|catmull-rom\|lanczos3. width = gutter + columns*(cell_width+gutter); height = gutter + rows*(cell_height+caption_height+gutter). |
| `output` | `object` | no | — | {"kind":"document"} opens the sheet as a new document, or {"kind":"export", preset \| settings + destination + pattern, metadata_policy?} writes it. A sheet is composed at 8 bits, so an export output with bit_depth 16 is refused before any cell is built. |

## `list_metadata_policies`

File > Export… > Metadata policy > Manage…: list the bounded versioned metadata-policy library. Policies live outside every document. A file that is not a readable policy is reported as a `broken` row — {file, code, reason, repairable} with code one of unreadable, oversize, not_json, unknown_version, invalid_schema, duplicate_name — instead of refusing the whole library; repair is RAW-only, so repairable is always false here.

Takes no arguments.

## `save_metadata_policy`

File > Export… > Metadata policy > Manage… > Save As…: store a policy under a name. A library write is a preference: no Undo step, no Action step, and no document changes because a policy changed.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | — |
| `policy` | `object` | yes | — | {exif\|xmp\|iptc\|density: default\|keep\|drop, stamp:{author,copyright}\|null}. default defers to strip_metadata; density keep is identical to default. There is no orientation rule. |
| `replace` | `boolean` | no | default `False` | — |

## `delete_metadata_policy`

File > Export… > Metadata policy > Manage… > Delete: remove ONE library file. Pass exactly one of name (a listed policy) or file (any library file, including a broken one that has no name); passing both or neither is refused. Recorded steps keep their resolved policy.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `file` | `string` | no | — | A library file basename from list_metadata_policies (a row's `file`). Pass exactly one of name or file; a broken entry has no name. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | — |

## `select_magnetic`

Trace a Magnetic Lasso outline along image edges and close it into a selection. points (2–10,000 canvas [x, y]) replay the pointer: the first is the starting click, every later one a pointer move, except the indices listed in anchors (strictly increasing, 1…n−1), which are clicks that fasten an anchor there. width is the edge-detection radius in px (1–256, default 10), contrast the edge strength in % below which a gradient is not an edge (1–100, default 10), frequency how soon anchors fasten by themselves (0–100, default 57; 0 fastens only when a move's work budget runs out or the points loop back within 2·width of the last anchor after going farther around an enclosed area, not retracing their way; at width ≥ ~205 every move fastens). Moves closer than max(1, width/4) px to the previous one are coalesced (the last point never is). close "magnetic" (default) traces back to the start, "straight" joins it straight. Time grows with the number of points, and each point costs more at low frequency. Recorded as the resolved select_freehand outline; the reply adds outline_points. One Undo. In a 32-bit float document the edges are traced on the composite's display codes (the profile's curve over values clamped to 0–1, never the tone map or the view exposure), so a value above white traces as white. Mirrors the Magnetic Lasso tool. Works on a CMYK document: Grow and Similar compare the ink as the Magic Wand does, the Magnetic Lasso reads the view, and the rest edit coverage. In a Lab Color document it reads the document's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows). On an Indexed Color document a colour selection samples the palette colours, each pixel its index's colour (so a duplicate entry's pixels select with its twin's); the selection, Quick Mask and alpha channels work as on RGB and change no index. A red, green, blue or alpha channel, or the luminosity, refuses (the one channel is Index). A Bitmap document: it edits the selection only; the plane is unchanged.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `anchors` | `array<integer>` | no | items: 1–∞ | — |
| `close` | `string` | no | one of `magnetic`, `straight` | — |
| `contrast` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `feather` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `frequency` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | — |
| `points` | `array<array<number>>` | yes | 2–10000 items | — |
| `width` | `number` | no | — | — |

## `select_color_range`

Select sampled colors, a hue preset, skin tones or a tonal range from the composite. RGB samples are encoded document-profile values. Tolerance is Lab ΔE76 (0–200); softness is 0–100. Tonal presets use L*: shadows0–35, midtones35–70, highlights70–100. The hue presets reds, yellows, greens, cyans, blues and magentas select each pixel by its share of that hue: a primary (R, G, B) is max(0, channel − the larger other), a secondary (Y, C, M) is max(0, the smaller of its two − the third), times (2 − the largest channel) and capped at full, over the encoded values (0–1) (at 32 bits the display codes; on a CMYK document its view); they take no samples, tolerance or softness. skin_tones selects skin colours: ΔE76 in the document-profile Lab from (70, 18, 19), full within 18 and fading to none over a further 0.25 × fuzziness (0–200, default 40; 0 is a hard edge), over the encoded values (at 32 bits the display codes; on a CMYK document its view); it does not match Photoshop's Skin Tones (measured), takes no samples, tolerance or softness, and is the only range fuzziness applies to. out_of_gamut selects the pixels View > Gamut Warning flags: colours the window's proof profile (else the default proof preset, else Working CMYK) cannot hold, ΔE76 above 5 between a colour and its relative colorimetric round trip through that profile, over the same 8-bit codes the warning proofs (the display codes at 16 and 32 bits). It is all or nothing and takes no samples, tolerance or softness; a CMYK document is all in gamut, so it selects nothing (everything with invert). Its reply adds proof_profile. invert (default false) selects the complement. localized (Localized Color Clusters, sampled only; needs points: one canvas [x, y] per sample, in order) weights each sample by 1 − d/R, d the pixel's distance to its point and R cluster_range (0–100, default 100) % of the canvas's longer side. Zero-alpha pixels stay outside. Mirrors Select > Color Range. In a 32-bit float document the tolerance or colour distance compares the display-encoded copy (the document profile's curve over each value clamped to 0–1, never the tone map), so a value above white compares as white; the output is native 65,536-level coverage. In a CMYK document this reads the document's Display P3 view of its ink (sample_color's center_rgba16 are that view's codes), and the selection is coverage at document size. In a Lab Color document samples and samples16 are the document's L*a*b* codes (as sample_pixel reads them), and tolerance and softness are in L*a*b* units of the largest per-channel difference (|ΔL*|, |Δa*| or |Δb*|), measured against Photoshop's Color Range in Lab, not ΔE76. Every range runs: highlights, midtones, shadows and custom read the codes' own L*; the hue ranges and skin_tones read the codes' 16-bit ProPhoto RGB (Hue/Saturation's space), skin_tones' Lab the codes' own; out_of_gamut proofs the Display P3 view, as the gamut warning does. On an Indexed Color document a colour selection samples the palette colours, each pixel its index's colour (so a duplicate entry's pixels select with its twin's); the selection, Quick Mask and alpha channels work as on RGB and change no index. A red, green, blue or alpha channel, or the luminosity, refuses (the one channel is Index).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `cluster_range` | `number` | no | 0–100 | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `fuzziness` | `number` | no | 0–200 | — |
| `invert` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `localized` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `lower` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | — |
| `points` | `array<array<integer>>` | no | 0–32 items | — |
| `range` | `string` | no | one of `sampled`, `reds`, `yellows`, `greens`, `cyans`, `blues`, `magentas`, `shadows`, `midtones`, `highlights`, `skin_tones`, `out_of_gamut`, `tonal` | — |
| `samples` | `array<array<integer>>` | no | 0–32 items | — |
| `samples16` | `array<array<integer>>` | no | 0–32 items | — |
| `softness` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `tolerance` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `upper` | `number` | no | — | — |

## `quick_select`

Grow edge-aware connected color regions from 1–4096 integer canvas seed pixels. Tolerance and edge are Lab ΔE76 limits0–200; transparent pixels form barriers. brush_size (1–512 px, default 1) paints each seed as a disc of that diameter: everything opaque under it is selected and grows outward, and an enclosed gap smaller than one dab is filled. seeds × brush_size² must stay under 64,000,000, and seeds closer together than a quarter of the brush size add little. smooth (0–4, default 0) averages colour over a (2·smooth+1)² window without crossing an edge, so noise and texture do not stop the growth; the tool uses 1. enhance_edge (default false) then refines the result's edge against the picture and smooths it. Omitting all three grows from the seed pixels alone. Uses the captured composite and retains its alpha. In a 32-bit float document the distances and enhance_edge read the composite's display codes (the profile's curve over values clamped to 0–1), so a value above white compares as white. Mirrors dragging the Quick Selection tool. In a 32-bit float document the tolerance or colour distance compares the display-encoded copy (the document profile's curve over each value clamped to 0–1, never the tone map), so a value above white compares as white; the output is native 65,536-level coverage. enhance_edge (Select and Mask's edge stage) refines on the same display codes there. In a CMYK document this reads the document's Display P3 view of its ink (sample_color's center_rgba16 are that view's codes), and the selection is coverage at document size. In a Lab Color document the ΔE76 tolerance and edge read the codes' own L*a*b* values. On an Indexed Color document a colour selection samples the palette colours, each pixel its index's colour (so a duplicate entry's pixels select with its twin's); the selection, Quick Mask and alpha channels work as on RGB and change no index. A red, green, blue or alpha channel, or the luminosity, refuses (the one channel is Index). A Bitmap document: it edits the selection only; the plane is unchanged.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `brush_size` | `number` | no | 1–512 | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `edge` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `enhance_edge` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `feather` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | — |
| `seeds` | `array<array<number>>` | yes | 1–4096 items | — |
| `smooth` | `integer` | no | 0–4 | — |
| `tolerance` | `number` | no | — | — |

## `transform_mask`

Transform only original mask coverage in canvas coordinates; layer pixels stay unchanged. Density, feather and linking are retained. An optional pivot [x, y] records the point the matrix was built around; it does not change the result here, and a relative Action replay keeps the angle, scale and skew about it. Available in a 32-bit float document: the resample is premultiplied over the extended-range samples, each layer's RGB is clamped to that layer's own visible range so a filter's ringing never leaves it, an output alpha below 2^-24 becomes transparent, and a float result past 67,108,864 pixels refuses before any work. Masks stay 16-bit coverage and resample exactly as at 16 bits. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `filter` | `string` | no | one of `nearest`, `bilinear`, `bicubic`, `lanczos3` | — |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index; defaults to the active layer. |
| `matrix` | `array<number>` | yes | 6–6 items | Affine [a,b,c,d,tx,ty], matching CGAffineTransform. |
| `pivot` | `array<number>` | no | 2–2 items | — |

## `inspect_subjects`

Analyze foreground objects (model "objects", the default) or individual people (model "people") without changing the selection. Reports 1-based instance IDs and coarse canvas bounds from the Vision instance map. Model "people" lists people numbered left to right. IDs are valid only for the same model and image revision. Refuses people when Vision's human-body and face detectors find no person. In a 32-bit float document Vision reads the tone-mapped 8-bit display at view exposure 0. Mirrors the Select Objects and Select People pickers. In a CMYK document this reads the document's Display P3 view of its ink (sample_color's center_rgba16 are that view's codes), and the selection is coverage at document size. In a Lab Color document the model reads the document's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows); the selection is colour-free coverage. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `model` | `string` | no | one of `objects`, `people` | — |

## `select_subjects`

Select multiple foreground objects (model "objects", the default) or individual people (model "people", numbered left to right). Choose instances, one point [x,y], or a region {x,y,width,height}; omit all three to select every object, or every separated person. Region hit tests the coarse instance map. IDs are valid only for the same model and image revision; supply expected_revision from inspect_subjects to reject stale IDs. A recorded instances list re-resolves on replay: Person N is the Nth from the left in the replayed image. A person's edges come from Vision's accurate person segmentation. Foreground objects may include people; use select_people for dedicated aggregate person coverage. Mirrors Select > Select Objects and Select > Select People. In a CMYK document this reads the document's Display P3 view of its ink (sample_color's center_rgba16 are that view's codes), and the selection is coverage at document size. In a Lab Color document the model reads the document's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows); the selection is colour-free coverage. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `expected_revision` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | — |
| `feather` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `instances` | `array<integer>` | no | 1–unbounded items; items: 1–∞ | — |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | — |
| `model` | `string` | no | one of `objects`, `people` | — |
| `point` | `array<number>` | no | 2–2 items | — |
| `region` | `object` | no | — | — |
| `region.height` | `number` | with parent | — | — |
| `region.width` | `number` | with parent | — | — |
| `region.x` | `number` | with parent | — | — |
| `region.y` | `number` | with parent | — | — |

## `select_people`

Select all people as one aggregate coverage mask using Vision's dedicated accurate person segmenter. Does not identify individual people; for individuals use select_subjects with model "people". Refuses when Vision's human-body and face detectors find no person. In a 32-bit float document Vision reads the tone-mapped 8-bit display at view exposure 0. Mirrors Select > All People and the Select People picker's All People. One selection Undo; native pixels unchanged. In a CMYK document this reads the document's Display P3 view of its ink (sample_color's center_rgba16 are that view's codes), and the selection is coverage at document size. In a Lab Color document the model reads the document's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows); the selection is colour-free coverage. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

## `inspect_faces`

Find faces with Vision face landmarks without changing the selection. Reports 1-based face numbers, left to right, with canvas bounds and the parts each face has landmarks for. Numbers apply to this image revision. In a 32-bit float document Vision reads the tone-mapped 8-bit display at view exposure 0. Mirrors the Select > Face Parts picker's face list. In a CMYK document this reads the document's Display P3 view of its ink (sample_color's center_rgba16 are that view's codes), and the selection is coverage at document size. In a Lab Color document the model reads the document's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows); the selection is colour-free coverage. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

## `select_face_parts`

Select parts of faces as smooth anti-aliased 16-bit coverage built from Vision face landmarks: face (outline with an estimated forehead), skin (face minus eyes, brows and lips), eyes, irises, eyebrows, lips (minus the mouth opening) or mouth (the opening). Choose faces by 1-based number from inspect_faces, or one point [x,y] inside a face; omit both for every face. Refuses when no face is found. Mirrors Select > Face Parts. One selection Undo; native pixels unchanged. In a CMYK document this reads the document's Display P3 view of its ink (sample_color's center_rgba16 are that view's codes), and the selection is coverage at document size. In a Lab Color document the model reads the document's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows); the selection is colour-free coverage. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

## `object_select`

Select the foreground object inside a region: give exactly one of region {x, y, width, height} or points (a closed path of 3–10,000 canvas [x, y]). The objects are Vision's foreground instances (inspect_subjects lists them); every instance with a real presence inside the region is selected, clipped to the region, and one that only clips its edge is left out. refine then follows the picture's own edge within a few pixels of the outline: it defaults to true at 8 and 16 bits and to false in a 32-bit float document, where Vision reads the tone-mapped 8-bit display at view exposure 0 and the result is its outline clipped to the region; refine: true runs the edge stage there on the display codes (the profile's curve over values clamped to 0–1), where an above-white subject on an above-white background is flat white. Refuses when no object is inside the region. The reply lists the instances chosen, instance_count and refined, which says whether the edge stage ran. One selection Undo; pixels unchanged. Mirrors dragging the Object Selection tool. In a CMYK document this reads the document's Display P3 view of its ink (sample_color's center_rgba16 are that view's codes), and the selection is coverage at document size. In a Lab Color document the model reads the document's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows); the selection is colour-free coverage. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `feather` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | — |
| `points` | `array<array<number>>` | no | 3–10000 items | — |
| `refine` | `boolean` | no | — | Refine the outline against the picture's edges (default true at 8 and 16 bits, false at 32-bit float, where true refines on the display codes). |
| `region` | `object` | no | — | — |
| `region.height` | `number` | with parent | — | — |
| `region.width` | `number` | with parent | — | — |
| `region.x` | `number` | with parent | — | — |
| `region.y` | `number` | with parent | — | — |

## `refine_selection`

Select and Mask: refine the current selection's coverage and write it to one of four outputs, as one Undo. edge_radius (0–64 px) re-estimates coverage from the picture's own colours within that distance of the selection's edge, so a hard selection follows soft or fine edges; smart_radius fades that estimate where the picture has no edge, keeping a hard edge across flat colour. brush is the Refine Edge brush: up to 256 strokes {mode, radius, points} in canvas px, applied in order — add always refines under the stroke (with or without edge_radius), subtract never does. Then Smooth, Shift Edge, Feather and Contrast (smooth/feather 0–64 px, shift −64–64 px, contrast 0–1). output: selection (default), mask (a new or replacement mask on layer), new_layer (a "Refined Cutout" layer whose alpha carries the coverage) or new_layer_with_mask (the same layer with the coverage as its editable mask); both layer outputs hide every other top-level layer and keep the composite's own alpha. decontaminate replaces fringe colour with the estimated foreground colour by decontaminate_amount (0–1, default 1); it changes pixels, so it needs a layer output and a fully opaque composite. Computes from the current coverage once. The reply adds new_layer (the new layer's index) for the layer outputs, and decontaminated. Not learned matting: hair against a busy background and glass stay approximate. On a 16-bit document coverage is refined at 65,536 levels, a mask output is a native u16 mask on the unchanged RGBA16 layer and a layer output keeps RGBA16. On a 32-bit float document the same holds with RGBA32 float: edge_radius and the brush read the composite's display codes (the profile's curve over values clamped to 0–1, never the tone map), so a value above white refines as white; a layer output keeps the float composite's values, above white included; decontaminate is unavailable. Works on a CMYK document: the edge stage reads its Display P3 view, and new_layer / new_layer_with_mask put the composite's ink on the new layer (decontaminate runs on the ink). In a Lab Color document the edge stage guides on the L*a*b* codes per channel, and decontaminate solves per channel on the codes (the linear mix Normal compositing uses).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `brush` | `array<object>` | no | 0–256 items | — |
| `brush[].mode` | `string` | with parent | one of `add`, `subtract` | — |
| `brush[].points` | `array<array<number>>` | with parent | 1–8192 items | — |
| `brush[].radius` | `number` | with parent | 0.5–512 | — |
| `contrast` | `number` | no | 0–1 | — |
| `decontaminate` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `decontaminate_amount` | `number` | no | 0–1 | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `edge_radius` | `number` | no | 0–64 | — |
| `feather` | `number` | no | 0–64 | — |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | — |
| `output` | `string` | no | one of `selection`, `mask`, `new_layer`, `new_layer_with_mask` | — |
| `shift` | `number` | no | -64–64 | — |
| `smart_radius` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `smooth` | `number` | no | 0–64 | — |

## `select_similar`

Colour-based, NOT a pixel-radius expand (that is modify_selection grow): Select ▸ Grow / Select ▸ Similar. Every pixel at least 50% selected is a reference; their range on seven projections — R, G, B, A, R−G, G−B and R−B — widened by tolerance on both sides decides which pixels of the composite are admitted, so a hue shift counts about double against the tolerance. The admitted region is ADDED to the selection at full coverage, promoting partly selected pixels that fall in range. contiguous=true is Select ▸ Grow (four-connected from the selected pixels); false (default) is Select ▸ Similar (the whole image). At 16 bits the tolerance is scaled ×257. Repeating a call can grow further. Reports changed:false and adds no undo step when nothing new would be selected. Errors with no selection. In a 32-bit float document the projections are the display-encoded copy, so a value above white compares as white. In a 32-bit float document the tolerance or colour distance compares the display-encoded copy (the document profile's curve over each value clamped to 0–1, never the tone map), so a value above white compares as white; the output is native 65,536-level coverage. Works on a CMYK document: Grow and Similar compare the ink as the Magic Wand does, the Magnetic Lasso reads the view, and the rest edit coverage. In a Lab Color document at 16 bits, global and contiguous (Grow) compare the Magic Wand's Lab rule against the box of the selected pixels' codes (measured against Photoshop). At 8 bits both are unavailable until their Lab tolerance rule is measured (#5). On an Indexed Color document a colour selection samples the palette colours, each pixel its index's colour (so a duplicate entry's pixels select with its twin's); the selection, Quick Mask and alpha channels work as on RGB and change no index. A red, green, blue or alpha channel, or the luminosity, refuses (the one channel is Index).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `contiguous` | `boolean` | no | — | true = Select ▸ Grow, false (default) = Select ▸ Similar. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `tolerance` | `number` | no | 0–255 | 0–255 (default 32), as the Magic Wand's. |

## `get_precision`

Document precision and the qualified operation/target matrix shared by UI, MCP and Actions. A Grayscale document answers color_mode gray, mode gray8, gray16 or gray32, its gray_profile, and its own supported_tools, supported_menu_items and blend_modes; every other tool refuses for good, by name. A Lab Color document answers its own lists: color_mode lab, mode lab8 or lab16, white_point D50, channels lightness, a and b, and the supported_tools, supported_menu_items and blend_modes of its gate.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `convert_precision`

Intentionally convert document precision. structure "flatten" (the default) converts the captured rendered appearance to one raster layer and loses editable layers/groups/adjustments/masks, keeping every saved channel (alpha and spot: name, options, ink, each value ×257 to 16 bits or nearest to 8 bits; a 32-bit document's 16-bit channel values carry unchanged to 16 bits). structure "preserve" converts keeping every layer, group, adjustment, text/shape description, mask, channel, style, Blend If, knockout, clipping, lock, link, label, comp, embedded source, warp, guide and the ruler origin: 8-bit to 16 widens each value by 257; 16-bit to 8 quantizes each record (RGB per dither, alpha nearest); a float document converts to either mode with each record tone-mapped by its own map (then quantized for 8-bit). mode rgba32 converts an 8- or 16-bit document to 32-bit float and requires structure "preserve": each 16-bit value (an 8-bit value first times 257) is decoded through the document profile's tone curve to linear light, alpha is value/65535, masks and channels keep their values, the result composites in linear light under the clip tone map, and converting back returns every original value; a blend mode, effect or adjustment a float document cannot hold, a warp, a profile with no matrix/TRC model and a result too large to save and reopen at 32 bits block by name. Its reply carries the plan (rendering_differences, discarded, blocked) and preview_delta, and a blocked record refuses by name with the document unchanged (a layer holding a 32-bit float Camera RAW development is one: redevelop it with raw.output_encoding sdr16, or rasterize it, first). flatten=true is required unless structure=preserve; dry_run=true returns the plan without editing. One Undo restores the original. Promotion adds no missing source detail; ordered RGB dithering applies only to 8-bit output, never alpha. On a 32-bit float document BOTH modes apply the document's tone map: rgba16 keeps 65,536 values per channel and stays linear-light, rgba8 keeps 256. mode rgba32 converts an 8- or 16-bit document INTO 32-bit float (structure "preserve" only): each value is decoded through the profile's tone curve to linear light, which invents no HDR information, and converting back returns every original value. structure:"preserve" is admitted on one in either mode: every layer is carried and each raster is tone-mapped per record (then quantized for rgba8, RGB per dither), with the result linear-light. On a CMYK document mode is cmyk8 or cmyk16 (Image ▸ Mode ▸ 8/16 Bits/Channel): 16 → 8 rounds every ink, alpha, mask and alpha-channel sample to the 8-bit grid and keeps vector masks, 8 → 16 changes only the declared depth. A Grayscale document takes mode gray8, gray16 or gray32 (Image ▸ Mode ▸ 8/16/32 Bits/Channel, one undo step): 16 → 8 rounds every sample to the 8-bit grid, 8 → 16 keeps them, → 32 decodes them to linear gray; from 32 bits it refuses, and hdr_toning with bit_depth 8 or 16 converts. structure and flatten do not apply. A Lab Color document converts between mode lab8 and lab16 (Image ▸ Mode ▸ 8/16 Bits/Channel): 16 → 8 puts every L*, a*, b*, alpha, mask and alpha-channel value on the 8-bit grid, 8 → 16 keeps every value; dry_run answers the plan. 32 Bits/Channel is unavailable in Lab Color. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good. A Duotone document refuses 16 and 32 Bits/Channel for good (mode rgba16 and rgba32, and gray16 from 8 bits and gray32); gray8 from 16 bits keeps the inks.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `dither` | `string` | no | one of `none`, `ordered` | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `flatten` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `mode` | `string` | yes | one of `rgba8`, `rgba16`, `rgba32`, `gray8`, `gray16`, `gray32`, `lab8`, `lab16` | gray8, gray16 and gray32 apply to a Grayscale document, and only there. lab8 and lab16 apply to a Lab Color document, and only there. |
| `structure` | `string` | no | one of `flatten`, `preserve` | — |

## `place_image`

Layer > Place Embedded… / Place Linked…: place an image file as a new layer. A PNG, JPEG or TIFF (8-bit, 16-bit or floating-point), a JPEG XL/HEIC/AVIF/JPEG 2000 still, or an H.264/ProRes 4444 movie frame lands as an ordinary raster layer: its pixels are converted into the document's profile and depth, and nothing of the file is kept, so the reply's source is null. When the ordinary open converted from or ignored the file's embedded colour profile, the reply's disclosures names it. A camera RAW file (CR3, CR2, NEF, ARW, DNG and the other formats open_document develops) becomes a retained RAW layer at any document depth: its 16-bit development is the master in an 8- or 16-bit document, where raw.output_encoding linear_float refuses. In a 32-bit float document the master is the 32-bit float (linear) development (values above white kept) unless raw names output_encoding sdr16 or grain, which give the 16-bit master rendered into linear light. The camera file is embedded, so redevelop_raw, RAW presets, synchronization and RAW locals work on it, and a linked layer keeps its link through them. It develops with raw (open_document's develop settings) over the exposure of an Adobe Camera Raw .xmp sidecar beside the file; the sidecar's other settings are not applied and the reply's disclosures names them. A place is sized by the file's resolution against the document's. Optional `layer` (anchor, default the active layer) and `position` (`above` the anchor, `top` of the root level, or `into_group` for a group anchor, default `above`) choose where it lands; the reply reports the `position` used. In a Grayscale document the placed pixels land folded to their gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule, R = G = B, as a plain layer with no retained source; a camera RAW file refuses (Doctored keeps RAW layers on RGB documents only). In a Lab Color document the picture renders into 16-bit ProPhoto RGB and lands as L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, a plain layer that keeps no linked source; a camera RAW file refuses. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `decoder_version` | `string` | no | — | Optional exact system decoder version guard for those files. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `host_frame` | `object` | no | — | Optional movie or Live Photo selection {kind:still\|video,time? or time_value/time_scale}. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Anchor layer index (default: the active layer). A group is a legal anchor. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Layer name; default source filename. |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | Local image, movie or camera RAW file. |
| `position` | `string` | no | one of `above`, `top`, `into_group` | Where the new layer lands relative to `layer`: above it (default), at the top of the root level, or as the top child of a group. |
| `raw` | `object` | no | — | Develop settings for a CAMERA RAW (CR3, CR2, NEF, ARW, DNG, Apple ProRAW, ORF, RW2, RAF, SRW, PEF). Omit it, or any key in it, to keep the value the file itself reports — an empty object is a valid "as shot" develop, and an agent open never shows the Develop dialog either way. Ignored, with a note in the result, for a file that is not developed as a camera RAW — one Core Image will not develop, and one that is already open, use redevelop_raw to change an already-open retained RAW. Keys: exposure (stops, -4..4); temperature (2000..50000 K) and tint (-150..150) — one coupled white balance, so passing either leaves the as-shot balance and the other half comes from the file; tone_curve (0..1, the global curve, 0 = linear); shadows (0..2, no effect while tone_curve is 0); contrast (0..1, LOCAL contrast on edges); sharpness (0..1); detail (0..3); luminance_noise (0..1); baseline_compensation (−4..4 stops relative to each camera's own captured baseline); moire (0..1, only supported camera decoders); vignette {edge_exposure:−4..4, center:[x,y] normalized0..1, falloff:0.25..4} applies calibrated manual source lens compensation after local development. source_geometry is an explicit lens profile {profile_id,center:[x,y],radial:[k1,k2,k3],red_scale,blue_scale,filter}; its native inverse radial/TCA sampling follows local composition. Global transfer preserves each target's native local masks and optical calibration. grain {amount:0..100 (required), size:0.5..4 px (default 1), roughness:0..100 (default 50)} is the Add Grain kernel applied LAST, after local development, vignette and explicit optics; amount 0 removes it, omitted size/roughness take the defaults (not the saved values), and its seed is the first 8 bytes of the embedded camera file's SHA-256, so redevelopment, reopen, presets and sync reproduce identical grain. texture, clarity and dehaze (each −100..100, 0 = off) are Filter ▸ Presence on the finished 16-bit development, after local development, vignette and explicit optics and just before grain (dehaze first, then texture and clarity of the dehazed picture); their radii scale with the image's long side, so the look does not depend on resolution; an omitted one keeps its saved value. color_noise (0..1); lens_correction (bool, Enable Profile Corrections: the lens profile the file carries, or when its decoder has none the bundled Lensfun profile matched at the first development (never both); omitted, it is ON for every file that carries one or matched one, not as shot, and open_document reports lens_profile {lens, supported, enabled, source: decoder\|lensfun\|null, lensfun: {id, model}\|null}); highlight_recovery (bool, needs macOS 26 or newer and refused by name below it). A value outside its range is refused by name rather than clamped. A control this particular file's decoder does not support is refused. output_space selects the retained master encoding, normalized SDR16: srgb (default on initial open), display_p3, adobe_rgb (Adobe RGB (1998)) or prophoto_rgb (ProPhoto RGB at gamma 1.8 with no ROMM linear toe, best in a 16-bit document). A colour outside the chosen space is clamped per channel to 0 or 65535 in it; neutral highlights clip at the same exposure in every space. get_raw_source reports the source; get_color_profile reports the document profile, which redevelopment preserves. Omit output_space during redevelopment to retain the saved choice. output_encoding selects the master: sdr16 (normalized 16-bit SDR, the default on open) or linear_float, the 32-bit float (linear) development: scene-linear f32 in output_space's primaries with the highlights the sensor recorded above the SDR white kept above 1.0. At tone_curve 0, where it starts unless one is named, it is linear in exposure with no highlight shoulder, so it looks brighter in the highlights than the 16-bit development until tone-mapped, and where a channel exceeds white it differs in hue as well (the 16-bit development moves such a colour toward white). With it tone_curve and shadows are the decoder's own under the extended range and keep values above white (shadows is inert at tone_curve 0); grain applies on the display encoding (each channel's encoded value moves by the 16-bit grain's offset for the pixel's encoded luma, unclamped, so a pixel at or above white keeps its value); nonzero texture, clarity or dehaze are refused. It exists only in a 32-bit float document: open_document with it opens one (refused with precision rgba8), place_image into a float document uses it by default, and it refuses on a layer of an 8- or 16-bit document. RAW presets and sync never carry it. as_shot_white_balance:true restores captured as-shot balance and cannot combine with temperature/tint. Omitted redevelopment fields keep saved values. |
| `source_fingerprints` | `array<string>` | no | — | Optional original-file SHA-256 guards for a still, movie or Live Photo pair. |
| `storage` | `string` | no | one of `embedded`, `linked` | Only a camera RAW file reads it: linked keeps the file's absolute path and fingerprint beside the embedded camera file. Every other image is placed as plain pixels either way. |
| `x` | `integer` | no | — | Initial canvas X offset, default 0. |
| `y` | `integer` | no | — | Initial canvas Y offset, default 0. |

## `rasterize_artwork`

Layer > Rasterize Artwork: remove a text/shape description, or a Generative Layer's generated tag (generative_fill), while preserving exact current pixels, mask and profile. Undo restores editability. Use before perspective distortion or deliberate raster editing. Works on a CMYK document: the layer's colours are stored as ink in the document's profile — pass ink (fill_ink, stroke_ink, a run's or a stop's ink) as C, M, Y, K percent for exact ink, or a colour, which separates through the profile (relative colorimetric with BPC); an edit that passes no colour keeps each ink exactly, and the reply reports the ink in percent beside the appearance hex. A Grayscale document rasterizes a type, shape or fill layer to its gray pixels, as on an RGB document.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | Layer index; default active layer. |

## `get_image_source`

Layer > RAW Source…: a RAW layer's retained source — identity/revision, dimensions, master and rendered depth, profile, affine, the raw development and current link_status (embedded/current/changed/missing/unreadable). Checks a linked file's fingerprint without changing the document. source=null for every other layer.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | Layer index; default active layer. |

## `rasterize_image_source`

Layer > Rasterize RAW Layer: detach the camera original and its development, preserving exact current layer pixels. Undo restores them. Required before destructive pixel edits of a RAW layer.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | Layer index; default active layer. |

## `redevelop_raw`

Layer > Redevelop RAW: patch the retained RAW's effective development recipe and regenerate its genuine 16-bit source below existing retouch layers. Omitted fields keep SAVED values, including white balance. Requires the captured decoder implementation/version; unavailable decoders leave the saved rendering intact. Original camera bytes are embedded; no source path is needed. Preserves accumulated affine, masks, layer properties and other layers. Empty/unchanged requests are no-ops; successful changes use one Undo. Explicit normalized SDR sRGB, Display P3, Adobe RGB (1998) or ProPhoto RGB source encoding; document profile stays unchanged and an 8-bit document quantizes only the fallback. In a 32-bit float document the 16-bit development is rendered into linear light, as a placed image is, unless raw.output_encoding is linear_float: the layer then keeps a 32-bit float (linear) master with values above white (tone_curve and shadows apply and keep values above white; grain applies on the display encoding; nonzero texture, clarity or dehaze refuse), and sdr16 switches it back; the layer's locals are kept either way. linear_float on a layer of an 8- or 16-bit document refuses. Unsupported controls refuse.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | Retained RAW layer; defaults to active layer. |
| `raw` | `object` | no | — | Develop settings for a CAMERA RAW (CR3, CR2, NEF, ARW, DNG, Apple ProRAW, ORF, RW2, RAF, SRW, PEF). Omit it, or any key in it, to keep the value the file itself reports — an empty object is a valid "as shot" develop, and an agent open never shows the Develop dialog either way. Ignored, with a note in the result, for a file that is not developed as a camera RAW — one Core Image will not develop, and one that is already open, use redevelop_raw to change an already-open retained RAW. Keys: exposure (stops, -4..4); temperature (2000..50000 K) and tint (-150..150) — one coupled white balance, so passing either leaves the as-shot balance and the other half comes from the file; tone_curve (0..1, the global curve, 0 = linear); shadows (0..2, no effect while tone_curve is 0); contrast (0..1, LOCAL contrast on edges); sharpness (0..1); detail (0..3); luminance_noise (0..1); baseline_compensation (−4..4 stops relative to each camera's own captured baseline); moire (0..1, only supported camera decoders); vignette {edge_exposure:−4..4, center:[x,y] normalized0..1, falloff:0.25..4} applies calibrated manual source lens compensation after local development. source_geometry is an explicit lens profile {profile_id,center:[x,y],radial:[k1,k2,k3],red_scale,blue_scale,filter}; its native inverse radial/TCA sampling follows local composition. Global transfer preserves each target's native local masks and optical calibration. grain {amount:0..100 (required), size:0.5..4 px (default 1), roughness:0..100 (default 50)} is the Add Grain kernel applied LAST, after local development, vignette and explicit optics; amount 0 removes it, omitted size/roughness take the defaults (not the saved values), and its seed is the first 8 bytes of the embedded camera file's SHA-256, so redevelopment, reopen, presets and sync reproduce identical grain. texture, clarity and dehaze (each −100..100, 0 = off) are Filter ▸ Presence on the finished 16-bit development, after local development, vignette and explicit optics and just before grain (dehaze first, then texture and clarity of the dehazed picture); their radii scale with the image's long side, so the look does not depend on resolution; an omitted one keeps its saved value. color_noise (0..1); lens_correction (bool, Enable Profile Corrections: the lens profile the file carries, or when its decoder has none the bundled Lensfun profile matched at the first development (never both); omitted, it is ON for every file that carries one or matched one, not as shot, and open_document reports lens_profile {lens, supported, enabled, source: decoder\|lensfun\|null, lensfun: {id, model}\|null}); highlight_recovery (bool, needs macOS 26 or newer and refused by name below it). A value outside its range is refused by name rather than clamped. A control this particular file's decoder does not support is refused. output_space selects the retained master encoding, normalized SDR16: srgb (default on initial open), display_p3, adobe_rgb (Adobe RGB (1998)) or prophoto_rgb (ProPhoto RGB at gamma 1.8 with no ROMM linear toe, best in a 16-bit document). A colour outside the chosen space is clamped per channel to 0 or 65535 in it; neutral highlights clip at the same exposure in every space. get_raw_source reports the source; get_color_profile reports the document profile, which redevelopment preserves. Omit output_space during redevelopment to retain the saved choice. output_encoding selects the master: sdr16 (normalized 16-bit SDR, the default on open) or linear_float, the 32-bit float (linear) development: scene-linear f32 in output_space's primaries with the highlights the sensor recorded above the SDR white kept above 1.0. At tone_curve 0, where it starts unless one is named, it is linear in exposure with no highlight shoulder, so it looks brighter in the highlights than the 16-bit development until tone-mapped, and where a channel exceeds white it differs in hue as well (the 16-bit development moves such a colour toward white). With it tone_curve and shadows are the decoder's own under the extended range and keep values above white (shadows is inert at tone_curve 0); grain applies on the display encoding (each channel's encoded value moves by the 16-bit grain's offset for the pixel's encoded luma, unclamped, so a pixel at or above white keeps its value); nonzero texture, clarity or dehaze are refused. It exists only in a 32-bit float document: open_document with it opens one (refused with precision rgba8), place_image into a float document uses it by default, and it refuses on a layer of an 8- or 16-bit document. RAW presets and sync never carry it. as_shot_white_balance:true restores captured as-shot balance and cannot combine with temperature/tint. Omitted redevelopment fields keep saved values. |

| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | Retained RAW layer; defaults to active layer. |

## `inspect_raw_development`

Develop RAW > Fit / 100%, Before / After, Histogram and Clipping: inspect the complete original u16 developed source before document transforms, retouch, masks and selection. Returns Before then After PNG display images plus full-source original-code histograms and exact endpoint counts. Optional raw patch previews new settings without committing; omitted raw reads saved pixels without a decoder. region chooses native source pixels, not a scaled approximation. Normalized output clipping is not sensor saturation. A 32-bit float (linear) development's PNG images are its SDR-clipped view: its values are clamped to 0…1 and encoded by its profile, so a red marker there means at or above white (sample_pixel reads the layer's real values). Its histogram reads the float samples: storage rgba32_float, stop bins over -12…+6 EV, above_white_rgba, exact_one_rgba, below_zero_rgba and exact_zero_rgba (the histogram tool's float schema). When either master is 32-bit float the reply adds hdr_preview: before_peak, before_divisor, before_marked, after_peak, after_divisor and after_marked, the largest RGB value of that side's extended image (markers excluded), its divisor and its clipping-marked pixel count (all null for a 16-bit side). It follows the Develop window's HDR view on a screen with headroom: Fit, or with region the 100% region at divisor 1; clipping marks samples at or below 0.0 and at or above 1.0.

| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | Retained RAW layer; defaults to active layer. |

## `migrate_raw_decoder`

Apply the exact reviewed RAW decoder candidate from preview_raw_decoder_migration. Requires its current preview_id; source, revision, target and selection must match the review. Preserves original camera data, layer geometry and other layers, with one Undo. Actions records the approved prior/new descriptors and refuses replay against a different source, recipe or current decoder.

## `edit_raw_development`

Develop RAW > Apply: prepare globals and native local masks together, preserve original camera bytes and local resources in both fallback depths, then publish one Undo. Empty/equivalent edits add no history; Cancel/stale/unsupported requests preserve the saved result. Local mask and decoder work use bounded sequential stages. In a 32-bit float document the 16-bit development is rendered into linear light, as a placed image is; a 32-bit float (linear) development (raw.output_encoding linear_float) blends its locals in float with no clamp, reads a range's Lab from the linear base (a value above white is L* 100) and applies the vignette as a linear gain. A local tone refuses there: "RAW local tone controls are not available for a 32-bit float development."

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `before_masks` | `array<string>` | no | — | Optional exact ordered prior mask SHA guards. |
| `before_recipe` | `string` | no | — | Optional exact recorded prior descriptor guard; Actions supplies this automatically. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | Retained RAW layer; default active. |
| `operations` | `array<object>` | no | 0–256 items | Ordered native local edits, max16 locals (at most 4 camera locals; fewer above about 32 MP, where the core's 1 GiB source resource cap binds — the refusal names the figure)/4096 total brush dabs/256KiB. Every edit has op and stable ASCII id. create adds a native mask (mask.op empty, full, radial, linear, subject, people or sky; full covers the whole frame, for a local limited by its range alone); update patches controls; mask applies a native command; remap uses map:RawSourceMap (EXIF/affine only, same canonical dimensions); reorder changes index; remove uses only id. Coordinates are canonical oriented source pixel centers before explicit lens geometry. A camera local (exposure_offset ≠ 0 or white_balance not inherit) mixes its own alternate camera development, which recovers clipped highlights; at most four. create and update take tone {exposure (−4…4 stops, a linear-light gain on the global development), contrast, whites, blacks, saturation, clarity, texture, sharpness (−100…100), highlights, shadows, noise_reduction (0…100); absent keys 0, unknown refused}, which replaces the local's whole tone (null or every key 0 removes it): it adjusts the global development as the earlier locals left it (overlapping tone locals compound in order; on a camera local it adjusts that local's camera development) inside the coverage, with no camera re-development; Highlights recovers the bright side, Shadows lifts the dark side, Whites and Blacks move the white and black points, Clarity and Texture boost mid- and fine-scale local contrast, and last Noise Reduction smooths luminance noise (Reduce Noise at radius 0.5, luminance up to 0.1) and Sharpness sharpens (Smart Sharpen, radius 1 px, amount up to 150 %) or, below 0, softens (Gaussian Blur up to 3 px); their radii are fixed in pixels. Dehaze is not a local control. Locals mix in order before vignette and optical sampling. Tone runs on the 16-bit development at every document depth. create and update take range, which multiplies the mask's coverage and replaces the local's whole range (null removes it): {luminance:{low,high,low_falloff?,high_falloff?,invert?}, color:{lab:[L,a,b] or sample:[x,y], amount, falloff?, invert?}}, one or both. It is evaluated on the global development before any local, as CIE L*a*b* (D50) through the developed profile, so a local's own exposure or white balance never moves its selection. luminance: low and high are L*/100 with 0 ≤ low ≤ high ≤ 1; each falloff (0…1, default 0 = hard) is the width of the soft edge outside its bound. color: full inside ΔE*ab amount (0…200) of lab, fading over falloff (0…200, default 0); sample names a source point instead and is resolved to the mean Lab of the 5×5 pixels there. invert (default false) flips a component. Generated masks: mask {op: subject} (every foreground subject, as Select Subject), {op: people} (as Select All People) or {op: sky} (the sky model's own matte, as Select > Sky reads it, without the edge refinement), with no other field, is made by Vision or the sky model from the global development before any local, vignette, lens geometry and grain, and stored as ordinary native coverage that brush, invert, density, feather and range then refine. It is recomputed on request only: stored coverage never changes by itself, not on a global edit, a preset, Sync Settings or redevelop_raw. {op: mask, id, command: {op: subject}} (or people, or sky) is Recompute: it replaces the local's whole coverage from the global development of this call (brush strokes and invert made since are not replayed) and marks the local generated; a radial, linear, empty or full command clears the mark, brush, invert and remap keep it. When nothing is found the call is refused with 'No subject was found in the image.', 'No people were found in this image.' or 'No sky was found in this image.' and nothing changes; with no sky model in the store a sky mask is refused with 'the sky model is not installed; download it in Settings ▸ Models'. update does not take generated. |
| `raw` | `object` | no | — | Develop settings for a CAMERA RAW (CR3, CR2, NEF, ARW, DNG, Apple ProRAW, ORF, RW2, RAF, SRW, PEF). Omit it, or any key in it, to keep the value the file itself reports — an empty object is a valid "as shot" develop, and an agent open never shows the Develop dialog either way. Ignored, with a note in the result, for a file that is not developed as a camera RAW — one Core Image will not develop, and one that is already open, use redevelop_raw to change an already-open retained RAW. ## `get_raw_locals`

Develop RAW > Local list/overlay: inspect saved local controls and native mask metadata without decoding camera data. Reports maximum_locals (16) and maximum_camera_locals (4). A local with a tone reports tone with all eleven keys. A local with a luminance or colour range reports it as range, every field present and a colour always as lab (a sample point is resolved when the edit is applied). A local whose coverage was generated reports generated: subject, people or sky (absent otherwise); its mask is the stored coverage, which only a recompute replaces.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | Retained RAW layer; default active. |

| `id` | `string` | yes | — | — |

| `space` | `string` | no | one of `canonical`, `developed` | Canonical authored coverage (default) or derived post-optical coverage. |

## `add_live_photo_layer`

Layer > Place Live Photo: place one frame of a Live Photo or movie as an ordinary raster layer at the document's depth, and select it. A same-basename JPEG/HEIC and movie pair defaults to its original still; a bare movie defaults to its first presentation sample. Pairing is by filename, not asset-ID verification. Optional kind/time selects a movie frame. The source files are not kept in the document: the layer is plain pixels, converted into the document's profile. Optional `layer` (anchor, default the active layer) and `position` (`above` the anchor, `top` of the root level, or `into_group` for a group anchor, default `above`) choose where it lands; the reply reports the `position` used. In a Grayscale document the placed pixels land folded to their gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule, R = G = B, as a plain layer with no retained source; a camera RAW file refuses (Doctored keeps RAW layers on RGB documents only). In a Lab Color document the picture renders into 16-bit ProPhoto RGB and lands as L*a*b* codes by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule, a plain layer that keeps no linked source; a camera RAW file refuses. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `decoder_version` | `string` | no | — | Optional exact system decoder-version guard. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `kind` | `string` | no | one of `still`, `video` | — |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Anchor layer index (default: the active layer). A group is a legal anchor. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Layer name; default source basename. |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | Supported movie, or either half of a same-basename JPEG/HEIC and movie pair. |
| `position` | `string` | no | one of `above`, `top`, `into_group` | Where the new layer lands relative to `layer`: above it (default), at the top of the root level, or as the top child of a group. |
| `source_fingerprints` | `array<string>` | no | — | Optional original-file SHA-256 guard. |
| `time` | `number` | no | — | Video seconds; greatest presentation timestamp <= request, inside track start..<end. |
| `time_scale` | `integer` | no | 1–∞ | — |
| `time_value` | `integer` | no | — | Exact rational movie-time numerator; pair with time_scale. |

## `list_raw_presets`

Develop/Layer > RAW Presets: list bounded versioned saved user settings. Every row carries its library `file` and its on-disk `schema_version` (1, 2, 3 or 4). A file that is not a readable preset is reported as a `broken` row — {file, code, reason, repairable} with code one of unreadable, oversize, not_json, unknown_version, invalid_schema, duplicate_name — instead of refusing the whole library, so one bad file never hides the good ones or blocks Develop. Native recipes remain independent; listing never changes documents.

Takes no arguments.

## `save_raw_preset`

Develop > Save Preset: save explicit sparse raw settings OR copy explicit fields from a source RAW layer. Camera-specific recipe defaults, identity and decoder are never copied. As Shot refers to each receiving camera. Library writes do not enter document Undo or Actions.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `fields` | `array<string>` | no | 1–unbounded items; unique items; items: one of `exposure`, `white_balance`, `tone_curve`, `shadows`, `contrast`, `sharpness`, `detail`, `luminance_noise`, `color_noise`, `lens_correction`, `highlight_recovery`, `output_space`, `baseline_compensation`, `moire`, `vignette`, `grain`, `texture`, `clarity`, `dehaze` | Explicit controls to copy. white_balance copies Custom temperature+tint, or requests each target's own captured As Shot balance. Unselected controls keep their saved values. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | RAW layer, default active. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | Preset display name, 1–120 characters. |
| `raw` | `object` | no | — | Develop settings for a CAMERA RAW (CR3, CR2, NEF, ARW, DNG, Apple ProRAW, ORF, RW2, RAF, SRW, PEF). Omit it, or any key in it, to keep the value the file itself reports — an empty object is a valid "as shot" develop, and an agent open never shows the Develop dialog either way. Ignored, with a note in the result, for a file that is not developed as a camera RAW — one Core Image will not develop, and one that is already open, use redevelop_raw to change an already-open retained RAW. Keys: exposure (stops, -4..4); temperature (2000..50000 K) and tint (-150..150) — one coupled white balance, so passing either leaves the as-shot balance and the other half comes from the file; tone_curve (0..1, the global curve, 0 = linear); shadows (0..2, no effect while tone_curve is 0); contrast (0..1, LOCAL contrast on edges); sharpness (0..1); detail (0..3); luminance_noise (0..1); baseline_compensation (−4..4 stops relative to each camera's own captured baseline); moire (0..1, only supported camera decoders); vignette {edge_exposure:−4..4, center:[x,y] normalized0..1, falloff:0.25..4} applies calibrated manual source lens compensation after local development. source_geometry is an explicit lens profile {profile_id,center:[x,y],radial:[k1,k2,k3],red_scale,blue_scale,filter}; its native inverse radial/TCA sampling follows local composition. Global transfer preserves each target's native local masks and optical calibration. grain {amount:0..100 (required), size:0.5..4 px (default 1), roughness:0..100 (default 50)} is the Add Grain kernel applied LAST, after local development, vignette and explicit optics; amount 0 removes it, omitted size/roughness take the defaults (not the saved values), and its seed is the first 8 bytes of the embedded camera file's SHA-256, so redevelopment, reopen, presets and sync reproduce identical grain. texture, clarity and dehaze (each −100..100, 0 = off) are Filter ▸ Presence on the finished 16-bit development, after local development, vignette and explicit optics and just before grain (dehaze first, then texture and clarity of the dehazed picture); their radii scale with the image's long side, so the look does not depend on resolution; an omitted one keeps its saved value. color_noise (0..1); lens_correction (bool, Enable Profile Corrections: the lens profile the file carries, or when its decoder has none the bundled Lensfun profile matched at the first development (never both); omitted, it is ON for every file that carries one or matched one, not as shot, and open_document reports lens_profile {lens, supported, enabled, source: decoder\|lensfun\|null, lensfun: {id, model}\|null}); highlight_recovery (bool, needs macOS 26 or newer and refused by name below it). A value outside its range is refused by name rather than clamped. A control this particular file's decoder does not support is refused. output_space selects the retained master encoding, normalized SDR16: srgb (default on initial open), display_p3, adobe_rgb (Adobe RGB (1998)) or prophoto_rgb (ProPhoto RGB at gamma 1.8 with no ROMM linear toe, best in a 16-bit document). A colour outside the chosen space is clamped per channel to 0 or 65535 in it; neutral highlights clip at the same exposure in every space. get_raw_source reports the source; get_color_profile reports the document profile, which redevelopment preserves. Omit output_space during redevelopment to retain the saved choice. output_encoding selects the master: sdr16 (normalized 16-bit SDR, the default on open) or linear_float, the 32-bit float (linear) development: scene-linear f32 in output_space's primaries with the highlights the sensor recorded above the SDR white kept above 1.0. At tone_curve 0, where it starts unless one is named, it is linear in exposure with no highlight shoulder, so it looks brighter in the highlights than the 16-bit development until tone-mapped, and where a channel exceeds white it differs in hue as well (the 16-bit development moves such a colour toward white). With it tone_curve and shadows are the decoder's own under the extended range and keep values above white (shadows is inert at tone_curve 0); grain applies on the display encoding (each channel's encoded value moves by the 16-bit grain's offset for the pixel's encoded luma, unclamped, so a pixel at or above white keeps its value); nonzero texture, clarity or dehaze are refused. It exists only in a 32-bit float document: open_document with it opens one (refused with precision rgba8), place_image into a float document uses it by default, and it refuses on a layer of an 8- or 16-bit document. RAW presets and sync never carry it. as_shot_white_balance:true restores captured as-shot balance and cannot combine with temperature/tint. Omitted redevelopment fields keep saved values. |
| `replace` | `boolean` | no | default `False` | — |

Layer > RAW Presets > Delete: delete ONE library file. Pass exactly one of name (a listed preset) or file (any library file, including a broken one that has no name); passing both or neither is refused. Saved documents and recorded Actions keep their effective settings.

## `repair_raw_preset`

RAW Presets manager > Repair: rewrite ONE broken library file (list_raw_presets `broken` row with repairable: true) as a canonical schema-4 preset. The stored name is trimmed and precomposed, unknown top-level keys are dropped, and each raw control is kept only if it decodes on its own — every dropped key is named in `dropped`. The file moves to its canonical digest name. An oversize, non-JSON, unknown-version or duplicate-name file is refused naming its code; nothing is read past 8 KiB and no unknown future version is ever rewritten.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `file` | `string` | yes | — | A library file basename from list_raw_presets (a row's `file`). Pass exactly one of name or file; a broken entry has no name. |
