## `sync_raw_settings`

Layer > Synchronize RAW Settings: copy only selected fields from a RAW source to explicit open-document/layer targets. locals: true (the Masking checkbox) REPLACES each target's local adjustments with the source's, in order, ids, names and controls kept: drawn coverage is resampled per axis in normalised coordinates of each RAW's oriented frame, feather is scaled to the target's size, a range keeps its Lab, and Subject/People/Sky are detected again on each target (brush or invert refinements on them are not carried). A generated local that finds nothing or whose model is not installed is skipped; result.skipped names each and result.note sums them. Give fields, locals: true or both. All target results and projections prepare before any publication. Each changed document gets one independent Undo; a sync that changes nothing adds none. Actions record resolved document-local apply_raw_settings without document IDs. Maximum 32 target layers.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `fields` | `array<string>` | no | 1–unbounded items; unique items; items: one of `exposure`, `white_balance`, `tone_curve`, `shadows`, `contrast`, `sharpness`, `detail`, `luminance_noise`, `color_noise`, `lens_correction`, `highlight_recovery`, `output_space`, `baseline_compensation`, `moire`, `vignette`, `grain`, `texture`, `clarity`, `dehaze` | Explicit controls to copy. white_balance copies Custom temperature+tint, or requests each target's own captured As Shot balance. Unselected controls keep their saved values. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | 0–∞ | RAW layer, default active. |
| `locals` | `boolean` | no | default `False` | Masking: replace each target's locals with the source's. |
| `targets` | `array<object>` | yes | 1–32 items | — |
| `targets[].document_id` | `integer` | with parent | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `targets[].layer` | `integer` | with parent | 0–∞ | RAW layer, default active. |

Internal experiment: refuses unless assisted annotation is enabled for this launch (DR_ASSISTED_ANNOTATION=1, or the AssistedAnnotationEnabled default). Mirrors File > Open Assisted Annotation Case…, which only such a launch shows. Opens one case in the gated annotation window; a human session stops at the task card and a synthetic session starts its 5-minute, 20-gesture budget at once. Refuses a locked case or a live session.

| `workspace` | `string` | yes | — | Absolute path of the prepared workspace directory (the one holding manifest.json, cases/ and replays/). |

Internal experiment: refuses unless assisted annotation is enabled for this launch (DR_ASSISTED_ANNOTATION=1, or the AssistedAnnotationEnabled default). The open annotation session's elapsed time, gesture budget, applied strokes, recorded events and current label-plane hash.

| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |

| `points` | `array<array<integer>>` | yes | 1–unbounded items | Polyline samples [[x,y],…] in canvas pixels, clamped to the canvas. More than 256 samples are decimated to 256 keeping the first and last; the recorded points are exactly what is rasterized. |

## `assisted_finalize_case`

Internal experiment: refuses unless assisted annotation is enabled for this launch (DR_ASSISTED_ANNOTATION=1, or the AssistedAnnotationEnabled default). Mirrors the annotation window's Submit button for a synthetic session: writes <workspace>/replays/<case_id>.json and locks the case.

Takes no arguments.

## `get_proof_setup`

What this window is soft-proofing through: the profile name, the intent, the two simulate flags and whether Proof Colors and Gamut Warning are on. VIEW STATE — proofing changes no pixel, writes no undo step and leaves every render and export untouched. failure is the refusal that last turned proofing off by itself (null otherwise); the next toggle or setup clears it. default_preset is the saved proof preset a window with no setup proofs through (⌘Y, ⇧⌘Y, set_proof_setup and render_proof with no profile), or null. On a CMYK document the proof profile is CMYK (profile "working_cmyk" is Color Settings' working CMYK), preserve_numbers sends the ink to it unconverted, plate (cyan, magenta, yellow or black) shows one plate of the proof device as grey, ink dark, and gamut_warning true overlays gamut_color on every ink the proof profile cannot hold (none when preserve_numbers), out_of_gamut counting them; the proof is Display P3 (space "display-p3"). On an RGB document plate needs a CMYK proof profile and preserve_numbers refuses. A Grayscale document at 8 or 16 bits proofs as RGB: its composite, R = G = B, through its Gray profile, so preserve_numbers refuses as on an RGB document; a 32-bit Grayscale document refuses, as a float document. A Lab Color document proofs as RGB: its Display P3 view (what the canvas shows) through the proof profile, so render_proof answers space "display-p3", exact true proofs the 16-bit view, and preserve_numbers refuses as on an RGB document. A Duotone document refuses it for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `string` | no | — | Which open document; defaults to the frontmost. |

## `set_proof_setup`

Chooses the medium the canvas is simulated on and turns Proof Colors / Gamut Warning on or off — View ▸ Proof Setup ▸ Custom… (or a saved preset in that submenu) and the two View toggles. Every key is optional and an absent one keeps its current value; with no profile, no preset and no setup on the window, the default proof preset is used, and with none of those the call is refused. preset turns proof_colors on unless proof_colors is passed. This is VIEW STATE: no undo step, no dirty flag, no history entry and nothing a save_copy would carry. Turning gamut_warning on turns proof_colors on, because a warning with no proof has nothing to warn about. With no setup, no preset and no default preset, turning proof_colors or gamut_warning on seeds the Working CMYK proof, as ⌘Y and ⇧⌘Y do. On a CMYK document the proof profile must be CMYK, and gamut_warning flags the inks it cannot hold (none when preserve_numbers). On a CMYK document the proof profile is CMYK (profile "working_cmyk" is Color Settings' working CMYK), preserve_numbers sends the ink to it unconverted, plate (cyan, magenta, yellow or black) shows one plate of the proof device as grey, ink dark, and gamut_warning true overlays gamut_color on every ink the proof profile cannot hold (none when preserve_numbers), out_of_gamut counting them; the proof is Display P3 (space "display-p3"). On an RGB document plate needs a CMYK proof profile and preserve_numbers refuses. A Grayscale document at 8 or 16 bits proofs as RGB: its composite, R = G = B, through its Gray profile, so preserve_numbers refuses as on an RGB document; a 32-bit Grayscale document refuses, as a float document. A Lab Color document proofs as RGB: its Display P3 view (what the canvas shows) through the proof profile, so render_proof answers space "display-p3", exact true proofs the 16-bit view, and preserve_numbers refuses as on an RGB document. A Duotone document refuses it for good. One exception: a call whose only keys besides document_id are proof_colors and gamut_warning, each false, is admitted, so a document converted into Duotone with Proof Colors on can turn proofing off.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `black_point_compensation` | `boolean` | no | — | Black point compensation (ISO 18619): maps the source's darkest colour onto the destination's so shadows do not block up. Default false. |
| `document_id` | `string` | no | — | Which open document; defaults to the frontmost. |
| `gamut_color` | `string` | no | — | The warning overlay, "#RRGGBB"; default "#808080". |
| `gamut_warning` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `intent` | `string` | no | one of `perceptual`, `relative`, `saturation`, `absolute` | Rendering intent. relative (the default) keeps in-gamut colours exactly and clips the rest; perceptual compresses the whole gamut; saturation favours vividness; absolute keeps the source white so the medium's own tint shows. A profile without its own table for an intent falls back to A2B0/B2A0. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Profile name, with profile:"installed". |
| `path` | `string` | no | — | Absolute path, with profile:"file". |
| `plate` | `string` | no | one of `cyan`, `magenta`, `yellow`, `black`, `none` | Show one plate of the proof device as grey, ink dark — View ▸ Proof Setup ▸ Working Cyan/Magenta/Yellow/Black Plate. Needs a CMYK proof profile; none clears it. |
| `preserve_numbers` | `boolean` | no | — | A CMYK document only (refused on RGB): send its ink to the proof profile unconverted — Proof Setup's Preserve CMYK Numbers. |
| `preset` | `string` | no | — | A saved proof preset's name (list_proof_presets): its profile, read back now and accepted only when its sha256 is the saved one, and its simulation fields. Refused beside profile. Explicit fields below still apply on top. |
| `profile` | `string` | no | one of `file`, `installed`, `working_cmyk` | Where the proof profile comes from: "file" with an absolute path, "installed" with a name from list_installed_profiles, or "working_cmyk" (Edit ▸ Color Settings' working CMYK, View ▸ Proof Setup ▸ Working CMYK). |
| `proof_colors` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `simulate_ink_black` | `boolean` | no | — | Show how far from black the medium's darkest tone is. |
| `simulate_paper_white` | `boolean` | no | — | Show the medium's own white instead of the display's. |

## `render_proof`

The proofed picture as a PNG, plus how many pixels fall outside the proof gamut. Uses preset when given, else the window's current setup, else the default proof preset, with any key below overriding it FOR THIS RENDER ONLY — the window's own setup is not changed. The gamut rule is a CIE76 ΔE*ab above 5.0 between a colour and its own round trip through the proof at RELATIVE COLORIMETRIC, independent of the intent being rendered. At 8 bits the composite is proofed. At 16 bits the composite's 8-bit display codes are proofed — what the canvas shows; exact:true proofs the full 16-bit composite instead, on the background worker (about 17 s at 24 MP; mask adds a second pass). source in the reply says which: "composite" or "display". A 32-bit float document refuses. A CMYK document proofs its ink through a CMYK profile into Display P3 (space "display-p3", source "cmyk"). On a CMYK document the proof profile is CMYK (profile "working_cmyk" is Color Settings' working CMYK), preserve_numbers sends the ink to it unconverted, plate (cyan, magenta, yellow or black) shows one plate of the proof device as grey, ink dark, and gamut_warning true overlays gamut_color on every ink the proof profile cannot hold (none when preserve_numbers), out_of_gamut counting them; the proof is Display P3 (space "display-p3"). On an RGB document plate needs a CMYK proof profile and preserve_numbers refuses. A Grayscale document at 8 or 16 bits proofs as RGB: its composite, R = G = B, through its Gray profile, so preserve_numbers refuses as on an RGB document; a 32-bit Grayscale document refuses, as a float document. A Lab Color document proofs as RGB: its Display P3 view (what the canvas shows) through the proof profile, so render_proof answers space "display-p3", exact true proofs the 16-bit view, and preserve_numbers refuses as on an RGB document. A Duotone document refuses it for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `black_point_compensation` | `boolean` | no | — | Black point compensation (ISO 18619): maps the source's darkest colour onto the destination's so shadows do not block up. Default false. |
| `document_id` | `string` | no | — | Which open document; defaults to the frontmost. |
| `exact` | `boolean` | no | — | 16 bits only: proof the full 16-bit composite rather than its display codes. Default false; no effect at 8 bits. |
| `gamut_color` | `string` | no | — | — |
| `gamut_warning` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `intent` | `string` | no | one of `perceptual`, `relative`, `saturation`, `absolute` | Rendering intent. relative (the default) keeps in-gamut colours exactly and clips the rest; perceptual compresses the whole gamut; saturation favours vividness; absolute keeps the source white so the medium's own tint shows. A profile without its own table for an intent falls back to A2B0/B2A0. |
| `mask` | `boolean` | no | — | Also report the mask's own out-of-gamut count. |
| `max_side` | `integer` | no | 64–4096 | Longest side of the returned PNG; default 1024. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | — |
| `path` | `string` | no | — | — |
| `plate` | `string` | no | one of `cyan`, `magenta`, `yellow`, `black`, `none` | Show one plate of the proof device as grey, ink dark — View ▸ Proof Setup ▸ Working Cyan/Magenta/Yellow/Black Plate. Needs a CMYK proof profile; none clears it. |
| `preserve_numbers` | `boolean` | no | — | A CMYK document only (refused on RGB): send its ink to the proof profile unconverted — Proof Setup's Preserve CMYK Numbers. |
| `preset` | `string` | no | — | A saved proof preset's name (list_proof_presets): its profile, read back now and accepted only when its sha256 is the saved one, and its simulation fields. Refused beside profile. Explicit fields below still apply on top. |
| `profile` | `string` | no | one of `file`, `installed`, `working_cmyk` | Where the proof profile comes from: "file" with an absolute path, "installed" with a name from list_installed_profiles, or "working_cmyk" (Edit ▸ Color Settings' working CMYK, View ▸ Proof Setup ▸ Working CMYK). |
| `simulate_ink_black` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `simulate_paper_white` | `boolean` | no | — | — |

## `describe_profile`

Everything this build can say about an ICC profile file: its name, version, class, device space, PCS, whether it has a matrix/TRC model or colour tables, which intents have their own table, its media white, whether a proof can run through it (proofable, and proof_refusal naming the missing A2B or B2A table and any floating-point D2Bx/B2Dx twin when it cannot), whether a 16/32-bit convert accepts it as a destination (high_depth_destination; for a matrix/TRC profile where it is false, export_refusal and convert_refusal are the sentences an export or a convert into it is refused with, else null), and — when it cannot be used — a refusal naming what it is (a named-colour list, a device-link or abstract profile, an nCLR separation space such as 2CLR-4CLR or 6CLR, a CMY, HSV or other space that is not RGB, Gray or CMYK, a multiProcessElements table, a D2Bx/B2Dx-only profile, an oversized table).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | Absolute path to an .icc/.icm file. |

## `list_installed_profiles`

The ICC profiles installed on this machine — the ColorSync folders, Adobe's, which is where the press profiles live, and the printer-driver paper profiles under /Library/Printers. Each entry reports its device space and whether this build can decode into it, encode out of it and proof through it, and high_depth_destination: whether a 16/32-bit convert_profile accepts it as a destination (a matrix/TRC model whose curves pass the high-depth precision checks).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `kinds` | `array<string>` | no | items: one of `rgb`, `gray`, `cmyk` | Device spaces to list; omit for all of them. |

## `list_proof_presets`

View > Proof Setup > (the saved presets): list the bounded versioned proof-preset library. Each preset reports its fields, its library `file`, and `available` — whether its profile can be read back now (the saved path with the saved sha256, else the installed profile of the same name with it) — with `unavailable_reason` when it cannot. A file that is not a readable preset is a `broken` row — {file, code, reason, repairable} with code one of unreadable, oversize, not_json, unknown_version, invalid_schema, duplicate_name — instead of refusing the whole library; repairable is always false here. default_preset is the preset a window with no proof setup uses (⌘Y, ⇧⌘Y, set_proof_setup and render_proof with no profile), or null.

Takes no arguments.

## `save_proof_preset`

View > Proof Setup > Custom… > Save…: store this window's CURRENT proof setup — the profile's name, path and sha256 (never its bytes), the intent, black point compensation, the two simulate flags and the warning colour — under a name. Proof Colors and Gamut Warning are not part of a preset. warning is present when the profile is not installed, because the preset stops working if that file moves. A library write is a preference: no Undo step, no Action step. A 32-bit float document has no soft proof and refuses. A Lab Color document proofs as RGB: its Display P3 view (what the canvas shows) through the proof profile, so render_proof answers space "display-p3", exact true proofs the 16-bit view, and preserve_numbers refuses as on an RGB document.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `string` | no | — | Which open document's window; defaults to the frontmost. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | Proof preset name, 1–120 characters. |
| `replace` | `boolean` | no | default `False` | — |

## `delete_proof_preset`

View > Proof Setup > Custom… > Delete (a listed preset) or View > Proof Setup > Delete Broken File (a broken file): remove ONE library file. Pass exactly one of name (a listed preset) or file (any library file, including a broken one that has no name); passing both or neither is refused. Deleting the default preset clears the default.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `file` | `string` | no | — | A library file basename from list_proof_presets (a row's `file`). Pass exactly one of name or file; a broken entry has no name. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Proof preset name, 1–120 characters. |

## `set_default_proof_preset`

View > Proof Setup > Custom… > Default for new windows: choose the preset a window with no proof setup proofs through, or null to clear it. A library write is a preference: no Undo step, no Action step.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `name` | `['string', 'null']` | no | — | Preset name, or null to clear the default. |

## `export_pdf`

Export the flattened document as a single-page PDF at its own print size, with its colour profile embedded (File ▸ Export as PDF…). Takes every export_image setting but format: the page holds one image at bit_depth 8 or 16 (default: the document's remembered export depth, capped at 16; an 8-bit document exports at 8), compressed as zip (lossless, the default) or jpeg (8-bit only, the system ImageIO encoder at jpeg_quality, so not byte-comparable with export_image's JPEG). Transparency travels as a soft mask. A 32-bit float document writes its tone-mapped projection. The result's bits_per_component, compression and has_soft_mask are read back from the written file. A Grayscale document writes its composite, R = G = B, as on an RGB document. A Lab Color document exports through its Lab → RGB conversion, as Export As does (a contact sheet cell is its Display P3 view). A Duotone document exports through its inks: the file is RGB in the document's profile, rendered as the canvas shows it, and the reply's duotone says so.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `compression` | `string` | no | one of `zip`, `jpeg`; default `zip` | How the page's image is compressed; jpeg is 8-bit only. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `metadata_policy` | `string` | no | — | A saved metadata policy name, resolved at delivery. |
| `overwrite` | `boolean` | no | default `False` | — |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | Where to write the PDF. |
| `settings` | `object` | no | — | export_image settings without format; bit_depth 8 or 16. |

## `inspect_vector`

Report what a PDF or SVG file is — its page count and each page's size in points — without opening it. Use it before open_document's page and ppi.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | — |

## `get_evaluation`

How this document's projection evaluates its stack: "encoded" (the default — layers composite on the stored numbers) or "linear_light" (each layer is decoded through the document's colour profile, composited in linear light and re-encoded once at the output). The reply also carries the operator table — what linear light evaluates and what it still refuses, with the phase that owns each refusal — and linear_light_refusal, the sentence naming the first layer and operator this document could not evaluate. With preview:true it adds a MEASURED difference between the projection on screen and the one the other policy would produce (mean_abs / max_abs in the document's own codes, changed_fraction over all RGBA samples). Reads only.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `string` | no | — | Which open document; defaults to the frontmost. |
| `preview` | `boolean` | no | — | Measure what switching would change. Renders the document twice, so leave it off unless the number is wanted. |

## `set_evaluation`

Chooses this document's evaluation policy — Image ▸ Evaluation…. One undo step; a policy the document already has is reported unchanged rather than failing. "linear_light" changes what every blend, opacity and mask means, and it REFUSES the operators this phase has not migrated: the non-separable and Dissolve blend modes, layer styles, Blend If, a guided Shadows/Highlights, Image Size, and a colour profile with no matrix/TRC model. The refusal names the layer and the operator, and it applies afterwards too: adding one of them to a linear-light document is refused on the tool that would have added it. Switch back to "encoded" to use them.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `string` | no | — | Which open document; defaults to the frontmost. |
| `policy` | `string` | yes | one of `encoded`, `linear_light` | The evaluation policy to apply. |

## `get_tone_map`

How this 32-bit float document's extended-range linear samples become SDR numbers — on screen and in every 8-bit or 16-bit deliverable. "clip" pins everything at or above white to white; "reinhard" maps the white point exactly to white and compresses everything below it, so highlights above 1.0 stay distinguishable. The reply also carries the float operator table — what the mode evaluates and what it refuses, with the acceptance criterion for each refusal — and float_refusal, the sentence naming the first operator this document could not evaluate. Reads only; refused on a document that is not 32-bit float.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `string` | no | — | Which open document; defaults to the frontmost. |

## `set_tone_map`

Chooses this 32-bit float document's tone map — Image ▸ Tone Map…. One undo step; a map the document already has is reported unchanged rather than failing. "white" belongs to "reinhard" ONLY (1…65504, 4 by default) and is refused on "clip" rather than ignored. The map never touches the stored samples: a 32-bit float export writes them exactly as they are, and undo restores the previous map.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `string` | no | — | Which open document; defaults to the frontmost. |
| `operator` | `string` | yes | one of `clip`, `reinhard` | The tone map operator to apply. |
| `white` | `number` | no | — | Reinhard's white point in linear multiples of diffuse white, 1…65504. Refused with "clip". |

## `move_layers`

Moves a SET of layers by a relative delta — the Move tool's drag and the arrow-key nudge. One moveLayers call and one undo step: a group's subtree and every linked partner follow, and a position lock on any of them refuses the whole set by name. dx is canvas pixels right, dy is canvas pixels down. dx = dy = 0 is reported as an unchanged no-op rather than an error, so a recorded drag that ended where it began replays cleanly. To place ONE layer at an ABSOLUTE position use set_layer_properties' offset_x/offset_y instead (that setter writes one entry and does not follow links). move_layers ignores the selection and moves whole layers; to move only the selected pixels use move_selected_pixels. duplicate: true is the Move tool's ⌥-drag and ⌥+arrow with no selection: it duplicates `layers` (their subtrees; the copies are unlinked and land directly above their sources) and moves the COPIES, one "Duplicate Layer" undo step, and the copies become the layer selection; a zero delta still duplicates, in place. Duplicating is never lock-refused; moving the copies refuses by name when an original, an enclosing group or a group original's descendant carries a position lock (a link partner's lock never refuses). The reply adds `copies` (the copies' indices) and "duplicate": true, and `moved` lists the copies. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document it runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document a move keeps every pixel's index exactly: the one layer stays canvas-sized at the origin, pixels moved past the canvas are dropped and the uncovered area is the transparent index, or with none the entry nearest white, the background colour. duplicate refuses (a copy makes a second layer). On a Bitmap document it runs on the 8-bit gray storage with its sampler and every pixel goes back white where its gray over the background at its alpha reaches 128, else black; area it uncovers takes the background, white; a whole-pixel move or nearest sampler keeps each bit. On a Bitmap document duplicate true refuses: A copy move makes a second layer, which a Bitmap document cannot hold.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `duplicate` | `boolean` | no | — | Default false. True duplicates the layers and moves the copies (the Move tool's ⌥-drag / ⌥+arrow with no selection). |
| `dx` | `integer` | yes | — | Canvas pixels to move right (negative moves left). |
| `dy` | `integer` | yes | — | Canvas pixels to move down (negative moves up). |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | yes | — | Layer indices to move; duplicates are refused. In a recorded Action this is {"$layers": "selected"}. |

## `move_selected_pixels`

Moves the SELECTED PIXELS of one layer by a whole-pixel delta — the Move tool's drag and arrow nudge with a selection active. The layer's pixels × the selection coverage float, move by (dx, dy) and composite back Normal source-over; the hole they leave is transparent (alpha a·(1−coverage), no Background fill), pixels that would land off the canvas are discarded, the layer mask stays put, and the selection moves with the pixels — ONE undo step, "Move". Needs an active selection (move_layers moves whole layers). Consecutive calls on the same layer and target, with the document and selection as the last call left them, move ONE floating selection as consecutive Move drags do: each call is one undo step and pixels the float passed over come back; any other edit, a selection or layer change commits it. One pixel layer only: with several layers selected in the panel, name one with `layer`. Groups, adjustment layers, Quick Mask and a retained source refuse by name; Lock Pixels / Lock All refuse, Lock Transparency and Lock Position allow it. A text or shape layer is rasterized and the result says so. dx = dy = 0 is an unchanged no-op. `duplicate: true` is the Move tool's Option-drag and Option-arrow: no hole, the original stays and the COPY lands source-over, the selection moves with the copy — ONE undo step, "Duplicate". An empty selected area (no opaque pixel under the selection) refuses. Works at 8 and 16 bits and in a 32-bit float document (f32, nothing quantized). `target` "mask" or "channel:<name>" moves the selected area of the layer's mask or of an alpha channel instead — at 8, 16 and 32-bit float (masks and channels are 16-bit coverage there): the plane's selected coverage floats (feathered edges carry through) and lands at (dx, dy), and the vacated area takes `background` (a hex, default #000000) as coverage gray, the background-colour rule for a plane without transparency; `duplicate` leaves no hole. A mask's stored rect grows to hold what lands on the canvas (a group's mask is clipped instead), a channel stays canvas-sized, and the layer's pixels and any description stay. Lock All refuses a mask (Lock Pixels allows it); a channel has no lock; Quick Mask refuses. The reply names the target and background and carries mask_bounds or channel in place of layer_bounds (no layer for a channel). `target` "red", "green", "blue" or "alpha" moves ONE colour channel of the layer's selected pixels instead, at 8, 16 and 32-bit float: only that component lands (the other components and the alpha stay, the layer never grows), the red/green/blue vacated area takes `background`'s 0.30/0.59/0.11 luma rounded to an 8-bit code (default #000000), Alpha's is transparent; selected pixels with no stored alpha float nothing, so a selection over only transparent pixels refuses with "The selection holds no pixels in this colour channel." Lock Pixels refuses, and Lock Transparency an Alpha target too; a text or shape layer is rasterized and the reply is the layer target's. In a CMYK document target is "layer" (the ink), "mask", "channel:<name>" or ONE ink plate, "cyan", "magenta", "yellow" or "black": the other plates and the transparency stay, and the vacated area takes background's (a hex, default #000000, as the UI takes the background swatch) 0.30/0.59/0.11 gray read as ink, 1 − gray, as an RGB channel takes its gray; red, green, blue and alpha refuse by name. In a Grayscale document target is layer, mask or channel:<name> (the Gray channel is the layer; red, green, blue and alpha refuse for good). In a Lab Color document it runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes; target is layer, mask, channel:<name>, lightness, a, b or alpha (red, green and blue refuse: a Lab document's planes are lightness, a and b). On lightness, a or b the vacated area takes that plane's code of background (its L*a*b* by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule: round(L*·255/100), round(a* + 128) or round(b* + 128)); on alpha it is transparent. On an Indexed Color document a move keeps every pixel's index exactly: the one layer stays canvas-sized at the origin, pixels moved past the canvas are dropped and the uncovered area is the transparent index, or with none the entry nearest white, the background colour. A selection with partial coverage maps each changed pixel to its nearest palette entry; target {channel: n} moves an alpha channel as on RGB; a mask target refuses for good, a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses (the one channel is Index). On a Bitmap document it runs on the 8-bit gray storage with its sampler and every pixel goes back white where its gray over the background at its alpha reaches 128, else black; area it uncovers takes the background, white; a whole-pixel move or nearest sampler keeps each bit.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `background` | `string` | no | — | A mask or channel target's vacated-area colour as a hex (#RRGGBB), read as coverage gray; for a red, green or blue target the background colour whose 0.30/0.59/0.11 luma fills the vacated area; default #000000. Refused with a layer or alpha target. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `duplicate` | `boolean` | no | — | Move a COPY and leave the original (the Option-drag or Option-arrow); default false. Echoed in the result. |
| `dx` | `integer` | yes | — | Canvas pixels to move right (negative moves left); \|dx\| ≤ 1,000,000. |
| `dy` | `integer` | yes | — | Canvas pixels to move down (negative moves up); \|dy\| ≤ 1,000,000. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index whose selected pixels move; default the active layer. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | What moves: "layer" (default, the layer's pixels), "mask" (the layer's mask), "channel:<name>" (an alpha channel) or "red", "green", "blue", "alpha" (one colour channel of the layer). |

## `transform_selected_pixels`

Free-transforms the SELECTED PIXELS of one layer — ⌘T with a selection active. The BOX is the float's opaque bounds — the bbox of the layer's pixels with alpha > 0 under the selection, as ⌘T opens it; an empty float refuses. The layer's pixels × the selection coverage float, resample once through the transform (premultiplied, with `sampler`) and composite back Normal source-over; the hole they leave is transparent (alpha a·(1−coverage), no Background fill), pixels that would land off the canvas are discarded, the layer mask stays put, and the selection is transformed with the same map to become the new selection — ONE undo step, "Transform Selected Pixels". Pass transform_layer's rotate / scale / scale_x / scale_y / translate_x / translate_y (around the BOX's center by default, or around / pivot_x / pivot_y), OR `corners` for a distort/perspective of the box — not both. Needs an active selection (transform_layer transforms whole layers and ignores the selection). One pixel layer only: with several layers selected in the panel, name one with `layer`; links are ignored. Groups, adjustment layers, Quick Mask and a retained source refuse by name; Lock Pixels / Lock All refuse, Lock Transparency and Lock Position allow it. A text or shape layer is rasterized and the result says so. An identity is an unchanged no-op. Returns the box, the layer's new bounds and the new selection bounds. `duplicate: true` is ⌥⌘T, Free Transform a Copy: no hole, the original stays and the transformed COPY lands source-over, the selection transforms with the copy — ONE undo step, "Transform Copy"; echoed in the result. Works at 8 and 16 bits and in a 32-bit float document (f32, nothing quantized; a filtered resample clamps each RGB component to the floated pixels' own visible range and drops alpha below 2^-24). `target` "mask" or "channel:<name>" transforms the selected area of the layer's mask or of an alpha channel instead — at 8, 16 and 32-bit float (masks and channels are 16-bit coverage there): the BOX is the selection's bounds, the plane's selected coverage floats (feathered edges carry through) and lands back through the same resample, and the vacated area takes `background` (a hex, default #000000) as coverage gray, the background-colour rule for a plane without transparency; `duplicate` leaves no hole. A mask's stored rect grows to hold what lands on the canvas (a group's mask is clipped instead), a channel stays canvas-sized, and the layer's pixels and any description stay. Lock All refuses a mask (Lock Pixels allows it); a channel has no lock; Quick Mask refuses. The reply names the target and carries mask_bounds or channel in place of layer_bounds. `target` "red", "green", "blue" or "alpha" transforms ONE colour channel of the layer's selected pixels instead, at 8, 16 and 32-bit float: only that component lands (the other components and the alpha stay, the layer never grows), the red/green/blue vacated area takes `background`'s 0.30/0.59/0.11 luma rounded to an 8-bit code (default #000000), Alpha's is transparent; selected pixels with no stored alpha float nothing, so a selection over only transparent pixels refuses with "The selection holds no pixels in this colour channel." Lock Pixels refuses, and Lock Transparency an Alpha target too; a text or shape layer is rasterized and the reply is the layer target's. The box is then the selection's bounds. In a CMYK document target is "layer" (the ink), "mask", "channel:<name>" or ONE ink plate, "cyan", "magenta", "yellow" or "black": the other plates and the transparency stay, and the vacated area takes background's (a hex, default #000000, as the UI takes the background swatch) 0.30/0.59/0.11 gray read as ink, 1 − gray, as an RGB channel takes its gray; red, green, blue and alpha refuse by name. In a Grayscale document target is layer, mask or channel:<name> (the Gray channel is the layer; red, green, blue and alpha refuse for good). In a Lab Color document it runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes; target is layer, mask, channel:<name>, lightness, a, b or alpha (red, green and blue refuse: a Lab document's planes are lightness, a and b). On lightness, a or b the vacated area takes that plane's code of background (its L*a*b* by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule: round(L*·255/100), round(a* + 128) or round(b* + 128)); on alpha it is transparent. On an Indexed Color document the one layer transforms in place: a whole-pixel translation, or a nearest sampler (and, for selected pixels, a selection with no partial coverage), keeps every pixel's index exactly, a floated transparent pixel landing nothing; any other edit resamples the colours and maps each changed pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as uncovered area), unchanged pixels keeping theirs. Uncovered area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour. A warp is applied at once and keeps no editable field (get_warp answers null; clear and bake change nothing). duplicate on transform_layers or transform_again refuses (a copy makes a second layer). Selected pixels of an alpha channel (target {channel: n}) transform as on RGB, the layer untouched; a mask target refuses for good (an Indexed layer holds no mask), and a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses (the one channel is Index). A Bitmap document: not available in Bitmap mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `around` | `string` | no | one of `center`, `top_left` | The pivot: "center" (default) or "top_left" of the BOX. pivot_x / pivot_y override it. |
| `background` | `string` | no | — | A mask or channel target's vacated-area colour as a hex (#RRGGBB), read as coverage gray; for a red, green or blue target the background colour whose 0.30/0.59/0.11 luma fills the vacated area; default #000000. Refused with a layer or alpha target. |
| `corners` | `array<array<number>>` | no | — | Four [x, y] canvas destinations of the BOX's top-left, top-right, bottom-right and bottom-left corners (a convex quad); exclusive with the matrix arguments. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `duplicate` | `boolean` | no | — | Transform a COPY and leave the original (⌥⌘T); default false. Echoed in the result. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index whose selected pixels transform; default the active layer. |
| `pivot_x` | `number` | no | — | Explicit pivot x in canvas px. |
| `pivot_y` | `number` | no | — | Explicit pivot y in canvas px. |
| `rotate` | `number` | no | — | Rotation in degrees around the pivot; POSITIVE IS CLOCKWISE on screen. |
| `sampler` | `string` | no | one of `nearest`, `bilinear`, `bicubic`, `lanczos` | Resampling filter, default bicubic (Catmull-Rom). Whole-pixel moves are lossless whatever this says. |
| `scale` | `number` | no | — | Uniform scale multiplier (1 = unchanged, negative mirrors); magnitudes clamp to 0.001-100 and 0 is refused. |
| `scale_x` | `number` | no | — | Horizontal scale multiplier, overriding scale. |
| `scale_y` | `number` | no | — | Vertical scale multiplier, overriding scale. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | What transforms: "layer" (default, the layer's pixels), "mask" (the layer's mask), "channel:<name>" (an alpha channel) or "red", "green", "blue", "alpha" (one colour channel of the layer). |
| `translate_x` | `number` | no | — | Move right by this many canvas px, after the rotation and scale. |
| `translate_y` | `number` | no | — | Move down by this many canvas px, after the rotation and scale. |

## `transform_again`

Repeats the last committed Free Transform — Layer ▸ Transform Again (⇧⌘T), or with `duplicate` Layer ▸ Transform Again with Copy (⌥⇧⌘T). The APPLICATION remembers ONE transform, shared by every document: the canvas-space matrix, pivot included, its sampler and the canvas size of the document it was committed in. It is set by every committed ⌘T / ⌥⌘T in the app and by transform_layer, transform_layers, distort_layer and transform_selected_pixels (and by transform_again itself), only when the edit changed something; a parallelogram distort stores its affine, and a TRUE PERSPECTIVE is remembered as its corners over its source rectangle. Undo, redo, history and closing a document never change it, and it is never saved. It repeats only in a document whose canvas is the size it was committed on: an edit that changes the canvas size makes it unavailable until the size is back (undo, or sizing back), Rotate 180°, the flips and a quarter turn of a square canvas keep it, and it is never remapped. The matrix is applied VERBATIM in canvas space — no pivot is re-derived from the new target — so repeating a 15° turn on the same content gives 30° about the same pivot, a 10 px move becomes 20 px, and a different layer turns about the same canvas point; a true perspective repeats as the same canvas-space perspective (the reply carries source_rect and corners in place of matrix). With one, a text, shape or artwork layer in a layer target needs rasterize_artwork (transform_layers' rule), and a target the map would fold past its horizon refuses in band, changing nothing. The target is ⌘T's: with a selection, the ACTIVE layer's selected pixels (transform_selected_pixels' rules: one pixel layer, the hole transparent, the selection transformed with them); without one, the selected layers with their groups' descendants and linked partners (transform_layers' rules). ONE undo step, "Transform Again", or "Transform Again with Copy" with `duplicate`: over a selection a transformed COPY of the pixels lands and no hole is left; without one the selected layers are duplicated, the copies transform and become the layer selection (the result lists `copies`). Refuses in band when no transform is remembered or it was committed on a canvas of another size (the refusal names both sizes), on a Position lock (layers) or a Pixels lock (selected pixels), for an empty selected area, a group, an adjustment layer, Quick Mask and several layers selected with a selection. A described layer whose pixels are resampled is rasterized and the result says so; with an affine memory, one text or shape layer at 8 bits composes into its description instead. `duplicate` with no selection applies the same rules to the COPIES (transform_layers' duplicate rules): one copied text or shape layer at 8 bits composes into its own description, a remembered true perspective over described copies needs rasterize_artwork, and rasterized_layers lists the copies whose description was dropped. Works at 8 and 16 bits and in a 32-bit float document, with or without a selection. With a selection, `target` "mask" or "channel:<name>" repeats onto the selected area of the active layer's mask or of an alpha channel (transform_selected_pixels' plane rules: the box is the selection's bounds, the vacated area takes `background`, default #000000) — also in a 32-bit float document; the memory itself stores no target, so each call names it. A mask or channel target with no selection refuses (transform_mask transforms a whole mask). With a selection, `target` "red", "green", "blue" or "alpha" repeats onto that colour channel of the active layer (transform_selected_pixels' colour-plane rules, `background`'s rounded 30/59/11 luma as the red/green/blue vacated value). In a 32-bit float document it repeats a layer transform, and with a selection a Free Transform of the selected pixels (the floated pixels' RGB is clamped to their own visible range). Available in a 32-bit float document: the resample is premultiplied over the extended-range samples, each layer's RGB is clamped to that layer's own visible range so a filter's ringing never leaves it, an output alpha below 2^-24 becomes transparent, and a float result past 67,108,864 pixels refuses before any work. Masks stay 16-bit coverage and resample exactly as at 16 bits. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document the one layer transforms in place: a whole-pixel translation, or a nearest sampler (and, for selected pixels, a selection with no partial coverage), keeps every pixel's index exactly, a floated transparent pixel landing nothing; any other edit resamples the colours and maps each changed pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as uncovered area), unchanged pixels keeping theirs. Uncovered area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour. A warp is applied at once and keeps no editable field (get_warp answers null; clear and bake change nothing). duplicate on transform_layers or transform_again refuses (a copy makes a second layer). Selected pixels of an alpha channel (target {channel: n}) transform as on RGB, the layer untouched; a mask target refuses for good (an Indexed layer holds no mask), and a red, green, blue or alpha target refuses (the one channel is Index). A Bitmap document: not available in Bitmap mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `background` | `string` | no | — | A mask or channel target's vacated-area colour as a hex, read as coverage gray; for a red, green or blue target the background colour whose 0.30/0.59/0.11 luma fills the vacated area; default #000000. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `duplicate` | `boolean` | no | — | Transform a COPY and leave the original (⌥⇧⌘T); default false. |
| `rasterize_artwork` | `boolean` | no | — | Authorize rasterizing text, shape or artwork layers (or their copies, with `duplicate`) when the remembered transform is a true perspective and the target is layers; default false. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | With a selection: "layer" (default, the active layer's selected pixels), "mask", "channel:<name>" or "red", "green", "blue", "alpha". |

## `reorder_layers`

Moves SEVERAL layers to one place in the stack — the layers panel's multi-row drag. One undo step. `at` is the insertion index in the CURRENT numbering (the drop line: 0 is the bottom, layer_count is above everything), NOT reorder_layer's `to`, which numbers the stack with the moved subtree already taken out. Entries keep their relative order and their subtrees, and every one lands at `depth`. Refused when `at` falls inside one of the moving subtrees, and when the (at, depth) pair would not leave a well-formed tree — an entry at depth d needs an enclosing group, and the topmost entry sits at depth 0. Returns `landed`, the new index of each entry in the order given. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good: it needs more than one layer, and an Indexed Color document holds one.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `at` | `integer` | yes | — | Insertion index in the current numbering (0 … layer_count). |
| `depth` | `integer` | no | — | Level everything lands at; omit for the level the entry below the line sits in. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | yes | — | Layer indices to move; duplicates are refused. An entry that already travels inside another named GROUP should be left out. |

## `run_batch`

Plays an action over every image in a FOLDER, writing the results into another folder — the Batch window, headless. Returns a batch_id immediately; poll batch_status for progress and the per-file report, and cancel_batch to stop at the next file boundary. ONE batch runs at a time app-wide, and while it runs every other tool is refused in band except batch_status, cancel_batch, job_status, cancel_job and resource_usage. Naming: {name} is the input's basename and {n} a 1-based number zero-padded to the file count's width; the extension is always the chosen format's. {n}, and a preset pattern's {index}, are positions in THIS run's file list, so re-running over a folder that has gained or lost files renumbers the outputs instead of colliding with the earlier run's — the skips below cannot catch that. A name that would land outside the output folder, one a previous file in the run already claimed, and an existing file without overwrite are each SKIPPED with a reason — a batch never writes over a file it did not create in this run. stop_on_error (default true) halts the run at the first failed step AND leaves that file unwritten; false writes each file in whatever state the action left it and lists the failures against it. With `preset` the delivery goes through quick_export instead, and the preset's folder, pattern and options replace output/name_template/overwrite; the preset's name is expanded before each encode, and a file that already exists is SKIPPED with a reason too — never overwritten, and never a halt, even with stop_on_error. A parameter that will not bind, and a preset whose destination folder does not exist, are refused HERE, before any file is opened, with no batch_id. A preset naming a profile that cannot be exported into (describe_profile's export_refusal) is decided per file at run time: a file not already in that profile fails its row with that sentence and is not written, while a file already in it exports unchanged under a non-absolute intent without black_point_compensation.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `embed_profile` | `boolean` | no | — | Write the ICC profile; default true. |
| `format` | `string` | no | one of `png`, `jpg`, `tiff`, `bmp`, `gif`, `webp` | Output format; default png. Ignored with `preset`. |
| `input` | `string` | yes | — | Folder of images, top level only — a batch never recurses. |
| `jpeg_quality` | `integer` | no | — | 0–100, JPEG only; default 90. |
| `metadata_policy` | `string` | no | — | Named metadata policy overriding the preset's own (list_metadata_policies). Preset mode only. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | Action to play on each file. |
| `name_template` | `string` | no | — | Output name pattern, {name} and {n}; default "{name}". No "/" or ":", and no extension. |
| `output` | `string` | no | — | Folder the results are written into; created if missing, and it must not be the input folder. Ignored (and unnecessary) with `preset`. |
| `overwrite` | `boolean` | no | — | Replace an existing output file; default false, which skips it with a reason. |
| `parameters` | `object` | no | — | Values for the action's declared parameters (list_actions {name} reports them). Refused at submission if a required one is missing or a value is the wrong type. |
| `preset` | `string` | no | — | Export preset to deliver through (list_export_presets). A batch never overwrites and never suffixes: a file that already exists is skipped, not a halt (the -2, -3, … names are quick_export's own interactive form, not a batch's). Its destination folder must exist, or the run is refused with no batch_id. |
| `stop_on_error` | `boolean` | no | — | Halt at the first failed step and leave that file unwritten; default true. |
| `strip_metadata` | `boolean` | no | — | Drop EXIF/XMP/IPTC; default false. |

## `batch_status`

How the running batch — or the last one that finished in this session — is getting on: running, processed, total, and the full report with one row per file (wrote / skipped / failed, each with its reason). One of the few tools that answers WHILE a batch runs.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `batch_id` | `string` | no | — | Optional; only one batch runs at a time, but passing the id refuses an answer about a different run. |

## `cancel_batch`

Stops the running batch at the next file boundary. The file in flight finishes — a core call cannot be interrupted, and abandoning a half-written output is worse than one more file. Poll batch_status for the final report.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `batch_id` | `string` | no | — | Optional; see batch_status. |

## `package_action`

Writes an action and the FILES it uses into a <slug>.draction bundle — the only way to make an action somebody else can run. Each file argument (place_image.path, add_live_photo_layer.path, and convert_profile/assign_profile.path when profile is "file") is copied into the bundle's assets/ folder and rewritten IN THE BUNDLE to {"$asset": "<basename>"}; the action in the library is not modified. Two DIFFERENT source paths sharing a basename become logo.png and logo-2.png, each step pointing at its own; the same path used twice is one entry. A missing source file refuses the whole call, naming the path, and leaves no partial bundle. quick_export's destination is deliberately NOT an asset — it is a per-machine output folder, not an input.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `destination` | `string` | yes | — | FOLDER the bundle is written into; the bundle itself is named after the action's slug. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | Action to package. |
| `overwrite` | `boolean` | no | — | Replace an existing bundle of that name; default false, which refuses. |

## `import_action`

Installs a <slug>.draction bundle into the action library: the action, then its assets/ files beside it, so every {"$asset": …} step resolves. The bundle's own decode refusals surface verbatim, by step number. `name` renames it on the way in. Without overwrite a name that is already taken refuses rather than replacing an action somebody built; with it, both the action and its assets folder are replaced.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Install under this display name instead of the bundle's own. |
| `overwrite` | `boolean` | no | — | Replace a same-named action and its assets; default false. |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | The .draction FOLDER (it holds action.json and assets/). |

## `set_layer_label`

Layer > Label: mark one layer or a `layers` SET with a colour label, in ONE undo step. A label is panel bookkeeping — it changes no pixel and is exempt from the layer locks, like a rename — and it persists in the .doctored at both depths and in a layered PSD's `lclr`. The reply reports `layers` (written), `skipped` (already at that label) and `changed`; when every entry is skipped no undo step is added. On an Indexed Color document the one layer takes a name, a colour label, locks, visibility (hidden, it renders clear, keeps its indices and saves hidden in .doctored; a kept-palette export refuses until it is shown) and an offset (a whole-pixel move: the layer stays canvas-sized at the origin, so the offset reads 0 after and pixels moved past the canvas are dropped); open applies to groups only; opacity and blend mode are not available in Indexed Color.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `label` | `string` | yes | one of `none`, `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue`, `violet`, `gray` | A colour label. Photoshop's palette and its `lclr` codes, so a label survives export to PSD and back. "none" clears it. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index (0 = bottom); omit for the active layer. An index may name a layer GROUP, which carries a label like any other entry. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | no | — | Several layers, exclusive with `layer`. In a recorded Action this is {"$layers": "selected"}. |

## `find_layers`

The layers panel's filter bar: find entries by name substring (case- and diacritic-insensitive), by kind and by colour label, ANDed. A READ — no document changes — and it walks EVERY entry whatever a group's disclosure state is, so a match inside a closed group is reported. Each row carries index, id, name, kind, label and depth.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `kind` | `string` | no | one of `raster`, `adjustment`, `text`, `shape`, `group`, `embedded` | raster, adjustment, text, shape, group, or embedded (a camera RAW layer). |
| `label` | `string` | no | one of `none`, `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue`, `violet`, `gray` | A colour label. Photoshop's palette and its `lclr` codes, so a label survives export to PSD and back. "none" clears it. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Name substring. |

## `list_layer_comps`

Window > Layer Comps: every layer comp of a document, in list order. A READ — no document changes. Each row carries index, name, comment, the three `captures` flags, `stale_count`, `locked_count` and one `entries` row per layer with its CURRENT `layer` index (null when the layer is gone), the core's stable `id`, the `name` it was recorded under, `stale` and `locked`. An entry binds by that PERSISTED id at every depth, so a comp survives a save, a reopen, a reorder AND a rename; `locked` is a real answer at every depth too (a position-locked layer keeps its recorded offset and reports it). Each entry also carries the state the comp RECORDED — exactly what apply_layer_comp writes back — in get_document's vocabulary, each key present only when the comp captured it: `visible` (visibility), `offset` [x, y] (position; RASTER layers only), and `opacity`, `blend_mode` and `style` (appearance). `style` is the object set_layer_style takes, or null when the layer had no style when the comp was recorded. Each row also carries `unrecorded`: the layers ({layer, id, name}) the comp has no entry for and that are not groups — the ones apply_layer_comp would hide. A Grayscale document holds layer comps, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored; applying one skips a recorded blend mode or style the mode cannot hold. A Lab Color document holds layer comps, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored and through Image ▸ Mode between RGB, Grayscale and Lab Color; applying one skips a recorded blend mode or style the mode cannot hold.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `save_layer_comp`

Window > Layer Comps > New…: record the document's CURRENT per-layer visibility, position and appearance under a name, in ONE undo step. A comp holds no pixels, no selection and no history — that is what create_snapshot is for — and it travels in the .doctored at both depths. Up to 64 per document; a duplicate name is refused. A Grayscale document holds layer comps, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored; applying one skips a recorded blend mode or style the mode cannot hold. A Lab Color document holds layer comps, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored and through Image ▸ Mode between RGB, Grayscale and Lab Color; applying one skips a recorded blend mode or style the mode cannot hold.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `appearance` | `boolean` | no | — | Record each layer's opacity, blend mode and layer style. Default true. Naming ANY of visibility, position or appearance states the WHOLE set: an unnamed flag becomes true. |
| `comment` | `string` | no | — | Free text shown beside the comp. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | The comp's name. Comp names are unique within a document and are the handle every one of these tools takes. |
| `position` | `boolean` | no | — | Record each RASTER layer's offset (a group and an adjustment have none). Default true. Naming ANY of visibility, position or appearance states the WHOLE set: an unnamed flag becomes true. |
| `visibility` | `boolean` | no | — | Record each layer's visibility. Default true. Naming ANY of visibility, position or appearance states the WHOLE set: an unnamed flag becomes true. |

## `apply_layer_comp`

Window > Layer Comps > Apply: put the document back into the state a comp recorded, in ONE undo step. Only the attributes the comp captures are written. The reply reports `applied` (the layer indices that were written), `stale` (entries whose layer is gone, by the name they were recorded under), `locked` (bound entries whose recorded POSITION a layer lock forbids — their visibility and appearance still apply) and `changed`; when the document already held that state no undo step is added. Apply also HIDES every layer the comp has no record of (one added, placed, pasted or duplicated after the comp was saved or last updated), at any depth, whatever the comp captured and whatever its locks, except groups, which keep their visibility; the reply names those layers in `hidden_unrecorded`. A Grayscale document holds layer comps, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored; applying one skips a recorded blend mode or style the mode cannot hold. A Lab Color document holds layer comps, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored and through Image ▸ Mode between RGB, Grayscale and Lab Color; applying one skips a recorded blend mode or style the mode cannot hold.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | The comp's name. Comp names are unique within a document and are the handle every one of these tools takes. |

## `update_layer_comp`

Window > Layer Comps > Update / Options…: re-record a comp from the document's current state, and/or rename it, re-comment it and change which attributes it captures. `recapture` defaults to true; with it false only the name, comment and flags move, and the comp's stale entries are dropped while its bound entries take their layers' current names. A recapture records every layer, so a layer the comp had no record of is no longer hidden by apply; with `recapture` false it stays unrecorded and apply still hides it. A Grayscale document holds layer comps, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored; applying one skips a recorded blend mode or style the mode cannot hold. A Lab Color document holds layer comps, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored and through Image ▸ Mode between RGB, Grayscale and Lab Color; applying one skips a recorded blend mode or style the mode cannot hold.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `appearance` | `boolean` | no | — | Record each layer's opacity, blend mode and layer style. Default true. Naming ANY of visibility, position or appearance states the WHOLE set: an unnamed flag becomes true. |
| `comment` | `string` | no | — | Replaces the comp's comment. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | The comp's name. Comp names are unique within a document and are the handle every one of these tools takes. |
| `new_name` | `string` | no | — | A new name for the comp. |
| `position` | `boolean` | no | — | Record each RASTER layer's offset (a group and an adjustment have none). Default true. Naming ANY of visibility, position or appearance states the WHOLE set: an unnamed flag becomes true. |
| `recapture` | `boolean` | no | — | Re-record from the current state. Default true. |
| `visibility` | `boolean` | no | — | Record each layer's visibility. Default true. Naming ANY of visibility, position or appearance states the WHOLE set: an unnamed flag becomes true. |

## `delete_layer_comp`

Window > Layer Comps > Delete: remove one comp, in ONE undo step. The document's layers are untouched — deleting a comp forgets a recording, it does not undo one. A Grayscale document holds layer comps, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored; applying one skips a recorded blend mode or style the mode cannot hold. A Lab Color document holds layer comps, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored and through Image ▸ Mode between RGB, Grayscale and Lab Color; applying one skips a recorded blend mode or style the mode cannot hold.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | The comp's name. Comp names are unique within a document and are the handle every one of these tools takes. |

## `reorder_layer_comp`

Window > Layer Comps (drag a row): move one comp to FINAL index `to` (counted with it taken out, as reorder_layer counts). The list order is what ◀ ▶ step through and what list_layer_comps returns, and it travels in the .doctored. ONE undo step; the comp's own index adds none. Layer locks do not apply. A Grayscale document holds layer comps, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored; applying one skips a recorded blend mode or style the mode cannot hold. A Lab Color document holds layer comps, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored and through Image ▸ Mode between RGB, Grayscale and Lab Color; applying one skips a recorded blend mode or style the mode cannot hold.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | The comp's name. Comp names are unique within a document and are the handle every one of these tools takes. |
| `to` | `integer` | yes | 0–∞ | The comp's FINAL index in the list, 0 first. |

## `new_document`

File > New…: start a document with no seed image — dimensions in px/in/cm/mm at a PPI, a colour profile, 8, 16 or 32 (float) bits, and a background fill. Pass `preset` to use a saved document preset instead of the explicit fields (mixing the two is refused). Creating a document is not recorded as an Action step, for open_document's reason. color_mode "cmyk" makes a CMYK document at depth 8 or 16 in profile "working" (Color Settings' working CMYK) or a CMYK profile path.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `background` | `string` | no | default `transparent` | transparent, white, black or a #rrggbb colour. A transparent document's one layer is named "Layer 1"; a filled one's is "Background". |
| `color_mode` | `string` | no | one of `rgb`, `cmyk`, `gray`, `lab`; default `rgb` | File > New's Color Mode. cmyk makes a CMYK document of ink at depth 8 or 16: white is bare paper, transparent alpha 0, black or a #rrggbb colour separated through the document's CMYK profile. gray makes a Grayscale document at depth 8, 16 or 32: the background's luminance in the Gray profile. lab makes a Lab Color document (D50) at depth 8 or 16: the background converted from sRGB, relative colorimetric. |
| `depth` | `integer` | no | one of `8`, `16`, `32`; default `8` | 8, 16 or 32. 32 is a 32-bit float document holding linear light: the 16-bit fill converted as convert_precision rgba32 converts it, so white is exactly 1.0, black and transparent 0, and a #rrggbb colour its value decoded through the profile's tone curve. |
| `height` | `number` | no | — | A length in `unit`; rounded to whole pixels, 1 to 20000 per side. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | The window title; omit for Untitled. |
| `ppi` | `number` | no | default `300` | Print resolution, 1 to 30000. Pixels never change with it — only the print size does. |
| `preset` | `string` | no | — | A saved document preset's name. |
| `profile` | `string` | no | default `srgb` | srgb, display_p3, or the path of an RGB ICC profile file; with color_mode cmyk, working (the default: Edit ▸ Color Settings' working CMYK) or the path of a CMYK ICC profile; with color_mode gray, working (the default: Edit ▸ Color Settings' working Gray), a Gray space (dot_gain_10, dot_gain_15, dot_gain_20, dot_gain_25, dot_gain_30, gray_gamma_18, gray_gamma_22, sgray) or the path of a Gray ICC profile; with color_mode lab, lab (the default and only value). A GRAY profile is refused by name for rgb. |
| `unit` | `string` | no | one of `px`, `in`, `cm`, `mm`; default `px` | — |
| `width` | `number` | no | — | A length in `unit`; rounded to whole pixels, 1 to 20000 per side. |

## `list_document_presets`

File > New… > Preset: list the bounded versioned document-preset library. A file that is not a readable preset is reported as a `broken` row — {file, code, reason, repairable} with code one of unreadable, oversize, not_json, unknown_version, invalid_schema, duplicate_name — instead of refusing the whole library; repair is RAW-only, so repairable is always false here.

Takes no arguments.

## `save_document_preset`

File > New… > Save Preset…: store a size, unit, PPI, profile, depth and background under a name. A library write is a preference: no Undo step, no Action step.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `background` | `string` | no | default `transparent` | transparent, white, black or a #rrggbb colour. A transparent document's one layer is named "Layer 1"; a filled one's is "Background". |
| `color_mode` | `string` | no | one of `rgb`, `cmyk`, `gray`, `lab`; default `rgb` | File > New's Color Mode. cmyk makes a CMYK document of ink at depth 8 or 16: white is bare paper, transparent alpha 0, black or a #rrggbb colour separated through the document's CMYK profile. gray makes a Grayscale document at depth 8, 16 or 32: the background's luminance in the Gray profile. lab makes a Lab Color document (D50) at depth 8 or 16: the background converted from sRGB, relative colorimetric. |
| `depth` | `integer` | no | one of `8`, `16`, `32`; default `8` | 8, 16 or 32. 32 is a 32-bit float document holding linear light: the 16-bit fill converted as convert_precision rgba32 converts it, so white is exactly 1.0, black and transparent 0, and a #rrggbb colour its value decoded through the profile's tone curve. |
| `height` | `number` | yes | — | A length in `unit`; rounded to whole pixels, 1 to 20000 per side. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | Preset display name, 1–120 characters. |
| `ppi` | `number` | no | default `300` | Print resolution, 1 to 30000. Pixels never change with it — only the print size does. |
| `profile` | `string` | no | default `srgb` | srgb, display_p3, or the path of an RGB ICC profile file; with color_mode cmyk, working (the default: Edit ▸ Color Settings' working CMYK) or the path of a CMYK ICC profile; with color_mode gray, working (the default: Edit ▸ Color Settings' working Gray), a Gray space (dot_gain_10, dot_gain_15, dot_gain_20, dot_gain_25, dot_gain_30, gray_gamma_18, gray_gamma_22, sgray) or the path of a Gray ICC profile; with color_mode lab, lab (the default and only value). A GRAY profile is refused by name for rgb. |
| `replace` | `boolean` | no | default `False` | — |
| `unit` | `string` | no | one of `px`, `in`, `cm`, `mm`; default `px` | — |
| `width` | `number` | yes | — | A length in `unit`; rounded to whole pixels, 1 to 20000 per side. |
