## `get_view`

The Navigator's readout: this window's zoom, the centre and the rectangle it is showing (canvas pixels, top-left origin), the canvas size, the view rotation, the view's ordinal, the document's revision and the document-wide sync_pan_zoom switch, plus exposure (the window's view exposure in stops; 0 unless the document is 32-bit float) and exposure_displayed (true once the canvas shows the image rendered for that exposure; false at 0 stops, where there is nothing to render, unless HDR Preview shows the extended-range view), and View > HDR Preview: hdr_preview (the window's switch), hdr_preview_displayed (true once the extended-range image is on screen), edr_headroom (the screen's potential EDR headroom; above 1 means HDR Preview can engage), edr_layer (the canvas layer is EDR-configured), edr_content_peak (the largest RGB value of the extended-range image on screen, null when none); with image_hash true the reply adds view_image_sha256 (SHA-256 of the image the canvas draws, null when none; off by default because it hashes the whole image). A read; view state is per window and is not recorded as an Action step. Omitting `view` ALWAYS means view 1 — the document's first window, never whichever one is key.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `image_hash` | `boolean` | no | default `False` | — |
| `view` | `integer` | no | — | Which view (window) of the document, as list_views reports it. Omit it for view 1 — the document's FIRST window, never whichever window happens to be key. |

## `set_view`

Navigator: click-to-centre, drag-to-pan and the zoom slider, plus View > Rotate View and View > 32-bit Exposure. Pass at least one of zoom, center, rotation, fit, exposure, hdr_preview or sync_pan_zoom. `rotation` turns the VIEW only, never a pixel: degrees, positive CLOCKWISE, normalized into (-180, 180]. `fit` is Zoom to Fit and cannot be combined with zoom. `exposure` is a 32-bit float window's view exposure in stops, and its redraw is asynchronous (exposure_displayed). `hdr_preview` is View > HDR Preview (hdr_preview_displayed). `sync_pan_zoom` is DOCUMENT-wide, not per view. This writes NO document — no pixel, no undo step, no dirty flag and nothing a save_copy would carry — so it is not recorded as an Action step, on set_proof_setup's precedent. The reply is the READ-BACK state: the clip view constrains its own origin, so a centre near an edge lands where it can. Omitting `view` ALWAYS means view 1, never whichever window is key.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `center` | `object` | no | — | The point to centre the well on, in canvas pixels (top-left origin). Outside the canvas it is refused by name. |
| `center.x` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `center.y` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `exposure` | `number` | no | — | View > 32-bit Exposure: this window's view exposure in stops, -20 to 20, on a 32-bit float document. Gain 2^stops on RGB before the tone map, alpha untouched, so a negative exposure brings values above white into view on screen. It changes how the WINDOW draws, never the samples: readouts, samplers, render, exports and saved files do not see it (render has its own exposure argument). 0 is the document's own display. Outside -20…20, and non-zero on a document that is not 32-bit float, it is refused by name. The canvas redraws asynchronously: the reply usually carries exposure_displayed false, and a later get_view reports true once the exposed image is on screen. |
| `fit` | `boolean` | no | — | Zoom to Fit. Cannot be combined with zoom, which would be two answers to one question. |
| `hdr_preview` | `boolean` | no | — | View > HDR Preview: this window's switch, on by default. On an EDR screen (get_view edr_headroom above 1) a 32-bit float window then shows values above 1.0 brighter than white, with the view exposure applied and no tone map; off, or on any other screen, the tone-mapped view stays as it is. Accepted at every depth, it acts only on a 32-bit float document, and never while the Tone Map sheet previews a map. View state only: readouts, render, exports and saves never see it. The redraw is asynchronous (hdr_preview_displayed). |
| `rotation` | `number` | no | — | View-only rotation in degrees, positive CLOCKWISE. Normalized into (-180, 180], so 370 reads back as 10. It turns the VIEW, never the pixels: the render is byte-identical before and after, and every coordinate this surface takes stays document space. |
| `sync_pan_zoom` | `boolean` | no | — | Window > Sync Pan & Zoom. DOCUMENT-wide, not per view: with it on, a zoom or pan in one view is applied to the document's other views. Rotation is never synchronized. |
| `view` | `integer` | no | — | Which view (window) of the document, as list_views reports it. Omit it for view 1 — the document's FIRST window, never whichever window happens to be key. |
| `zoom` | `number` | no | — | Magnification: 1 is 100 %. 0.02 to 32; outside that it is refused by name rather than clamped. |

## `list_workspaces`

Window > Workspaces: the bounded versioned workspace-layout library. A file that is not a readable workspace is reported as a `broken` row — {file, code, reason, repairable} with code one of unreadable, oversize, not_json, unknown_version, invalid_schema, duplicate_name — instead of refusing the whole library; repair is RAW-only, so repairable is always false here.

Takes no arguments.

## `save_workspace`

Window > Workspaces > Save Workspace…: store this window's frame, the right panel's visibility, tab and width, the rulers/grid/snap toggles and the current tool under a name. The document's zoom and scroll position are deliberately NOT stored — those are per document (get_view/set_view). A library write is a preference: no Undo step, no Action step.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | Workspace display name, 1–120 characters. |
| `replace` | `boolean` | no | default `False` | — |

## `restore_workspace`

Window > Workspaces > <name>: apply a saved layout to this window. `applied` is a fresh capture taken AFTER the apply, so it reports what actually landed. A frame that lies inside the usable area (the union of the screens' visible frames) is kept exactly. Otherwise it is moved, and shrunk if needed, wholly onto one display. A full-screen window keeps its frame, and a tool the document's depth refuses is skipped rather than refused.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | Workspace display name, 1–120 characters. |

## `delete_workspace`

Window > Workspaces > Delete Workspace > <name>: remove ONE library file. Pass exactly one of name (a listed workspace) or file (any library file, including a broken one that has no name); passing both or neither is refused.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `file` | `string` | no | — | A library file basename from list_workspaces (a row's `file`). Pass exactly one of name or file; a broken entry has no name. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Workspace display name, 1–120 characters. |

## `open_second_view`

Window > New View for “<document>”: a second window on the SAME document. One picture, one history, one undo stack; each window keeps its own zoom, scroll, view rotation and — on a 32-bit float document — view exposure. A 100 % detail beside a fit overview is what this is for — pass zoom/center/rotation/fit/exposure to set the new view up in the same call. Writes NO document, so it is not recorded as an Action step.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `center` | `object` | no | — | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `exposure` | `number` | no | — | 32-bit float documents only: the new view's exposure in stops, -20 to 20 (set_view describes it). |
| `fit` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `rotation` | `number` | no | — | — |
| `sync_pan_zoom` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `zoom` | `number` | no | — | — |

## `close_second_view`

Close ONE view of a document. `view` is required. The document's LAST view is refused by name: closing it would close the document, which an MCP client does with close_document (the in-app Assistant asks the user to close it in the app). Closing a view changes no document: the pixels, the history and the unsaved-changes flag are exactly what they were.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `view` | `integer` | yes | — | Which view (window) to close, as list_views reports it. REQUIRED — there is no default, because closing the wrong window is not something a caller can take back. |

## `list_views`

The document's open views: each one's zoom, centre, visible rectangle, view rotation, view exposure (exposure, exposure_displayed) and ordinal, plus whether it is the key window. `sync_pan_zoom` is DOCUMENT-wide, not per view. A read.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `get_color_samplers`

The document's Color Samplers (Info panel ▸ Color Samplers): up to 10 pinned points read live from the composite. Each sampler reports index (0-based), label ("#n", as the Info panel numbers it), x, y, sample_size and sample_pixel's own reading at that point and size — the 8-bit byte fields, or the 16-bit/32-bit float composite report. Committed values only. A read. In a Lab Color document each sampler is sample_pixel's own reading: its codes are L*, a*, b* and alpha, and it adds lab {l, a, b} with no RGB reading.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `set_color_samplers`

Replace the document's Color Samplers — the Color Sampler tool's add, move and delete, and View > Clear Color Samplers: pass the whole new list, [] to clear. At most 10; each x/y must lie on the canvas and sample_size must be 1, 3 or 5 (default 1). A refusal leaves the list unchanged; it is refused by name while a gesture, an edit or a job is running on the document. The list is saved with the document (.doctored, and PSD image resource 1073, which stores no sample size): setting it dirties the document but adds no undo step and is not recorded as an Action step. A crop, canvas size, flip, rotate, straighten or resize moves the samplers with the content and drops any that land off the canvas; ordinary undo and redo keep the current list, and undoing a geometry edit restores the list from before it. The reply is get_color_samplers' plus changed. Each sampler reports index (0-based), label ("#n", as the Info panel numbers it), x, y, sample_size and sample_pixel's own reading at that point and size — the 8-bit byte fields, or the 16-bit/32-bit float composite report. Committed values only. In a Lab Color document each sampler is sample_pixel's own reading: its codes are L*, a*, b* and alpha, and it adds lab {l, a, b} with no RGB reading.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `samplers` | `array<object>` | yes | — | The new list, in order (#1 first). |
| `samplers[].sample_size` | `integer` | no | one of `1`, `3`, `5` | Side of the averaged square; default 1. |
| `samplers[].x` | `integer` | with parent | — | — |
| `samplers[].y` | `integer` | with parent | — | — |

## `fill_selection`

Fills the active selection — or the whole target when nothing is selected — with ONE colour through a blend mode at an opacity: Edit ▸ Fill…, and Edit ▸ Fill with Foreground/Background Color (⌥⌫ / ⌘⌫; ⇧ keeps transparency). A feathered selection fills in proportion to its coverage. At 8 bits the layer never grows; at 16 and 32 bits a trimmed layer grows to the changed pixels, as the 16-bit brush does — at neither depth under preserve_transparency or Lock Transparency. On a mask or alpha channel the colour becomes its coverage gray (Rec. 709 luma). A red, green, blue or alpha target takes ONE value in that channel alone, 0.30 r + 0.59 g + 0.11 b of the colour's document components (measured against Photoshop, not the Rec. 709 gray: rounded to a code at 8 bits, unrounded at 16 and 32), at opacity × coverage whatever the pixel's alpha. On all of these Hue/Saturation/Color/Luminosity refuse and preserve_transparency refuses. ONE undo step, "Fill". A text or shape layer is rasterized and the result says so. Groups, adjustment layers' pixels, Lock Pixels / Lock All and a retained source refuse by name; Lock Transparency keeps the layer's alpha exactly as preserve_transparency does. Under either, every pixel keeps its alpha exactly: a transparent pixel stays empty, and on a semi-transparent one the colour mixes in at the fill's own opacity × coverage, not boosted by the kept alpha. A fill that changes nothing answers changed:false with a note and adds no undo step. 8-, 16-bit and 32-bit float documents (the 16-bit reply adds storage: "rgba16_unorm" for a layer, "u16" for a mask, colour plane or channel). At 32-bit float the reply's storage is "rgba32_float" for a layer or a colour plane and "u16" for a mask or alpha channel; the colour fills as linear light and only Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Darker Color, Linear Burn, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Pin Light, Difference, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity are available on a layer. There a red, green, blue or alpha target takes its 0.30 r + 0.59 g + 0.11 b value unquantized (of rgba32's linear numbers when rgba32 is passed), in Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Difference or Subtract; Darker Color and Lighter Color refuse there by name. In a 32-bit float document rgba32 replaces color with linear-light numbers, above white included (a mask or alpha channel clips them to 0–1). In QUICK MASK (or with target "quick_mask", which refuses by name outside Quick Mask) it fills the whole Quick Mask coverage with the colour's coverage gray at every depth, 32-bit float included (Edit ▸ Fill…, ⌥⌫ / ⌘⌫ in Quick Mask), ONE undo step "Fill" that leaves the file clean, and answers get_selection's fields plus changed and target "quick_mask"; layer, any other target and preserve_transparency are refused there. In a CMYK document this paints in INK on a layer (or its mask): pass ink [c, m, y, k] in percent (exactly the Color Picker's C/M/Y/K), or color, which converts through the document's CMYK profile; every blend mode but Pass Through, evaluated on 1 − ink. Target cyan, magenta, yellow or black paints that ink plate's stored 1 − ink, and channel:<name> an alpha channel, as a 16-bit colour plane or channel is painted: color's grey is painted (white leaves no ink) and ink refuses. On an RGB document ink refuses. In a Grayscale document the layer is filled with color's gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule (its luminance in the Gray profile), R = G = B; target is layer, mask, quick_mask or channel:<name> (the Gray channel is the layer; red, green, blue and alpha refuse for good), ink refuses, and blend_mode takes the Grayscale modes. In a Lab Color document the layer is filled with color converted by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule (color_space document takes the L*a*b* values as unit codes, exactly); target is layer, mask, lightness, a, b, alpha or channel:<name> (red, green and blue refuse: a Lab document's planes are lightness, a and b), ink refuses, and blend_mode takes the Lab modes. On an Indexed Color document the edit runs on the RGB storage, then each changed pixel goes back onto the palette by the Brush's rule: paint takes the entry nearest the colour (an edge pixel when its coverage is at least 131/255, else it keeps its index), and an erased pixel keeps its index until its alpha falls below 128, when it takes the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the entry nearest the current background colour). Painting takes every blend_mode: a changed pixel is compared with the mode's full-strength colour over its old colour and takes the entry nearest that colour, by the same 131/255 rule; sample_all_layers is off. On a Bitmap document it paints in black and white: the colour becomes black or white by its gray (128 and above is white), the edit runs on the 8-bit gray storage at its opacity, and every pixel goes back to white where its gray over the background at its own alpha reaches 128, else black, so a soft edge lands hard where its coverage reaches about half and a stroke under 50 % opacity changes nothing. blend_mode Normal, Darken or Lighten only (another refuses); sample_all_layers is off (the one layer is the composite). An erased or cleared pixel takes the background, white.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `blend_mode` | `string` | no | one of `Normal`, `Dissolve`, `Darken`, `Multiply`, `Color Burn`, `Linear Burn`, `Darker Color`, `Lighten`, `Screen`, `Color Dodge`, `Linear Dodge (Add)`, `Lighter Color`, `Overlay`, `Soft Light`, `Hard Light`, `Vivid Light`, `Linear Light`, `Pin Light`, `Hard Mix`, `Difference`, `Exclusion`, `Subtract`, `Divide`, `Hue`, `Saturation`, `Color`, `Luminosity` | Blend mode (default Normal). The four HSL modes refuse on a mask, colour plane or alpha channel. |
| `color` | `string` | no | — | Fill colour, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA (its alpha scales the fill). Required unless rgba32 is passed — the swatches are not read. |
| `color_space` | `string` | no | one of `srgb`, `document`, `display_p3` | How color is read. srgb (default): an authored sRGB hex, converted once into the document. document: the hex IS the document's own bytes (sample_color's hex). display_p3: a Display P3 hex, converted once into the document. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | CMYK document only: C, M, Y, K ink in percent 0–100. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index; default the active layer. |
| `opacity` | `number` | no | 0–1 | Fill opacity 0–1 (default 1), separate from the colour's alpha. |
| `preserve_transparency` | `boolean` | no | — | Keep the layer's alpha exactly as it is (default false); on a semi-transparent pixel the colour mixes in at the fill's own opacity × coverage, not boosted by the kept alpha. Lock Transparency does the same. Layer target only. |
| `rgba32` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | 32-bit float documents only, instead of color: [red, green, blue, alpha] as linear light in the document's primaries (sample_color's center_rgba32 / mean_rgba32), red, green and blue 0–65504 (above 1 is above white) and alpha 0–1, used as they are. Takes no color_space; an 8- or 16-bit document and Quick Mask refuse it. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | layer (default), mask, red, green, blue, alpha, channel:<name> or quick_mask (the Quick Mask coverage; the default while in Quick Mask, and what a recording made there saves). |

## `stroke_selection`

Strokes the active selection's edge with ONE colour through a blend mode at an opacity: Edit ▸ Stroke…. The band is width px wide, inside, centred on (default) or outside the selection's 50% contour — Layer Style ▸ Stroke's bands, so the two agree pixel for pixel. For inside (and center's inner half) the canvas edge is an edge too, so select_all + inside strokes a frame; select_all + outside has nothing to stroke and answers changed:false with a note. With nothing selected it strokes the TRUE edge of the layer's own pixels (its alpha; the mask is excluded), in layer space, including any part of the layer beyond the canvas — layer target only: a mask, colour plane or alpha channel needs a selection. The reply's outline is "selection" or "layer_edge"; an empty layer answers changed:false with a note. A layer-edge band grows the layer to cover it in the same undo step, past the canvas if the band reaches there (a stroke wholly off the canvas still answers changed:true); a selection's band is bounded by the canvas, and one that reaches past a trimmed or offset layer's pixels grows that layer to cover the canvas, so Outside and Center strokes land at full width. Neither grows with preserve_transparency or Lock Transparency, which keep the layer's alpha exactly; on a semi-transparent pixel the colour then mixes in at the stroke's own opacity × coverage, not boosted by the kept alpha. On a mask, colour plane or alpha channel the colour becomes fill_selection's gray for that target, Hue/Saturation/Color/Luminosity refuse and preserve_transparency refuses. ONE undo step, "Stroke". Refusals, rasterizing and Lock Transparency are fill_selection's, and Quick Mask refuses by name. A stroke that changes nothing answers changed:false with a note and adds no undo step. 8-, 16-bit and 32-bit float documents (the 16-bit reply adds storage: "rgba16_unorm" for a layer, "u16" for a mask, colour plane or channel; at 16 and 32 bits a selection's band grows a trimmed layer only to the pixels it changes). At 32-bit float the reply's storage is "rgba32_float" for a layer or a colour plane and "u16" for a mask or alpha channel, only Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Darker Color, Linear Burn, Lighten, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Pin Light, Difference, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity are available on a layer, a red, green, blue or alpha target strokes that one channel with fill_selection's value, modes and refusals, and rgba32 replaces color with linear-light numbers, above white included. In a CMYK document this paints in INK on a layer (or its mask): pass ink [c, m, y, k] in percent (exactly the Color Picker's C/M/Y/K), or color, which converts through the document's CMYK profile; every blend mode but Pass Through, evaluated on 1 − ink. Target cyan, magenta, yellow or black paints that ink plate's stored 1 − ink, and channel:<name> an alpha channel, as a 16-bit colour plane or channel is painted: color's grey is painted (white leaves no ink) and ink refuses. On an RGB document ink refuses. In a Grayscale document the stroke paints color's gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule, R = G = B, at 8, 16 and 32 bits, with a selection or on the layer's edge; ink refuses, and blend_mode takes the Grayscale modes. In a Lab Color document the stroke (a selection's band, or the layer's edge with nothing selected) is painted with color converted by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule (color_space document takes the L*a*b* values as unit codes, exactly); target is layer, mask, lightness, a, b, alpha or channel:<name> (red, green and blue refuse: a Lab document's planes are lightness, a and b), ink refuses, and blend_mode takes Normal, Dissolve, Multiply, Linear Burn, Darker Color, Screen, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity; Darken, Color Burn, Lighten, Color Dodge, Difference, Exclusion, Subtract and Divide are unavailable. On an Indexed Color document the edit runs on the RGB storage, then each changed pixel goes back onto the palette by the Brush's rule: paint takes the entry nearest the colour (an edge pixel when its coverage is at least 131/255, else it keeps its index), and an erased pixel keeps its index until its alpha falls below 128, when it takes the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the entry nearest the current background colour). Painting takes every blend_mode: a changed pixel is compared with the mode's full-strength colour over its old colour and takes the entry nearest that colour, by the same 131/255 rule; sample_all_layers is off. On a Bitmap document it paints in black and white: the colour becomes black or white by its gray (128 and above is white), the edit runs on the 8-bit gray storage at its opacity, and every pixel goes back to white where its gray over the background at its own alpha reaches 128, else black, so a soft edge lands hard where its coverage reaches about half and a stroke under 50 % opacity changes nothing. blend_mode Normal, Darken or Lighten only (another refuses); sample_all_layers is off (the one layer is the composite). An erased or cleared pixel takes the background, white.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `blend_mode` | `string` | no | one of `Normal`, `Dissolve`, `Darken`, `Multiply`, `Color Burn`, `Linear Burn`, `Darker Color`, `Lighten`, `Screen`, `Color Dodge`, `Linear Dodge (Add)`, `Lighter Color`, `Overlay`, `Soft Light`, `Hard Light`, `Vivid Light`, `Linear Light`, `Pin Light`, `Hard Mix`, `Difference`, `Exclusion`, `Subtract`, `Divide`, `Hue`, `Saturation`, `Color`, `Luminosity` | Blend mode (default Normal). The four HSL modes refuse on a mask, colour plane or alpha channel. |
| `color` | `string` | no | — | Stroke colour, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA (its alpha scales the stroke). Required unless rgba32 is passed — the swatches are not read. |
| `color_space` | `string` | no | one of `srgb`, `document`, `display_p3` | How color is read. srgb (default): an authored sRGB hex, converted once into the document. document: the hex IS the document's own bytes (sample_color's hex). display_p3: a Display P3 hex, converted once into the document. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | CMYK document only: C, M, Y, K ink in percent 0–100. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index; default the active layer. |
| `location` | `string` | no | one of `inside`, `center`, `outside` | Where the band sits relative to the selection's edge (default center). |
| `opacity` | `number` | no | 0–1 | Stroke opacity 0–1 (default 1), separate from the colour's alpha. |
| `preserve_transparency` | `boolean` | no | — | Keep the layer's alpha exactly as it is (default false); on a semi-transparent pixel the colour mixes in at the stroke's own opacity × coverage, not boosted by the kept alpha. Lock Transparency does the same. Layer target only. |
| `rgba32` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | 32-bit float documents only, instead of color: [red, green, blue, alpha] as linear light in the document's primaries (sample_color's center_rgba32 / mean_rgba32), red, green and blue 0–65504 (above 1 is above white) and alpha 0–1, used as they are. Takes no color_space; an 8- or 16-bit document and Quick Mask refuse it. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | layer (default), mask, red, green, blue, alpha or channel:<name>. |
| `width` | `number` | yes | 1–250 | Stroke width in pixels, 1–250. Required. |

## `read_photoshop_adjustment_preset`

Read a Photoshop adjustment PRESET file and answer the adjustment it holds as {ok, op, params, file}: .acv Curves (RGB presets — the composite and the red, green and blue curves; a CMYK or multichannel preset refuses), .alv Levels (the composite black/white/gamma, its output levels and the red, green and blue stages as r/g/b objects), .ahu Hue/Saturation, .eap Exposure, .blw Black & White and .cha Channel Mixer (RGB presets; a CMYK preset refuses). Files over 64 KiB refuse. color_mode "cmyk" reads a .alv's or .acv's INK channels for a CMYK document's Levels or Curves: the composite and c, m, y, k (Levels stages on L = 1 − ink, Curves points on the ink axes); an RGB .acv and every other extension refuse there. Pass op and params to add_adjustment_layer to create the layer — params carry no `evaluation`, so an Exposure layer takes add_adjustment_layer's default. Changes no document and records no Action step. The UI path is Layer ▸ New Adjustment Layer ▸ From Photoshop Preset…, which opens the op's dialog prefilled with these values.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `color_mode` | `string` | no | one of `rgb`, `cmyk` | rgb (the default) or cmyk: read a .alv/.acv's ink channels. |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | Absolute path (or ~) to a .acv, .alv, .ahu, .eap, .blw or .cha file (a .cha must be an RGB Channel Mixer preset). |

## `detect_horizon`

Find the horizon's tilt with Vision — the Crop tool's Auto button. Reads the flattened composite (a 32-bit float document's tone-mapped display) and edits nothing. Found: {ok, found: true, angle, suggested_crop: {x, y, width, height, angle}} — angle is the Straighten angle in degrees in crop's sign convention, and suggested_crop's keys pass straight into crop. None: {ok, found: false, note} (not an error). Vision answers only for a clear, textured horizon tilted by about 1° to 10°, in steps of about 0.125°; for anything else use fit_crop with an angle or a line. The optional box x, y, width, height (integers, canvas coordinates, origin top-left; all four or none) is the crop box to fit and defaults to the whole canvas; it must lie inside the canvas, at least 1×1. The fit is the Crop tool's: the box keeps its aspect and, where it can, its centre and shrinks, to whole pixels, until every corner of the straightened result lands on image pixels (a 2-pixel margin from the canvas edge), so the crop shows no transparent wedges. It fits against the canvas and ignores layer pixels lying outside it. In a Lab Color document it reads the document's Display P3 view (what the canvas shows).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `height` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `width` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `x` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `y` | `integer` | no | — | — |

## `fit_crop`

The crop box for a straighten — the Crop tool's box fit, set by its Straighten field or its Straighten line. Give exactly one of angle (degrees, -45 to 45, crop's sign: positive turns the picture counter-clockwise on screen) or line [x1, y1, x2, y2] (canvas coordinates of two points on something that should be level or vertical in the UNROTATED image; the angle levels it, and a line steeper than 45° is made vertical). Edits nothing; the reply {ok, angle, x, y, width, height} passes straight into crop. The optional box x, y, width, height (integers, canvas coordinates, origin top-left; all four or none) is the crop box to fit and defaults to the whole canvas; it must lie inside the canvas, at least 1×1. The fit is the Crop tool's: the box keeps its aspect and, where it can, its centre and shrinks, to whole pixels, until every corner of the straightened result lands on image pixels (a 2-pixel margin from the canvas edge), so the crop shows no transparent wedges. It fits against the canvas and ignores layer pixels lying outside it. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document a move or a nearest sampler (crop, canvas size, the quarter turns and flips, nearest resize, rotation and perspective crop) keeps every pixel's index exactly; any other sampler resamples the colours and maps each pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as new area). New canvas area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the current background colour); a crop past the canvas takes the entry nearest its background_color.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `angle` | `number` | no | -45–45 | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `height` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `line` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | Two canvas points [x1, y1, x2, y2]; they must differ. |
| `width` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `x` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `y` | `integer` | no | — | — |

## `put_pixels`

Writes exact pixels onto one raster layer — pixel art, sprites, icons — in ONE call and ONE undo step. REPLACE semantics: each written pixel takes its colour's four bytes verbatim, alpha included, with no blending, so an alpha-0 colour writes transparency and #RRGGBB80 writes exactly alpha 128. Pass runs, buffer or both. runs: horizontal spans {x, y, length (default 1), color} starting at canvas (x, y). buffer: one rect {x, y, width, height, data} whose data is base64 of exactly width×height×4 straight RGBA8 bytes, row 0 at the top. The buffer is written first, then the runs in array order; the last write to a pixel wins. Coordinates are integer canvas pixels and everything must lie inside the canvas (refused by name otherwise). The selection is IGNORED — the coordinates are the confinement, as with transform_layer and move_layers. A write outside a trimmed or offset layer's pixel rect grows the layer to its union with the canvas in the same undo step (refused while its transparency is locked). 8-bit documents only. The reply gives pixels (distinct positions written), bounds and grew_layer; a write that changes no byte answers unchanged: true and adds no undo step. Use render with scale to see the result as crisp enlarged pixels.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `buffer` | `object` | no | — | One rect of raw pixels, written before the runs. |
| `buffer.data` | `string` | no | — | Base64 of exactly width×height×4 straight (non-premultiplied) RGBA8 bytes, row-major, row 0 at the top. |
| `buffer.height` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `buffer.width` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `buffer.x` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `buffer.y` | `integer` | no | — | — |
| `color_space` | `string` | no | one of `srgb`, `document`, `display_p3` | The space of every colour here, run hex and buffer bytes alike: srgb (default) converts once into the document's space; document writes the bytes verbatim; display_p3 converts from Display P3. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Raster layer index (default: the active layer; index is accepted too). A group or an adjustment layer is refused. |
| `runs` | `array<object>` | no | — | Horizontal spans, written in array order after the buffer. |
| `runs[].color` | `string` | with parent | — | #RGB, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA (required). |
| `runs[].length` | `integer` | no | — | Pixels to the right of x, x included (default 1). |
| `runs[].x` | `integer` | with parent | — | — |
| `runs[].y` | `integer` | with parent | — | — |

## `close_document`

Closes one open document — File ▸ Close. document_id is REQUIRED (there is no frontmost default). A document with unsaved changes is refused by name unless discard_changes is true, which LOSES those changes and their recovery copy; save_copy writes a copy first but does not clear the unsaved-changes flag. An open canvas session (text entry, a reopened shape, a Free Transform) is committed first, and a document with a dialog open in its window is refused. The app keeps running after its last document closes. For external MCP clients only: it is not offered to the in-app Assistant panel, and it may not be an Action step. Reply: closed {id, title, path}, discarded_changes and open_documents (the ids still open).

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `discard_changes` | `boolean` | no | — | Default false. True closes a document with unsaved changes and loses them. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | yes | — | The document to close, as list_documents reports it. REQUIRED. |

## `list_adjustment_presets`

An adjustment dialog's Preset popup: list the bounded versioned library of saved adjustment presets, all of them or one op's. Each preset is {name, op, params, file}: params are exactly what add_adjustment_layer, edit_adjustment_layer and apply_filter take for that op (never an `evaluation` — the document decides that), so LOADING a preset is passing its op and params to one of those tools; for bcs, apply_filter's filter is "adjust" with the params flat. A file that is not a readable preset is a `broken` row — {file, code, reason, repairable} with code one of unreadable, oversize, not_json, unknown_version, invalid_schema, duplicate_name — instead of refusing the whole library; repairable is always false here. Resolves no document, so it answers at every depth.

Names are unique per op. |

Presets exist for bcs, black_and_white, channel_mixer, color_balance, curves, exposure, gradient_map, hue_saturation, levels, photo_filter, replace_color, selective_color, shadows_highlights, vibrance, white_balance. A name already used for that op refuses unless replace is true; the same name under another op is a different preset. A library write is a preference: no Undo step, no Action step, and no document changes.

## `list_style_presets`

Window > Styles: list the style presets — the twelve built-ins (group “Default Styles”, read-only, builtin true, file null) first, then the user's groups A–Z, then ungrouped presets. Each row is {name, group, builtin, file, effects (the effect types), blending ({mode, opacity} or null: a preset saved with blending options also sets the layer's blend mode and opacity), style (the preset's style JSON, with include_style)}. A file that is not a readable preset is a `broken` row {file, code, reason, repairable}. Also answers `groups`. Resolves no document.

## `apply_style_preset`

A click on a Styles panel swatch: apply a style preset to `layers` as ONE undo step. Replace (default) sets each layer's style to the preset's; a preset without blending keeps each layer's own fill opacity, Blend If, knockout and Blend Interior option, one with blending also sets the layer's blend mode and opacity. add true is Shift-click: the preset's effects join each layer's style (a repeating effect — drop shadow, inner shadow, stroke, colour or gradient overlay — stacks on top, up to 10; any other replaces its kind). Every layer holds a style, a Pass Through group included (it then composites isolated); a layer that cannot take one is skipped and listed in `skipped` [{layer, reason}]; the call refuses only when no listed layer can. Answers {ok, layers, skipped?, unchanged?}: unchanged true adds no undo step. In a recorded Action, layers is {"$layers": "selected"}. In a Grayscale document a preset's colours are stored as their gray, as set_layer_style stores them. In a Lab Color document a style takes fill_opacity, knockout and every effect; an effect's blend takes Normal, Dissolve, Multiply, Linear Burn, Darker Color, Screen, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color, Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity (Darken, Color Burn, Lighten, Color Dodge, Difference, Exclusion, Subtract and Divide refuse); its colours are sRGB, converted at composite by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color's rule and stored as given. A pattern_overlay's or pattern stroke's tile (a preset or rgba) is sRGB too: each texel becomes its 8-bit L*a*b* values by that rule before scale and angle, and the tile is stored as given. blend_if takes channel red, green and blue, which are Lightness, a and b (each range on the stored values, a* = 0 at 128; not measured against Photoshop); gray refuses, an identity range included.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `add` | `boolean` | no | default `False` | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `group` | `string` | no | — | The preset's group, 1–40 characters, no “/”; omit for an ungrouped preset (a lookup with no group falls back to the built-in of that name). “Default Styles” is the read-only built-in group. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | yes | — | Layer indices (0 = bottom). |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | Style preset name, 1–72 characters, no “/”. |

## `save_style_preset`

The Styles panel's New Style…: save one layer's style as a preset. include_effects (default true) keeps its effects; include_blending (default false) keeps its fill opacity, Blend If, knockout and Blend Interior option and records the layer's blend mode and opacity. CMYK inks and pattern anchors are never stored. A name taken in the group refuses unless replace is true; saving nothing refuses. A library write is a preference: no Undo step, no Action step, and no document changes. In a Grayscale document a preset's colours are stored as their gray, as set_layer_style stores them. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| `include_effects` | `boolean` | no | default `True` | — |

| `name` | `string` | yes | — | Style preset name, 1–72 characters, no “/”. |

## `export_style_presets`

The Styles panel's Export Styles… (every preset, the built-ins included) or a group header's Export Group… (`group`, the built-in group's too): write the presets as a Photoshop style library (.asl) at `path`, replacing a file there. Each style is written with its effects at their own stored angles, its blending options (fill opacity, knockout, Blend Interior, Blend If) and, when saved with blending, its blend mode and opacity; colours are sRGB (a wide colour outside sRGB's gamut is clamped). A preset that cannot be written (a setting Photoshop's dialog cannot hold, Blend If on a CMYK plate) is named in `skipped` ("<name>: <reason>"). import_style_presets reads the file back. Answers {ok, exported, skipped, file}. Writes no preset and resolves no document.

## `straighten_layers`

Rotates layers so a line you name becomes level or plumb — the Ruler tool's Straighten Layer. (x0, y0)–(x1, y1) are the two ends of something in the picture that should be horizontal or vertical (a horizon, a wall edge), in canvas px. The layers turn about the canvas centre by the SMALLEST angle that lays the line along an axis (never more than 45°), so a nearly vertical line is made vertical. Applies to `layers` (default: the selected layers), with their groups' descendants and linked partners, as one undo step; the canvas size does not change (crop afterwards if the corners matter). The reply adds `rotation`, the degrees turned, counter-clockwise on screen. A line already along an axis changes nothing. Follows transform_layers' rules for locks and described layers. Works at 8 and 16 bits and in 32-bit float. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. A Bitmap document: Straighten Layer is the straightened crop, as the one layer cannot turn inside the canvas: crop at the Crop tool's fit of the whole canvas at the line's angle (fit_crop's box for that line), so the canvas shrinks to the window; the reply is crop's with rotation.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |

| `layers` | `array<integer>` | no | — | Layer indices to rotate (default: the selected layers). |
| `sampler` | `string` | no | one of `nearest`, `bilinear`, `bicubic`, `lanczos` | Resampling filter (default bicubic). |
| `x0` | `number` | yes | — | — |
| `x1` | `number` | yes | — | — |
| `y0` | `number` | yes | — | — |
| `y1` | `number` | yes | — | — |

## `perspective_crop`

Crops the document to a quadrilateral and squares it up — the Perspective Crop tool. `corners` are four canvas points in the order top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left (the corners of a sign, a painting, a page photographed at an angle); the result is a width × height canvas showing that quadrilateral flat. Every layer, mask and alpha channel is resampled; anything the quadrilateral reaches beyond the old canvas comes out transparent; guides are cleared. width and height default to the longer of each pair of opposite edges. One undo step. The corners must form a convex quadrilateral. Text and shape layers are rasterized, which needs rasterize_artwork: true; a camera RAW layer refuses the crop until it is rasterized. The four corners of the whole canvas at its own size change nothing. Works at 8 and 16 bits and in 32-bit float. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document a move or a nearest sampler (crop, canvas size, the quarter turns and flips, nearest resize, rotation and perspective crop) keeps every pixel's index exactly; any other sampler resamples the colours and maps each pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as new area). New canvas area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the current background colour); a crop past the canvas takes the entry nearest its background_color. A Bitmap document: it runs on the 8-bit gray storage and every pixel goes back white where its gray over white at its own alpha reaches 128, else black; area outside the corners takes the background, white.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `corners` | `array<array<number>>` | yes | 4–4 items | [[x, y] × 4]: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, in canvas px. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `height` | `integer` | no | 1–∞ | Result height in px (default: automatic). |
| `rasterize_artwork` | `boolean` | no | — | Authorize rasterizing text and shape layers; default false. |
| `sampler` | `string` | no | one of `nearest`, `bilinear`, `bicubic`, `lanczos` | Resampling filter (default bicubic). |
| `width` | `integer` | no | 1–∞ | Result width in px (default: automatic). |

## `trim`

Crops the canvas inward to remove an empty or flat border — Image ▸ Trim…. based_on says what counts as border: "transparent" (rows and columns whose every pixel is fully transparent), "top_left" or "bottom_right" (rows and columns whose every pixel exactly equals that corner pixel of the flattened image). top, bottom, left and right choose which edges may move (default: all four). Read from the flattened composite at the document's own depth; layers keep their pixels and nothing is resampled. One undo step; when no chosen edge has anything to trim, or everything would be trimmed away, nothing changes. The reply's `kept` is the rectangle of the old canvas that remains. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document a move or a nearest sampler (crop, canvas size, the quarter turns and flips, nearest resize, rotation and perspective crop) keeps every pixel's index exactly; any other sampler resamples the colours and maps each pixel to its nearest palette entry (alpha below 128 as new area). New canvas area is the transparent index, or on a document with no transparent colour the entry nearest white, the background colour (in the app, the current background colour); a crop past the canvas takes the entry nearest its background_color. A Bitmap document: not available in Bitmap mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `based_on` | `string` | no | one of `transparent`, `top_left`, `bottom_right` | What to trim away (default transparent). |
| `bottom` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `left` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `right` | `boolean` | no | — | — |
| `top` | `boolean` | no | — | — |

## `reveal_canvas`

Grows the canvas until it holds every layer's pixels — Image ▸ Reveal All. Layers that were moved, pasted or transformed partly off the canvas become fully visible; nothing is resampled and no layer moves relative to another. One undo step. The reply's `origin` is where the old canvas's top-left sits in the new one. Nothing changes when no layer reaches outside the canvas. Works on a CMYK document: the ink's five planes resample premultiplied by alpha as RGB does, and groups, clipping, modes, Fill and masks are kept. In a Lab Color document the resample runs the RGB kernel on the L*a*b* codes. On an Indexed Color document it always answers no change: the Index layer holds no pixel outside the canvas.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `copy_layers_to_document`

Copies layers from one open document into another — what dragging layers from one window's Layers panel (or its canvas, with the Move tool) onto another window does. `layers` of `document_id` (default: its selected layers), groups with everything inside them, land in `to_document_id` above its active layer and become its layer selection, as ONE undo step in the destination. The source document is not changed and the clipboard is not used. placement "auto" (default) lands them by Paste's rule (centred in the view, or on the selection); "in_place" keeps their canvas position. Depth and colour profile are converted to the destination's, as paste does for copied layers, and the reply is paste's: where the layers landed, their new indices and what the conversion changed. Unlike copy and paste of layers, a camera RAW layer lands as its current pixels, with no image source in the destination; one whose pixels are locked refuses by name. Refuses when both ids name the same document. Not recorded in Actions. Works on a CMYK document: ink is copied exactly; into an RGB document the layers convert (relative colorimetric with BPC). Into or out of a Grayscale document the layers convert as paste does, and type, shape and fill layers stay editable, each re-rendered from its authored colours (into Gray as their gray). Into or out of a Lab Color document the layers convert by the mode conversions (into Lab by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Lab Color, out of Lab by Image ▸ Mode ▸ RGB Color with black point compensation, Grayscale and CMYK through 16-bit ProPhoto RGB); profile preserve refuses across modes. On an Indexed Color document this refuses for good.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | The SOURCE document's id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `layers` | `array<integer>` | no | — | Source layer indices (default: the source's selected layers). |
| `placement` | `string` | no | one of `auto`, `in_place` | auto (default) or in_place. |
| `to_document_id` | `integer` | yes | — | The DESTINATION document's id from list_documents. |

## `get_file_info`

The document's file info — File ▸ File Info…: creator (an array of names), copyright, description and keywords (an array). Always all four keys; an absent field is an empty array or string. Each is read from the document's XMP (dc:creator, dc:rights, dc:description, dc:subject), else from the file's IPTC datasets, else from its EXIF Artist, Copyright and ImageDescription. Reads only.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `string` | no | — | Which open document; defaults to the frontmost. |

## `set_file_info`

Sets the document's file info — File ▸ File Info… ▸ OK. Pass only the fields to change: an omitted key keeps the document's own value, and an empty string or array clears that field. One undo step. The fields are saved in the .doctored and written into JPEG, PNG and TIFF exports as XMP (and as EXIF Artist, Copyright and ImageDescription when the document carries an EXIF block with room for them); a file's older IPTC copies of the four fields are removed so they cannot contradict it. The reply is {ok, changed, file_info}; a call that changes nothing reports changed:false and adds no undo step. No pixel changes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `copyright` | `string` | no | — | The copyright notice, at most 2000 characters, one line. |
| `creator` | `array<string>` | no | — | Who made the picture, one entry per person. One string is accepted as a one-entry list. Each entry at most 256 characters, at most 256 entries; entries are trimmed and blank ones dropped. An empty array clears the field. |
| `description` | `string` | no | — | A description or caption, at most 8000 characters. Line feeds are kept; other control characters are refused. |
| `document_id` | `string` | no | — | Which open document; defaults to the frontmost. |
| `keywords` | `array<string>` | no | — | Keywords, one entry each. One string is accepted as a one-entry list. Each entry at most 256 characters, at most 256 entries; entries are trimmed and blank ones dropped. An empty array clears the field. |

## `list_paths`

Lists the document's paths: Bézier outlines kept with the document — undoable, saved in .doctored, never drawn into the picture until one is filled, stroked or made a selection. Each has name, kind ("work": the one unsaved scratch path, always first and always named "Work Path"; "saved"), fill_rule, anchors (a count) and subpaths (set_path's own shape, so it can be edited and passed back). max_paths is the most a document holds. Canvas resizes, crops, rotations and flips move paths with the picture; moving or transforming a layer does not. Paths are not written to PSD, TIFF or any flat format. The Paths panel. A Grayscale document holds paths and vector masks, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |

## `set_path`

Creates a path or replaces one whole — what the Pen tool commits after each click or drag. With neither path nor name it is the WORK PATH (created, or replaced: a document has one). path (or name alone) names a SAVED path: replaced when the document has one of that name, created otherwise. name beside path also renames it in the same step (a work path becomes a saved one). An empty subpaths array stores an empty path. A path already equal to the shape answers changed:false. ONE undo step. A document holds at most 256 paths and 65536 anchors over all of them. 8-, 16-bit and 32-bit float documents. A Grayscale document holds paths and vector masks, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `fill_rule` | `string` | no | one of `nonzero`, `evenodd` | With subpaths: how overlapping subpaths fill. nonzero (default) fills everything a subpath winds around; evenodd makes a subpath inside another a hole. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | Without path: the saved path to create or replace. With path: its new name. At most 255 bytes, unique, not "Work Path". |
| `path` | `string` | no | — | The path to create or replace: a saved path's name, or "Work Path" (the default). |
| `subpaths` | `array<object>` | yes | — | The shape, in absolute canvas pixels (y down from the top-left; it may lie outside the canvas): [{closed, anchors}, …]. The segment from one anchor to the next is the cubic Bézier (point, out, next in, next point), a straight line when both handles sit on their points; a closed subpath also joins its last anchor to its first. Coordinates are kept to four decimals. At most 4096 subpaths and 32768 anchors, each coordinate within ±1000000. |
| `subpaths[].anchors` | `array<any>` | with parent | 1–unbounded items | — |
| `subpaths[].closed` | `boolean` | no | — | Default false. |

## `rename_path`

Renames a path. Renaming the work path SAVES it: it becomes a saved path and the document has no work path until the next one is drawn or traced. A name another path has, an empty name and "Work Path" refuse. ONE undo step. Double-clicking a row in the Paths panel. A Grayscale document holds paths and vector masks, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | — | The new name, at most 255 bytes. |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | A stored path by name: a saved path's name, or "Work Path" for the document's unsaved work path (list_paths). |

## `duplicate_path`

Copies a path as a new saved path named name, or "<its name> copy" (numbered until free) when name is omitted. ONE undo step. Paths panel ▸ Duplicate Path. A Grayscale document holds paths and vector masks, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `name` | `string` | no | — | The copy's name; must be free. |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | A stored path by name: a saved path's name, or "Work Path" for the document's unsaved work path (list_paths). |

## `delete_path`

Deletes a path. ONE undo step. Paths panel ▸ Delete Path. A Grayscale document holds paths and vector masks, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `path` | `string` | yes | — | A stored path by name: a saved path's name, or "Work Path" for the document's unsaved work path (list_paths). |

## `path_to_selection`

Makes the path's fill the selection: every subpath filled by the path's fill rule (an open subpath is closed by a straight line), with the same coverage a shape layer of that outline has. Takes path (a stored path's name) OR subpaths with an optional fill_rule (a shape that is not stored), not both. mode combines it with the current selection; feather softens it; anti_alias false gives a hard edge. A path that covers no canvas pixel leaves nothing selected (replace, intersect) and says so. ONE selection undo step. Answers get_selection's fields. Not in Quick Mask. 8-, 16-bit and 32-bit float documents. Paths panel ▸ Make Selection…. A Grayscale document holds paths and vector masks, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `anti_alias` | `boolean` | no | — | Soften the edge (default true); false selects each pixel the path covers at least half of, fully. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `feather` | `number` | no | 0–250 | Feather radius in pixels (default 0). |
| `fill_rule` | `string` | no | one of `nonzero`, `evenodd` | With subpaths: how overlapping subpaths fill. nonzero (default) fills everything a subpath winds around; evenodd makes a subpath inside another a hole. |
| `mode` | `string` | no | one of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect` | Default replace. |
| `path` | `string` | no | — | A stored path by name: a saved path's name, or "Work Path" for the document's unsaved work path (list_paths). |
| `subpaths` | `array<object>` | no | — | The shape, in absolute canvas pixels (y down from the top-left; it may lie outside the canvas): [{closed, anchors}, …]. The segment from one anchor to the next is the cubic Bézier (point, out, next in, next point), a straight line when both handles sit on their points; a closed subpath also joins its last anchor to its first. Coordinates are kept to four decimals. At most 4096 subpaths and 32768 anchors, each coordinate within ±1000000. |
| `subpaths[].anchors` | `array<any>` | with parent | 1–unbounded items | — |
| `subpaths[].closed` | `boolean` | no | — | Default false. |

## `selection_to_path`

Traces the selection's outline into the WORK PATH, replacing it: closed subpaths under the even-odd rule (a hole is a subpath inside another) that follow the selection's 50% contour within tolerance pixels — straight sides stay straight, corners stay corners, curves become smooth anchors. A larger tolerance gives fewer anchors; a part of the selection no larger than the tolerance is dropped. Refuses with nothing selected, in Quick Mask, and when the outline needs more anchors than a path holds (raise tolerance). The selection itself is unchanged. ONE undo step. The reply has path, anchors and subpaths. 8-, 16-bit and 32-bit float documents. Select ▸ Make Work Path…. A Grayscale document holds paths and vector masks, as an RGB document does, and keeps them in .doctored.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `tolerance` | `number` | no | 0.5–10 | How far, in pixels, the path may stray from the selection's edge (default 2). |

## `fill_path`

Fills the path with ONE colour through a blend mode at an opacity: the path's anti-aliased fill (its fill rule; an open subpath closed by a straight line), inside the selection when there is one. Takes path (a stored path's name) OR subpaths with an optional fill_rule (a shape that is not stored), not both. It is stroke_selection's commit with that coverage as the band, so the colour, color_space, rgba32, blend_mode, opacity, preserve_transparency, layer and target arguments, the layer growing to the filled pixels, the locks, the rasterizing of a text or shape layer and every refusal are stroke_selection's (Quick Mask refuses by name). A path that covers no pixel of the canvas (or of the selection) answers changed:false with a note. ONE undo step, "Fill Path". 8-, 16-bit and 32-bit float documents; the reply is stroke_selection's without width, location and outline. Paths panel ▸ Fill Path. In a CMYK document the path paints in INK on a layer: ink [c, m, y, k] in percent, or color converted through the document's CMYK profile; target cyan, magenta, yellow or black paints that ink plate with color's grey and channel:<name> an alpha channel (ink refuses there). In a Grayscale document the path is painted with color's gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule, R = G = B; ink refuses, and its blend mode takes the Grayscale modes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| `blend_mode` | `string` | no | one of `Normal`, `Dissolve`, `Darken`, `Multiply`, `Color Burn`, `Linear Burn`, `Darker Color`, `Lighten`, `Screen`, `Color Dodge`, `Linear Dodge (Add)`, `Lighter Color`, `Overlay`, `Soft Light`, `Hard Light`, `Vivid Light`, `Linear Light`, `Pin Light`, `Hard Mix`, `Difference`, `Exclusion`, `Subtract`, `Divide`, `Hue`, `Saturation`, `Color`, `Luminosity` | Blend mode (default Normal). The four HSL modes refuse on a mask, colour plane or alpha channel. |
| `color` | `string` | no | — | Fill colour, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA (its alpha scales the fill). Required unless rgba32 is passed — the swatches are not read. |
| `color_space` | `string` | no | one of `srgb`, `document`, `display_p3` | How color is read. srgb (default): an authored sRGB hex, converted once into the document. document: the hex IS the document's own bytes (sample_color's hex). display_p3: a Display P3 hex, converted once into the document. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `fill_rule` | `string` | no | one of `nonzero`, `evenodd` | With subpaths: how overlapping subpaths fill. nonzero (default) fills everything a subpath winds around; evenodd makes a subpath inside another a hole. |
| `ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | CMYK document only: C, M, Y, K ink in percent 0–100. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index; default the active layer. |
| `opacity` | `number` | no | 0–1 | Fill opacity 0–1 (default 1), separate from the colour's alpha. |
| `path` | `string` | no | — | A stored path by name: a saved path's name, or "Work Path" for the document's unsaved work path (list_paths). |
| `preserve_transparency` | `boolean` | no | — | Keep the layer's alpha exactly as it is (default false). Layer target only. |
| `rgba32` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | 32-bit float documents only, instead of color: [red, green, blue, alpha] as linear light in the document's primaries (sample_color's center_rgba32 / mean_rgba32), red, green and blue 0–65504 (above 1 is above white) and alpha 0–1, used as they are. Takes no color_space; an 8- or 16-bit document and Quick Mask refuse it. |
| `subpaths` | `array<object>` | no | — | The shape, in absolute canvas pixels (y down from the top-left; it may lie outside the canvas): [{closed, anchors}, …]. The segment from one anchor to the next is the cubic Bézier (point, out, next in, next point), a straight line when both handles sit on their points; a closed subpath also joins its last anchor to its first. Coordinates are kept to four decimals. At most 4096 subpaths and 32768 anchors, each coordinate within ±1000000. |
| `subpaths[].anchors` | `array<any>` | with parent | 1–unbounded items | — |
| `subpaths[].closed` | `boolean` | no | — | Default false. |
| `target` | `string` | no | — | layer (default), mask, red, green, blue, alpha or channel:<name>. |

## `stroke_path`

Runs the Brush or the Eraser along the path: every subpath is one stroke that follows its outline (a closed subpath returns to its first anchor; an open one is not closed; a one-anchor subpath is a dot), at one pressure. Takes path (a stored path's name) OR subpaths with an optional fill_rule (a shape that is not stored), not both. tool "brush" (default) is brush_stroke and "eraser" is eraser_stroke, and size, hardness, flow, spacing, angle, roundness, opacity, layer and target mean what they mean there — as do color, color_space, rgba32 and blend_mode, which the eraser refuses. The selection confines the stroke, and every refusal of the stroke tool applies (locks, groups, a RAW layer until it is rasterized). Nothing is painted unless every subpath fits one stroke: a subpath that flattens to more than 10,000 points or leaves ±100,000 px refuses the whole call, naming the subpath. ALL subpaths are ONE undo step, "Stroke Path". 8-, 16-bit and 32-bit float documents: a float layer is painted in linear light as brush_stroke paints it (rgba32 for a colour above white, the float blend modes) and erased as eraser_stroke erases it. The reply is the stroke's own, plus tool, subpaths, points and changed. Paths panel ▸ Stroke Path. In a CMYK document the path paints in INK on a layer: ink [c, m, y, k] in percent, or color converted through the document's CMYK profile; target cyan, magenta, yellow or black paints that ink plate with color's grey and channel:<name> an alpha channel (ink refuses there). In a Grayscale document the path is painted with color's gray by Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale's rule, R = G = B; ink refuses, and its blend mode takes the Grayscale modes.

| `blend_mode` | `string` | no | one of `Normal`, `Dissolve`, `Darken`, `Multiply`, `Color Burn`, `Linear Burn`, `Darker Color`, `Lighten`, `Screen`, `Color Dodge`, `Linear Dodge (Add)`, `Lighter Color`, `Overlay`, `Soft Light`, `Hard Light`, `Vivid Light`, `Linear Light`, `Pin Light`, `Hard Mix`, `Difference`, `Exclusion`, `Subtract`, `Divide`, `Hue`, `Saturation`, `Color`, `Luminosity` | Brush only: brush_stroke's blend mode (default Normal). |
| `color` | `string` | no | — | Brush only: hex colour, #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA (default #000000). |
| `color_space` | `string` | no | one of `srgb`, `document`, `display_p3` | Brush only: how color is read, as on brush_stroke. |
| `document_id` | `integer` | no | — | Target document id from list_documents; omit for the frontmost document. |
| `fill_rule` | `string` | no | one of `nonzero`, `evenodd` | With subpaths: how overlapping subpaths fill. nonzero (default) fills everything a subpath winds around; evenodd makes a subpath inside another a hole. |
| `flow` | `number` | no | — | brush_stroke's flow. |
| `hardness` | `number` | no | 0–100 | Edge hardness in percent (default 100 = crisp). |
| `ink` | `array<number>` | no | 4–4 items | CMYK document only: C, M, Y, K ink in percent 0–100. |
| `layer` | `integer` | no | — | Layer index; default the active layer. |
| `opacity` | `number` | no | 0–1 | — |
| `path` | `string` | no | — | A stored path by name: a saved path's name, or "Work Path" for the document's unsaved work path (list_paths). |

Takes no color_space; an 8- or 16-bit document and Quick Mask refuse it. |
| `roundness` | `number` | no | — | brush_stroke's roundness. |
| `size` | `number` | no | — | Stroke width in px (1-512, default 16). |
| `spacing` | `number` | no | — | brush_stroke's spacing. |

The segment from one anchor to the next is the cubic Bézier (point, out, next in, next point), a straight line when both handles sit on their points; a closed subpath also joins its last anchor to its first. Coordinates are kept to four decimals. At most 4096 subpaths and 32768 anchors, each coordinate within ±1000000. |
